Reinhard: "The souls inhabiting the holy relic meld and merge with your own soul. The destruction of soul matter only links to the destruction of physical matter when the resulting amalgam is damaged. No man in this world would die just by having their lid opened and the contents removed."
Ren: "So basically..."
*He was saying that my and Marie's souls weren't damaged, but only split apart. It wasn't the weapon's destruction that led to the destruction of the flesh, but rather the damage inflicted upon the souls within it.*
*The realization that Marie was perfectly fine made me exhale a sigh of relief.*
*However, I had trouble accepting that the truth was that simple. He spoke of the act as if it was easy to do, but I couldn't help but think otherwise. It seemed like he crushed a packet of peanuts without damaging the contents.*
Reinhard: "Do you understand now?"
*Though I still had some questions about the issue, I nodded wordlessly while averting my gaze from his.*
*The main deal was that he had abilities that were nothing short of divine, and that he used them to keep me alive.*
*Why did he do that, anyway?*
Ren: "Why did you go through with something so roundabout?"
*He could've killed me right then and there. Hell, he could kill me right now. Even if there were a hundred of me and we all banded up against him, we wouldn't stand a snowball's chance in hell.*
Ren: "What do you plan to do with me?"
Reinhard: "My plans for you? ...Hmm."
*Was my question really that strange?*
*Reinhard actually processed it with a pensive look on his face.*
Reinhard: "I merely wished to converse with you."
Ren: "Wha...?"
*Was he fucking around with me?*
*I almost shouted that out loud, but the pressure of his being had filled the room and gained so much density that my tongue failed to move.*
*I could feel that he was about to speak something laden with danger.*
*Words that would curse me if they entered my ears. Words that I shouldn't even hear, let alone listen to.*
Reinhard: "Zarathustra. Have you ever felt that you had already experienced a current event?"
Reinhard: "Even as you stand chained by dread beyond imagination, in absolute peril, haunted by terror incarnate, and even as you stare death itself in the eyes — have you ever found yourself feeling like you knew that exact experience?"
Ren: "..."
*I felt some recent memories of mine stir within my head.*
*Reinhard spoke words that were...*
*"This déjà vu just won't ever stop."*
*The same as his...*
*The only difference was in the way they presented it, but that could be chalked up to their personalities. However, there was absolutely no doubt that we were talking about the same thing.*
Reinhard: "Of course, the same goes for the pleasures that color our lives. Beverages that melt your tongue, music that tugs at your heart strings and dames of beauty that could fell vast empires. Have you ever felt that which is best in life to be akin to experiences borrowed through meager photographs?"
*That made me remember Himuro's visage.*
*I could still feel her warmth, and it allowed me to muster the foolhardiness of a suicidal madman.*
*A confrontation with this Golden man almost made believe that my lifespan was being chipped away, and yet, I looked at him head-on.*
Ren: "So what, then...? What are you trying to tell me...?"
Reinhard: "Well... The burdening grief accompanying that feeling can be equated to a mantle enveloping a challenger heading straight into the unknown we call 'death'. That is why I implore you to listen to what I have to say."
*Was he just messing around? I glared at him as if to ask that, and he only shrugged to indicate that I was misunderstanding him.*
Reinhard: "No, not at all. It just so happens to be that death is the optimal subject to refer to when wording the dread of foreknowledge."
Reinhard: "Thus, as one so disheartened by the idea of death, you deserve to know that it is not nearly as frightening as you think. What you truly ought to fear is the foreknowledge that deprives death of all its dreadful awe and solemn majesty."
*A thing more frightening than death itself?*
Reinhard: "To name an example... I recognize this very moment, this very space, this very atmosphere and our facing of one another."
Reinhard: "I have already spoken all these words to you, and I recognize that without fault."
*What the hell was he saying?*
*I didn't remember anything like that. However, he didn't sound like he was speaking of a hypothetical scenario.*
Reinhard: "Do you not remember?"
Ren: "You got the wrong guy."
*A forced retort.*
Reinhard: "Your memories are not failing you. This is, without a doubt, the very first time we talk to each other in these circumstances."
*The Golden phantom relaxed his lips and spoke something peculiar.*
Reinhard: "Hear and know that what I remember is not the past."
Ren: "Not the... past?"
Reinhard: "I remember the present."
*My head failed to work, my body failed to move, and as I felt something really unpleasant within the conversation; an urge to vomit built up within me.*
*The dread enveloping me felt so vast that I thought my heart would jump out of my chest. In the end, I fought through it to process what he was saying.*
Reinhard: "Long ago, I lived my own life. A life in which we met like we did and conversed like we are right now. You may not remember it, but I do."
*That was completely his own problem. He could spend days talking about it, and I still wouldn't remember shit.*
*Was he talking about a previous life?*
Reinhard: "Of course, I am not referring to the past. It is all about this very day and this very moment within this very space. I remember it all."
Ren: "Do you have a sort of precognition or something?"
Reinhard: "...You really do not seem to remember it. Are you perhaps a different person from the one before?"
*I couldn't be any less equipped to answer that question. None of what he said rang a bell, so he might as well have been talking to a wall.*
Reinhard: "To be able to see into the future would be true bliss. Sadly, I do not possess such a power."
*His lip shaped a self-deriding smile.*
Reinhard: "What I remember is the exact experience of the present, down to the most meager of sensations caught by my five senses. I am not recalling similar events; I only feel that I had done this in a previous life."
Ren: "Previous...?"
Reinhard: "What I am saying is that I am remembering the time when I, being not unlike the Reinhard Heydrich I am now, called you before me and had a similar dialogue on a day no different from this one."
*I didn't get him at all.*
*To me, the only present was now. This very moment.*
Reinhard: "So you claim that your present is naught but the moment that is now?"
Reinhard: "It must be pure bliss. I cannot help but envy you."
Ren: "What are you getting at...?"
Reinhard: "I wished to witness your person with my own eyes. You are not alone in the dark, for Karl has not primed me about anything, either."
Ren: "Karl...?"
*Karl? Who was that?*
Reinhard: "Karl Krafft. That is the name he gave me in his introduction. A transcendent who is no friend to the ordinary."
Reinhard: "For one thing about him, he claims to have had thousands of names. Surely you must know at least one of them. Faust, The Count of St. Germain, Paracelsus, Cagliostro..."
*Cagliostro?*
Reinhard: "And Mercurius... Likely the most recognizable of them all."
Ren: "..."
*This was giving me a headache. How long had the guy been alive?*
*Just by considering his relation to Marie, his minimum possible age was at least two hundred, but now I was supposed to process that he existed even prior to that.*
*And then I was supposed to believe that, come wartime, he changed his name to Karl Krafft and mingled with the Obsidian Round Table.*
*Not only that, but he was the one who met with the once-human Reinhard and Father Trifa, transforming them into the inhuman beings they now were.*
*Downright ridiculous. Even with the greatest proof sitting right before me, I couldn't just accept it so easily.*
Ren: "...Do you believe any of that?"
Reinhard: "I neither do nor do not. I fail to care, for that is not important."
Reinhard: "The crux of the matter is that he is an interesting fellow who possesses power and shares my objective. As such, there are no problems worth the breath."
Ren: "Objective?"
Reinhard: "I told you of foreknowledge, did I not?"
*As he spoke, Reinhard's voice was filled with malice for an enemy — for a fate that must be averted, and yet, I could feel a hint of awe for something of sacred divinity.*
Reinhard: "I began to know it when I befriended Karl. Since then, the world seemed dull beyond human words. My life prior to that was not one of many passions, either, but the realization only served to make it worse."
Reinhard: "The feelings you call achievement, release and satisfaction are completely alien to the heart that beats in my chest. Prior to Karl, I used to be oblivious to that fact, as well as the bliss it meant. A foolish bliss, but bliss nonetheless."
Reinhard: "Then, I realized that 'it' was not there."
Reinhard: "I led a life in which there was not a thing I could not do, not a rank I could not achieve, not an enemy I could not defeat, not a woman I could not bed, and no wealth I could not earn. And then, I realized that I lacked the delight, the excitement, and the hastening of the heart that any common man feels upon crossing even the smallest of mountains."
Reinhard: "Karl told me that I was not releasing my full potential."
Reinhard: "Now does that not sound trite? It is indistinguishable from the delusion of a young man intoxicated with the feeling of omnipotence, and yet, he was able to speak that out loud. Indeed, you would be hard-pressed to find anything more hackneyed."
Reinhard: "Apparently, I was born in the wrong world. The difficulty here is too low for me to even begin to care. Unwilling as I was, though, I was still an inhabitant. And as such, I tried to adapt and make the best of it... But then came Karl, stripping me of the heavy indifference I never knew I adorned."
Reinhard: "He made me aware of foreknowledge. Of the fact that regardless of what I do, I am perpetually tortured by tedium. In a sense, he is worthy of my grudge, for he destroyed the me that strived to be human."
Ren: "..."
*I probably didn't get half of what Reinhard was saying, but I understood that his goal could be boiled down to nothing more than...*
Ren: "You only want satisfaction?"
Reinhard: "Nothing more, nothing less."
*He answered with no hesitation or pretention — only childish straightforwardness.*
Reinhard: "To be precise, there are two things I want. One is the manifestation of a situation that I would find difficult to overcome even with all of my power. The other is the unknown that lies beyond that, though I know not which one will come first."
Reinhard: "The world we live in is not meant for me. Therefore, I will create and unleash one where I belong. I will summon a mountain that is worth the journey, then traverse it."
Reinhard: "That will be the demise of the olden order and the end of foreknowledge. We call it a ghetto, and rightfully so. Anyone within would easily become riotous."
*He was not of this world, so he would destroy it all and create one fit for him.*
*Hagall. Destruction. The day the olden order ends. The Dies Irae...*
*Spinne's words came back to me.*
*They must not be brought back to this world. They were monsters. Beasts beyond co-existence.*
*The construction of a magic circle. The rite of return. Competing murderers and the souls they sacrifice.*
*I see... So he was...*
Ren: "You're incomplete."
*He was already beyond all imagination, and yet, that was a display of only a few tenths, if not hundredths, of his total power. Honestly, he might as well have been a creature from a higher dimension.*
*If there was a world befitting this beast, I really didn't want to see it. It would surely be no different than witnessing the devil on his very own hellish throne.*
Reinhard: "Good eye. Indeed, I am but a shadow of my true self, so to speak. The greater part of me is currently in my own world that I created myself."
Ren: "How did you do that?"
Reinhard: "You will come to know when you understand Karl's sorcery. However, you can rest assured that nothing I am doing is extraordinary."
Reinhard: "Still, there is no denying that it is relatively grand in terms of scale. Both leaving and returning requires quite a large setting."
Reinhard: "First was Berlin, and now..."
*The Gold squinted his eyes and implicitly halted his words for several seconds, imploring me to imagine and word it myself.*
*An action reminiscent of a devil with a sick taste for human reactions.*
Ren: "This city..."
*With a creaking voice, I squeezed out those words.*
Reinhard: "Indeed."
Ren: "So—"
*Was that what he was getting at? What he wanted me to take away from this?*
Ren: "You're saying that this city and the people within it are nothing but props to you!?"
*Such hubris. Such inhumanity. So fiendish a thought that no human could think and act by it.*
Reinhard: "That anger of yours is misguided. Be aware that if it were not for us, this city would not exist in the first place."
Ren: "What?"
Reinhard: "There lived a man known as Haushofer. An authority on geopolitics, a self-proclaimed magician and, well... to put it bluntly, a plaything to Karl and I."
Reinhard: "He stayed in this country once. Now, what do you believe he was doing?"
Ren: "..."
*A dreadful thought passed through my mind.*
*Me, Kasumi, Shirou, Honjou... All of the current Suwahara inhabitants were born into a land noticed by these lunatics — into a city planned and built to be their little game board.*
Reinhard: "Shambhala. The eastern paradise. He was quite fond of that particular land. So fond, in fact, that the savory delusion drove him to explore into it. An interesting man, indeed. What a stroke of misfortune it was for him to be noticed by Karl."
Reinhard: "Haushofer had a record of several areas fit for Shambhala... This land was one of the finer picks in terms of soul quality, and — much to everyone's misfortune — it was also the one that caught Karl's attention. The rest, I believe, needs no further explanation."
*Haushofer and Karl, also known as Mercurius. They were two men on completely different levels.*
*To be a magician was an eccentric hobby born out of the madness caused by excessive amounts of learning... The former man was exactly that, but the latter was, without a doubt, the real thing.*
*So real, in fact, that he could turn a whole city into a stage setting.*
Reinhard: "Zarathustra Ubermensch -- the road to transcension."
Reinhard: "Goldene Hagalaz. Swastika. This Shambhala is but a sacred chest meant to release my ideal once opened. Much like the Ark of the Covenant from the holy scriptures. It is but an Ahnenerbe as large as a city."
Reinhard: "However, it is not just the city, either. All the lives inhabiting Shambhala, without exception, have no other purpose than to sustain us. Giving meaning to life might be the domain of philosophers or monks, but this is a case where they are absolutely unnecessary."
Reinhard: "After all, why would the lives within this town need a metaphysical concept to give them purpose when they already carry a meaning to their being as clear as it is clean?"
Ren: "..."
*This bastard just went and said it out loud.*
Ren: "We're fodder?"
Reinhard: "You seem to be averse to the term 'prop', so I tried expressing it in another way, but if you dislike that as well, what is there for me to do?"
Reinhard: "Swastikas only open to battles. The blossoming of bloodshed and the withering of souls. Thus, a vehement opposition is a necessity."
Reinhard: "A massacre of unarmed citizens is a mass execution and by no means a battlefield. It would not open the Swastika, nor would it fit my taste. The quality of souls would dwindle."
Reinhard: "You understand now, do you not? That is why you exist. And that is why you must conquer the eight battlefields, ushering in the fire and brimstone of my advent. Your refusal would only result in more senseless casualties — in short, you are left with no other options."
*He was completely right. I was utterly and thoroughly cornered.*
*Whether I fled or fought, Reinhard's return was inevitable. The only good method of dealing with this was to kill several of them at one Swastika, and I knew full well just how difficult that was.*
*Karl Krafft. An abnormally unpleasant character who was cunning beyond measure. I could understand why he was hated by Wilhelm and the others, but I had a hunch that the very malice directed at him was part of his absurd plot.*
*My situation was like that of a wanted criminal. Sakurai described it as a game of hide-and-seek, and that wasn't far off the mark at all.*
*I was a substitute to Krafft, the Vice Commander they so vehemently abhorred. And I knew the extent of their hatred first-hand, having been hunted by a few of them in the past.*
*But if that was the case, then...*
Reinhard: "What say you? Assuming you have attained an understanding of your own position, the time for decisions is at hand. Will you retreat or make your march?"
Reinhard: "Or will you face me here and now...?"
Ren: "...!"
*For a moment, my heart throbbed so loudly it reverberated within my ears.*
*Here is the place. Now is the time. The only time.*
*He had been pressuring me since this started and I couldn't even look him straight in the eye.*
*Thoughts and hubris beyond measure, a presence so overwhelming that I could physically feel it... Reinhard Heydrich was so far out of bounds that simply keeping myself together felt a struggle in itself.*
*However, I felt that this was also a golden opportunity. The moment when I had to throw away all thoughts about the probability of success and make a headlong dive into a battle against him.*
*And so, I stood up.*
Ren: "Give Marie back."
*Straightforward words that contained only what was necessary, spoken while glaring at the Golden monster and holding back the uneasiness and chills that felt like they could evaporate my body.*
Ren: "Just try and see if you can take me on, you bastard."
Ren: "Or are you afraid that you're too incomplete to handle me and her together?"
*A provocation so dangerous it made a tightrope walk seem a cakewalk. If he so desired, the beast before me could destroy a human without as much as lifting a finger.*
*Based on what Reinhard said thus far, I concluded that he wanted me to take up the role of their opponent. As ridiculous as that sounded, he wished for a fierce enough adversary to satisfy him.*
*Which meant that I, in my current state, was hardly even worthy to be killed. However, displaying fear or servility might disappoint him enough to end me.*
*I had to be a powerful foe. A mighty, ferocious hero that would make the beast wish to go all-out.*
*Stop tangling up, my damn tongue. Stop shaking, my fucking limbs. Shut up and slow down, my heart.*
Ren: "If I had Marie, beating you right now would be no big deal."
*To what was undoubtedly the greatest bluff in all of my life, he responded with—*
Reinhard: "Haha, hahahaha..."
*Reinhard hung his head, chuckled, and then threw it back and laughed out loud.*
Reinhard: "Hahahah, hahahahahah, hahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahah!"
Reinhard: "Splendid, hahahah! Oh dear, what an excellent piece of work. You prepared him too well for this, Karl!"
Reinhard: "But would you look at that... heh heh heh. I do know that we are not at the correct part of the process, yet I cannot help but feel frustrated. His desperation is also within the realm of foreknowledge, and thus, meaningless. Although, I believe I could accept it as another step on the road towards the gospel. The end is nigh!"
*With that, the hand covering his handsome face started to shine and drown the surrounding darkness in a golden light.*
Reinhard: "Take her."
Ren: "...Ghah!"
*Something came flying towards me, crashed into my chest and shot me backwards. The gold burning my eyes started to shrink and fade away as I began to feel him disappear.*
Reinhard: "I am not so savage as to lay a hand on the woman of my dearest friend. However, I do believe the possibility of a paramour might drive you to perfect — to elevate — your passion and affection alike."
Reinhard: "This is our brief parting, Zarathustra. Having displayed your dissatisfaction with my current power, you can no longer escape."
Ren: "Wait!"
*I shouted towards what was left of Reinhard's presence.*
*One more. Just one more thing I had to ask him before he left.*
*And that was—*
Ren: "What's Himuro's role in all this...? What is Theresia to you!?"
Reinhard: "...!"
*In response, Reinhard gave me a moment of silence before continuing.*
Reinhard: "Inquire with the priest."
*I asked Reinhard exactly because that guy didn't seem trustworthy, and yet that was the answer he so cheerfully gave me.*
Reinhard: "Interesting. I am very intrigued to know that you found a friend in Isaak's offspring. Or is it love, perhaps? Quite the philanderer, I see. And more of a man than Karl ever was. Hahahahahah—"
Reinhard: "I cannot wait. My heart aches with anticipation. Bless me with the light of the unforseen and break the chains of recurrence."
Reinhard: "When the final battle comes, I promise to face you with all of my Legion."
*With a laughter that roared throughout the space, the Gold shrunk with inverse proportion until it reached the boundary between one and zero and disappeared, leaving me with an explosion that blew me away once more.*
*...*
*...*
*...*
*...*
Ren: "...Shit."
*I hadn't blacked out. I was simply frustrated and ashamed by what had just happened. He held the upper hand the entire time, I failed to make him feel the least bit threatened, and then I displayed open relief when that hell had concluded. It all made me want to curse in frustration.*
Ren: "That aside, though..."
*I shifted my gaze to the side and breathed a sigh. As barely as I did it, I fulfilled my primary goal.*
Ren: "Welcome back, Marie."
Marie: "Nnh... Hm? What happened to me?"
*She sat next to me and tilted her head, all confused.*
Ren: "You don't remember anything?"
Marie: "Ah, well... maybe? I don't really know how to put this right now."
Ren: "I see..."
*We both went through some extraordinary stuff, but I guess it was best to leave them behind us for now. There were countless more important things to do and think about.*
*Reinhard told me that there was no escape, but fighting that beast mano a mano was the peak of stupidity. From here onwards, I had to do something to prevent him from showing himself ever again.*
*So, I had to figure out what that "something" was as soon as possible.*
Ren: "Marie, are you hurt anywhere?"
Marie: "Hurt? No, I'm fine."
Ren: "Try standing up."
*I helped her do that and started examining her from top to bottom, looking for anything wrong.*
*The fact that I was doing that with the mindset of a swordsman checking his blade for any nicks made me feel kinda bad, but I considered it a priority to get a grasp on her state before we did anything else.*
*After all, she had the appearance of a girl about my age, and eyeing her up from point-blank range was really damn discourteous, but... well, she wasn't the type of girl to mind it. Hell, if she did, even I would be too embarrassed to do this.*
*And so, with feelings of gratitude towards her obliviousness...*
Marie: "..."
*I would've liked to unroll her sleeves and raise her skirt, but...*
Marie: "..."
*Uhm, uhh... What the hell? Why was she looking at me like that?*
Marie: "Ren, you're too close."
*She put her hands on my chest and pushed me away — a clear statement that she didn't want me coming any closer.*
Ren: "...Wha-?"
*Her push wasn't very strong, but the surprise was so great that I staggered.*
Marie: "What were you trying to do?"
Ren: "Well, I just..."
*I only wanted to check if she was really not injured.*
Marie: "I told you that I'm fine. Don't stare at me so much. It's embarrassing."
Ren: "Emb-huh...?"
*Embarrassed? This girl? That couldn't be right, why would she...?*
Marie: "Your eyes were lecherous."
Ren: "Lecherous?"
*Where and how did she learn that word? Wait, since when did she even have feelings of bashfulness?*
*As I stood there, confused at the unexpected event, Marie looked around the area. Then, with another, serious expression I'd never seen on her, she spoke.*
Marie: "Ren, let's hurry up and leave. Something about this place doesn't feel right."
Ren: "O-Okay..."
*While I tried to get a grasp on the reasons for her change, she took the situation into her own hands and made me come after her as she strutted off.*
*And so, with the eyes of a person standing before a heavy obstacle, she opened the gate I went through.*
*Beyond which stood—*
Trifa: "Oh?"
Trifa: "Greetings, little lady. I nearly failed to recognize you."
*Valeria Trifa, the priest that brought me here. Marie stood proud and glared at him as one would glare at an enemy... Well, not like there was any doubt he was an enemy, but...*
*He gave a slight chuckle and...*
Trifa: "You too, Mr. Fujii. I am impressed that you are alive. I listened in on the conversation, and I was quite moved by your fiery words towards Him. Though you might not find it pleasant, I would like to say that you have my respect."
Ren: "Yeah, well..."
*I was going to give him a quick "Thanks for that", but then...*
Marie: "Who are you? You're so strange."
*As bad at reading the mood as ever, Marie broke into our exchange.*
Marie: "Two of you...? No. What a weird person... The face doesn't match. Hey, you..."
Trifa: "What is it, little lady? You can call me Trifa."
Marie: "Trifa, where is your body?"
Ren: "...?"
Trifa: "My..."
*Marie's words made me tilt my head in puzzlement. Father Trifa, on the other hand, narrowed his eyes with visible admiration.*
Trifa: "Well, little lady. This is supposed to be a secret, but the real me is imprisoned in a large castle. And I would be ecstatic if a courageous princess or a valiant prince came to rescue poor little old me..."
Trifa: "What do you say? Would you be so kind as to take up this quest for me?"
Marie: "Of course we would. We can start now, if you want."
Trifa: "I see. Now this is quite something. Hahaha..."
Ren: "Hey!"
*Their clearly meaningless exchange pissed me off to the point where I grabbed Marie's arm and pulled her away from him.*
Ren: "Don't get too close to her. Anyway, we're done here, right?"
Trifa: "Oh yes, indeed we are. I have fulfilled the mission that Lord Heydrich gave me, so you can take your leave right away..."
Trifa: "Unless..."
*He left off the rest of the sentence and his smile shifted into a crescent moon, his eyes opened sharp and his irises, reminiscent of frozen lakes, released a menacing glow.*
*The priest implied he would be ready for a battle here and now.*
Ren: "..."
*Well, that was definitely an option. Reinhard wasn't anywhere close, and I had Marie with me again, so having a go at fighting Father Trifa wouldn't have been a bad idea at all.*
*However...*
Ren: "Nah, I'll just get out."
*I subdued my emotions, heaved a sigh, and chose to retreat for the time being.*
Trifa: "I see. What a relief. If we battled here, I could not stop worrying about Theresia."
*Indeed. This was the church, and she was somewhere in it. Not to mention the possibility of Wilhelm, Rusalka and Sakurai being here, too.*
*If I inconsiderately went wild here, there was no telling what could happen to her.*
Trifa: "You might not trust me at all, but just for the sake of it, as a man of God, allow me to make a promise that I will not harm Theresia, nor let anyone else do so."
Ren: "Your 'God' is Reinhard, though, isn't it?"
Trifa: "Even if that was the case, know that he would not harm her, either."
Ren: "..."
*A few seconds passed as we glared at one another, and suddenly, my emotions wavered.*
*Even if I chose not to fight him now, I could still take Himuro and run away with her. Sure, their home field advantage made the probability of success extremely questionable, but if it meant rescuing her from these psychos, it might be worth it.*
Marie: "Hey, Ren, listen."
*As I considered that course of action, Marie pulled on my sleeve.*
Marie: "This person isn't lying."
Ren: "..."
*Really? Well, there was no denying that she displayed a lot of certainty, but damn, what the hell happened to her?*
*Crap, I couldn't help but feel uneasy about this. I had no clue what her change meant or where it would lead, so trusting her would be like a reckless gamble.*
Ren: "Why do you think so?"
Marie: "Because I can see the real him."
Ren: "..."
*Shit, I didn't get it at all. Father Trifa was Father Trifa, the very same nutjob shaking his shoulders as he held back his laughter at fuck knows what.*
*I had to make a decision.*
Marie: "..."
*Marie looked at me with sincerity and honesty that was never there before.*
*I didn't know the reason for her change, but I felt that it was something to be glad about.*
*The Marie I got from Mercurius was almost doll-like in demeanor and knew neither weal nor woe, so I always felt a bit uncomfortable about using her as a tool.*
*Now, though, she was voicing opinions she herself formed and asked me to believe in her as a partner. Who was I to reject that?*
Ren: "...Alright."
*I didn't trust Father Trifa at all, nor was I lowering my guard towards him. I had enough of his farces to last me a lifetime.*
*Instead, I believed in Marie. Not Father Trifa, but Marie, the girl at my side.*
Ren: "We're leaving. Lead us to the exit."
Trifa: "Why, certainly. Come along, then."
*Valeria Trifa respectfully bowed his head and started to show us the way out.*
Trifa: "Oh, I nearly forgot to tell you that your friend did not die. He might be worried about you, so do go and give him peace of mind."

*Kasumi's lowered voice was full of heart-rending anxiety. The wild-looking young man was the main reason she managed to stay put in the room for all those twelve hours.*
Kasumi: "Look, I'll stop asking about what you've been doing since you disappeared from school, so please, just tell me what's going on now. What do you mean, I shouldn't go to school? What did Ren get himself into? "
Shirou: "Ask him when he shows up."
Kasumi: "That idiot's not coming!"
Shirou: "Seems like."
*At this point, even Shirou seemed to have grown tired of the situation. He shrugged his shoulders and gave Ellie a look.*
Ellie: "Ah, I don't think so. She's already wary of me, and if it escalates into a fight she'll totally kick my ass. If you want to shut her up, do it yourself."
Kasumi: "What? Want your ass handed to you? Well, c'mon!"
Shirou: "What's with the kung fu stance?"
*Shirou scratched the back of his head and let out a sigh — even he had to admit he'd ended up in a dumb situation.*
Shirou: "Well, I might as well spill all I know, but the thing is — I doubt you'd believe me anyway."
Kasumi: "That's something for me to decide."
Shirou: "But you don't trust me, do ya?"
*Which meant it was a mere waste of time to explain things to her — Shirou let out another long and exhausted sigh.*
Shirou: "I can't imagine this not being a waste of time."
Ellie: "What can I do. You've brought this on yourself."
Shirou: "So how about we put this little convo on hold for now?"
*It would certainly have been a lot easier for Kasumi to trust Ren's word, but she had no guarantees he was truly coming, and it was not clear whether he would tell her anything even if he showed up. Or rather, he would most definitely try to keep it a secret. And Kasumi understood that very well.*
Kasumi: "Well, if you insist, but..."
*She raised a finger in front of Shirou.*
Kasumi: "Just tell me one thing, that's all I ask. I'll make it a question you can't dodge."
Shirou: "Alright. I'll reveal my three sizes, if that's what you want."
Kasumi: "I know them, so stuff it!"
Shirou: "You do?!"
Ellie: "Ah, Kasumi, share them with me later, ok?"
Kasumi: "So..."
*Kasumi did the best she could to calm down and refrain from snapping back at him — instead, she finally voiced her question.*
Kasumi: "Um..."
*While at first glance it would seem it had nothing to do with the present situation, Kasumi had a suspicion that her inquiry might have been connected to all the important answers she wished for. One question that she had been dying to ask all this time.*
Kasumi: "What made you two fight back then?"
*And in the precise moment she uttered those words—*
Kasumi: "...?!"
*The lights went out — all three had been suddenly enveloped in darkness, as if during a blackout.*
Kasumi: "What...?"
Shirou: "Time's up."
*Unable to see anything in the darkness, Kasumi tried taking a faltering step forward as a hand suddenly covered her mouth.*
Kasumi: "Wh—"
Ellie: "Shh. Keep quiet."
*Kasumi felt Ellie's voice at her very eartip — it seemed dry and serious, nothing like the relaxed tone the girl had been using before. What on earth was going on? Why was she so upset about a simple blackout? They all spent a few tense and confusing moments in complete silence. Eventually, Kasumi's eyes started getting used to the darkness.*
Ellie: "Can you hear anything?"
Shirou: "Yeah, though I wish I didn't have these ears right now."
Kasumi: "What are you talking about...?"
*What was going on? Kasumi listened as hard as she could in an effort to pick up a sound, to no avail. When the lights were still on, she heard the beat of club music in the distance, but it ceased when it went dark. Hardly anything to be surprised by, though — that was kind of how blackouts worked, after all. And yet...*
Kasumi: "Ah..."
*Kasumi finally realized what was wrong. How come she could not hear a single sound? There was a blackout. The lights suddenly went out. It might not have been the biggest scare ever, but people would get surprised nonetheless. At least Kasumi sure did at first. Why was the whole club still silent, then? There were hundreds of people in here — at least a few of them should have made a commotion.*
Shirou: "Sit tight, and don't move from here."
*Shirou addressed Kasumi before she had time to let out a cry herself. His manner of speech was no different from normal, but there was a certain dryness in his voice.*
Kasumi: "But..."
Ellie: "Calm down. There's been a miscalculation on our part. We weren't planning to involve you."
Shirou: "This would've gone differently if Ren was with us — timing's everything, huh. I thought bringing you around would make him come running. Did I misjudge the situation? Or did someone get in his way? Or maybe he tricked us all, and is actually a smooth-operator. Either way, sit tight over here, Twitsumi. If you cause a riot like you always do, you might wind up dead this time. "
Kasumi: "Dead...?"
*It wasn't like Kasumi was unfamiliar with the word — plenty of jokes utilized the expression of death — yet this time, it sounded like a foreign language to her. The weight and meaning of it had quite obviously changed.*
Ellie: "Listen to what he says. The guy has a point.We've got no choice but to improvise here. Man, I really wish we could've gotten the chance to learn about everything directly from Ren. "
*The two both made self-mocking smiles...*
Misc.: "Brought this upon ourselves, huh."
*...then pulled out something from inside their jackets.*
Kasumi: "Wh—"
*Kasumi felt light-headed as she realized what those were.*
Kasumi: "G-Guns...?"
*And big ones, too — like they were straight out of a movie. That quite exceeded the limit of any jokes Kasumi knew. After all, those were quite real. Despite having no knowledge of guns whatsoever, she could at least declare that one fact with confidence. Yet it wasn't the presence of guns that shocked Kasumi, but rather the situation that made taking them out necessary.*
Kasumi: "You're...  You're really not joking, are you...? "
*The cold, hard reality that someone or something that warranted lethal firepower had been on its way to this place. And the two were ready to fight it.*
Kasumi: "N-No! We should just run!"
Ellie: "And how do you suggest we do that?"
*Ellie dismissed Kasumi's proposal in a heartbeat.*
Ellie: "This is the only exit, and we'd have to pass through a long corridor to reach the hall. We're basically sitting ducks here. Nothing ventured, nothing gained, as they say. "
Shirou: "How appropriate. We're about to venture straight into the bellies of those monsters."
Ellie: "Then let's hope we can at least give them a stomach ache."
Shirou: "That so."
*The shoulders of the two suddenly vanished from Kasumi's sight — it appeared like they ducked.*
Kasumi: "...!"
*And in that moment, the door serving as their sole means of escape opened with an ominous creak. Kasumi cursed her own witlessness for momentarily hoping that it was help — Ren or someone else on their side — that had come.*
Kasumi: "Ugh...!"
*Expecting to see her rescuer, she peered straight at what had appeared in the doorway... ...and proceeded to ascertain its identity. The sight of the thing that met her gaze would have made anyone's mind spiral into insanity.*
*She felt as if she had been looking straight into the jaws of a werewolf. A monster with human limbs — but a beast's nature — returned her gaze. Pierced by its vile pair of eyes, Kasumi could not muster as much as a scream. It was neither a mask, nor a real wolf. But a stuffed head. Kasumi could not imagine how that could have happened, but it seemed like the stuffed head of a wolf had been attached to the decapitated body of a man. In short, a mutilated corpse was walking around. Its eyes — which one would expect to be lifeless beads of glass — glowed and writhed like simmering embers.*
Kasumi: "Wh-What is this...?"
*No way. No way. This is impossible. Impossible! Headless bodies didn't move. Stuffed animal heads didn't growl. Not even at the brink of madness could Kasumi acknowledge the logic of stakes skewering the dead body controlling it as if it were alive. It looked almost like a crude clay figure made by a child — the only difference was that the stakes serving as its bones had a will of their own.*
*The wolf's jaws opened and closed, making the kind of dreadful sounds it should have never been able to. Despite knowing this scene would haunt her nightmares, Kasumi couldn't help but listen closely to what the beast mouthed.*
Wilhelm: "Come..."
*Let's play a game together. And in the next moment—*
Wilhelm: "Hahahahahahahahahahaha—"
*The makeshift monster exploded with a deafening cackle.*
Kasumi: "...?!"
*Kasumi had no idea what had happened, nor did she want to know how it had been done. Still, despite falling to her knees and covering her head, she could not prevent the sounds of rending and melting flesh from filling her ears. Unable to cope with the situation anymore, Kasumi recalled that the most dangerous part of a grenade was not the actual explosion, but all of the shrapnel and pieces of destroyed matter that would follow in its wake.*
*That crude, makeshift werewolf was a bomb. A messenger. A demonstration. An ironic gesture towards a prey — all merely a sick joke birthed by a twisted mind. There was no way, of course, for Kasumi to realize that.*
Shirou: "Didn't take the bastard for the type to hold grudges."
*Kasumi regarded Shirou — firm on his feet and seemingly fully aware of what was going on — with complete and utter bewilderment.*
Kasumi: "I-I..."
Shirou: "It's alright. Just chill and stay in here."
Ellie: "We're gonna be back in a heartbeat, so hide in the room for now."
*Bits and pieces of gore from that dreadful explosion were hanging off Ellie and Shirou's clothes. Unbeknownst to Kasumi, though, all three of them might have equally been covered in blood.*
Kasumi: "N-No! Don't go...!"
Kasumi was thoroughly confused as to what was going on, but she knew the two would not come back if she let them go now. The whole situation was too surreal. So preposterous she almost laughed out loud. She felt certain of but one thing: that this place was devoid of all common sense — all that she would consider normal. 
Kasumi: "We've gotta run...! You can't seriously be thinking of fighting that thing!"
Ellie: "Weren't you listening? There's only one way out. You see, the guys who owned this place removed all emergency exits from it a while back — I mean, the name's "
*Bottomless Pit" and all. Apparently, they thought it was cool. But looking at it now, it seems like they only ended up making it their own grave. "*
Shirou: "Putting aside whether or not that was coincidence..."
*Shirou flashed a derisive smile.*
Shirou: "Well, all the better. Let's see if I'm as feeble a lackey as they think."
Shirou: "Either way, looks like I've been called out, so I've got no choice but to go."
*Kasumi had no idea what the two were blabbering on about. It sounded almost like they were discussing fatalistic philosophy, but rather than waste time listening to their nonsense, she had to figure out a way to stop them. Kasumi would never allow the two to rush to their deaths. If escape proved impossible, that left her with but one choice.*
Kasumi: "I'm coming too."
*Astonishment contorted the faces of her companions, but regardless of what looks they gave her, Kasumi would not back down.*
Kasumi: "You heard me. If you've got another gun, let me have it."
Ellie: "Huh? B-But... Um..."
Kasumi: "Even a metal pipe will do if that's all you have."
*Or rather, that might have been the smarter choice to begin with. If a vicious battlefield awaited her beyond that door, it was probably a better idea to bring a weapon she had been accustomed to.*
Kasumi: "You got nothing? Then I'll just make something myself."
*Kasumi glanced around the room, looking for something to use. It would've been perfect if they had a baseball bat, but it didn't seem like they did. The best she could think of was dismantling a chair and using one of its legs as a weapon. There were no tools around, but Kasumi figured she was strong enough to break the leg of a puny chair.*
Kasumi: "I'm sorry, just gimme a second."
Ellie: "W-Wait. Um, listen, Kasumi, sweetie."
Kasumi: "What? You better not tell me to stay put or I'll get real mad, okay?!"
*Ellie faltered a step back.*
Kasumi: "Sure, I'm scared. And I have no clue what the hell's going on. But we've got no choice, do we? You want me to just sit here and watch you guys get in trouble? Screw that! Or rather, if you guys can't take care of whatever's out there, I'm gonna end up trapped in here. I think it makes more sense for all three of us to go out and try to break through. "
Ellie: "Well, I suppose you're right on that account, but..."
Kasumi: "Right?   What the hell am I supposed to do if you two end up getting yourselves killed? Unless the thing out there lets me go, I'm done for. So combining our strength and running away together is the best and smartest choice here, understood? "
Ellie: "I... guess so?"
*Ellie found herself at a loss for words when faced with such an exorbitant display of common sense. Kasumi was most certainly right, and it was hard to think of any way to retort.*
Ellie: "B-But you know..."
*Ellie still tried to come up with something regardless, only to be abruptly interrupted by Shirou.*
Shirou: "I knew you were amazin'."
Kasumi: "Huh?"
*It was Kasumi's turn to be surprised, for there was an obvious glint of honest praise in Shirou's voice. It might as well have been the first time he addressed his childhood friend with that kind of tone.*
Kasumi: "What do you mean, amazing...?"
Shirou: "I mean you've got guts."
*The situation most certainly called for no jokes, and Shirou, despite himself, had been dead serious. He then proceeded to add the following in the most sober of tones.*
Shirou: "You're also levelheaded and optimistic. I'm legit impressed, you know. An average guy or gal would be pissing their pants right about now. You've been a paragon of justice and friendship ever since we were kids. Fuckin' hell, Ren's brain dead for not seeing just how much of a keeper you are. "
Shirou: "I give up. You're absolutely right. In which case, you should just get a steel mop from the closet over there. Just don't do anything stupid, a'ight? "
Kasumi: "Ah, okay..."
*Kasumi hesitated for a few seconds, blindsided by the sudden and unexpected support, but eventually went for the mop.*
Kasumi: "Y-Yeah. That's right."
*Her smile had been somewhat awkward, but what could she do? It was very much true that she felt scared, and the memory of the gruesome scene from before still lingered in her mind. But nothing would come from panicking in a situation like this. She had absolutely no idea what had been happening around her, but precisely because of that, she had to do her best to survive so she could learn the truth later. All that mattered now was getting out of this place alive. Before that, though, there was a question she had to ask, no matter what.*
Kasumi: "Listen, Shirou..."
*She momentarily stopped in front of the closet with the mop. It was the very same question that the blackout had interrupted. Something they had to discuss face to face.*
Kasumi: "Wh-Why did you and Ren fight back then...?"
*The answer to that question, however...*
Shirou: "I dunno."
*...came vague and obscured, and was followed by a swift impact to the back of her head.*
Kasumi: "...!"
*Shirou's words reached Kasumi before she had the time to comprehend what had happened.*
Shirou: "I really, honestly don't know. Well, I could tell you the superficial reason, but what you want is something deeper, the basis of what had lead us to that position to begin with, don't ya?"
*It was unclear whether Shirou had botched his attack, or if Kasumi managed to partially dodge it, but she did not lose consciousness right away. As her mind descended deeper and deeper into slumber, she could still make out some of Shirou's words. And even form her own.*
Kasumi: "Eleven years ago...?"
Shirou: "Yeah."
*The inception of it all. The day the fuse was lit. But then why did he choose to ignite it?*
Shirou: "Dunno. I seriously have no idea why I did what I did. I feel bad for you, honest, but that's all I can tell ya. It doesn't make sense to me even now. "
Kasumi: "Then what about this...?"
*This sudden betrayal.*
Shirou: "I just gave you what you wanted. This here is the most efficient way for us all to survive. No point in teaming up with idiots who ain't thinkin' about running to begin with, is there? "
Kasumi: "In other words..."
*Apparently, Shirou was dead set on fighting in this place.*
Shirou: "To tell the truth, I don't even know why I feel this way right now.  Not that it really matters. Anyway, sleep tight. Ellie, let's go. "
Ellie: "Yeah, yeah. But you know... Ren's gonna go mental if he learns you hit her."
Shirou: "See if I care. It's partly his fault."
Ellie: "To me, it seems like you're hoping to pick a fight with him, honestly."
Shirou: "Maybe. But I really don't know.  Why's it always that when I... "
*Kasumi could not make out any more words past that.*
Kasumi: "Wait..."
*Wait. Wait! Wait for me, you jerks! Why was Shirou always so reckless? Both eleven years ago, and two months ago. All of Shirou's actions would invariably put a dent in Ren's world. It was not like the two were on bad terms, nor were they actively trying to destroy the lives of the other. Yet, all of their quarrels would always end in Ren suffering.*
*So Kasumi — who had kept an eye on the two from early childhood — could easily predict that they were once again in a similar situation. The most efficient way for them to survive?Well, sure, he might as well have been right. If he had no intention of running to begin with, he might have had no other choice but to put her out of the picture. Still...*
Kasumi: "No, you can't..."
*This did not bode well for anyone. Kasumi could only see it going very bad. She had been too afraid to utter or even think of the fact, but...*
Wilhelm: "Yo, little lady."
*If Shirou and Ellie both lost...*
Wilhelm: "We've met before. Remember me?"
*The enemy had no reason to let her go. Nor did she have any means of resisting in her current, paralyzed state. The truth dawned upon Kasumi with raw and undiluted terror.*
Trifa: "...!"
*And everyone present could easily sense the surge. Those that could — the exalted ones — felt its poignancy tingling on their very skin. For by possessing senses that transcended mankind by a margin, they could no longer remain insensitive to the phenomenon. To them — apostles possessing inhuman powers — a massive extinguishing of souls was akin to a display of fireworks. Hence, every single one of them could tell— Including him—*
Trifa: "The third has opened."
*Valeria Trifa gazed up into the sky, his features bizarrely contorted. It was him who gave the order. It was him who told them to do as they wished. Yet how could this — of all things — happen? The arms he clutched around his chest trembled. It was neither a display of joy, nor excitement — the priest was terrified by the outcome his own foolish meddling had brought upon him.*
*It was so unlike the priest. Indeed, those that knew him would not be able to believe that the man shivering like a leaf in the wind was Valeria Trifa — the most terrifying man of the Obsidian Table. To laugh under these circumstances would have fit his disposition far more.*
Lisa: "What's wrong, Valeria?"

Lisa: "You've been acting strange all day. What's going on with you?"

*Trifa could not blame Lisa for growing suspicious, for the priest had not displayed such vulnerability in over sixty years. He answered the woman, feeling her narrowed eyes staring at his back.*
Trifa: "My hopes have just been shattered. That is all."
Lisa: "...?"
Trifa: "The wish — the miracle —that I nurtured within my heart for over six decades, barely able to contain it, has just been denied to me."

*Lisa felt the opening of the third Swastika just the same. That was all she knew, however — all the other details eluded her. Did something that might have put her and others at a disadvantage occur somewhere beyond her knowledge?*
Lisa: "Are you implying that there might be a problem with the Transmutation of Gold?"
Trifa: "No. Not a single one, I'm afraid."
Trifa: "If anything, the biggest and only factor that could threaten it has been eliminated tonight. No one would know — not even the personconcerned — but Bey has just distinguished himself in the most meritorious of war efforts. There is no turning back now. Hence, pray tell me, Lisa — do you harbor love for Theresia in your heart? "
Lisa: "..."

Trifa: "Would you punish her sins and light the altar of her sacrificial bonfire?"

Lisa: "I'm afraid of her. But there are times when I forget what Gold should mean to me. "
Trifa: "I see.  In that case, you are no different from the present me. "
*His face contorted into a grimace that looked much too painful to be labeled a wry smile — a mask of palpable suffering. Trifa continued gazing at the night sky, remaining motionless.*

But the moment I decided to be loyal and follow His word, I grew distant from our Gold — blurred and hazy, if you will. "

*Under the canopy of the lonely night, a single girl poured two glasses of champagne, waiting for her guest to arrive. The night called for no celebration in particular — she simply felt like drinking. And as long as she had a partner, she cared not who it was. To tell the truth, though, she did actually care just a little bit. The seat in front of her was reserved for someone she maintained some level of familiarity with. Rusalka: "I hope it's a man... Ah, but I guess a woman might do as well for a change."

Rusalka: "I mean, this place gives off that special vibe, doesn't it? The kind of spot that makes me wistfully excited, you know? Would be pretty depressing to spend a night like that with a woman."

Rusalka: "A coincidence, I'm guessing?"
Wilhelm: "Sure, a coincidence. But you see, I fuckin' despise coincidences, so I'm trying not to think too much about them when I'm satisfied."
*Wilhelm stormed the Bottomless Pit and massacred every single soul inside it, opening the third Swastika. That was all well and good. Still, the prey he was after never showed up, and that irritated him to no end. One might say he could have waited for the young man to show up, but that was an empty argument. Wilhelm sensed it was "fate" that kept them apart tonight.*
Wilhelm: "Don't you have anything to say, Malleus? I know you did this."
Rusalka: "Geez, what a man. Another one of your inexplicable hunches?"
*Although she made a face, Rusalka did not outright deny the other's claim.*
Rusalka: "And what if that's the case? You gonna punish me for it?"

And apparently, it was young men who needed the most personal space.*

*Just a group of forty or so students laughing and getting angry at each other, studying and falling in love, chatting and playing around...*

*Not even my consideration for Himuro could stop me from staring daggers at Sakurai.*

Kei: "If you're talking about Ayase, then I don't know."

*She was pissing me off to no end, but our main objective here wasn't to teach her a lesson, regardless of how much I would've liked that to be the case.*

Ren: "Himuro—"

*Ah, that wasn't it.*
*That was actually her way of answering it.*

Shirou: "Oh damn..."

Ren: "Cain!"
*If that thing was here, did it mean Sister Lisa was also around?*
Shirou: "Shit, it's too late."
*Shirou's voice trailed off. Sakurai looked away, while Himuro simply shivered in my grasp. I merely gazed at the spectacle before me, completely dumbfounded.*
*There was simply nothing I could do from here.*

Ren: "..."
Rea: "Don't look!"
*Himuro wrapped her hands around my back and pressed against me to block my vision, as if thinking she could escape this nightmare by merely refusing to acknowledge its existence.*
*But it was too late. Her frame was much too small to cover my eyes.*
*Some of the pieces of meat and entrails of what used to be my schoolmates were flung so hard they reached up to the third floor, splattering against the window in front of us.*
*I could make out a severed hand, and a piece of a leg stuck against the window frame. That red mush was probably the remains of someone's heart, and the thing that looked like a blown-up balloon must have been a lung.*
*I even spotted a jaw, an eyeball, a torn-off scalp with hair still clinging to it, as well as half a face, all destroyed beyond recognition.*

Ren: "Ah..."

*My day-to-day life, a place for me to return to... Why did a depraved fool like me ever delude himself into thinking he could protect them...?!*

*Sheer frustration made my tears flow, and I was unable to stop them. I'd barely even known the faces of those massacred students.*
*And that weighed the heaviest upon my soul. It felt like an insult to their memory.*
Ren: "Cain...!"
*I shoved Himuro aside, and rammed my fist into the window glass. Yet I lacked the strength to even shatter something as thin as that.*
*The window remained intact, as if mocking me for being completely powerless. As if telling me I could never save anyone. That I was just another sacrifice brought here to rot and be turned into sludge.*
Ren: "Show yourself, Wilhelm!"
*I let out a deafening scream from the very bottom of my heart, cursing the name of my mortal enemy.*
*I'd make him pay. I'd kill him. Cain, too. And the priest, and Rusalka, and then Sakurai, and that accursed Sister Lisa, as well.*
Ren: "I'm right here, dammit! Stop getting high on killing cannon fodder and come get me, you cowardly fucks!"
Wilhelm: "You've got some guts."
*The temperature around us suddenly shot ten or so degrees down.*
*A whole arrangement of scornful laughs — a snort, a chuckle, a guffaw, and a howl — reverberated across the walls, merging into one, continuous fit of maniacal laughter.*

Wilhelm: "Time for the main course, kid."
Wilhelm: "Do me a favor and become a filling dish, will ya?"

*Thus far, he had merely been playing around. But in this moment...*
Wilhelm: "[Sophie, Welken Sie](Wither to ashes, O my love). May the world behold your remains."
Wilhelm: "[Sophie, und weiß von nichts als dich hab' ich lieb](For only I know you, who perished by my love)"
*His voice reverberated across the night.*
*The third stage of Ewigkeit — I wasn't taught about it by anyone, but I could still feel it and comprehend its terror on my skin.*

Wilhelm: "[Der Rosenkavalier Schwarzwald](The Rose-Bearer in the Forest of Death)—"
Ren: "...!"
Rea: "Ah..."
Shirou: "Whoa!"

Wilhelm: "It's my Creation Figment. So what's your next move, kid?"

*Himuro shivered in my arms.*
Ren: "...!"

Kei: "..."

Wilhelm: "Damn straight, you know how it is, kids. So, which one of you do I get to fight?"
Misc.: "Shut up!"

Surging gunshots vanished, replaced by the roar of soaring stakes that tore the air asunder. Even if Shirou somehow managed to dodge the air-splitting arm, what would that accomplish in the end? His gun meant nothing. He'd tried it on the demon before, but the bullets couldn't even pierce his skin.*

Like before, he couldn't actually make out his foes' attacks. Not to mention that if even one of them hit him, he'd be done for. He was still as human as he was last time. He understood better than anyone that he'd break apart like a scarecrow if he got hit. And so to him, this was undoubtedly just as much a strenuous effort as it was a one-sided game whose result was already set in stone.*

*The Impaler — A cruel, bloodthirsty vampire. An atrocious scoundrel clad in the night's blessings in the shape of stakes forming all over his body. With his brutality and complete control of both offense and defense, he had no openings for his opponents to exploit. With decades of fighting experience, Wilhelm was leagues beyond Shirou Yusa in every aspect.*

Though he'd unleashed countless bloody stakes and supersonic punches — the entire hallway was completely decimated at this point — Shirou hadn't seen any of them. Yet Shirou paid no heed to the gradually accumulating cuts over his body and instead calmly thought over the design of the attacks he'd dodged up to this point.*
*The first thing he verified was that the demons of the Obsidian Round Table excelled in endurance and tolerance for damage. So long as he had to fight the bastards, it was an obvious decision to first figure out a method to actually wound them.*
*Looking towards things in the long run during a situation where a single hit would kill him instantly was insane in of itself. And to make matters worse, Shirou was yet unaware of the fact his foes had long eliminated all of their human weakpoints. So any onlookers would see Shirou's struggle naught more than folly— the cruel despair of being up a river without a paddle...*

The ivory demon was so interested in the young man that he was willing to play along with him to a certain level. Since he had a tendency to jest and underestimate his opponents — a trait held by many of those with overwhelming power — he was truly ideal for Shirou to try all sorts of tricks on. And what was more—*
