*All of his attempts to counterattack ended up in utter failure. Shirou's complaints about the bastard's fortitude were perfectly valid — his bullets could not even leave a scratch on his eyes and eardrums. The abomination did not even flinch. He may have had a human shaped body, but he possessed none of the weakpoints a human should — it didn't appear that modern guns could even irritate the demon of the night.*
*A wolf was no match for a rifle. The strong devoured the weak — such was the law of the world. And that ridiculously simple fact rendered all of Shirou's attempts to fight back completely futile. That was the nature of absolute strength. It allowed for no ifs, no questioning, and no doubts. One could not overturn the perfect laws of the food chain by mere tricks and scientific gadgets. Or at least... it should have been so.*
Shirou: "Well, but I know he's not that kind of guy."
*Shirou knew that his opponent wasn't the type who sought the sort of uncharming and faultless strength that would render him invincible. Wilhelm would be damned if he had to put up with boring fights and easy victories. All who opposed him were as much his food and prey as they were his rivals. He did not mind some resistance, or rather, he welcomed it with open arms.*
*In short, it was a matter of thrills. One needed challenges and a sense of achievement to truly feel alive. And so Wilhelm lusted for a battlefield where he could rejoice in fulfilling carnage. And if that craving was as deep-rooted in the vampire as Shirou thought...*
Wilhelm: "What's wrong? Realized it's useless to resist?"
Shirou: "Hold your horses, pal. I was just plannin' on what to do next."
*With that, Shirou suddenly turned to the very epicenter of the stake barrage and dashed forward. The two unwavering arrogances clashed. Both of them were certain in their victory. Both of them sought thrills. And with that bizarre twinge of empathy between them, the two finally shifted their battle into a true fight to the death.*
*Meanwhile... As Shirou and Wilhelm's battle waged on, Kei was out in the courtyard, trying to stop Cain's rampage. There was little distance between her and the dead berserker. She could close that gap in a beat, but even so...*
Kei: "Cain, stop this!"
*She cried out to the giant, hoping that her words — her voice — would bring him to a halt. She knew it was a spineless action. She knew it all stemmed from her fear to face reality. Yet Kei could not help herself.*
Kei: "...!!"
*At the next moment, her pleas were met with a roar and intense light as if to reject them. The lightning struck Kei, frying her flesh and bones. Her body went flaccid from the electricity coiling around her nerves, to the point she could barely move. The pain was so intense it froze her in place, and yet — at the sametime — her heart hurt far more than her body. For she felt that the lightning coursing through her were the cries of his endless grief.*
Kei: "Ghh, aaagh..."
*Countless thunderclaps ravaged her body in endless succession, prying a cry of pain out from behind her clenched teeth. She felt like she was about to lose consciousness with every single strike, but she kept her eyes on Cain and kept pressing forward.*
*And yet, anxiety still clouded her thoughts. Wouldn't he just run away the moment she drew close enough? Could he even properly recognize her? Even the agony that would've killed a hundred men she was currently exposed to was nothing next to those thoughts. The emotion driving her feet was akin to resignation. Yes. This was her punishment.*
*After all, she didn't want to see him like this. Even if he was being controlled and didn't have a scrap of his own will left behind, she still wanted him to stay beautiful as in her memories. She couldn't stand seeing him as a puppet of a witch. How ridiculous. Where did she get off acting like she was virtuous after all the lives she'd reaped so far? It was laughable. And why was it she could put up with it all when Babylon still held the strings? Was she under the impression that it didn't matter if he was being made to kill so long as someone with good conscience was behind it? If that wasn't self-satisfaction, then what was?*
*She was horrible. The worst. The absolute lowest. In her mind, she didn't deny that, but...!*
Kei: "Aah, agh...  Please. Stop it... already... "
*She could only keep pleading pathetically. She embraced and clung to him tightly, words her only tool to hopefully soothe him.*
Kei: "I've grown strong, you see... Now I can put up with harsh things a little better than before, you see.  So please, just stop this. At this rate, you'll... "
*... truly become nothing more than a disposable corpse. A puppet soldier controlled by the queen of shadows, fated to vanish as a sacrificed pawn. A mere tool. To her, that was beyond—*
Kei: "I will never al— agh!"
*A sharp pain ran through her abdomen before she could continue. It felt as if an insect was crawling within in her body and cutting up her innards with its claws.*
Kei: "Khh, this is..."
*Rusalka's curse was being invoked. A smirk of the cunning witch disguised in that ridiculous youthful form ran through her mind.*
*She said the curse would take effect if Kei betrayed them. Indeed, trying to stop Cain in this situation could count as betraying the Obsidian Round Table. But while Kei understood that, she did not loosen her grip around him. She couldn't. Otherwise, she would lose sight of the very thing she craved. She would lose the very core of her being that made her try and stop him to begin with.*
Rusalka: "Hee hee hee..."
*Then she heard the most grating and unpleasant voice she knew. She looked up to find the witch standing above her, looking exactly as she had just pictured her. She stood behind the fence on the school's roof, smiling as she looked down on Kei in the courtyard as though she had found something truly amusing.*
Rusalka: "So you really have betrayed us, haven't you, Leon?"
*Rusalka addressed Kei in a cheerful tone, not paying the slightest attention to her pain. Though Kei was no lip-reader, she could somehow hear what the witch was saying from this distance. Her tone made it sound as if she'd been sure Kei would betray her.*
Rusalka: "You gave Zarathustra a lot of support and you always seemed to dislike how Bey and I did things, so I figured it was only a matter of time before you betrayed us.  But well, it doesn't look like you can do much more in that state. Heh heh, go die a slow and painful death as you curse your own powerlessness. Cain, if you'd like, you can put that traitor out of her misery right now. "
*And with that, Rusalka moved away from the fence. Kei glared up in anger at the woman— no, at her enemy.*
Kei: "Traitor? I see, you are kinder than I thought, Malleus... I didn't know you considered me a comrade, given how much you took me for a fool.  It is an honor. But I'm sorry. I have never once felt anything for you... "
*Even pity. She would not think twice about casting her away. And now she'd use that to prove she belonged to the Obsidian Round Table. That she was just as depraved as the others.*
*Cain was not paying heed to the decay of his body, too busy with his rampage. The woman controlling the corpse would have to be defeated to bring him to a stop. That meant there was but one solution. All other circumstances were nothing compared to that. She resolved herself, let go of Cain, and then... she spoke.*
Kei: "[Formation](Yetzirah)..."
*Her Ahnenerbe manifested with those words. The ancient sword Hihi'irokane — shining scarlet wrapped in flickering flames like the sun — forged from a legendary vermillion metal described in the Takeuchi Documents, an account of the age of the gods. She held up her crude but well-sharpened blade and glared at the witch on the roof that she had to defeat.*
Kei: "Misfires, betrayals, friendly fire— nothing is impossible on the battlefield, is it? Then allow me to teach you something — even someone like me has a thing or two that I won't tolerate...! "
*For the witch's actions clashed against the very purpose Kei had decided to take up the sword — a purpose she would do anything for, even if it meant staining her hands in treachery. And so now she would teach the bitch that her prized treasure was not as frail as to give in to some weathered old crone. Kei would show her that she wasn't going to just look the other way and bear being mocked any longer.*
*Rusalka moved away from the fence to the center of the roof. She glanced down and smiled at a lone girl lying unconscious there, her lecherous gaze slithering along her torn clothes like a snake.*
Rusalka: "Kasumi... Time to wake up... Kasumi..."
*Rusalka gently stroked the girl's— Kasumi's— cheek, her fingers treading carefully as though she was treating a fragile porcelain doll.*
Kasumi: "Mmm..."
*Perhaps it had tickled, as Kasumi trembled slightly. Her consciousness began to emerge out of the sea of sleep. She faintly opened her eyes and looked around to get a grasp of what was happening to her. The first thing that came into her eyes was someone wearing a black uniform — Rusalka. Second was the dark sky. Last was the familiar scenery of the school roof. Once she'd acknowledged all that, Kasumi's consciousness finally attuned to reality.*
Rusalka: "Morning, Kasumi."
Kasumi: "Rusalka...? Huh...? Why? Why was I sleeping here of all places? Ah, it's already nighttime? What? What the heck is going on!?"
*Startled by the situation, she tried to sit up, but soon realized she couldn't move her body at all. Her body was in perfect condition. She hadn't been drugged, and her muscles didn't feel paralyzed, not even stiff. Her mind was also clear. She felt totally fine, and yet she couldn't move, as though she'd been bound from hand to foot.*
Rusalka: "Heh heh, oh Kasumi, you really are an energetic one. This is as fun as watching a dumb puppy unable to get out of a basket."
Kasumi: "?!"
*Kasumi gasped quietly, frightened by Rusalka's smile. All of her instincts screamed there was something very wrong about the sight before her.*
Rusalka: "Oh? Whatever could be the matter with you? Now you've gone as meek as a lamb... Eheh heh!"
*Rusalka could not help having her sadistic side stimulated by the sight of the terrified girl.*
Rusalka: "I really like that look on your face there. I just love seeing people with those terrified looks in their eyes. So..."
Kasumi: "Wh-What?"
Rusalka: "Show me more of that terrified face."
*The shadows at Rusalka's feet began to slowly bulge up. They took on a three-dimensional form, looking like slimes out of a video game. The shadows squirmed, filling Kasumi with visceral disgust.*
*They slowly crept towards their paralyzed prey, quivering and wriggling suggestively as they coiled around her limbs. Faced with what felt like an endless colony of giant worms crawling all over her skin, Kasumi broke out into goosebumps and screamed.*
Kasumi: "N-Noooo! Let me go! Eek! No! Let me go! Let me go!!"
Rusalka: "No. Can. Do... We're only just getting started."
*The tentacles tightened themselves around Kasumi even harder on Rusalka's cue. Kasumi's body creaked under the severe tension.*
Kasumi: "Ghhh...!! Eek... Ghh, ah... Gaah... Aaaah...!!"
*Kasumi let out voiceless screams at the stark intensity of the pain rushing through her. Her eyes flooded with tears that cascaded down her cheeks.*
Kasumi: "Ghh... Uuughh..."
*One of the shadows wrapped itself around Kasumi's neck and strangled her. With her breathing cut off, Kasumi's mouth widened like that of a goldfish begging for food.*
Kasumi: "Agh... ug... h... Aagh..."
*Kasumi flailed around as she flapped her mouth in an attempt to breathe. Tears, saliva, and mucus sullied her face. But the tentacles showed her no mercy, tightening their grip around her neck with enough force to break it.*
*Still suffocating, Kasumi began to black out. All she could make out in her blurry vision was the lewd and cruel smile on Rusalka's face.*
Kasumi: "Agh..."
*Just when the idea that she might die crossed Kasumi's mind, the shadow wrapped around her neck released its grip.*
Kasumi: "Aaah... Khehh... Khehh... Khohh...!"
*Kasumi choked on the sudden rush of fresh air that came flooding into her lungs.*
Rusalka: "Heh heh... Aw, I'm sorry. Did that hurt?"
Kasumi: "Khehh... Khehh... Rusalka, stop this already..."
Rusalka: "Like I said, no can do. We're only just getting to the main event. Heh heh... Don't worry, I'll be gentle this time."
*Rusalka snapped her fingers, and the shadows began to engulf Kasumi again.*
Kasumi: "Aaah... No, nooooo! St-Stop... Wait, do... Sto... Aah, no!!"
*Kasumi screamed from the sickening touch of the shadows crawling around her bare skin. It was a sensation like none other she'd ever experienced, and it terrified her to the very core.*
*For it had an otherworldly chill about it. What tormented her was not so much the shadows creeping on her skin as the sensation of them eating into her very core — her soul. The condensed light containing the root of the being known as Kasumi Ayase — her sacred land and the values that had ingrained themselves within — were at risk of being veritably violated.*
Kasumi: "No, aaah, agh... Noooooo!"
*Naturally, she couldn't take it. She felt she was going crazy. With her common sense of reality seemingly dimensions apart from what had been happening, there was no way she could retain her senses in this situation. She was just an ordinary girl, yet here she was, being assaulted by phantasmagoric shadows with a very real possibility she might not survive. Though she prayed it was a dream, she could not help feeling that the jaws of the monster she woke up in were very real. All she could do was scream... All she could do was lie there as the predator took great delight in toying with her prey.*
Kasumi: "Stop... it... Why are you doing these terrible things to me... ghh, mmgh, agh..."
Rusalka: "Terrible? Whatever do you mean? I'm just playing with you... And you seem like you're having fun from where I'm standing. Don't deny it."
*The girl's comment was uncalled for as far as Rusalka was concerned. It wasn't like she was an angel herself. After all, just a few nightsbefore— It was at that moment that it finally hit Rusalka.*
Rusalka: "You don't remember?"
Kasumi: "Ngh... Wh... What are you... talking about...?"
*Rusalka looked at Kasumi closely. There were no signs of her playing dumb.Apparently, all her memories of what had happened— of the weight of her sin — were completely gone.*
Rusalka: "Huh... So you lost your memories?"
*Now that was interesting. If Rusalka brought the girl's memories back, just how would she react? Would she cry? Scream? Break? Or... would she go mad? Just like how Rusalka herself renounced and cursed God in that cold cell, finding respite only in madness. Whatever the case, it would definitely be interesting. Rusalka smirked and spoke up in a sweet voice.*
Rusalka: "Heh heh... I'll help you remember."
*She walked up to the paralyzed Kasumi and seized the girl's chin in her fingers.*
Rusalka: "Now... look clooosely into my eyes..."
Kasumi: "Aaah. Aaaaah. Aah..."
*Kasumi stared at the image of herself reflected in Rusalka's eyes. What was it that the girl reflected in those blue eyes — Kasumi herself — had once done? Memories forgotten and suppressed slowly bloomed back to life like a blossoming flower.*
*A crimson flower that smelled of blood.*
Kasumi: "Aah. Aaah. Aaaaah... AAAAAAAAAAAAAH!"
*All the tragedies that had happened in that park rushed through her mind, momentarily overtaking all of her senses. Many deaths. The sensation of flesh. The resilience of bone. The warmth of splattered blood. Kasumi screamed at the display of those abominable memories. She tried to move out of an impulse to flee, but that was no use — the curse still left her thoroughly petrified.*
Rusalka: "Heh heh... Well? How does it feel to know the truth?"
*Kasumi's agony was Rusalka's pleasure. The witch's face warped into a wicked, malevolent smile.*
Kasumi: "No... It can't be... No! Nooo! NOOOOOOOOO!"
*Kasumi's eyes widened as she let out a piercing shriek. By the time the sound abated, the girl had lost consciousness.*
Rusalka: "Oh? Kasumi? Kasumiiii?"
*Rusalka lightly flicked Kasumi's cheek. However, the girl did not wake up no matter how many times she did so.*
Rusalka: "Oh my my, losing consciousness? Guess it hasn't fully connected with her yet. She might be more shameless than I thought."
*Rusalka's mouth curved like a crescent moon. In other words, she held the potential to join their side of the world.*
Rusalka: "Eheh heh heh, my, how indecent you look. I couldn't blame anyone getting the idea you're inviting them."
*Rusalka licked her lips and took a look inside Kasumi — at the form of the soul dwelling within her. Ah, so that was it. Rusalka understood what Kasumi's role was now. She had been chosen to be the first executioner. And the reason for that wasn't as trite as her mere relationship with the boy.*
*Now it all made sense. With blood of that lineage coursing within her, such an outcome was inevitable. If one merely looked at the results, they'd have to accredit the matter to the impeccable Mercury's design, but it would've been a remiss to undervalue Babylon's cunning, who at the time seemed to have pulled the wool over the eyes of most of the Obsidian Round Table.*
*As a woman herself, Rusalka had to express honest admiration for the potency of that maternal love. Unfortunately, as a witch, she could not help rejoicing at the prospect of laying her hands on such a trump card, her feelings of admiration overshadowed by malevolent gratitude. She had another heir to the devil's castle in her hands—*
*But before she could devour that sweet soul... The door leading from the roof to the school slammed open.*
*I rammed the iron door open with the force of inertia I'd accumulated dashing up the stairs.*
*I clenched my hands into fists. My head was burning with white heat. With my worst fears confirmed, it took all of my willpower to keep myself from snapping.*
*The witch stood there, smiling under the red moonlight.*
Rusalka: "Interrupting me during my playtime? How rude."
Rusalka: "But I'll make an exception for you. Welcome, Ren."
Ren: "RUSALKA!"
Rusalka: "You got here faster than I expected. Haha, that's a shame, you should have given us a few more minutes."
*Rusalka glanced down at her feet. Lying there was the prone form of none other than Kasumi.*
*Her body was entirely engulfed in shadows — only her face was still visible. All I could see from this angle was her expression, but the twisted look of agony there said it all.*
Ren: "Kasumi."
*You've done it now... Bring it on, bitch. You've crossed that one line that should never have been crossed.*
*She was still breathing? She'd only lost consciousness? Fuck that. Nothing could excuse what Rusalka had done. Not in a million years.*
*So—*
Ren: "Hold on, I'll save you!"
*I'll kill the little bitch.*
Ren: "Get you and your fucked up reality away from her now!"
*I quickly formed the guillotine, tempered with pure killing intent.*
*I stomped on the asphalt with enough force to break it to pieces and was about to unleash my blinding rage when—*
Rusalka: "[Formation](Yetzirah)."
*Rusalka recited the words to form her own Ahnenerbe.*
*It manifested in the form of long and crooked iron chains that immediately shot after me, shadowing my accelerated actions as though they had a will of their own.*
I could almost hear them murmuring: "I won't ever let you get away. Don't run. I'll drag you to your knees..."Her Ahnenerbe was like a clingy ex-girlfriend. 
*It felt so vindictive and fitting of her that I wanted to throw up. I wouldn't let such pathetic things interfere with my lightning dash.*
Ren: "Wha—!?"
*Yet I still couldn't believe what had just happened.*
*A single strike. A single slice of the guillotine had shattered Rusalka's Ahnenerbe. Like it was nothing.*
*It was too easy. There was no way a top class weapon fused with the soul of an apparently centuries old witch could break that easily—*
Rusalka: "Ahaha. Not bad, Ren. But it's not over yet."
*And more importantly, how could she possibly still be alive after I had shattered what should have been her very soul?*
*My question vanished a second later as huge stone walls covered in spikes suddenly sprouted from the ground at both of my sides.*
*Faced with the dual threat of getting crushed and impaled, I jumped with all my might before those execution tools could close in on me.*
Ren: "Ghh...! Zzgh!"
*Just made it— the spikes had grazed part of my leg, but I survived.*
Rusalka: "Ahahahahahaha! Well done!"
*My suspicions were confirmed. Not even an ounce of agony appeared on Rusalka's face as I sliced several spikes off one of the walls. It was like she was completely ignoring the principles of Ahnenerbe.*
*Dammit, I wasn't going to make any progress whether I ran or attacked at this point. I couldn't even approach Kasumi, much less do something about that bitch...*
Rusalka: "But you're still green. Just look at how unpolished your moves are."
*The deeply ominous undertone to her cheery voice sent shivers down my spine.*
*The next thing that showed up was a steel figure modeled after a girl. The double doors on its front were wide open, revealing its interior of countless sharp spikes.*
Rusalka: "Surely you've heard of this, Ren. It's Eiserne Jungfrau, also known as the Iron Maiden."
*Iron Maiden. Yeah. I'd heard of those, all right. It was the name of an insane torture device.*
*As the name implied, it was a so-called casket made of iron. What set it apart from the rest was that its front had a sculpture of a woman, while the inside was littered with iron thorns. Victims would be pushed into the casket while still alive and have the thorns skewer and drain them of blood until they expired.*
*Rather than a torture device, it was more of an execution device. It was probably also her Ahnenerbe, just like the chain and walls from before.*
Ren: "What the hell's going on!?"
*It was impossible. It was all utterly incomprehensible— and she allowed me no time to think.*
*The iron figure approached me in an attempt to swallow me in. It was obviously planning to turn me to Swiss cheese.*
*I evaded it with a somersault, but the chain was already waiting for me where I'd planned to land.*
Ren: "Tch... What the hell is this?"
*Yes, this clearly wasn't normal. I didn't claim to be an expert on their abilities, but this wasn't right. She was breaking the rules.*
*I thought there was only one Ahnenerbe for one person? Did she have multiple Ahnenerbe? If that were possible, why couldn't the others do it?*
*Since I didn't have all that many opponents, I didn't have much of a basis to go on. Yet Rusalka was clearly an abnormality. She had too many weapons, too many exceptions, and their forms were too irregular.*
*I almost felt like commending her for her diverse aptitude.*
*Even petty tricks became a work of art once polished to perfection. It seemed she had a perfect grasp on all the loopholes in this business.*
*Perhaps she'd noticed uneasiness past my glare, as Rusalka gave me a smug look, a bewitching smile on her lips.*
*Like a cat toying with a mouse — a vixen who beguiled countless men to their undoing.*
Rusalka: "Eheh, look at that face! It's clear you don't have a clue what's going on, huh? Just what is it you don't understand? Come on now, just ask and big sis Rusalka will tell you all you wish to know."
Ren: "Shut the fuck up, granny."
Rusalka: "Ahaha. Ooh, scary. Well, it's obvious what you don't understand even if you won't tell me... It's my Ahnenerbe, isn't it?"
Rusalka: "Confused? You can't figure it out? Ooh, now that really gets me going. I never thought I'd ever see you look so bitter!"
Rusalka: "Ahnenerbe meld with their user's soul. Once they break, so do their master. You're not wrong on that part, and your confusion is more than warranted."
Rusalka: "If I had to sum it up, there are exceptions to everything. The acts of driving a car or riding a horse might be different on the surface, but they are the same in the sense you're covering distance. And what we're dabbling in has just the same amount of versatility."
*In other words, it was not a matter of mastery, but a difference in areas. She understood a side of Ahnenerbe that neither I nor the rest of the Obsidian Table knew existed, and that made her an exception even among their ranks.*
*An old seeker of forbidden arts — the ancient witch of the abyss. And as if to prove my observation, she produced something that looked like a bundle of papers in her hand.*
Rusalka: "I only have one Ahnenerbe. It's this diary."
*A diary? That was Rusalka's Ahnenerbe? Then—*
Ren: "Then what the hell are those things?"
*I dodged the charging Iron Maiden and cut down the chains that tried to knock me off-guard from behind, not daring to stop even for a moment.*
*The bitch set up traps while we were in the middle of a conversation, and above all, nothing she said matched up with the facts.*
*If that eerie bundle of papers was her weapon of choice, then where the hell were those chains and torture devices coming from?*
Rusalka: "It's not strange at all. After all, Ahnenerbe are born from feeding on souls and concepts. It's not the shape, but rather the convictions contained within that's important."
Rusalka: "This country has one of those legends too, doesn't it? The one that says a scary Enma guy who judges the dead has a book filled with a list of their crimes. If I used that... What do you think would happen?"
Rusalka: "You don't seriously think I'd just bash you over the head with it, do you, Ren?"
*So was she trying to say the thing in her hands was a grimoire?*
*A fucked up picture book that she didn't use to physically assault others, but rather was filled with spells and other mumbo-jumbo. With that, all the pieces finally started coming together in my mind.*
*The Iron Maiden. Binding chains. Dark red spikes.*
*All the weapons Rusalka used had one thing in common—*
Ren: "Torture tools... I see, so that book is...!"
Rusalka: "Yes, you've got it. My Ahnenerbe is Elizabeth Báthory's diary."
Rusalka: "She spent her last years recording her whole history of using and enjoying those torture devices. You can fill in the rest, can't you?"
*Just as she finished that mocking remark, chains came rushing out of Rusalka's shadows like a tidal wave.*
*A whole bunch of cursed torture tools on par with Ahnenerbe and an Ahnenerbe that controls them? You've got to be shitting me.*
Ren: "Isn't that against the rules?"
Rusalka: "Right you are. But still, any damage done to the torture devices while in the Yetzirah Degree bounces back to my body, so it's not all that perfect."
Rusalka: "But you see, I'm a hard worker. I'm an expert at perfecting things over years and years of perseverance... See?"
*Though I was pretty much tearing through the surging sea of chains, barely even able to see ahead, it was almost like it had no effect on her. No matter how many different torture tools I attacked, it seemed like it was doing no damage to Rusalka.*
*It was like the car and horse example she told me. Unlike us, who used our Ahnenerbe in the way we were taught to, she discovered alternate methods and applied them at her will. Her cunning and mastery of the arcane made all those irregular powers possible.*
*As such, aiming for victory through shattering her Ahnenerbe was futile. It was not the diary, but she herself that I had to cut down.*
Ren: "You sure it was smart to spill all of your secrets like that?"
*But when it came to the source of her confidence—*
Rusalka: "Yeah, I don't mind. Having a jack-in-the-box of torture tools is ultimately just the power of my Yetzirah Degree. Letting you know about it won't change anything."
*In other words, she was still going easy on me. Summoning all those monstrosities was mere child's play to her.*
*She was at a deeper level I hadn't reached yet. Hers was not mere foolish cockiness — she had real power to back it up. It only seemed like she had let her guard down while she merely toyed with me.*
Rusalka: "Oh? Didn't Leon tell you? There are four levels of Ewigkeit that control Ahnenerbe— Assiah, Yetzirah, Beri'ah, and Atziluth."
*Sakurai had indeed told me about them before. But she hadn't given me a detailed explanation of Beri'ah or Atziluth.*
*Rusalka's mocking smile deepened as she read my expression.*
Rusalka: "I see. So she didn't tell you about the higher Degrees. I always thought that girl lacked in philanthropy, you know. But rest assured. Unlike her, I'll give you lots and lots of free education. All the way until you die."
Ren: "Your kindness has almost brought me to tears. So what are the other two?"
*Rusalka winked and blew me a kiss. Suppressing my exasperation, I asked her about Beri'ah and Atziluth. The whole situation irritated me to no end, but I had to get as much information out of her as I could.*
Rusalka: "First, let's talk about the Beri'ah Degree, or 'Creation Figment'. Beri'ah means to discover and impose upon the world a single rule that is convenient for you and your Ahnenerbe. It won't be bound by physics or even common sense. Even the most absurd of rules will become reality."
Ren: "Is that—"
*Was that really possible?*
*Rusalka didn't appear to be lying.*
Rusalka: "Eheh heh heh. You're thinking it sounds too good to be true, don't you? It's the power to swindle the world, so to speak. That's the Beri'ah Degree. Although in a way, you could say it's still limited by the confines of this reality."
Rusalka: "A Beri'ah that affects all those within the practioner's pre-determined range is called Hegemony. It holds the power to change the very world around you. Bey is a prime example of that."
Rusalka: "On the opposite side of the spectrum is Trascendence — one's ability to change themselves. I guess Kristoff would fit the bill, but Machina's a better example. Though you've never met him, have you?"
Rusalka: "Beri'ah come in many shapes and sizes, but they're all miraculous techniques without equal. The practictioner's craving and affinity with their Ahnenerbe decides what rule you ultimately arrive at."
Ren: "Craving—"
*An unfulfilled dream you kept on chasing and wishing for. If creation meant fulfillment of that dream, then I...*
*My craving would probably be...*
Rusalka: "Whether you're a Hegemony or Transcendence type is naturally coded into you, and changing it later on is quite a challenge. Though, no matter which you end up with, just by reaching this level, you distinguish yourself from from the mediocre."
*Ah, so that was it. That was why she was so confident. I must have looked like nothing more than a bug to her in my present state.*
Ren: "If it's so great, then what's this Atziluth that's supposedly above it?"
Rusalka: "No one's reached the Atziluth Degree, so I don't know much about it. Apparently it's an ultra-powered version of Beri'ah."
Rusalka: "I do have a hypothesis, though... My guess is that once you activate Atziluth, the Beri'ah's rule emanates out beyond the practitioner's conscious range."
Rusalka: "Well, we can look forward to it when you make it that far."
Rusalka: "However—"
*Her face suddenly warped for but a single second.*
Rusalka: "Although, it also brings about implications I'd rather not think about."
*She stared at me with a face full of complex and contradictory emotions as she resumed her attack.*
*Giant stone walls and needles so big that they were more like long sharp lances shot at me. I dodged the stone slabs, but the flesh off my left arm vanished as I tried to bounce one of the needles off.*
Ren: "Gwaagh!"
*A single touch of a needle was enough to melt through my clothes and burn my skin like acid. Rusalka broke out into another sadistic grin when she saw it eat into my bones.*
Rusalka: "Well? Was my explanation easy to understand?"
Ren: "Yeah... kinda."
*Rusalka sounded like she was enjoying herself.*
*I didn't learn all that much about Atziluth, but I felt I understood the basic principles of Beri'ah now.*
*It was all about discovering a rule that made all sorts of unrealistic and convenient phenomena happen, and forcefully imposing it on yourself and others.*
*In that case, the pitch black darkness currently covering the school and the red moon in the sky were...*
Ren: "So this night is a Beri'ah in action, you say?"
Rusalka: "Yes, that's correct. This is Bey's Beri'ah. With his Beri'ah in action, this whole world is in his belly."
Rusalka: "But right now, there are too many powerful alien bodies inside, so he can't seem to manifest its full power. Also, he's probably holding back so he doesn't accidentally break his new toy right away."
*Me, Rusalka, Sakurai, and Cain... The four of us were all drawn into his world, and he showed a great interest in Shirou. He didn't want to kill him instantly, and thus was still was going easy on us.*
*When she said we were in his belly, she probably wasn't speaking metaphorically or anything. If I was the only one here and he went all out, my soul would've probably melted into this bloodsucking night in a few minutes or so.*
*All the questions plaguing me had been answered. As such, now was finally the time for...*
Rusalka: "Okay then, your free lesson is over."
*With that somewhat regretful voice, she told me she was done playing around.*
Rusalka: "Take a good look, Ren. I'm gonna show you everything."
*She was playing with me just like Wilhelm was. She never had any intention of letting me get out of this alive from the start.*
*Though she hadn't made any suspicious moves and I couldn't feel any killing intent from her, the air around me suddenly froze over.*
*It was coming... The craving — the Creation Figment — of an ancient witch in a child's body was on its way to tear this reality.*
*Her long hair, the same color as the moon, danced in the darkness.*
Rusalka: "[In der Nacht, wo alles schläft](Within the dark of night, a sleepless night, )"
*It was an echo different from a voice.*
Rusalka: "[Wie schön, den Meeresboden zu verlassen.](I part with the water's womb in jubilance...)"
*Something that wasn't air passed through me — a vibration that shook not my eardrums, but my soul.*

*Straining my eyes, I forced a show of will to protect this place, whatever the cost.*
*In response, she...*

*Her voice was gentle and peaceful enough to make me feel unpleasant...*
*She sounded like a caring mother dealing with a child throwing a tantrum.*
*That voice and its tone was completely like the one she used when we talked at the church.*

Lisa: "I mean, she's the only one you care about in there, right?"
Ren: "...!"
*She drove me up the fucking wall.*
Ren: "...Don't give me that shit."
*The monotony of my own voice surprised me. I was so furious it was dizzying.*
*We were this late in the game, and yet she still acted unreasonably considerate of me.*
*And, no matter how small, a part of her believed I would accept her ludicrous offer.*
*Yeah, she was completely right about me not being a saint, but...*

*The primary reason why I stood before Lisa and told her to retreat was that one girl.*
*Stopping Reinhard's return? Heeding some heroic sense of justice? No, it was all in the fact that―*

Ren: "That's the reason why I can't let you kill anyone. Neither Kasumi, nor anyone else."

*So that Marie could become the fifth person in our group.*

*To her, Lisa was like a mother or an elder sister. With all the years they spent together, I was certain Himuro respected her, and nothing could convince me otherwise.*
*And, as her friend, I had to protect her most cherished dreams.*
Ren: "No matter what you are, you're like family to her. In what fucked up world would a person enjoy having a murderer for a relative!?"
Lisa: "...!"
*For a few moments, Sister Lisa was at a loss for words.*
Lisa: "Thank you. I'm being honest when I say that it's an honor to have you praise me that much."
Lisa: "But I can't oblige."
*She hanged her head with a smile on her face and―*
Lisa: "I can't think thoughts as nice as yours. That's just the kind of woman I am. Rea knows that, too."

*Her military boots rang out loud as she took a step forward and started walking towards the hospital while seemingly ignoring me.*

Lisa: "He and I will open this Swastika."
Kei: "Understood."
Ren: "...!"

*I'd seen it before and instantly recognized it.*
Kei: "To be honest, I couldn't be more pleased with this set-up. He and I still had a score to settle, and I really didn't want him to think that I gave my all last time."

*She came here, too? But wait, then Sister Lisa will...!*
Lisa: "Your optimism made you underestimate us. Hard to believe you're Karl Krafft's substitute."
Lisa: "Though that's part of what makes you such a wonderful man, it got you into a terrible situation. I never said I'd do this one-on-one."

Ren: "...!"
Kei: "I told you before, didn't I? No cheating."

Kei: "That goes for the both of us. You're probably clueless about it, but you did a good job of trying my patience."
Kei: "In fact, you're doing it right now by underestimating me."

*I wasn't just imagining it. Something was clearly wrong. An object burning that brightly should never turn colder.*

*It was as if Sakurai herself was being detached from this universe.*
*I recalled something she once told me.*
*The third Degree of the Ewigkeit channeled through an Ahnenerbe charged with souls... She spoke of its existence, but didn't tell me the truth behind it or what it meant.*
Kei: "[Die dahingeschiedene Izanami wurde auf dem Berg Hiba](The goddess Izanami, her light forever extinguished)"
Kei: "[an der Grenze zu den Ländern Izumo und Hahaki zu Grabe getragen.](Sleeps her final rest beneath Mt. Hiba amidst Izumo and Hoki, neighbor-lands standing vigil)"

Kei: [Bei dieser Begebenheit zog Izanagi sein Schwert,](On its burial grounds Lord Izanagi stood,)[das er mit sich fuhrte und die Länge von zehn nebeneinander gelegten](His ten-grasp steel drawn)[Fäusten besaß, und enthauptete ihr Kind, Kagutsuchi.](As Kagutsuchi's head fell to dust beneath the kinslayer's blade)"

*Silent, calm and lacking in heat, her tone was completely unlike the bizarre flame she had become.*

*Her craving enabled her sword to permeate my blade, rendering me unable to block.*

*The explosive sounds made Lisa momentarily halt her step before resuming her entrance to the hospital. Leon was overdoing it. The show she was putting up back there probably awoke most of the patients, and upon seeing the commotion, they would surely make things really messy. At the very least, there would be people trying to evacuate. When that happened, the place would quickly turn into a ghastly slaughter show. She would have to complete her business while surrounded by the constant screams and shrieks of people panicking like ants in a poked anthill. Lisa always had certain concerns about Sakurai's growth, and it seemed like they had become reality. Though she praised the girl's resolution and admired her ability to seal her seat within the Obsidian Table at such a young age, such a hotheaded person could break at any moment.*
*Without time to expand her limits and horizons, she wasn't capable of taking detours and considering different angles. Though that life made Sakurai sharp, she had the frailty of glass shards or needles. People like her wouldn't live long, especially not on a battlefield... However, considering her lack of attempts to address the issue, Lisa knew she wasn't in any position to judge people. She held sentiments towards Rea, Fujii and pretty much everyone else, but she never acted upon them. All she did was console herself by simply reminding herself of their existence. That side of Lisa's nature would surely get a certain acquaintance who used to be her friend to severely scold her.*

Those two had perfectly opposing personalities, but they shared that harsh strictness, likely due to the status they were born with. With those trifling thoughts within her head, Lisa entered the patient ward and found herself surrounded by an unexpected silence.*

The scent of chemicals stinging her nose and the cold sensation of the linoleum under Lisa's feet made her heart restless. There weren't many things she found less pleasant. In fact, she had a distinct dislike for the very concept of hospitals. They were hotbeds of treatments, research, success, failure, birth and death... Gardens where life was tampered with.*

Cain's unyielding muscles and deathly pale skin under which no blood would flow were both ghastly and menacing, representative of the madness within every inch of his gargantuan body.*

Kei: "Let's say that Ayase were to die today."

*She claimed they were all worthless compared to the dear people she had lost.*

Kei: "Shut up!"
Kei: "Shut up! Shut up shut up shut up! You don't know anything about this! You've never lost anyone and always lived a carefree life! There's absolutely nothing..."
*The anger became an explosion she transformed into propulsive power. Her face contorted from rage, Sakurai kicked off the ground with a piercing cry.*
Kei: "You know nothing about me!"
*With a violent explosion of emotion, she burst towards me...*
Eleonore: "What an eyesore. You have lost, cur."
Kei: "Aaaghh!"
*...and instantly had something crush her.*

*I followed the direction of her eyes and instantly noticed the irregularity.*
*A magic circle of striking red environed the entire hospital area while radiating with power great enough to instantly destroy everyone within.*
*I felt like I was on the palm of a giant. The deep crimson circle embodied flame itself, but both its heat and wickedness were a dimension beyond that of Sakurai's.*
*I could only liken them to hellfire.*

*Wrong. That was Rubedo.*
Eleonore: "None of you move. Not a single ant is getting away from me."
*Sakurai uttered the person's name in a trembling voice.*

Eleonore: "Come, then, Krafft's spawn. My loge will now test the sharpness of the blade dedicated to Lord Heydrich. If I find it dull, know that even your bones will crumble to ash."
*High above, clad in whirling, crimson flames, the incarnation of scorching heat tore a large hole in the air and made her presence known.*
*With a single glance, I could tell her power far exceeded ours. Like Reinhard, she was an entity more fit for hell itself than our human realm.*
Ren: "Marie..."
*Could I win against her? Dammit, I couldn't see the slightest chance.*
Trifa: "...!"
Lisa: "...!"
*Upon noticing the abnormality, Trifa and Lisa sprang away from each other. The giant cadaver stood still between them and abated their fiery intensity.*
Trifa: "...What a predicament. Speak of the devil, indeed."
*His murmur carried a hint of frustration unbefitting his warm nature, but the circumstances made it no less than agreeable.*
Trifa: "Lady Samiel... Such hastiness."

By ignoring those factors and forcing it, they could only appear as incomplete shadows of their true selves ― just like Reinhard. Nonetheless, the Lady was indeed menacing. Even with most of her power sealed away, she was still beyond the ability of anyone present. Trifa did expect her intrusion, but he gravely underestimated the forces she would bring. Seeing the opportunity, he instantly decided on what to do.*
Trifa: "Lisa, let us make an armistice. It is not the right time for us to continue this. Our esteemed Lady Samiel was ordered to open the fifth. Surely you must feel that the sights are already set. "

If she pulled the trigger, both the people and buildings would become dust. But even if she didn't, escape was impossible. With their lives in Samiel's hands, one could only agree it wasn't the time for petty squabbling.*

*Lisa's response was cold and emotionless. She knew that his propositions always had ulterior motives behind them, so she couldn't just follow them blindly.*
Lisa: "Samiel... Eleonore would never attack the Divine Vessel. Step into the open and face her head-on. Then she'll have no choice but to open this cage."

Lisa wasn't exaggerating when she said that no one could find the priest, should he genuinely wish to remain hidden. After all, he managed to fool even Eleonore, even when she had the whole area in the palm of her hand. Lisa wanted to know his motive.*

Surely there is nothing you would gain were I to show myself to her, no? She cares not for the person we are fighting about.  And that means..."

Lisa: "I refuse."

Even when made aware of the other Sonnenkind within the hospital, Eleonore wouldn't care as long as the legitimate one was fine. In fact, she'd gauge her as impure and purposely purge her with her own hands. I know Eleonore's personality much better than you do. "

Trifa: "Then..."
*Her unreasonable response made Trifa raise an eyebrow in doubt. He couldn't see why she was being so stubborn when a literal gun was pointed straight at them.*
Trifa: "Lisa, are you saying you only wish to save the 'girl' by your own hand? Do you truly crave self-consolation to such an extent? How thoroughly pointless. Do not ignore reality. One wrong move you make could lead to Lady Samiel pulling the trigger and killing everyone but myself. Why would you want such a meaningless closure? "

*Lisa sighed with resignation, disappointment and pity she couldn't hide even if she tried.*
*Why couldn't he understand it? Why was he so distorted? He wasn't like this in the past. When she met him, he might've looked undependable and meek beyond compliment, but he was still human. A child of God devoted to His service, often grieving for humanity's virtues and wickedness. He escaped into the golden Divine Vessel to overcome that grief, but that might just have been his greatest disaster.*
Lisa: "The shell you now wear is too tough to allow you to read minds, isn't it, Father? I know little to nothing about the burdens of your past power, but hiding in the Divine Vessel has only made you rotten. The ventilation just isn't good enough to heal any wounds. "
*The inside was festering and inflamed. He might've been unaware of it, but the priest he used to be was worn-out and crumbled, and the Divine Vessel was completely empty... ...or perhaps filled with a swirling chaos of boiling rot.*

We are monsters unable to do anything without killing someone. Us protecting something is an absurd notion in and of itself. And that's why... "

Lisa: "...I want you to stand still and not do anything. I'm leaving my eyehere — one wrong move on your part and Cain will attack."

Trifa: "Wait."
*As Lisa turned around and began to make her leave, Trifa spoke to her in a silent voice, void of any anger or frustrations and unbefitting someone whose movement was sealed. It was peaceful, like that of a caring brother talking to a darling sister.*
Trifa: "If you believe it to be our final farewell, then why not be a dear and refrain from calling me that? In all honesty, it greatly sours the ending."
Lisa: "I think it suits you, though. A feminine name like Valeria is perfect for someone being dragged around by Lord Heydrich's anima. The only man here now is Fujii. And ― as a man ― he has a duty to help women, just like I ― as a mother ― have a duty to help him. "

Trifa: "Hmm... I wonder."
*Having been left behind, Trifa began to ponder. Lisa's eye was nested in the mask, providing her with a visual feed of all it saw. Indeed, it rendered him unable to move. He put that aside, however, as something else tugged at his mind.*
Trifa: "Lisa, you mentioned something awfully curious. 'The only man here now is Fujii.', she said.  Why did she fail to include Cain? "
*It was a marionette ― a dead puppet. Number II of the Obsidian Table was but a tool without a self. Thus, it would be completely reasonable to not recognize him as a full-fledged human, but such cold realism was unlike Lisa Brenner. Did she simply forget? Used the wrong words? Or perhaps...*
Trifa: "Because it is right?"
*Trifa emotionlessly gazed up at the towering giant silently looking down on him, after which one side of his mouth rose up to distort into a grin.*
Trifa: "You had a poor endgame, Lisa. Being a good person is respectable indeed, but a battlefield is not the right place to let your true feelings slip by your tongue. Oh, it seems that really was our last farewell. You left here with the reaper riding on your back. "
*With the giant still looking at him, the priest sounded a silent, grieving laugh and bid his comrade goodbye. Within the darkness that could end at any moment, the two irregularities stared at one another without even flinching.*
Eleonore: "...Hmph. I believe I've told everyone not to move, but it seems like that fool still doesn't know how to listen.Well, it matters not."
*Standing on the rooftop water tower, the crimson woman considered me, her gaze replete with scorn. I assumed she was talking about Sister Lisa.*
Eleonore: "On your feet, cur. I'm allowing you to act, so get over here."
Eleonore: "A certain nuisance of a woman wants to spout some of her nonsense at me, but I refuse to lend an ear to any of it. You keep her busy so I can complete my mission."
Kei: "...Yes, milady."
*After being practically flattened by the attack, Sakurai awkwardly got up and glared at me as if she had something to say. Her body was flesh and bone again, likely due to the powerful strike.*
Kei: "..."
*She leapt towards the rooftop while kicking off street lights and walls. I couldn't see her anymore, but I didn't care and couldn't mind her even if I tried.*
Eleonore: "I believe I've challenged you to come at me, brat."
*Eleonore von Wittenburg, a Battalion Commander of the Obsidian Round Table. The commanding presence of the crimson knightess rejected even the possibility of idle thoughts — a fact I realized to a sickening degree just by standing in front of her.*
*Her soul, its scope and density all transcended the realm of the ordinary. While Reinhard was dreadful because I couldn't even gauge his limit, the power of the woman before me was perceivable, making my fear of her more precise and genuine.*
*At the very minimum, her soul encompassed a single army of several tens of thousands. I knew it wasn't the kind of thing to be easily measured, but the number had to be at least ten times greater than that of Sakurai's.*
*With that in mind, I couldn't help but ponder the difference in power between us.*
Eleonore: "What's wrong? Are you coming or not? Surely you must know that there's not much you can do from there. This isn't your combat range, after all."
Eleonore: "Oh, I see..."
*Her long hair of sanguine, blazing crimson swayed and rustled, making chills run down my spine.*
Eleonore: "You realized what I was capable of, didn't you?"
Ren: "...!"
*Right when I followed my instincts and jumped away, a pillar of fire burst out right where I stood.*
Eleonore: "Good intuition. You pass the first test. But is running all you can do?"
*She followed up with a barrage of continuous explosions, filling the area with flames and dust. The once familiar surroundings of the hospital were now reminiscent of minefields...*
*...or grounds that have been thoroughly ravaged by carpet bombing.*
*She was right — this was beyond my preferred combat range. If I wasn't at melee range — where my right arm could reach the enemy — I had no means of attacking.*
Ren: "Khh... ghaah!"
*However, my instincts told me not to get close to her.*
*She wasn't a sniper, but a gunner. Therefore, carelessly reducing the distance between us would only make it easier for her to hit me. Not to mention my position was already disadvantageous.*
*Eleonore was on the rooftop, at least 20 meters above me. It wasn't a distance I could jump, and even if I could, I'd only become the perfect target.*
*Running into the hospital was out of the question; I couldn't even begin to guess how many would die if we chose to do battle inside.*
*Basically, I was checkmated. She was a ranged attacker with the higher ground — there was nothing I could do against her.*
*A headlong charge towards her would only work if her destructive power was low, and it was the exact opposite of that. A single hit would instantly incapacitate me.*
*As much as I wanted to call her unfair, that'd be a stupid thing to say. Eleonore was a warmaker, and these were her tactics. Sister Lisa was completely right ― I was downright naïve to think it'd be a one-on-one battle.*
*Shit. Fuck! What should I do? What can I do?*
Eleonore: "Is that it? Let me remind you that I'm not keen on being disappointed."
Eleonore: "If you plan a repeat of this farce in front of Lord Heydrich, you might as well drop dead right here and now. I may have been told to temper your soul, but I do not recall being forbidden from killing you."
Eleonore: "Well? I'm waiting."
Ren: "...!"
*I shuddered as I sensed more pillars of fire. However, unlike the previous ones, which came from the ground, these four were created and released in the empty space surrounding me.*
*My only means of dodging was to jump skywards, but doing so left me hanging in the air at the mercy of gravity, completely defenseless.*
*She didn't miss the opportunity and launched more of her crimson flames towards me. The blinding, scorching heat shot me down like a plane.*
Ren: "Ah... gha..."
*I could neither move, nor muster a single word. The intense attack felt less like facing a wall of flame and more like a crash into a giant crag. The explosive torrent sent me flying and even left me unable to feel pain.*
Eleonore: "Oh? You didn't burn up. Not bad."
Eleonore: "Then how about this?"
*I looked up and caught Eleonore within my vision. Flames gathered before her, drawing a symbol in the air. The heat condensed within was incomparable to anything she had thrown at me thus far.*
Ren: "Hh, agh―khh..."
*Fuck. No. There was no way I could take that hit. It'd all be over like nothing.*
*Even if all I could do was crawl, I had to move out of the way. That attack would evaporate my very soul.*

Eleonore: "...this could be what separates you from the rest. Let's do this."

*I had to stand up and get away. My location just couldn't be worse...*
*But even if I dodged the attack, the hellfire would land on the ground and create a giant explosion.*

*I forced my feet downwards and directed a lot of power into them. It almost felt like the ground could collapse.*
Ren: "Jump!"
*With each of my limbs on the ground, I pushed them all with great force to fly into a tremendous jump. My determination and fighting rush made the intracerebral hormones flow at full capacity, driving my tattered body back into working shape.*
*And with this―*
Eleonore: "Well done. That was heroic... but foolish."
*The devilish cannon's angle became horizontal, meaning the fire wouldn't level the hospital.Now, I had to―*

*Blocking felt futile. And I was pretty sure no one on the planet could actually take a shot from that thing head-on and live to tell the tale.*

*That determination almost ascended to creed as I turned it into pure power.*

*The guillotine soaring through the air. My battle cry piercing the skies. My soul on the verge of an explosive burst. I could no longer think of what would come next.*

*I'd return to my day-to-day life and bring her with me into the sunlight.*
*It wasn't beyond my reach. Nor was it lost.*
*I had to survive ― I couldn't die.*
*I wouldn't die. I'd win this!*
*My consciousness was blown away by the scorching explosion born at the moment the hellfire kissed my blade.*
*A loud reverberation rang out as a blossom of flame bloomed into the night. The scattered cannon fire vanished before reaching ground, while the one responsible for the spectacle dropped onto the rooftop with a trail of smoke behind him.*
Eleonore: "...Hmph."

*With only four Swastikas open, her power was limited to only about half of her full potential, and the attack she had just released wasn't even on the Yetzirah level. All she did was test him. However, Rubedo was not one to indulge in trivial games upon the field of battle. She preemptively set a limit on the firepower she'd use, but beyond that, she wasn't holding back at all. By surviving such an attack, the boy was clearly the victor, and the woman had no intention of doing anything to sully the winner's glory. This meant the completion of one of the missions given to her, but...*
Eleonore: "Still... this certainly is a problem. I've yet to conclude my other mission, but with you in that state, I'll feel as if I stole the outcome."
*The opening of the fifth Swastika ― the mass slaughter and sacrifice of the lives within the hospital. The boy tried desperately to prevent that from happening, but his consciousness couldn't bear the overwhelming pressure and he went out cold, ultimately making the situation less than interesting.*

Eleonore: "On your feet, boy. If you claim to be a hero, then overturn the impossible. Lord Heydrich won't be as lenient as I. Transcend common sense. Whatever man musters from nothing denotes his true worth. "
*The strength allowing people to stand when their legs could no longer support them, and miracles permitting them to topple overwhelming odds. Every hero in humanity's history had their names praised exactly because they achieved the unachievable. One could call it a privilege of those loved by God. To such people, the word 'impossible' was a trigger to an explosion that propelled them towards even greater heights. In Eleonore's eyes, there were only two types of people ― those who sprouted wings when pressured, and those who didn't.*
*And of course, 'wings' didn't simply refer to the ones that grew on the back. It could be anything that made one soar the heavens, such as...*

Me, you and Kircheisen are all from the BDM, yet for some reason, only you came out as a wretch. You, a mother? Don't make me laugh, you toxic whore. And you, cur... you're just about useless enough to properly follow this order. If that idiot makes a move, kill her on the spot. "

*Her hand reached towards Marie...*

*She couldn't speak. Even breathing felt a toil. That was what it meant to touch her. As long as Ren was unconscious, her body was nothing but an instrument of death. That was as normal as it was standard, however...*

*Eleonore forced great power into her grip. Aside from failing to understand, Marie couldn't believe what was happening. How could a person live after being decapitated?*

Marie: "B-But I..."
*Everyone she ever touched met a swift end. She never questioned it, or thought any more of it. Ren mentioned similar things to her, but Marie couldn't quite comprehend what determination meant.*

*They were important to her. Why, though? What made them so dear?*
Marie: "With Ren, I can touch anyone and they would touch me, too."
Eleonore: "And that's why you made an attempt on my life? Don't you see the contradiction?"
Marie: "Ah―"
*She started wanting physical contact and came to understand the pleasure it provided. She realized there was something to earn from it and acknowledged the truth that she actually received it. That made her finally understand what it meant to rob others of someone they held dear. The fear of having it taken away. The heartache of seeing it slip through the fingers. *What had been the cause of it all?*
*Discontent knew no boundaries. No man throughout history would ever claim that he desired nothing from life, or that he felt blissfully content with his status quo. For such was the nature of the human race. Step after step, pressing ever onwards — it was that very greed and insatiable curiosity that defined the history and legacy of man. As such, it was by no means an emotion to be shunned. If there was no greed to drive men forward, they would have most likely remained as monkeys, inhabiting uncultivated forests for all eternity.*
*As such, Rusalka would not deny the concept. One could not pry unfairness, discontent, terror, and hunger from a world fashioned by mankind — without these, men would simply be unable to sustain themselves. She knew that. She knew that better than anyone. She understood both herself, and the nature of men. And she thought she had already made peace with the fact.*
*At times, however, she allowed her thoughts to wander. Onwards and onwards — higher and higher, beyond where the eye could see. It was the ambition and crystallized greed of mankind; the power that made them soar, the power that bestowed upon them wings — aspiration and invention. A prayer of bliss and positive energy. Yet men were not strong creatures. Or rather, all of them concealed darkness within their hearts. Like two sides of a coin — a positive surface would always conceal a negative underbelly. In short...*
Rusalka: "Why is it always me...?"
*If there were wings that could liberate one from the ailments of reality, so were there pitfalls waiting to trap the hapless. While some men focused on soaring the skies, others plotted how to bring them down and shackle them. Discontent was alien to no one; it had been in the nature of men to look for the highest mountain to conquer, and there were ways to do so without attaining the gift of flight.*
*The easier, the better — another manifestation of mankind's greed, and a notion that gave birth to their hunger. In layman's terms, one would label it envy — the wish to drag those superior or more endowed than oneself down into the pits of your dwelling; to drown them in the dark waters of a bog. That would fill those below with the illusion that they were, in a way, equal or even superior to those above.*
*It was the easiest way to make oneself feel grand while also avoiding the troublesome labor of learning how to fly. It was but another primal instinct of man. It might not have had the power to give birth to anything, but it could alleviate fear. It was quite a natural thing to possess. Indeed, hindering those ahead of you was all part of being human.*
*And so, even a being of the lowest of castes held the power to be an architect of cheap tragedies.*
*The village in question was located deep in the mountains, in a rural area like any other. Its inhabitants were simple men that lived their lives with a discontent that had been ubiquitous among people of the age. A community of farmers — as ignorant as they were poor — who worried more about how the weather would shift the next day than mastering the art of reading and writing. In short, the kind of isolated, rural community one could find anywhere. Depending on the viewpoint, they were members of the bottom layer of global society, maintaining their stability only because they had never been exposed to those better than themselves — those that could fly. Equality reigned supreme in their modest world.*
*Unable to fly, they would all observe those that could, spouting complaints to each other. They shared in that common discontent. *Who was at fault? What caused the problem? The men there were good at blaming other forces for their misfortunes. Consequently, one could either go ahead and keep blaming the very nature of reality, or give up and take the world for what it was. *Her mind had already been made.*
*A beat of the heart. A shiver of the soul. His consciousness — after a lifelong slumber — had been pulled back from the edge of unreality. He might have been having a dream. Upon further consideration, he realized he could never feel and fully comprehend reality. The very concept had felt befuddled to him from the day he was born. He could not understand it very well, and so he decided there was little meaning in trying. Any concept — simple or complex — was governed by and obeyed constant laws. If there were those that tripped, there had to be those that gave them the shove. Yet mulling over the loss that the fall itself might have incurred was beyond pointless.*
*One should rather concentrate on standing up as soon as possible. And — of course — it would be ludicrous to carry on as if nothing had happened after such an action had been successfully performed. One would have to make sure no one could ever give them another shove. In short, the process required a sort of supercompensation. One had to make sure those that shoved them regretted their choice. As otherwise, the situation would never change for the better.*
*And that was precisely why it came to pass that he awoke. One could call it a crisis prevention system, an automatic defense — a preliminary interception device. Well, the details of it mattered little. It was a part of the mechanism of most things to include structures that would invariably protect themselves. Human bodies possessed white blood cells — a legion of champions who would protect and pursue any external threat.*
*And it wasn't the brain that commanded them. It was the jurisdiction of the heart to control the warriors that had been dissolved in the bloodstream. Indeed, the heart — its rhythmic melody reverberated all across this space. The hell that gave home to millions trembled at the very notion of his awakening.*
Reinhard: "As you wish."
*It received permission from the brain — the supreme commander. Although, words should have mattered little between the two. The heart was an involuntary muscle — as such, it required no one's permission to function as it saw fit. It would race fast when ordered to stop, or come to a halt when required to beat faster — it all depended on the right conditions. Such was the nature of this cogwheel. Only the irrevocable laws governing it could dictate its actions.*
*In short, what transpired then was merely the brain talking to itself. It would have been foolish to try and address a part of oneself that possessed no ability to listen or obey one's commands. But was it really true in this case?*
Reinhard: "Most commendable. Your loyalty shall not go unrewarded."
*Any concept — simple or complex — was governed by and obeyed constant laws. The heart might have been an involuntary muscle, but it could also never work against its host.*
*If a cog had been designed to suit one's purpose, it could only do so as long as the two were bound by the same laws. As such, the excitement of the brain could take the form of a placebo and affect the heart. Thus, permission from the Lord only enhanced the workings of the intricate mechanism that sustained His power.*
Reinhard: "Do as you wish, Isaak. Make the essence of the castle known. My feeble, lovable servants — if your lust for each other's blood can no longer be contained... "

*And with that whirl of inexplicable sensations, Lisa Brenner opened her eyes.*

A price needs to be paid to have your wishes granted. Rea: Putting aside who exactly you want to bring back, it's all a matter of weight, isn't? The thing you want is incredibly heavy, so you need a lot of things to even the scales. And I'm one such sacrifice... "
*In short, the weight of Rea's life was light compared to the life Lisa wished for — the barter would not make sense otherwise.*
Lisa: "It's called equivalent exchange."
*Although human lives should have been equal, their value would differ depending on who was weighing the scales.*

The girl understood the feeling with almost painful clarity. For it was not a seldom guest to her own heart — naïve ideals had no place between the two.*

In the end, she refused to sleep or rest for five days straight and still managed to carry out all her duties with perfection. She bragged to me that we were on completely different levels, too. Not because it would put me beneath her, but because I enjoyed the process of competing. I grew quite fond of the days we spent fighting each other, wishing they'd go on forever. And so I had to always match her. After all, if she got too far ahead, I could no longer compete with her on equal ground. We both raced onward relentlessly, and before we knew it... we grew up.  And one day, we came to a point where our competition could no longer be laughed off as a simple game. "

Lisa: "Yes, the Nazis."
*Germany, as well as the state of the world in that age. Rea only knew of it from textbooks, but she could nonetheless imagine it. If two students had been competing to the point where their rivalry bordered on the extraordinary, society would not turn a blind eye. And so the stage for their rivalry changed, elevated to never before seen heights, brought ever closer to the core. They had to keep marching onwards, beyond the point of no return, shouldering a colossal responsibility that could no longer be cast aside.*

I admit there were a number of people who cared little about whether or not we won the war as long as it did not affect their personal lives, but for most, such thoughs were beyond comprehension. At the very least, they went against my own basic mindset. Do you think the children of this generation would understand even a fraction of what we felt back then? "

*At the very least, it felt alien to Rea herself. Some thought that just because one happened to have been born to a particular country — and forced to live within its society — it did not automatically entail unconditional servitude to that nation. But that was merely the misguided, shallow mindset of those who knew nothing of history. The culture and traditions passed down within one's country constituted the very framework of its people's thinking; rob a country of all that, and the result was a dead nation.*

Gender equality is all well and good, but you have to remember that different people are better fit for different roles. In that sense, my friend had been like a shark, whose ocean was the battlefield — no one could compare to her. So can you imagine what happened to the girls that tried following in her footsteps? "
*Rea paused to think for a few moments. Her first impression was that it must have been tough for them.*
Rea: "I can imagine everyone writing them off."

*Partaking in a battle meant putting your life on the line. Someone unfit for its hurdles would very likely wind up dead.*

*Understanding dawned in Rea's mind. In the end, the only thing left to Lisa was to elevate her rivalry with that friend of hers to its utmost limits.*

*Much like Lisa, she rushed onwards without paying any attention to her surroundings, and eventually found herself beyond the point of no return.*
Lisa: "So I won't dismiss her way of life. But no one should have ever tried to be like her. Where would you find another girl half as talented and hard-working as her? It was bad to give them the wrong idea, and the situation wasn't as forgiving as to discredit my opinion as mere meddling. "

Lisa: "Yeah. I suppose that's not so far from the truth."
*Which one of them would garner more supporters? Lisa ended up being unable to back down from that fight. Not to mention it was her love for her country that drove her forward.*
Lisa: "I had to beat her, no matter what."
*A smile that was far too faint to be called self-scornful crept onto Lisa's lips. It was childish stubbornness that started it all. And by this point, Rea finally understood that...*
Rea: "Is that friend of yours still..."
Lisa: "Yes, she's still around. Even now."
*Lisa's compatriot remained in the Obsidian Table to this day. That couldn't have been Kei, and Rusalka was out of the question. Then...*
Lisa: "Eleonore von Wittenburg. She's now a part of Lord Heydrich's Imperial Guard. You'll have a chance to meet her, sooner or later. I think it was around this time of the year in 1939... ...that we met Lord Heydrich. "
*And with that, their competition escalated to an even more destructive level.*
Lisa: "Eleonore's strength grew to unimaginable heights."
*And so Lisa had to chase after her. For the sake of the Fatherland, she could not allow herself to fail. Both transcended the limits of mortal women.*

From children who could memorize a hundred cards in barely a moment, to those who could dribble a ball all the way up to the top of a mountain. But all of them — through some fault on my part — ultimately died. "
Rea: "..."
*Rea had heard of psychic children herself. Just like there were squadrons of child soldiers in the army, so would other fields benefit from children being reared specifically for them. The sooner they could get familiar with their future craft, the better.*
*The idea was to remove certain shackles limiting one's brain. To do this, they would fill the children's minds with information during an impressionable age, when their convictions and common sense had yet to develop. If you taught a child that it was possible to raise a cup without hands, they would believe it, and carry out the feat without a shred of doubt or hesitation. But that meant opening brain channels that regular people never used, and more often than not led the children's minds to overheat. The same way one could tear their muscles when infused with too much adrenaline, one could also fry their brains and end up a vegetable, or even dead.*
Rea: "That's a pretty big contradiction..."
*Choosing to serve her country as a woman, she reared its children. Yet that only resulted in making Lisa Brenner the most wicked woman of them all in the eyes of the world — no others murdered as many children as she did.*
Rea: "Is that the root of your regrets?"
Lisa: "Yes, that is my sin."
*Her one and only wish was to save the children that her actions cast into the flames. A desire she craved enough to even sacrifice Rea's life to see it fulfilled.*
Rea: "I see. So that's what happened."
*And so, of course, she noticed yet another contradiction.*
Rea: "I'm your granddaughter. Or maybe even great-granddaughter, I suppose."
Lisa: "..."
*Silence could only mean confirmation. Rea went on.*
Rea: "I don't want to hear the numbers, but I imagined you killed a lot."
*She murdered countless children.*
Rea: "And to atone for that, you're going to kill me now? That sounded like a contradiction to me at first, but now I see — that's how you repent."
*Lisa wished to be freed from the sin of having massacred the children of other mothers. And to do that, she had to sacrifice her own blood. In short, to put her own lineage to death. And to suffer the agony of a just punishment. Ah, but if that was true, it would make her such a diligent yet clumsy woman — the most unfortunate case of wasted effort in the world.*

*The faintest and most ephemeral of smiles had been plastered on Rea's lips in that moment.*
Rea: "Sorry for having made you talk about these things. So please stop being so hard on yourself, grandma."
*Lisa could no longer bear the girl's gaze.*
Lisa: "Stop it...!"
*Her voice burst out with the intensity of a shriek. She jumped up from her chair — almost collapsing to the ground — and covered her face to escape Rea's eyes, yet failed to hide the tears gushing out through the spaces between her fingers.*

*It would have made more sense if she called her a witch. Or a helpless fool. Lisa would have been able to bear any scornful or contemptuous remarks. But... what on earth was this?*
Lisa: "You told me to cut the lousy acting. So what on earth is this supposed to mean? You're being unfair."
Rea: "What do you mean, unfair?"
Lisa: "I know you've got no intention of dying."
*Why did the girl regard her — a fool who sold her soul to the devil — with the compassionate eyes of a saint?*
Lisa: "Makes me wonder who you take after. I thought I was pretty good at concealing my true feelings, but you're unbelievable. When did you become such an actress?  That gave me quite the shock, just like you had planned. "

*Rea cocked her head to the side in a genuine expression of puzzlement, then gave the nun a long and hard look.*
Rea: "Why would my struggle for survival and not hating you for what you did be mutually exclusive?"

Rea: "You've got a one-track mind."
*That was why she made stupid mistakes. Her outlook was too narrow, her mind too stubborn. Rea would never want to think in only ones and zeroes.*
Rea: "Those clothes you wear might just be for show, but maybe you should heed your own teachings for a change and think more positively."
*Otherwise, how could she properly listen to the worries of other people?*

*Lisa replied with a tired voice.*
Lisa: "You're getting the wrong idea. I'm a far worse woman than you think."
Rea: "I don't believe people who say things like that about themselves."

Rea: "Huh...?"
*Siblings? What was that supposed to mean?*

*Right. She had to ask about that name.*

So your idea about my repentance is completely off. I wasn't trying to punish myself through the pain your sacrifice would cause me. Isaak was the one who got the power. He was the one who took after his father. He had been more fit for the role, and so, I could not love him.  I thought I might as well let them have him. I thought it wouldn't hurt me much if I sacrificed him. And you belong to the same lineage. Can you still claim not to hate me? "

*"So despise me. Curse me with every disgusting word you know."Rea could not help but see Lisa urging her on like that. For if the girl didn't, the woman would find herself unable to cast her off.*

*Receiving an unexpected answer, Lisa found herself at a loss for words. To Rea, however, it was far from unexpected. Her lousy attempt to play the villain was so cheesy it failed before ever reaching the girl. Rather, the more wicked she tried to appear, the more she looked like a wailing child.*

Rea: "I believe I've already told you. All I want is to save Fujii."
*She merely wished for him to survive, and not get hurt if possible.*

*A lie. An act. A calculation. Was that truly enough to threaten everything they had in the past?*

*That alone was true and would never change. Her motivations notwithstanding, Lisa Brenner had most certainly brightened Rea's life up until this point. And no matter what happened, the girl's opinion on that would not change.*

*Did she wish for the girl to die, annoyed with the whole act?*

It doesn't matter if I don't know what made me fall for Fujii—  Rea: All that matters are my true feelings here, in my chest! Mine is small so I can tell what's going on there better than you! "

*And then — with a broad grin on her face — she finished the wine and tossed the glass to the ground, shattering it to pieces.*

The magnanimity and benevolence it contained drove Rea to the verge of tears. Ahh, so that was what people called "relief".*

*The meaning of her words, and the fact she used plural—*
Lisa: "Isn't that right, Valeria? I've just had my eyes opened, too."
*Happiness and relief filled Rea's heart to the brim — she felt like an entire army had just come to her aid.*
Trifa: "Yes, indeed. At this point, we can no longer turn back."
*Trifa, too, uttered his words while looking deep into the sky. It seemed as if his gaze had pierced the dark canopy above, glaring at whatever horrors had been lurking beyond its veil.*
Trifa: "Be patient, my beloved children. I will save you."
*A fissure ran across the priest's cheeks as his blue pair of eyes fell shut, never to be opened again; the Divine Vessel — the tangible proof of his oath to be Him — began to waver. His very craving had been on the verge of collapse, but at the same time, the phenomenon came as a divine blessing.*
Trifa: "You shall come with us, Malleus. You might not have planned for it, but it was none other than you who caused this."
*Rusalka's meddling led Trifa to discover a path that would allow him to, at long last, be reborn as a true swan.*
Rusalka: "What...?"
