*He hit her with raw, murderous intent while showing no resolve to actually kill her, and when she tried to leave, he told her to die. While it was true that the Obsidian Round Table was a band of weirdos who were no friends to reason, Wilhelm was taking it way too far.*
Rusalka: "Stop wallowing in your insanity, Kaziklu Bey!I've had enough, I'll―"
*A battle. Right here. In the church. Rusalka built up her resolve to fight and sounded a war cry to summon her Ahnenerbe. But...*
Wilhelm: "Drop dead and crack open the sixth Swastika with your life, you old hag."
*...it happened right when he spoke.*
Rusalka: "Oh..."
*Rusalka placed both of her hands on her stomach and started writhing.*
Rusalka: "Ogh... agh, oh... ubph, oh... ogheeeehh!"
*Vomit fell and splattered on the floor.*
Wilhelm: "Oh boy. Ya lookin' good, Malleus."
*The witch saw Wilhelm's smile and the blindingly white fangs within. And then...*
Shirou: "Just wait."
*...she heard a low voice echo throughout the chapel and realized its source.*
Wilhelm: "Khah!"
*Wilhelm laughed while trailing his fingers through his forelocks.*
Rusalka: "No way... no way... this can't be real. This... this is just..."
*Rusalka's expression was distorted. Not with pain or suffering... ...but fear.*
Rusalka: "Agh... oh... gieeeeeghh!"
*The bicentennial witch's blood and guts scattered all over the room. Some of it even reached the ceiling of the chapel. The witch bent her petite body backwards as something crawled out of her abdomen, right from about where the womb was.*
*Chains rattled as they were dragged. The weapon that used to belong to Rusalka drew a metallic, blood-red line on the floor. Tightening its grip on the chains, the thing from the witch's stomach stood up straight.*
Shirou: "Hmmph... Guess that's that."
*An empty voice with no hint of tension in it. Almost reminiscent of someone intoxicated.*
Shirou: "I'm back! ...That's what I'm supposed to say here, right?"
*Shirou Yusa had been reborn into something unlike a common human.*
Wilhelm: "Heheh, hahahahah, ahahahahhahahahahahahahah!"
*Maddened laughter thundered throughout the chapel, nearly making its very walls tremble. The pale vampire writhed and convulsed, unable to control himself. This was what he sought. The thing above his own karma.*
Wilhelm: "Not bad! Not bad at all! I'm amazed you actually made it happen! Hey, ya bratty shitbag. Tell me, how confident were ya?"
Shirou: "Huh?"
Wilhelm: "This is some downright hilarious bullshit! It's too ridiculous to even be a gamble!"
Shirou: "Hah!"
*Shirou snorted with agreement.*
Shirou: "Well, I can see why this would seem like bullshit. I mean, I didn't even consider my chances."
Wilhelm: "Huhh?"
Shirou: "I'm telling ya that I wasn't actually goin' for this. Just like you said, it wasn't even a gamble. If one thing's true, though ― I never once thought I'd die. "
*Shirou's nonchalant words made Wilhelm fall silent, then widen his eyes and burst out into another roaring laugh.*
Wilhelm: "You didn't count your chances, nor had a will to lose? It's almost like you weren't thinking anything at all! Hahahah, ahahahahah! You fucking brat, take it easy on my sides!"
Shirou: "I don’t even give enough of a shit about you to try and make ya laugh, you pasty motherfucker. Anyway, I got a grasp on how this works when we brawled last time, so all I had to do was get into a situation where I could snatch a toy away from you bastards. "
*All Ahnenerbe ran on souls they were fueled with. Though being consumed deprived a person of their mortal shape, they could still live on a spiritual level.*
Shirou: "I had a good specimen, too. That playful little blonde ghost looked like she had a will of her own."
*Stronger souls could maintain their consciousness after being devoured and even return to reality in a corporeal form.*
Shirou: "So there's really no reason why it shouldn't be possible to take it from the inside."
Wilhelm: "Well, you ain't wrong."
Wilhelm: "But really, fuckers who are able to do that are stupidly rare. It's not even about whether you can or can't take it. Souls given shape through 'formation' are exactly that. What you did is more like, uh... nah, fuck it. Any more talk of this shit would spoil the mood. Let's just fucking do this already. "
Shirou: "Well, that's fine by me, but..."
Shirou: "...what's your deal? Were ya expectin' me to come out?"
Wilhelm: "I was about... twenty percent sure."
Shirou: "Huh? Is that high or low?"
Wilhelm: "Real fuckin' high. I told ya, this kind of shit is stupidly rare. Honestly, if ya didn't pull through, I thought of tearing ya out of Malleus' stomach myself... And I think I should thank ya for not making me do that. She might be worthless, but we've been hanging for a pretty fucking long time, so I wasn't so hot on killing her myself. "
Shirou: "Oh? Now that's damn sympathetic of ya."
Wilhelm: "Well, we already have a rabid dog with no gauge for this kind of shit."
Shirou: "Huh?"
*Puzzled at the answer, Shirou lowered his guard when...*
Wilhelm: "Come on! Let's do this!"
*...the demon closed in on him with inhuman speed and gave him a heavy punch that blew Shirou's lightweight body away, making him break through the wall, ravage the ground and ruin the pavement as he went.*
Shirou: "You fucking old fart!"
*Clad in black, the pallid shadow went after him for another hit, which Shirou avoided by throwing his chains onto a nearby roadside tree and forcefully changing the course of his flight. The large cedar he used had its trunk neatly broken.*
Wilhelm: "Hahh. Not bad at all. You learned a lot in that whore's stomach, didn't ya? You're hanging better than Zarathustra."
Shirou: "Don't spout bullshit names to my face while I'm still in a waking haze."
Wilhelm: "Oh, sorry about that. I'm way too fucking giddy at the moment, so you'll have to deal with it for now. Alright!?"
*Stakes darted out of his whole body. The dead of night shrouded them all with a stygian black tint as they all converged towards Shirou from every possible ― and impossible ― direction. The next moment, however, the night-colored stakes were all bound by the creaking silver chains growing out of Shirou's hand. A fusion type. The offensive combat style where flesh and Ahnenerbe merge to become one. Seeing all that, Wilhelm formed a grin.*
Wilhelm: "Good shit, you brat. It's just like mine. That type fits us like a glove, doesn't it?"
*Wilhelm didn't seem the least bit surprised by his attack being nullified. Instead, he simply raised his glove-covered hand while slowly putting power into his fingers to form a fist.*
Shirou: "You're sure spouting a lot of shit tonight."
Wilhelm: "Oh come on, let me express it all. I haven't felt like this in ages. Fighting the guy I want to fight is a rare thing for me. So rare, in fact, that the smart thing to do right now would be to end it before anyone gets in the way, but it just so happens that I'm a fucking idiot. "
*Wilhelm discarded his sunglasses in a swift move, revealing his blood-red eyes, burning fiercely with a crimson flame.*
Wilhelm: "Let's have some fun. Give me all you've got. Don't you dare bore me, you brat."
*He threw a punch with his right hand. The attack was vigorous enough to tear the air apart, and Shirou instantly knew it would open a hole in any kind of defense he could take. His only choice was to dodge. However, a stake from Wilhelm's elbow flew right where moved. The vampire's Ahnenerbe could make them grow on any place on his body, which easily allowed him to break certain basics rules of combat, like trajectory and distance. Getting too close for comfort for longer than necessary could easily lead to Shirou's demise.*
Shirou: "Ghhh!"
*He raised his chain-covered hand and used it as a shield, but some of the stakes broke through the spaces between the chains and bit about three centimeters into his flesh. Shirou retaliated with several shots, but all his bullets were deflected and fell pitifully to the ground. Offense and defense were one and the same, so hitting the opponent was as difficult as dodging. Wilhelm reigned supreme when it came to hand-to-hand combat.*
*The minor stake injuries on Shirou's arm were making it lose its moisture. A clean hit would surely result in complete mummification. Evasion was the only way to avoid it, but too many less than perfect dodges would eventually dry him out. Indeed, Wilhelm was strong. Definitely not someone Shirou could easily beat just by getting an Ahnenerbe.*
Shirou: "You fucking hedgehog. Your abilities piss me off."
*The stakes were just like a vampire's fangs, and the avarice of the killing power behind them made him well worthy of the Impaler's title.*
Wilhelm: "What? Did ya think we were gonna duke it out? As much as I like your guts, what you're doing ain't very clever."
*Shirou met Wilhelm's provocation with a wry smile.*
Shirou: "Cut me some slack. I'm still just getting the hang of it. I'll be trying lots of things like... this!"
*The chain slithered and instantly extended to a length of twenty meters, neatly representing the limit of Shirou's current effective range.*
Wilhelm: "Oh boy... ya wanna have a tug of war?"
*Wilhelm threw an excited glance at the chain tightly coiled around his arm. With his speed, he could've easily dodged it, but he purposely accepted the challenge.*
Wilhelm: "Well, looks like I'll have to teach ya a few of the basics."
Shirou: "Like how physical strength is the crux of the brawl?"
Wilhelm: "Well, sure, there's that―"
Shirou: "Ngh...!"
*Pulled to the limit, the chain instantly lost its slack and creaked while being dragged to both sides. There was a neat equilibrium in the forces ― or so it seemed.*
Wilhelm: "You conceited little shit! The only ones who could take me on at physical strength are freaks like Cain or Machina. Though yeah, you ain't too fucking shabby, either..."
Shirou: "Hh, gah!"
*Slowly, but surely, the balance crumbled to Wilhelm's side. Shirou was pulled as the tensile strength within the chain easily surpassed ten tons, making the ground under his feet break and his boots smoke due to the friction.*
Wilhelm: "I told ya, duking it out with me ain't very clever. All ya can do is keep a distance and dance around like an idiot. Otherwise, you'll..."
*A remarkably stronger pull made Shirou's body go up into the air, rendering him unable to make any significant movements as he was dragged towards Wilhelm.*
Wilhelm: "...end up like this!"
Shirou: "So what?"
*The resounding scream of the Desert Eagle. Just as Shirou couldn't move, so was Wilhelm unable to dodge. However―*
Wilhelm: "Hahah!"
*...he deflected all the bullets with only his left arm. Shirou's gun was a standard weapon meant for humans, and as such, it couldn't do much harm to a demon's flesh. At least, that was what most would think.*
Wilhelm: "What!?"
*Surprisingly, Wilhelm's arm started leaking white smoke. Using the opportunity caused by the event's surprise factor, Shirou made the entwined chain bend.*
Shirou: "Orraaahhhh!"
*Using all of the springing power within his body, he made a turn as he landed on solid ground and threw Wilhelm away. He couldn't even allow himself to calculate the trajectory, so the swing had no leniency and carried all of his power, body and soul behind it. The attack was just about inhuman enough to significantly damage the demon. However...*
Shirou: "...!"
*...Shirou hurriedly unchained him, making Wilhelm's tall body give in to the centrifugal force and fly while mowing down the trees in his way. As deadly as it seemed, that wasn't nearly enough to give him any damage. The vampire could only be beaten by attacks from an Ahnenerbe. Did the young man made a mistake? No ― definitely not.*
Wilhelm: "Nice instincts you got there. You almost died just now, you know that?"
Shirou: "...Well, yeah. Somehow."
*Wilhelm walked out of the darkness while toppling trees to the sides. Except for a few bullet marks on his left arm, he was completely unharmed. Standing there, he gulped down a grin as he spoke in a deep voice.*
Wilhelm: "A rookie's 'Yetzirah' is like paper to me. I can easily tear that shit apart if I feel like it."
*The destruction of an Ahnenerbe meant the death of its user. Shirou had never heard of that law, but he could feel it in his bones. Any strategy involving the chaining of his opponent was, in fact, a double-edged sword.*
Wilhelm: "Hmph. Glad to see you're perceptive. That aside, you're always smiling, aren't ya?"
Shirou: "What about it?"
Wilhelm: "Well, it's just that it was there right from the fucking start. This is the third time I meet your ugly mug, and that smug grin is the only thing I ever saw on it."
*They met on the road near the church, and then again in the park at night.*
Wilhelm: "You couldn't do shit against me in either of those battles, but that fucking smile of yours still endured."
Wilhelm: "Why, though?"
*Despite Wilhelm's relaxed posture, it was easy to tell he was waiting for the right time to deliver a deadly blow. His speech was only a method of distraction meant to create an opening, something Shirou was fully aware of.*
Wilhelm: "There's something you seek in battle. Is it glory? The fight itself, maybe? Or perhaps..."
*His boots made a light ― and almost cheerful ― sound.*
Wilhelm: "The unknown!?"
*The beast closed in. Taking him head-on would've been suicidal, while his stakes prevented any attempts at dodging.*
Shirou: "That..."
*Shirou quickly decided on what he had to do.*
Shirou: "...ain't any of your fucking business."
*He sprang backwards and made his chain twine around the vertex of the church ― the large cross. Then, with a forceful pull, he retreated to the rooftop, though not with the intention to blindly run away. Wilhelm was far above him at both physical strength and mobility, so he could never best him in a fight on level ground. Shirou had to limit the area to even have a chance.*
Wilhelm: "Guess I hit the mark. Battles are all about prediction. You guess what the others are thinking and outwit 'em. To lose is to let 'em go beyond what you expect. So yeah, if it's the unknown you want, you should be fucking loving this, no? "
Shirou: "It ain't that simple."
*Replying in a bored manner, Shirou cautiously analyzed the situation. Though he distanced himself from the pallid demon, it wasn't nearly enough to be safe from his attacks. If Wilhelm so desired, he could close the space between them in less than a heartbeat. However, that very distance was Shirou's effective range.*
*The past few minutes of brawling made him get a good grasp of The Blood Countess ― his newly-obtained Ahnenerbe — and it definitely wasn't something unfit to fight Wilhelm. After all, it wasn't just chains, but a whole set of different tools. The powered bullets from before were proof of its versatility. He ran simulations of his next course of action as he spoke in his usual, nonchalant tone.*
Shirou: "Even after I survive a battle, I never feel like I succeeded at something. All I can ever think is 'Oh, this shit again' and nothing more. This sensation overcomes me whenever it's all over, like a splash of disappointment."
Wilhelm: "...I see how it is. Wish that fucker Mercurius was here to hear ya."
*After a moment's chuckle, the demon wiped the grin off his face.*
Wilhelm: "Right then, you shitbag. Check this out. There's no way this one ain't unknown to ya."
Shirou: "...!"
*Something was coming. Shirou instantly felt it and made his chains form a net-like wall in the air before him, but that wasn't enough to calm his uneasiness.*
Wilhelm: "I've had enough, kid. It's been fun, but from this point on, I'm going all out."
*That feeling ― that ominous sensation — was likely...*
Wilhelm: "[Wo war ich schon einmal und war so selig](Where did I taste of old such rapture celestial?)"
*Wilhelm's voice reverberated into the stygian night as his surroundings began to shift away from reality.*
Wilhelm: "[Wie du warst! Wie du bist! Das weis niemand, das ahnt keiner!](All thy soul, all thy heart — their perfections who can measure?)"
Wilhelm: "[Ich war ein Bub', da hab' ich die noch nicht gekannt.](I had been but a child before I knew you.)[Wer bin denn ich? Wie komm'denn ich zu ihr?](But who am I? What fate brings her to me?)[Wie kommt denn sie zu mir?](What fate brings me to her?) [Wär' ich kein Mann, die Sinne möchten mir vergeh'n.](Should I be unworthy to live as a knight, may death claim me here and now!)[Das ist ein seliger Augenblick,](For there is no abyss deep enough)――[den will ich nie vergessen bis an meinen Tod.](to rob me of this blissful memory.) "
*The darkness warped like an amoeba as an even deeper night engulfed the sunless sky.*
Wilhelm: "[Sophie, Welken Sie](Wither to ashes, O my love.)"
*The pavement on the surface cracked, dried up, and shattered.*
Wilhelm: "May the world behold your remains."
*The trees withered until they became sand.*
Wilhelm: "[Es ist was kommen und ist was g'schehn, Ich mocht Sie fragen](What has come o'er me, what has come to pass?)"
Wilhelm: "[Darf's denn sein? Ich möcht' sie fragen: warum zittert was in mir?](I fain would ask her: oh, why trembles all my soul? Has bitter wrong, a sinful deed been done?) [Sophie, und seh' nur dich und spür' nur dich.](I gaze and see but you, feel but you.) [Sophie, und weiß von nichts als nur: dich hab' ich lieb](For only I know you, who perished by my love.) "
*A darkness so deep it defied description erupted into the world.*
Wilhelm: "[Sophie, Welken Sie](Wither to ashes, O my love.)"
*Wilhelm chanted, his pallid face distorted by joy. With ferocity, dissipation and excessive satisfaction... ...his aria reached its climax.*
Wilhelm: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
Wilhelm: "[Der Rosenkavalier Schwarzwald](The Rose-Bearer in the Forest of Death)—"
Shirou: "...!?"
*And so the night had been born. The darkness already dominant in the hours of dusk now cloaked itself in hues deeper, thicker than ever before. The veil of the all-decaying Schwarzwald raised the gloom while the Moon wore a brilliant light. A space where darkness and light underwent a constant increase. The genesis of an otherworld that cemented its creator's principal craving as its dominant rule. In other words...*
Wilhelm: "This is the Beri'ah Degree. And from the looks of it..."
*His black coat melted into the night.*
Wilhelm: "...you're not quite here yet, huh? That's a bit of a let-down, but I guess there ain't much to be done about that."
*As if raised by the darkness, the demon's white gloves, ivory hair, pale skin, and the rest of him whole began to merge with the night.*
Wilhelm: "You're gonna die. As thanks for all the fun ya gave me, I won't hold back one bit."
*Shirou looked straight into the blood-red eyes shining within the darkness.*
Wilhelm: "Go on and struggle."
Shirou: "...!"
*A thunderous burst filled the soundscape. After instantly jumping to a height of ten meters and concealing part of the moon with his silhouette, Wilhelm unleashed a barrage of stakes from both of his hands. The rate of fire rivaled that of an M61 Vulcan. Under the continuous blitz not unlike a carpet bombing, the rooftop instantly came to more closely resemble a pincushion.*
Wilhelm: "Dodge dodge dodge dodge! Run around like the pig you are and bring me to my climax! Don't you dare fucking stop!"
*Following the vampire's insane cackle, the storm of stakes grew in intensity. Shirou barely dodged them all as he started to feel his strength gradually fade. Within his Rozenkavalier Schwarzwald, Wilhelm was the hunter, and all else were prey for him to feed on. The rooftop Shirou stood on melted ― no, turned to sand ― as his vitality was drained away. Not only that...*
Wilhelm: "Hahhah!"
*...but Wilhelm's speed when he landed and dashed towards Shirou was even greater than before. It came as no surprise that his own world would supply him with more power. Vampires thrived in the darkness, so a pitch black night like this would push their power to the very limit. Shirou went to the rooftop to strip the demon of the advantage he had on a level field, but it turned out he only forced himself into an open coffin where his movement was hindered.*
Shirou: "Ghh, ogh!"
*The flying stakes, the punches and the kicks were too much for Shirou to keep track of, for the deep darkness camouflaged the flow of the attacks. With Wilhelm and his Ahnenerbe possessing the power to deliver a lethal blow with a single hit, the demon's space was indeed a maelstrom of death itself. Within the night sewn by deathly thorns, the knight of the rose was unmatched.*
Shirou: "Not until I try out all I have!"
*Slipping through yet another wave of the ruthless stake storm, Shirou aimed and shot towards Wilhelm's pair of vividly crimson eyes dancing boisterously within the darkness. Obviously, a normal gunshot wouldn't even work as a distraction, however... ...the tenebrous target dodged to the side, leaving behind the explosive sound of a breaking rooftop and going straight into the rattle of Shirou's chains. Right before the metal coiled around the vampire's ankle, a stake appeared to take its place. Wilhelm laughed as he stood tall on his own weapon.*
Wilhelm: "Hah! Not bad at all. You're holding up pretty fucking well."
Shirou: "I guess. But oh man, I haven't seen stilts since I was a brat. You old-fashioned shithead."
*Their mid-battle exchanges were momentary while their fights were repetitive. Where Wilhelm attacked ten times and consistently shaved away Shirou's vitality, the boy could only counterattack once or twice while constantly failing.*
*Though the demon's speed was an undeniable nuisance, the real problem were the stakes. They turned into a phalanx from up close and projectiles from a distance, not to mention that he could use them to take the brunt of Shirou's blows. At the moment, it was nearly impossible for the boy to directly destroy Wilhelm's Ahnenerbe, so going for a battle of weaponry was the height of folly. The only way Shirou could beat him was through damage to his body.*
Shirou: "Well... that ain't exactly easy when you're fighting a fucking hedgehog."
*Basically, there weren't many openings in his defense. The tampered bullets were relatively useful, but as long as the demon kept frantically moving around, they would never affect the course of the fight. He could try a reckless head-on assault while ignoring the onslaught, but it would most likely get both him and his weapon pierced and broken. Based on what Shirou knew, he calculated that Wilhelm's chance of surviving such an attack was seventy percent, while the boy himself would surely die in the process. If the destruction of an Ahnenerbe resulted in inflicting damage to the user, then...*
Shirou: "Hah!"
*After several tens of fruitless offenses and defenses, Shirou suddenly formed a wry smile.*
Shirou: "...Well, thirty percent is just about enough for a cleanup hitter."
Wilhelm: "Huhh?"
Shirou: "For now, though, I'll just reach some more bases. Come on, don't underestimate me, you shit!"
*One shot after the other, Shirou released a barrage of gunfire. The distance between them was too great for him to get a clear shot, but there were things he could test by doing that, such as his Ahnenerbe-enhanced bullets and a certain other possibility that recently flashed through his mind.*
Wilhelm: "Oh? Not too bad. Adaptable, aren't ya?"
*Jumping around on his very own thicket of stakes, Wilhelm dodged the shots while working his thinker.*
*Standard bullets weren't even worth the effort to evade, but Shirou's gunfire was something entirely different. Each and every projectile was brimming with the abilities of his Ahnenerbe... ...and there was no better proof of that than the yet-unhealed gunshot wounds on his arm.*
Wilhelm: "You started with the poison. And now it's... "
*Suddenly, a .50AE bullet exploded right before his eyes.*
Wilhelm: "...needles!"
*Bursting like buckshot, it released dozens of needles. Though their damaging power was low, a hit to the eye would nonetheless be severe — and that was exactly what Shirou intended.*
Wilhelm: "Hah! I can see right through ya!"
*However, the pallid vampire dodged them all. His reaction speed was beyond belief. The bullet came towards him at mach speed and burst into needles only a few centimeters before his eyes. Even if he knew his opponent's intentions, evading that was downright ludicrous. It proved that his reflexes were beyond human knowledge. He then kicked away a stake at his side and shielded himself from the bullet storm that followed, only to be greeted by a large wheel.*
Wilhelm: "Retard."
*His face warped with contempt and ridicule. Wilhelm couldn't grasp why Shirou formed such a large target for him. Had he already forgotten the rule?*
*The wheel closed in, but the demon didn't even bother dodging it and faced it head-on. As they both knew, when two Ahnenerbe clashed, the one that came out on top was always the stronger and better tempered. Thus, the wheel shattered into dozens of pieces that toppled the cross behind him. The seemingly silver symbol slipped and fell into the darkness while making a high-pitched sound. Game. Set. Match. The boy's blunder determined the outcome. Wilhelm didn't know why his opponent made such a reckless move, but his dissatisfaction far outweighed his confusion.*
Wilhelm: "Don't pull this boring fuckery with me. Did you forget the shit I told you? Huh!?"
*Breaking an Ahnenerbe broke the user. The destruction of the wheel made Shirou fall to his knees and forced blood out of his mouth.*
Wilhelm: "Hey, piss-stain, is that really all you got? You were doing so well until the mid-point and now you're..."
Shirou: "Don't you fucking worry... I was just trying something."
Wilhelm: "Huh?"
Shirou: "It's just as I thought. Losing a single weapon doesn't kill me."
*Still kneeling, Shirou looked at Wilhelm with an indomitable grin on his face, as if to ridicule his confusion. During the whole of their battle, he tried and succeeded at forming twelve weapons. Chain, needles, wheel, fetters, dagger, fretsaw, poison, chair, funnel, screws, mask, and a stone plate. A varied set of instruments, united only by the purpose to torture and inflict suffering. That was the true nature of the Ahnenerbe Shirou had inherited. Adorning the name of "Elizabeth Báthory" ― the maddened countess ― it was a collection of tools specialized in the drawing of blood.*
*The woman penned the nightmarish notebook during her later years, while confronting death in the solitude of a windowless chamber within her own castle. With all the tools and methods of torture it covered, it was no doubt a pandemonic tome written in the blood and pained screams of thousands. Shirou was able to grant form to any of the tools penned within, and due to their sheer number, the destruction of a single one wouldn't automatically spell his doom.*
Shirou: "...Well, I'd say the difference in our strength has just been balanced out."
*Quantity over quality. His tools were weak, but if a single item's destruction didn't mean his death, victory wasn't a delusion.*
Shirou: "My chances now are at least fifty percent... It'd be even easier if I could pull the shadows that bitch had, but I guess it ain't that simple."
*Since Rusalka's Nachtzehrer was an original born through her "Creation Figment", there was no reason for Shirou to be able to use them. It didn't matter, though. He knew he'd do just fine with what he had.*
Shirou: "Let's end this, you bastard."
*Shirou stood up and carried out another "formation", wringing out all the tools of torture he could summon at once, spreading them throughout his surroundings. They were as much weapons as they were armor. He'd risk his life with every attack, but it was definitely worth a shot.*
Shirou: "Leave even one of these intact and you lose. Not gonna chicken out on me, are ya, First Lieutenant?"
Wilhelm: "..."
*The harsh reality of Shirou being unable to catch up to Wilhelm's speed remained, allowing the vampire to potentially put the boy into a checkmate by simply keeping his distance while barraging him with stakes. Shirou provoked the vampire precisely in order to prevent him from taking that route. Would he take the bait, or...?*
Wilhelm: "Khah! Hahah, khahahahah, hahahahahahahahahah! Ahahah, hahahahah, hahahahahahahahahahahahah! "
Wilhelm: "You're a fucking riot!"
*Wilhelm's reply was a cackle laden with sadistic bliss.*
Wilhelm: "Oh yeah, of course I'll take it! Playing along with a brat's games is what we mature adults do. Bring it. The party's in full swing, so let's dance with all we've got. I'll be eating your fucking soul, so get ready to try and tear me apart from the inside. "
Shirou: "Oh, dude..."
*Shirou's voice had a hint of shock in it.*
Shirou: "That sounds so fucking gay, holy shit."
*He made a step forward... ...and instantly accelerated.*
Wilhelm: "Come on! Come on, come on, get over here!"
*With twelve instruments of torture formed around him, Shirou made a headlong dash towards Wilhelm, who took him on while cackling like a madman.*
Shirou: "Uohhhhhhh!"
*His thunderous roar shook the twin-layered night. In the moment that would part their life and death, Shirou prepared himself for the rose-stake heading towards his heart...*
Rea: "...Nn."
*Rea Himuro woke up to a splitting headache.*
Rea: "This is..."
*Her body was heavy and her mobility was limited. Upon looking around, she saw a great hole in the wall of the chapel and felt the torrents of battle flowing through it. Someone was fighting outside. After a short scan of her memories from before she lost consciousness, she guessed it to be Wilhelm and...*
Rusalka: "...Uh."
*...Rusalka. Yet in truth, the witch was actually lying in her own pool of blood, clearly on the verge of death.*
Rusalka: "Shit... Shit... Stop it, Bey... Don't use your 'Creation Figment' here."

Rusalka: "You really are a strange one, aren't you?"

*And so, living longer than anyone else was all she could come up with. She had no idea what else she could have done. Maybe she would have discovered something, had she caught up with and gazed at the true face of the man of shadows. But the more time passed, the more she was left behind. Pain, sadness, and loneliness gnawed at her heart — she failed to catch up to and grasp that ephemeral moment of her life.*
Machina: "The moment you first felt that instinct of self-destruction, your lifespan had already come to an end. Malleus, all your actions betray your wish to die. I envy you, for you can find your ultimate end. "
*The man's words betrayed no hint of sympathy or emotion, yet there was no mistaking it that he genuinely felt envious of the woman.*
Rusalka: "Huh? What the hell are you even talking about? Boy, you really are irritating."
*Surrounded by clouds of dust, Rusalka fell to her knees with a sob.*
Rusalka: "I hate you. I hate you all. I hated you all from the very start."
Rusalka: "Whatever. I don't care anymore. I did my best, but it was still not enough."
Machina: "..."
Rusalka: "Go ahead and do your thing."
Machina: "Very well."
*Machina clenched his fists again. If there was one good thing about them, it was that they killed faster than one could feel pain.*

Machina: "I wouldn't know."
Rusalka: "No one will leave me behind?"
Machina: "All will be swallowed by the chaos that is Heydrich."

*The man's sombre fist fell upon Rusalka. However, in the split second before it robbed her of life—*
Machina: "But I wish for the end of this world."
*The witch that lived for three hundred years could not help making a smile at the dryness of the Einherjar's remark. It had been a genuine smile, embroidered with nothing. The two were completely different, yet she felt almost like she was talking to him. Unfortunately, her smile would never reach its true target — the man of the ephemeral moment.*
*Fiery winds and dust filled the entirety of the space between them. An average man would have had his lungs scorched from within by a single breath of this seething air, yet in the midst of this hellish place, there billowed a single wisp of smoke with almost surreal grace. Her blood-crimson hair fluttered in the wind like raining hellfire. And although half of her face had been horribly burned beyond recognition, the rest of it boasted undeniable feminine beauty. Seething passions mingled with blood-curdling frigidity — the hideous meeting the beautiful, fire merging with ice. The terror-instilling [half-demon](Zentaur) then addressed the two, as flames of absolute zero raged all around her.*
Eleonore: "Do my ears deceive me? I could have sworn I heard two fools insulting my master. "
*They were all but an extension of the castle, rendering any attempts at a secret conversation meaningless. Eleonore narrowed her eyes at the two guests, smoke escaping her lips.*
Eleonore: "Kristoff."
*Valeria Trifa used his body as a shield to protect his companion from the deadly flames.*
Eleonore: "Brenner."
*Lisa Brenner glared at Eleonore from behind Trifa's back.*
*They both faced Rubedo — one of the Gold's Imperial Guard — with unwavering conviction burning in their eyes. Yet Eleonore laughed the display off as a ridiculous farce.*
Eleonore: "Well, do as you wish. Whatever madness may have ravaged your minds, I care very little for it. I belong to the Imperial Guard, and it is merely my duty to exterminate scoundrels that threaten my lord. Have at you, shameless thugs. Not even the stigma has helped your tainted minds to comprehend the magnificence of Gold. I cannot allow cancerous cells like you to survive. I shall eradicate you without a trace. "
*Despite the severity of her words, Eleonore's tone remained gentle. If anything, she happily welcomed this outcome. Love, murder, friendship, respect, animosity — they all amounted to the same for an immortal, blood-thirsty Einherjar. Killing was hardly different from offering a loving embrace to a friend. The luster of her tremendous soul dwarfed even the raging heat waves. Much like Machina, she was not a being mortals could defeat. The Battalion of Three was all a part of Reinhard.*
*Thus, the question was how to escape, rather than how to prevail. How to distract her. How to buy more time. That was what Trifa and Lisa should have concentrated on, but Eleonore allowed no room for tricks. Even among the three Imperial Guards, she was the hardest to slip past. She lacked the aloof nature of Machina, as well as the madness of Schreiber. Only ironclad loyalty bound her to her lord. There was no room for games or chaos in her heart. Therefore, if there was but one gap to be found in her perfect armor, it would be the penchant for self-destruction — a concept that Reinhard prioritized above all else. Yet...*
Trifa: "This hardly bodes well. I should have kept my mouth shut. Am I no longer even a substitute in your eyes? "
Eleonore: "Without your plating, you are certainly not."
*Eleonore stated it like an obvious fact, but it was only then that Lisa came to see the abnormality ravaging the priest.*
Lisa: "Valeria..."
*Cracks and fissures littered Trifa's exposed flesh. All present could understand what it meant.*

*As Eleonore snapped her fingers, palpable contempt burning in her eyes... ...Trifa's body shattered.*
Lisa: "...!"
*Rejection response. Trifa reached the limit before Eleonore's attack could find him. His soul surged forth as the explosion scorched the priestly robes that clad the now empty vessel. However, both Lisa and Eleonore reacted in a peculiar fashion. The latter shuddered in awe and looked away from that glorious display of naked virility. The former made a self-scornful face, as if reminded of an old sin.*

Eleonore: "So that's what you think."

*Lamentation. Wrath. Envy. Fear. A whole range of emotions — all aimed at a person she found unable to comprehend. For as long as she lived, Eleonore von Wittenburg would refuse to acknowledge Lisa Brenner. The demonic flames raging in her eyes made that clear enough.*
Lisa: "So you heard everything. About how I answered him, I mean. "
*"In the end, who was the father?" Despite drowning Lisa's answer in an assault of flames, deep in her heart, Eleonore wished to know the truth.*

*So Lisa stood up and addressed her former friend.*
Lisa: "Do you find it unforgivable?"
*Valeria Trifa did not die — he was merely torn away from the vessel. Still, it did not change the fact that he was evicted from the room and that Lisa now faced the crimson knightess alone. Anyone could realize that Lisa's position was hopeless. Still—*
Lisa: "I manipulated his corpse."
*A mask manifested on Lisa's open palm. It reeked of death, filling the whole room with the stench of a graveyard.*
Lisa: "I admit to being a harlot. The worst kind, no less."
*A giant monster materialized out of thin air.*
Lisa: "But you're in no position to condemn me!"
*There was no hint of despair in Lisa's eyes. Despite the hopelessness of her situation, she did not feel like backing down.*
Lisa: "What right to do you have to lecture me on cowardice and deceit? You were no better a woman than me, Eleonore!"

*A greatsword three meters in length fell on Eleonore, spewing purple lightning in all angles. But before it could finish its arc—*
Eleonore: "Very well."
*Eleonore stayed in place, taking the tremendous blow without even attempting to defend herself.*
Eleonore: "I don't understand female emotions. They are complicated and fickle beyond belief — a defective tool not to be trusted; an instrument used only to conveniently justify the madness of the mind. I neither know, nor wish to possess such a thing. In that sense, I indeed fail to stand on the same battlefield as you, for I cannot even comprehend it. "
*Eleonore did not exhale so much as a grunt when her right shoulder took the dead warrior's blade. The blow decimated the floor below her feet, yet she brushed it off as if it was the mere jab of a stick. Her eyes slightly narrowed.*
Eleonore: "And I suppose this is another fool that dedicated herself to that battlefield of yours?"
Lisa: "...Yes, I suppose that would make it so."
*The blade of the greatsword still shimmered in fierce, purple lightning. Both women understood what that meant. As such, there was no point in prolonging the conversation any further.*
Eleonore: "In that case, take this."
Lisa: "...!"
*Eleonore shook the cigar between her lips, and a single spark crumbled down from it, touching the giant's body during its descent. That was all that happened, and yet the dead warrior was instantly engulfed in violent, crimson flames.*
Eleonore: "Allow me to cremate you. I can barely stomach to look at you like this."
*The difference between the strength of the two was nearly comical. The giant vanished within the flaming inferno — not even Lisa could escape the burns. She made her Ahnenerbe disappear the moment the flames erupted, but that was not enough for her to escape the explosion unscathed. Lisa staggered with a soundless wail on her lips, burns littering the entirety of her body. Eleonore meanwhile continued in a calm voice.*
Eleonore: "Don't blame the cliff for being high after jumping off. The battlefield you speak of is no different from being roasted alive. You dance atop a grill, refusing to jump off. And then you blame the world for being unable to fly. You all sought the salvation of Gold. And it's only fair you would pay for it with your souls. You are thieves. You should revel in the flames of redemption, yet instead you cower in fear at its sight. And you should know that no wings would ever sprout on the backs of hopeless fools. "
*They had bent the knee to Reinhard Heydrich once. They were beguiled by His power, scorched by its magnificence, and piled up countless bodies in the name of His glory.*
Eleonore: "You would fight Lord Heydrich? You, who plundered His boon, and dared think of it as a disgrace? Don't make me laugh, Brenner. I detest you from the bottom of my heart! "
*Eleonore cared not for the fool's circumstances, reasoning, and emotions — she would not even entertain the idea of acknowledging them. The crimson knightess seethed in silent fury.*
Eleonore: "How can you be so shameless?"
*How could she possibly defile the concept of honor to that extent?*
Eleonore: "All things in the world have a cause and a result. And the present has delivered an answer to your past. It's only fair you return the corpses you piled up. After all, it wouldn't even be the first time for you— "
*Countless rifles manifested behind Eleonore's back. Lisa felt as if an army of spears had been pointed at her neck, but she displayed no fear. She merely let out a sigh.*
Lisa: "Are you talking about Isaak?"
*Once in the past, she sacrificed her own flesh and blood to the Gold. Beguiled by the promise of miracles, she let go of her own son.*
Lisa: "I wonder if he spent all this time resenting me."
*Not minding the numerous muzzles pointed at her, Lisa tossed her head up and gazed at the ceiling. Did the heart of Valhalla — her son — resent its mother?*
Lisa: "I was afraid of him. I couldn't look him in the eye. He reminded me of my sins. And so, I let go of him. He was the embodiment of my transgressions and disgrace — a weakness I lacked the strength to face. He was too much like his father. "
Eleonore: "..."
*Eleonore slightly furrowed her brows, but remained silent. Lisa's words filled her with disgust and insulted all of her ideals, yet she could not bring herself to interrupt the woman. Unable to comprehend the peculiar sensation, Eleonore furrowed her brows even further. But all that did was irritate her further.*
*And so, she forced her lips to part.*
Eleonore: "He... does not possess the quality to resent another."
*Isaak — the first Sonnenkind — possessed nothing. A fact that ought to surprise no one, for he lacked the very foundations of such things. And it was none other than Lisa who had made him so.*
Eleonore: "One cannot feel sorrow or hatred unless they are robbed of something. But have you given him anything to be robbed of?"
Lisa: "No."
*Lisa bestowed upon him nothing. She gave him no foundations. And so there was no way emotions could have sprouted in the bastard who had possessed nothing to begin with.*
Lisa: "And that's why he's trying to swallow everything instead."
*He had nothing. Thus, he craved everything. Heaven and Hell, God and Satan — all things in Creation, from the first universe that was, to the last that will ever be.*
Lisa: "Love is the harbinger of destruction."
*Lisa made a tired smile, her eyes glazed in the recesses of her past.*
Lisa: "It's all very simple. In the end, it was me who made him like his father. I didn't give birth to a monster — I turned him into one myself.  Now I finally understand it all. "
Lisa: "So listen, Eleonore. All I want now is to save that child. It might be in complete opposition with my initial wish, but that's the truth. Does it make me disgusting in the eyes of your creed? "
Eleonore: "Very well."
*One of the rifles went off.*
Eleonore: "Your reasoning is that of a whore. You once cast him aside like a burden, yet you're trying to act the mother now? I might not be a woman in my heart, but even I can tell how rotten you are."
Eleonore: "You shamelessly act like a representative of women and mothers around the world, yet all you are is a disgrace. If anything, you are an enemy to all of womankind.  Let me be blunt with you, Brenner — Babylon is a harlot. She can only give birth to carrion that defiles the world. "
*Four successive shots pierced Lisa's shoulders, chest, and belly, yet she took them all without any hint of resistance.*
Eleonore: "You make me sick, Brenner. Do you fancy yourself a martyr now? You're merely substituting pain with pleasure. As such, I won't permit you an easy death. I'll scorch your flesh, little by little, until there is nothing left but bones. If you wish to atone for your sins, then scream and wail in despair — that shall be a requiem for your children. I've heard more than enough of your hypocrisy for one day. "
*The quantity and speed of her shots kept increasing. By the time Eleonore ended her speech, Lisa was already fighting off a torrent of bullets.*
Lisa: "You're completely right."
*Yet she refused to fall. If anything, it seemed like she was slowly advancing forward.*
Lisa: "I'm fully aware that there are few women more wretched than me. I know I'm a hypocrite, and that I'm fast to turn a blind eye to things that inconvenience me. I know I brought this all on myself. "
Lisa: "I truly have no way of retorting to any woman who would decide to condemn me. After all, they'd be right — I had been in the wrong from the very beginning."
By this time, she had turned into a bloody mess: her tongue, teeth, and even vocal cords were utterly decimated, yet still her voice rang clear and resolute. Step after step, she pressed ever onwards. Her voice grew ever closer. Eleonore couldn't believe what she glimpsed and heard through the torrent of bullets and clouds of smoke. Inexplicable. Unfathomable to an eerie level. Her common sense could not find an explanation for this phenomenon. 
Lisa: "Don't run away from me."
Eleonore: "...!"
*Eleonore realized she was about to take a step back.*
Eleonore: "You filth!!"
*A scream spilled forth from her lips as she launched a missile to decimate her foe once and for all.*
*The incoming warhead. The sizzling conflagration. Realizing that death was near, Lisa made a faint smile. The two could never see eye to eye. Even a reunion after sixty long years had turned into a bloodbath. At this point, Lisa could only laugh. They fought all the time. They could not help competing. Their BDM days were those of constant struggle against each other — they even fought over who could wake up earlier.*
*Those were naïve and childish days. Whenever Lisa tried recalling the nostalgic radiance of those times, Eleonore would always pop up in her mind's eye. And that was the same for the crimson knightess, was it not? "You make my blood boil, Eleonore. Why do you keep popping up in all of my nice memories?" "I'm tired of constantly seeing that dumb mug of yours. Get out of my head."Why couldn't she ignore her, despite detesting her so? Why was she still trying to compete with her at this point? The whole thing felt ridiculous.*
*Hadn't they fought enough? Hadn't they competed enough? No matter how much their life changed, it seemed like they simply could not get enough of going at each other's throats. Eleonore refused to acknowledge Lisa's way of life.Lisa refused to admit defeat against Eleonore. The stubbornness of the two reached unbelievable heights. What could have been the initial cause for this decade-spanning conflict?*
*It didn't matter which one of them represented the correct bearing of a woman. There was no point for either of them to run for elections at this point, long after they abandoned their Fatherland. Therefore, it was merely a vague feeling that they had unfinished business between each other that drove them forward. They both grew old, their many years swallowed by the river of time, yet still they refused to stop their flight, finding themselves racing at the very edge of hell. There was most likely something that the two had accidentally left behind, and were now merely struggling to retrieve it.*
*"Wouldn't you agree, Eleonore?"*
Eleonore: "Stay away from me, you filth...!"
*Eleonore declared she would scorch the woman's flesh to the bone little by little; that she would make her cry out in despair. And never in her life had she gone against her word — she prided herself on seeing all of her promises through to the end. So where had her dignity vanished in that moment?*
*Why did she end up launching a Panzerfaust? Why did she suddenly decide to scorch the woman in an instant? Would she have been in danger otherwise? Would she have damaged herself, had she did not make that decision? No. The very notion of that was impossible — the world would sooner turn upside down before that woman could hurt her. Yet... yet she could not contain her anger. She felt an inexplicable sense of defeat come over her.*
*They clashed and fought countless times, more than enough to make her sick of the ordeal. They were no longer children trying to outperform one another. How long would this senseless bickering continue? Both of them had long been fed up with it and lost interest. And yet, they still found themselves unable to turn a blind eye to even the most meager of discords. "You make me sick, Brenner. Every last thing about you rubs me the wrong way."*
*But why was it so?*
*The issue of the matter might have lied with the fact that the two have never fought over anything truly child-like. They bickered over thousands of things, and yet, that alone seemed to have slipped through their fingers. "You see, Rea is cute beyond words." "A genuine little lady." And that was what the two lacked.*
*Lisa's youth... Eleonore's youth... "Do you now understand what we missed out on?" Even though it was something natural to all young women. As such, refusing to go through the correct motions, the two ended up never growing up, remaining as two callow brats, forever barred from proper womanhood.*
*Therefore—  Lisa Brenner now craved to become a mother. Rea, Isaak, and the children in her heart... She wished to hold them all tight in her arms. And to do that, she had to settle the score with Eleonore, once and for all. "May this defiled body of mine hold out for just a little while longer."*
*And as the hundredth shot ruptured... ...her prayer reached its target.*
*A dry sound reverberated across the hall, neither caused by a bullet, nor by an explosion. It was small — almost inaudible — compared to the thunder of gunfire that had dominated the room just moments before. Eleonore could not comprehend as to what could have caused it, nor why one of her cheeks suddenly grew numb. What did Lisa do to her?*
Lisa: "I believe I've told you, Eleonore, that you alone have no right to condemn me. You, who never once had the courage to stand on a woman's battlefield. "
Eleonore: "..."
*It was Lisa's hand — having suddenly emerged from the mantle of smoke and dust covering the air — that hit Eleonore's cheek.*
Lisa: "In the end, I never got the chance to have a proper fight with you. You kept running away... "
*All of Eleonore's bullets found their mark. Lisa tried neither to dodge, nor to defend against them. She simply endured. Despite having suffered mortal wounds, she held on with an iron will to maintain her crumbling body, delaying the moment of her demise. It was no easy feat. At this point, it was nothing short of a miracle, exceeding any reasoning known to man. As such, Eleonore failed to comprehend it, allowing herself to be hit straight in the face. If there was an expression to describe what led to this outcome, it would have to be sheer feminine tenacity. For indeed, it lay beyond the comprehension of the crimson knightess, who had cast aside her womanhood.*
Lisa: "You've never shown me your true feelings. You only ever hid yourself behind a convenient mask, spouting irrefutable arguments... like a fool! Yet behind that mask, you were just a coward, Eleonore. "
*Lisa Brenner was a repugnant woman — the concept of ethics itself would condemn her. And that was true — she could not deny it. Yet neither did she wish to listen to those that used her bearing to justify their wrath.*
Lisa: "If you're going to hate me, at least have the common decency to tell the reason straight to my face."
Lisa: "Society? The nation? All you did was run away from me, hiding behind fancy-sounding reasons. You couldn't accept the fact that I stole the man you loved. That's all there was to it. "
*Eleonore said nothing; there was no way for Lisa to tell what was going on in her mind. Nonetheless, the crimson knightess did not attempt to deny the accusation. Was that how she expressed mercy during the final moments of her once-comrade's life? Or was she merely rendered speechless by the ludicrousness of the comment? Or could it be she really had no words to retort it with? All that was clear was that she failed to deny Lisa in that moment.*

Eleonore: "Speak for yourself."

Eleonore: "You and Kircheisen both spouted that same nonsense, without even considering that others might feel differently compared to you."
Eleonore: "And this is why I despise women. That's all you've got in your silly heads. Is a woman that knows not the touch of a man nothing more than a pathetic creature in your minds? There are as many mindsets and ways of life as there are people. "

Eleonore: "I have."

Eleonore: "If anything, not a day goes by without me thinking about it. But it is nothing as naïve and callow as your rotten mind might imagine."
Eleonore: "I yearn not for warmth, but flames. I wish to burn in a fire eternal for all time to come."
Lisa: "That's one passionate confession."
Eleonore: "I care not how you interpret it. You're scum, but your grit got the better of me.It would be remiss of me not to show you proper respect. Sleep now, Brenner. Should you feel discontent, we can always have another fight. "

*But in response to that parting line...*
Lisa: "That's why I said it was unfortunate."
*...Lisa only made a faint smile.*
Lisa: "Ah, forgive me. I can finally hold you in my arms, Isaak. I'll join you, so please, let Rea... "
*The devil's castle trembled in the wake of her fading voice. For a moment, the demonic structure appeared like a giant cradle, with a newborn babe peacefully listening to its mother's lullaby inside.*
Isaak: "Mother."
*Isaak cocked his head in response to the scream of a soul he had absorbed. Well, in truth, he could not literally proceed with such an action — he had no real body to speak of. He was merely a part of the whirling chaos. A mere drop in the ocean, but also a heart — the most important cog of the mechanism.*
Isaak: "Mother has melted into me."
*Therefore, he could now understand her. A new drop fell into the ocean that he supervised, the resulting ripple telling him of everything that transpired. "Ah, I see."And so Isaak — the core of the devil's castle — molded a new soul into its thick walls.*
*He felt nothing else. He was simply that kind of being, and molding anything new that fell into his sea was but a natural process for him. And he would continue to do so up until his being overflowed, emanated, and swallowed all there was in the world. Maintaining this sea — this castle — was the gear's sole duty.*
*And that was why, despite realizing that he had swallowed his own mother, he felt nothing in particular. Joy, sorrow, resentment, wrath, or desolation — none of it colored his psyche. Unable to feel exhaustion or boredom, he merely quivered in the synchrony of the ripple. That was all. He loved all and everything. And thus, he swallowed without discrimination. All would be equal before the swirling chaos of Weltall — from a newborn babe grieving for its mother's milk to a vile criminal despised by all of mankind. Sonnenkind — the favorite of the Gold's children — was that kind of being.*
*Or at least, that was how it had been until now. Everything should have ended here, and yet...*
Isaak: "...What?"
*A slight incongruity. He kept turning like the diligent gear he was, proceeding with his operation like a well-oiled machine, yet he suddenly became aware of an aberration within his system.*
Isaak: "Is someone crying?"
*Or was that a scream? An odd creak escaped Isaak's being as he rotated according to the usual protocol.*
*The turning of gears would generate sound, so there was nothing odd with the occurrence — such a concept was not applicable to his being. It was only true in the world ruled by common, physical laws. The same did not apply to the sea under his supervision. The melody of grinding gears meant but one thing — abrasion. They would clash against each other and scream in agony as parts of them ended up eroding to nothingness. Hence why regular gears would only hold for a couple of years and required constant maintenance and replacing. No mechanical part that caused sound could function for an eternity.*
*As such, what on earth could have happened? No change occurred in Isaak. He felt nothing. Yet he could feel abrasion in his being. In other words, there was someone else who cried within himself. In that case...*
Isaak: "I see..."
*He finally remembered that he swallowed someone else in his aloofness. There had been two gears currently within himself.*
Isaak: "You lament Mother's passing, Theresia?"
*The devil's castle trembled. Isaak Eins Sonnenkind paused to ponder as how to treat this phenomenon that cast a shadow upon his duty.*
Isaak: "We will erode and disappear if you keep crying like this forever."
*That way, they could not remain as eternal gears. Isaak could not fulfill the mission bestowed upon him by the Gold.*
Isaak: "There is something extraneous in you."
*The girl possessed something he was bereft of.*
Isaak: "I know not my mother."
*But the girl did.*
Isaak: "Hence, you cry."
*Hence, he would erode.*
Isaak: "Fine. Then let me swallow your love."
*Isaak opened his eyes.*
*They sparkled in gold, as if able to see through everything — yet they looked at nothing. Beauty and ugliness; holiness and vileness — all were equal, no more special than rocks and trees, before his gaze. The eyes that Lisa Brenner could not bear to look straight into. The eyes that were the reason he turned out like this. He received no alternative.*
*Nor the emotions to resent or lament that fact. As such, Isaak was on the verge of devouring the forbidden fruit. He desired to know its taste.*
*No differences should have been allowed between Sonnenkinds.*
Isaak: "I will make you like myself. Or rather... "
*What made his voice tremble? Or was that a sneer?*
*He loved all and everything. And thus, he swallowed without discrimination. All would be equal before the swirling chaos of Weltall — from a newborn babe grieving for its mother's milk to a vile criminal despised by all of mankind. And yet...*
Rea: "Do you hate me?"
*Lisa Brenner melted into the castle, causing a ripple of valiant motherhood to wash over it — the very same feeling she harbored towards Rea Himuro. If Isaak indeed felt resentment towards the girl... ...then that made him unworthy of the title of Sonnenkind, the most beloved of the Gold's children.*
Isaak: "May you know Hell, Theresia."
*A slight abrasion that occurred due to a barely perceptible creak. Yet that was enough to upset the gears of the castle's heart.*
*In that case, he had to re-evaluate his concept of Hell. It was the lowest world of deafening screams that sinners would be cast into after their inevitable demise. That was about it. But what did the words "lowest" and "screams" mean in this context? Torment. Treading a mountain of needles, swimming in a sea of flames, crawling through a valley of ice — anyone with a semblance of imagination could come up with countless images at will. And none were wrong. In other words, Hell was where one died over and over again. If it was indeed a place prepared to punish sinners for their transgressions, then making it as undesirable as possible made sense.*
However, depending on the time or place, the concepts of good and evil could change — there was no less trustworthy law devised by mortals. What would be the factors that led one to be cast into a mountain of needles, sea of flames, or a valley of ice? Wilhelm: "Isaak, you piece of shit, you promised all that crap, and delivered nothing. Or are you implyin' I don't matter? Well, I don't care if you do. "

Wilhelm: "I've always had but one wish, both now and back then."
*He turned around and disappeared into the darkness, seemingly having lost all interest in the battle about to unfold within the walls of the castle.*
Wilhelm: "Try not to kick the bucket, shithead. Only I've got the right to end ya."
*Who was he addressing? The one certainty about him were his starved eyes, burning crimson like a pair of roses.*
*As the violent storm blew Alfheim apart, calm and deliberate steps — in polar contrast to the raging winds — creeped through the castle. It was not like they had a particular goal. They were neither trying to hide, nor lazing away from an exercise — creeping was, indeed, the highest speed they could muster. As such, their master must have been an insect. It had no wings or feathers, and out of its limbs, only the right arm and the left leg remained.*
*Pitiful. Miserable. Puny. It was rare for such an abject creature to exist in the gorgeous castle of Gold. Its very existence soiled its surroundings, yet the thing laughed.*
Trifa: "Hah... hah hah..."
*It was not a laugh born of madness — the creature no longer possessed the faculties to go insane. It left half of its body parts lying on the bloody trail behind it. But then why did it laugh?*
Trifa: "Ahh, it hurts..."
*Ahh, it was so painful.*
Trifa: "Ahh, I cannot see..."
*Ahh, his tongue trembled.*
Trifa: "Ahh, how can I be so..."
*He was so desperate to keep on living. He had been filled with delight.*
*The pitiful insect crawling on the floor was once known as Valerian Trifa. Despite suffering a mortal wound, he slipped past the eyes of the raging beast as it lost its mind, and somehow managed to escape alive. It was not that hard. Schreiber only reacted to life in his present state, and so the moribund Trifa barely registered to his senses. In short, all went according to the plan. In a way, one could call it success.*

*Before him lay the giant gates leading to the throne room. The priest used Lisa and Rusalka precisely to reach this place.*
*No one could have broken through the Battalion of Three alone. Not to mention, one of them constituted the priest's natural enemy. As such, realizing that the task was impossible on his own, he sacrificed the other two as pieces on a chessboard. He pitted Rusalka against Machina — the most problematic of them all. He used Lisa's and Eleonore's conflict to seamlessly discard the Divine Vessel, and faced Schreiber himself. There, he planned either to destroy, or at least besmirch Albedo. And now was the moment of truth where he reached his ultimate goal.*
Trifa: "I demand entry...!"

Reinhard: "So you came. You've done well, Divine Vessel. Or would you now prefer a different name?"
*Reinhard addressed Trifa — who had sacrificed everything to brave the three Hells and reach his throne — in the most soothing of tones. He had been the center of this universe. He — the preeminent and omnipotent — praised the struggle of the insect at his feet with the all-loving affection of a monarch.*
Reinhard: "To tell you the truth, you have surprised me. I have never thought you would be able to leave my side. As such, your undertaking has entertained me greatly. And so I ask, what made you go that far? "
Trifa: "I wonder..."
*Trifa's life was about to leave his mangled body. That he held out for this long was a miracle in itself; it would not have been surprising in the least if he dropped dead the very next second. Yet he showed no signs of actually being in a hurry. In fact, he seemed to have been enjoying the conversation, as his bloodless cheeks contorted in a faint, mangled smile.*
Trifa: "I am afraid I do not know what Your Lordship means. Could it have inconvenienced You to have a jester among your vassals?  Surely You would not say that a change in me posed a problem to you. "
Reinhard: "I never once claimed that you have inconvenienced me."
*Reinhard answered with a smile. He, of course, knew everything.*
*This conversation had been a repeat of one he had in ages past. To think he would obey foreknowledge to such minute details... Such was Trifa's answer. Deliberately pitting Reinhard Heydrich against foreknowledge meant nothing but rebellion.*

*An internal split within the Obsidian Round Table. Sowing the seeds of conflict among them could potentially snare the particular individual. He was not guided by logic. When asked what he based his conclusion on, he would not have been able to answer. But something made him suspect it to be true. Dangerously so.*
Trifa: "Johann is alive."

Trifa: "You see, Lord Heydrich, there is one thing I could never be certain of. I loved Theresia. I thought her to be more precious than the world itself. But I did not know whom those feelings belonged to, and so I was left in doubt, forever blind to the truth.  "
Trifa: "I even suspected her foolhardy actions to be the manifestation of Isaak's will. What other answer was there? Johann had run away from him. And so he was trying to get him back. And if that was so, at whom had my love been directed? Where did it manifest itself? I thought, and pondered, and contemplated, but the answer nevertheless eluded me. "

Trifa: "And the result could not have been worse. Theresia herself made my plans fall apart as my essence began divulging from the Divine Vessel. An outcome that called for the greatest despair, yet instead I laughed at it with joy. For even now, despite it all, my love for Theresia remains unwavering! "
*Which was why he instigated a loyal rebellion, and paved the way to this outcome. One foot in the grave, Trifa sung in triumphant jubilance.Reinhard regarded the priest from above and gently parted his lips.*

The corpses of my dear children would only keep piling up for as long as I kept running. As such, I made up my mind to finally face forward. I decided not to allow that accursed Hell to consume the last child that pulled my hand. And I resolved to liberate the others that I doomed.  I am here, Lord Heydrich. "

*It was still uncertain whether his choice had broken through his creed.*

*Whoever reached his throne would have their wish granted. He would promise to hear out all desires — even if it meant His own destruction. If Trifa wished for the liberation of both Rea and the children, He could not refuse.*
Reinhard: "Such are the laws governing this castle — I cannot refuse a request from a champion who paid the price I deemed equal for the feat. Go ahead: name your golden miracle. "
Trifa: "In that case..."

The fate of the whole world depended upon Trifa's choice. What miracle would Trifa — the former wicked saint and a breaker of shackles — desire from the Lord of the Dead?*
Trifa: "I beg of you, Lord Heydrich — talk to Isaak, if only once in your life."

Reinhard: "What do you mean?"
Trifa: "I meant what I said quite literally. What does Your Lordship think of his birth?"
Reinhard: "And what should I think?"
*Reinhard asked another question. The situation had now transcended the unusual and entered the realm of the outright abnormal.*
Trifa: "He is nothing to You. All those besides Yourself are but targets for Your destructive love. You have no interest in a person's identity, origins, and goals. "
Trifa: "As such, you gave little to no consideration to what I have told you. In fact, you hardly listened."
*Failing to comprehend the origins and target of his love drove the priest insane. Despite spelling it out to Reinhard, not a single word reached the Golden Beast's heart. For the Gold possessed no such thoughts at all. His soul transcended mankind, and was capable of engulfing the whole world in a monarch's equal love. His creed had been so indiscriminate that His very being refused to comprehend the notion of having someone special.*

Trifa: "I have overlooked something in the past. Back when the Divine Vessel had been first presented to me as an experiment, Your Lordship — whom we staged to be assassinated and even prepared a grave for — was vulnerable for just one moment."
*June of 1942.*
Trifa: "Isaak, who grew five times faster than a normal child, drew his first breath that day.  And it hardly needs pointing out that his mother was Lisa Brenner.  Did it dawn upon you now? It is the same date! "
Reinhard remained silent. Discerning what could have been going on in his mind — or even if the story itself was true — was impossible. One thing remained certain, however: that the priest wore an expression of triumph as he finally slipped into the other world. 
Trifa: "Your sheer magnificence causes You to overlook the most trifling of things. Isaak, and..."
*And what?*
Trifa: "So please, grant my wish. As long as you do, I will be able to go in peace.  I wish to be a martyr to my love of Theresia and the children. Being able to brag to Lisa in the afterlife that I offered the final embers of my life to fulfill my little girl's plans...   would be the epitome of bliss. "

*Valerian Trifa crumbled to dust, his remains dispersing in the air.*
Reinhard: "..."
*Silence fell upon the lonesome throne room. Reinhard stood up, walked to the place where the priest had perished, and kneeled down on one knee. He ran his fingers along the ground that, by now, had nothing but traces of dust remaining on it — even the blood was moments away from vanishing.*
Reinhard: "You aim to flee with your victory, priest? But I shan't let you escape."
They were inside Gladsheim Weltall — The Fifth Universe of Gold. It was the pantheon of those who had died in battle: a hell of infinite resurrections. As such, it would not have been impossible to revive Trifa here and now in order to make him finish his line. None who came back to life here as Einherjar could defy Reinhard. 
Reinhard: "Your speech has been most interesting. As such, promise to keep entertaining me until the end of times."

*The sombre knight and the crimson knightess manifested behind Reinhard as He raised his face. Schreiber: "Gib deine Hand, du schön und zart Gebild!"
*No consciousness remained in Schreiber's mind. His ego had long since crumbled — he was no more than an indiscriminate maelstrom of carnage now. And in the eye of that tornado — the most terrible of raging beasts — stood he, or rather, she.*
Marie: "...!!"
*Marie had sealed Ren's ego within his subconscious, and was now the one controlling his body. In a way, one could think of it as a malfunction of the Ahnenerbe, though it was nothing as simple or negative. She wished to protect him. She craved to save his soul. For the young man by the name of Ren Fujii had been an oddly irritating man. He held his tears when sad, remained steadfast when terrified — he was a paragon of endurance and mock bravado. He took everything on his shoulders, as if getting hurt and spilling blood was a part of his inborn duty.*

In that sense, Marie currently possessed both the ultimate resolve and the acute mentality for battle. She was able to synchronize with her master to the level where she could forcefully invoke his very craving.*

Ren's Creation Figment possessed the power to slow one's own time, resulting in incredible speed in the real world. To Marie's eyes, all existence appeared as if frozen in place. And yet...*

*So that was the essence of it. Wolfgang Schreiber evaded physical contact to an incomprehensible degree. His craving to never be touched and caught up to manifested in the form of ungodly speed. As such, his acceleration had no limits.*

Even Marie was unable to decapitate others without direct touch.*

Both possessed the power to accelerate without limits, yet one condition drew a lethal difference between the two. One could grow faster beyond any limit.The other could grow faster than anyone else. Even if Marie reached the speed of light, Schreiber would still be faster. For he would — in theory, at least — accelerate to always be one step ahead. Marie's own strength proved to be her undoing. It turned the ashen knight of madness into the most powerful existence there ever was.*

However, the number of times he hit Marie had left his own limbs in ruins, spurting blood in all angles.*
Schreiber: "Ich bin noch jung, geh, Lieber!"

Yet he was an Einherjar of Nibelheim — a champion of the fallen who discovered endless carnage beyond the precipice. His zeal refused to acknowledge the collapse of his world. It could contradict itself as many times as it wanted — he did not care.*
A devilish logic. Absolute, palpable insanity. Even if his own arms were to break while pulverizing his foes, Schreiber would not take notice. No lethal collapse would occur, as the beast did not realize he had been touched — and with that, the laws of the demonic magic would respond, healing his wounds at an ungodly speed. In short: the more he killed, the stronger he would become. His craving being the evasion of physical contact, Schreiber did not exactly possess a robust body. In exchange, however, all those he killed and devoured would serve as fuel for regeneration. Under these circumstances — his state of absolute, savage madness — the ashen knight was almost immortal. 
*His maddened bloodlust raged like a whirlwind. He was a tempest that transcended the very concept of speed. He was Hróðvitnir — the one who would devour heaven and earth alike in a single gulp. The more he killed, the stronger he became. In truth, he — having sown the seeds of destruction and regeneration in a seemingly infinite fashion — sheltered exactly 185,731 souls behind that eyepatch of his. His souls were a mix of warriors and powerless innocents, yet in terms of sheer numbers, he exceeded Eleonore and Machina threefold. His world record of murder would not be broken — not now, and not ever.*

Schreiber: "Gib deine Hand, du schön und zart Gebild!"

Eleonore: "Who do you take me for? I might not look it, but I'm a champion. I have lived through thousands of battles and seen tens of thousands of deaths. In essence, we differ in terms of sheer experience. You can be as fast as you want, or even invisible, but straightforward bloodlust will only ever make me yawn. You are too easy to read. This time, she would not let him dodge. Her speed should have transcended the very concepts of prediction and intuition. The blade of the guillotine crashed into the neck of its target with ungodly speed. Yet—*

Machina: "You lack conviction."

Marie: "Ah—"

Marie: "...!"

Marie: "Huh?!"

*Freshness was just one of the many values humanity applied to anything in existence. The most obvious and ubiquitous use of it was in temporal degradation of items relating to necessities of life, such as clothing, food and shelter. But what of ideological, conceptual and emotional freshness? Little thought was needed to realize that it was all in the lack of knowledge.*
*Reactions to the unknown ― surprise, excitement, or perhaps disgust... The myriads of vivid, humane emotions budding in the breast only by the virtue of the experiences being new... ...and the curiosity driving us to seek them. Beyond doubt, that was what elevated humanity from standard primates to the prime of the world. No matter how masterful the composition, how fragrant the wine, how delicious the gourmet meal, how attractive the person bedded, repeatedly indulging in any such pleasures for days on end eventually made one bored as the enthralling activities decayed and became part of the stagnation known as everyday life. Humanity had a formidable affinity for acclimation. Continuity of any action could make a person adapt to it to the extent where they moved not by excited will, but disinterested reflex. People saw no value in phenomena that lost their freshness.*
*With that in mind, what would become of a man to whom everything was foreknowledge? At first, he would likely struggle against it, trying all the different activities in locations just as varied. But upon realizing that foreknowledge was a wall too great for him to scale, he would choose to do nothing. His empty days would pass as if he was in hibernation, scarcely distinguishable from a warm cadaver. And at the apex of his despair, both silent and profound, he would arrive at the gates of madness. A single craving would come to dominate his mind.*
*A desire for the unknown ― a moment of freshness, vibrant and pure. As simplistic as it seemed, that was an optimal description of the man's life.*
*Standing on the twilight shore, still and alone, he considered many questions. How great was the distance he walked? How long was the time marching beside him? What was the oldest memory within him? Even in the days he spent at the ancient desert kingdom, pronouncing himself Djehuty and acting as the Scribe of The Gods, he could recall the disinterest and weariness already torturing him. What was happening before that? How far into his past would he have to delve to find his origin? He didn't have the faintest notion.*
*However, a long time ago, he formed a theory. He didn't know whether his existence traced back to the creator of humanity or the genesis of the cosmos, but he had little doubt that it was close. After all... His foreknowledge emanated and resulted in the world warping into something it shouldn't have been.*
*What came first? The chicken or the egg? He became aware of the concept of foreknowledge and began to yearn for the unknown... ...but that craving of his gave birth to nothing but more foreknowledge. His rule created a world sealed away in a Ghetto of torturous familiarity and made it emanate onto all of the cosmos. That was his theory for reality's design. It was reasonable assume he was akin to the roots of humanity, which brought him to another one of his theories. Specifically, the question of what would happen to the plant if its roots were cut off.*
*Despite never making any attempts to prolong his life, he waseverlasting ― the perpetually wandering Ahasver. As the creator of the rule governing this ever-enduring eternal recurrence, he couldn't die as long as it persisted. Even if it was possible to kill him, the act would surely be equal to the genocide of all humanity. As a rootless tree would fall, so would the cosmos crumble without him. Therefore...*
Mercurius: "I would have to create a being able to end me and have him destroy all that is... Or bring life to an existence able to transcend me and make my law void. I feel they are one and the same. Although I know not which of them is the unknown and which is foreknowledge, nor am I aware of what would become of me."
*It would be an overwriting ― the emanation of the new rule would alter foreknowledge. The man faintly chuckled as he restlessly walked the twilight shore. The moment they would fall here was inching ever closer. The curtains would rise for the Day of Wrath only when Destruction and Apotheosis descended upon this singularity.*
Mercurius: "This is likely to be the last time."
*The man muttered with no discernable emotion in his voice as Marguerite Breuilh silently sang at his side. Her voice was sweet and earnest ― far more moving and emotional than it was back when he lived as Cagliostro. The girl was undergoing rapid changes.*
Mercurius: "Does your heart belong to him, Marguerite?"
*A whisper too silent for her to hear, followed by a gentle smile. Clearly, it was time for him to teach his substitute the proper way to love her... ...for it was likely that the act would remove the lock.*

*She didn't believe that the impossible vision of his back was a mere illusion.*

Kei: "Ah..."

*She addressed the silent giant before her with a few hesitant words.*
Kei: "It was a dream of a certain possibility. One where I'm, well... more normal, I guess... I went to school, had friends, and even participated in club activities. Funny, right?  And then I thought that maybe that version of me could've actually been born somewhere... Beyond help, aren't I? It almost sounds like I'm about to give up. Although, I did think that it seemed like a lot of fun. After all... "

And the changes could be both fortunate and unfortunate. Thus, she couldn't help but think. Maybe — just maybe — she had a completely different life prepared for her. A possibility far too distant. An alternative road available only at a crossroad she chanced upon on a day long past.*
