*The giant gave no reply to Kei's soliloquy, nor was she expecting it. She simply wanted to engrave her feelings onto herself, ascertaining who she really was. So she wouldn't break. So she could still stand and fight.*

Trifa: "As you can clearly see, I am perfectly fine."

He said he was going to be a shield, and he was doing it splendidly: by taking all the blows, he allowed not a single one to stray into anyone else. I watched the onslaught as the numbness in my body began to fade. 
Shirou: "Hey, what kind of show is this?"

The slashes released so far amounted to more than fifty, and it seemed like the storm wouldn't stop even after a hundred more. It had only one target — the unarmed and defenseless priest. Cain's massacrous blade displayed raw determination to hit, damage, and kill him as many times as it took. All of the blows were meant to destroy the priest with utmost haste, and none of them were feints or fakes. No one caught up in that barrage could come out unharmed. And yet...*

If reason was at work, the target would have lost his original form and scattered into the wind like a cloud of dust...*

Cain was far above and beyond him at both physical power and movement speed. In terms of battle prowess — the ability to effectively slaughter anenemy — Valeria Trifa couldn't hold a candle to the cadaver. However, that was where the giant's superiority ended. *My Creation Figment.*

Trifa: "..."

*.*
*Father Trifa casually took Cain's blow and tilted his head to the side. The power in its offense was clearly greater than mine, which made for a great show of his endurance.*

*I had to increase my speed — to wring out my all and go faster than ever before.*

I'm fully willing to accept any punishment Lord Heydrich will bestow upon me. The true act of disloyalty would be letting you escape. What will you do now? You need her alive, don't you? "
*Eleonore shifted her gaze towards the one being that didn't seem to belong there.*
Eleonore: "I saw through your plot. This one's the twin's descendant.  What was his name, again? "
Machina: "Johann."
*Rubedo and Nigredo detailed the situation as Trifa stood silent, not even trying to hide any of it.*
Eleonore: "Yes, Johann. I had never thought that he survived. It's so much like Brenner to let him live, and it's so much like you to design this scheme. Although, while she was just foolish, you are downright filthy. Nonetheless, this girl is truly pitiable. "
Eleonore: "I feel like letting her die here and now — while she's still oblivious to all of this — would be an act of mercy. Well, that aside... "
*With a cold grin and a light chuckle, Eleonore turned around, as if to display that she didn't even need to see what happened next.*
Eleonore: "Checkmate, Kristoff. Your pilgrimage ends here."
*Just then, the sombre knight launched another metallic strike towards the priest.*
Trifa: "Ghh, ah..."
*He didn't dodge — or, rather, he couldn't. Considering he was facing two veteran Battalion Commanders, one might say this was all too obvious. By dodging the first blow, the priest got into a position they found desirable. Then, while Eleonore sealed his ability to escape and conversed with him, Machina perfected the distance between them. Everything was planned. Now, Kasumi Ayase was on the same straight line as Trifa and Machina. Had the priest dodged the attack, she would have surely died, so he could do nothing but accept it. The results of the blow were palpable.*

*He pulled back the fist he had launched, displaying the kind of placidity that seemed to imply a complete lack of worry about any counterattacks. His defenselessness was on a completely different dimension compared to Trifa's. While the priest didn't protect himself due to absolute certainty of his endurance, the sombre knight had unshakeable confidence in his attack power.*
Machina: "You're more dependent on him than anyone else."

Rea: "Ah..."
*Trifa was being pummeled into his demise, unable to do anything to stop it. The sight made Rea subconsciously reach out towards him. Alas, he was too far. She was just as powerless as the priest himself. Though Rea was the one who sparked this event, its flow was completely out of her hands. She was confused about what she should do. The girl simply didn't know how to feel about that priest.*
*One blow after the other, the iron Nigredo continued punching Trifa. Every hit seemed to shave something away from him — make him break, shatter, and gradually disappear. It was over for him. The priest would be defeated and perish. Even with her untrained eyes, she could still easily predict the outcome of their battle. However...*
Rea: "Why...?"
*She couldn't help but voice the exact same question she had asked herself countless times before. Why was he so keen on keeping her alive?*
*A woman this wicked. A girl this dangerous. Choosing to kill her would be far more reasonable, and that was exactly what she thought he was trying to do just a moment ago. But...*
Trifa: "Kh, uohhh!"
*With an unbefitting, serious expression on his face — all the while voicing groans of genuine desperation — he forced himself to stand strong and brave as he faced an undefeatable foe. Was it for her sake? Was it her fault? Did she do anything for him that would warrant such a fervent struggle? She didn't understand him. The girl just couldn't guess what the priest was thinking. And yet, even after witnessing his sacrificial devotion, Rea couldn't help but be scared of him.*
*Did that make her a lowlife? A pile of human filth? Or perhaps something entirely detached from humanity? What did Valeria Trifa mean to Rea Himuro, and what did the Sonnenkind mean to Kristoff?*

*Eleonore spoke up as if to prevent Rea from reaching towards him again. With her back turned to the heated battle, the woman came to stand right next to the girl.*

Anti-magic, anti-physical, anti-time, anti-accident... He gained a perpetual shield that strengthened such defenses to the utmost limit. And the other secret is his armor... "
*Eleonore revealed the Divine Vessel's greatest mysteries in a completely nonchalant manner, like it was the most obvious thing in the world. As she listened, Rea nearly fainted. A perfectly reasonable reaction, considering that...*

*They were about to break the barrier which had been sealing Reinhard's castle — his Creation Figment — for over sixty years. The results of such an act were no doubt evident even to the slowest thinker. The otherworld that perpetually expanded within the unbreakable vessel was about to be released. The event would be akin to the burst of a balloon filled with the amount of water held back by a dam.*
Eleonore: "When the shield is gone, no one will be able to stop the castle's emanation. Without the levee, the Legions of Valhalla would pour out. Although, as things are now, it would only be a Creation that's only edging on Emanation. Nonetheless, the acting commander will then be relieved of his post. We're done with this worm, so let him melt into the seventh Swastika. Do you see, Theresia? The inexplicable sentiments you harbor for him are... "

Rea: "Stop!"
*Rea raised her voice to stop the woman's words. It was an action completely opposed to her intentions, as she actually wanted — and had to — know the truth behind it. However, it was too hard for her to accept the answer she began to see. Even if she could untangle the complex feelings she had been wrestling with all this time, it was already far too late... Was she worried about Father Trifa? Or did she fear him? Was she worried about the Divine Vessel of Gold? Or did she fear him?*
*Sixty years ago, Valeria Trifa had a completely different appearance. After all, his body wasn't the one he had now. The source of her swaying feelings was the fear her grandfather felt towards the one he believed to be his father. She inherited it through her very soul. Rea was bound by that fear, and led the priest to his place of execution while being completely unaware of who he really was. In an attempt to protect Fujii, she accidentally pressed the switch to the release of ultimate despair. Was there anything she could do to make up for it? Rea didn't see how she could turn back now.*
*She thought herself a fool... ...and a thoughtless little girl. She had always known that Karl Krafft's Ars Magna wasn't weak enough to be ruined by someone as meager as her.  She knew it well, yet she still brought about such a harrowing predicament. If they let her, she would've killed herself right then and there.*
Eleonore: "This won't be the last time you feel suicidal. Or perhaps you'll become attached to life, instead? I care not either way."
*Memento mori. Eleonore uttered the curse and silently chuckled to herself before going on in a business-like manner, as if to proclaim that she was done with the girl.*
Eleonore: "The climax will be the opening of the eighth. Make sure to amass as much of it as you can, Theresia. That prayer of yours will assist in repainting the world with Gladsheim's colors."
Eleonore: "Also, I'm sure I don't have to say this, but that girl over there is your blood relative — the grandaughter of Isaak's failure of a younger brother, who was believed to be dead. Kristoff planned to use her to disrupt the pentachroma. It would prevent the emanation of the castle while still allowing him to steal the immortality — that is, the endless restorative abilities — of the Gold. What a truly wretched way of thinking. Don't you agree? There's no need for you to worry about him. That man is a genuine scumbag, not worthy of a single tear. "
*Upon saying that, Eleonore shifted her gaze from Rea and instantly changed her attitude.*
Eleonore: "Now tell me, cur. Why are you staring at me like that?"
Kei: "..."
*She then addressed another person in a condescending manner — Sakurai Kei, who was splendidly ignored by everyone present.*
Eleonore: "I've seen you at the edge of my vision several times now, dancing more pitifully than a tamed monkey. Are you asking for a punishment? I'm in a good mood right now, so I don't mind. Name yourself, whelp. What drives you to make such a mockery of my subordinate? "
Eleonore: "What motivates you to sit in Kircheisen's seat and act so disgraceful?"
*There wasn't a hint of anger in her tone. She looked down on Kei so much that she didn't even deem her worthy of her rage. People who got angry at animals were rare, so why would Eleonore get mad at someone she likened to a monkey? However, the woman had no intention of tolerating the girl's savageness. Her eyes were freezing cold — a perfect show of her intention to not grace Kei with a hint of warmth.*
Kei: "I..."
*While being practically bound in place by the chills running across her entire body, Kei spoke up in a trembling voice.*
Kei: "Kei Sakurai. First Lieutenant Beatrice Kircheisen's successor since eleven years ago..."
Eleonore: "So it was Kristoff."
Eleonore: "I see. So that's why you're so pitiful. A puppet, and part of the cursed bloodline. Now, what should I do with you...?"
*The priest's predicament continued even as they talked. Not only was Trifa incompatible with Machina, but he also had nearly none of the battle prowess of the sombre knight. It was a one-sided battle that wouldn't last longer than a few more minutes. Completely certain of Trifa's impending doom, Eleonore began to see him as a dead man. After all...*
Eleonore: "After the emanation of Valhalla, that one brat will have to become a badge of honor on either Machina or our Lord. Thus, the sacrifice to the eighth will have to be someone other than him."
*...the woman looked down at Kei, talking about how they would open the final Swastika. If Ren was dedicated to either her lord or kamerad, what would be the appetizer? At the moment, they had three potential candidates for the role.*
Eleonore: "It's unsightly when the numbers don't match. However, the boy that killed Malleus is Schreiber's prey, and I expect no calculated plotting from his muders. I have no way of knowing when, where, and how he plans to kill the boy, so it's best to simply exclude him.Tell me, you cur. What do you think we should do with the other two? "

Kei: "So, Lady Samiel, what you are saying is..."
*The woman's words and mannerisms were far too blatant for Kei not to understand their implications. After all, Eleonore presented it as if she was talking to a monkey. Kei certainly considered herself stupid, but even she could comprehend the crimson knightess' words to a nauseating extent. The girl muttered with a creaking voice.*
Kei: "...that I should die here?"
Eleonore: "Either you, or that thing."
*The pallid mask was still violently shaking as Kei held it close to her heart... ...and Tubal Cain was still sealed within.*

*After an ominous pause, Eleonore's eyes flashed with a wicked glint. Kei's entire body shuddered when, suddenly, a crimson flower bloomed before her.*
Eleonore: "...did you actually believe you would survive until the eighth?"

I might even decide to keep you around as a pet or a jester. "

Their battle was akin to the clash of a thousand against several tens of thousands. Facing her would be a fool's errand, and the situation allowed for no means of escape.*
*So what could she do now? What could she choose and believe in? She lived through hell while harboring the desire to survive until she gained the grace of Gold through the opening of the eighth Swastika. But alas, that dream was now on the brink of collapse. More importantly...*

And so, one of the already-graced was standing before her now: Eleonore, a monster of a woman commanding a hellish army, speaking of reason far too detached from sanity. Immortal, indestructible, and perpetually resurrecting demons of war; eternal slaves to strife. Kei was being coerced into accepting something like that. 
Kei: "I can't. I fail to see it the way you do."
*She tightly embraced the mask within her hands. Lisa Brenner's Ahnenerbe was already breaking, and the added pressure seemed almost to hasten it.*

Kei: "This wouldn't be the least bit different. In the end, we're still..."

Kei: "This isn't what I've been fighting for all this time!"
*She sought paradise on the fields of slaughter, and searched for peace at the end of gory rivers of blood. A dream so convenient and egoistic that anyone would look down on her for following it. Kei knew full well that the people she had killed would never find peace after meeting such an end. She knew it, yet couldn't bring herself to care. Hers was a dream too dear to be hindered by conscience and morals, and she saw nothing wrong with that.*

The craving of the origin of life is greatness and abundance. If you don't want a blaze to fade, you must make it larger. And if you wish to relight a faded flame, you must lead it to a greater fire. In other words... "

To fight Eleonore, who had the upper hand due to the distance between them, Kei had to attack fast — before the woman had a chance to shoot her. At the very least, the girl had to act before Rubedo got a chance to release her flames.*

Eleonore: "You fool. Come at me again, greenhorn."
Kei: "..."

The blow Kei received wasn't powerful enough to leave her with a critical injury, but it distanced her from Cain. That harsh reality, as well as Eleonore's words from earlier made the woman's intentions clear.*
*Rubedo was going to evaporate Cain and leave the girl alive to have her become the sacrifice to the eighth.*
Kei: "No..."
*No. Don't go. Don't leave me. Would her own powerlessness make Kei lose someone dear to her again? Kei fought so hard to overturn the burdening past, only to be met with the very same conclusion. There was no way the girl could tolerate it.*
Eleonore: "No need for grief. I'm here to bring you salvation.I'll purify that rotten vessel and release you, foolish little Brünhild. Join me — we shall ride together till the very twilight of time. Heheh, hehehahah, hahahahahahahahahahah! "
*Her laugh, tinted with joy, grew in proportion to the ever-expanding flames. Eleonore wasn't even looking at Kei. She stared intently at the giant corpus of the charging cadaver, her gaze harboring unmistakable affection. However, the love of Einherjars — immortal champion of the fallen — was...*
Eleonore: "Let us meet in Valhalla, my dear subordinate. It fills me with supreme bliss to have the joy of ending this life of yours."
Eleonore: "[ein bräutliches Feuer soll dir nun brennen,](I'll present you with the most fervorous of flames,)[wie nie einer Braut es gebrannt!](no bride shall ever be your equal!) [Wer meines Speeres Spitze furchtet, durchschreite das feuer nie!](For he who fears the tip of my lance shall never pass through the river of flames!) "
*Suddenly, she snapped her fingers. Auf Wiedersehen, Thrud Walküre Kircheisen. That marked her final goodbye.*

Wilhelm: "Well, yeah. Nothing and no one — I don't see a single change."

Both the peerless supremacy that exceeded his by a margin, and the nether realm summoned by its power — they all remained at heights he could never aspire to reach. They were there for him. The same applied to the Battalion of Three as well. Neither Machina, nor Samiel, nor Schreiber had changed in the slightest. All and everyone had been trapped within endless battlefields, connected to each other, their bodies and souls assembling the framework of Hell.*
Wilhelm: "Samiel kept blabbering on about glory or whatever, and now you have me wondering: maybe I do have some of it myself."
Wilhelm: "After all, I'm in the presence of the one and only Gold. Can't exactly escape the all-illuminating radiance now."
Reinhard: "Indeed, First Lieutenant. You have already proven yourself worthy of my grace. However, does my blessing's true nature not upset you in the slightest?"
Wilhelm: "Hah! You kiddin' me?"
*He snorted, denying the accusation with a barely contained laugh. The very notion was ludicrous. Others might have had their issues with the truth, but that was an incredibly silly question to ask someone like him.*
Wilhelm: "Don't group me together with those yellow suckers, Lord Heydrich. I'm not like them. The right to become a Fang of the Beast is the greatest reward there is. Those that treat it as a curse are spineless fools terrified by the graves they themselves dug.  The idiots have no idea what they're missing out on. What could be greater than warring for an eternity? Yours is the only true Valhalla. "
*He didn't doubt for a second that he had been blessed. He spoke like a true villain, his eyes pregnant with fervor and bloodlust. Those words were the proof of his fealty, foretelling his boundless desire to ride the waves of endless strife. However—*
Reinhard: "Then tell me, Bey. What is it that you covet?"
*His golden pair of eyes saw through the shrewdly-veiled discontent right away.*
Reinhard: "You are a phoenix risen from midnight's ashes. You've lived true to your desires, sucking blood as one inhales air.  As such, my blessing to you is not a curse, but a favor — your most coveted reward. And that is fine. There is nothing grander than to seek fulfillment. As another man who had spent ages in search of a spark capable of igniting my soul, I understand your feelings very well. And that is also why I'm puzzled. "
Reinhard: "You proclaimed yourself fulfilled. And I can very clearly see that to be true. Why is it, then, that I still feel you close to myself, as a kindred in starvation? The more fulfilled you are, the more you crave for. You hunger as you feed. You contradict yourself, Bey. I didn't take you for a man with a penchant for concealment. If the void in your heart had truly been without bounds, you would have never sworn loyalty to me. "
*Wilhelm would have had no reason to serve the Gold if his true desire had been outside the realms of His power. And he was a man who would rather see the world burn than be sneaky and conceal his passions.*
Reinhard: "As such, your joy is that of anticipation. You have not yet been fulfilled, but instead have discovered a way to soothe your hunger. A way to transcend Karl's prophecy — the curse engraved upon your very soul.  "
Wilhelm: "Khh— Hehahh!"
*Wilhelm affirmed Reinhard's words with a chortle he failed to contain. He never supposed it was possible to hide anything from his lord, anyway. As such, he instead chose to savor the joy of being understood so thoroughly, and put his true wish into words.*
Wilhelm: "Yes, as your Lordship says, there is a small suggestion I would like to make.  My instincts told me what was going on, but the answer was so obvious it ultimately made me hesitate and I ended up losing my chance up until this day. "
*For such was the fickle nature of fate. The stench was so strong it blocked his nose, and he missed what had been going in front of his very eyes.*
Reinhard: "In other words, you had suspected it all along."
Wilhelm: "That's right. Guess you could call him a constant thorn in my side."
*Their beginning was odd and had no end. They never reached a final point. As such, regardless of how much he struggled, he could only ever keep going in circles. That was exactly why Wilhelm would never be graced with a proper conclusion, no matter what he did. All things he reached out to claim for his own would slip through his fingers. As such, he had to put an end to the very first of such occurrences. One that had been denied to him for over sixty years. All he needed now was permission.*
Wilhelm: "What would you say to granting me the seat of Albedo if I managed to exterminate him?"
Reinhard: "Well, well..."
*The two golden eyes narrowed in amusement as they bore into Wilhelm, despite the Beast already knowing all there was to know about the ivory Lieutenant.*
Reinhard: "Fighting Schreiber is your wish, then?"
Wilhelm: "I'm just sayin' a mad beast has no place masquerading as a knight. He is no longer worthy... Nah, the role was too heavy for him to bear from the get-go. It was a mistake to knight him. "
*Wilhelm almost chuckled at the superficiality and emptiness of his excuses. Both of them knew the truth, yet continued the farce nonetheless, smiling.*
*After all, the following bout would be one that decided the composition of the Round Table — he needed an official concession from their Lord. As such, he had to become a gallant warrior worthy of the saga of the ages.*
Wilhelm: "And, well... everyone acknowledges the freak's power, and I'm no exception. The question is whether or not he's worthy of his name. It might have been good as a leash to control the monster, but what point is there to dress up and embellish a mindless beast? "
Reinhard: "I see."
Reinhard: "But as you have said, Schreiber is a monster without peer.A Vanargand through and through. No one can subdue him."
Wilhelm: "Then I will become the first to do so. All the others have failed because it's my fate to tame him, and I was robbed of my chance once before. Surely you still remember, Lord Heydrich."
*For He was the very reason why a bout between beast and vampire was left perpetually unfinished.*
Reinhard: "Yes, hahaha... I remember, of course. You claim it was partially my fault?"
Wilhelm: "Yes. Which means—"
*For a heartbeat, the ivory demon failed to contain himself, his countenance lighting up with palpable madness.*
Wilhelm: "Defeating Schreiber might finally grant me fulfillment."
*Wilhelm's true wish and craving rose up his throat like twin snakes guiding each other's way, unveiling themselves in all their glory. It was the first time he had called his nemesis by name.*
Wilhelm: "And my success would also mean that I transcended the words of Mercurius."
Reinhard: "With that, you would become the spearhead of the Obsidian Table, the sole champion who managed to rescind Karl's prophecy — the glorious Albedo."
*That meant the destruction of one's inborn creed. Each member of the Obsidian Table was trapped by Karl Krafft's duality of blessing and curse in one, for the Mercury magician unveiled both the strengths and weaknesses of their fates. There was not a single exception to this rule. Not even Reinhard Heydrich could escape its shackles.*
*For that very thing proved to be His greatest dilemma. To rid oneself of karma's chains was indeed the greatest, most coveted wall for all Einherjar.*
Wilhelm: "I might even be able to show You the way. What do You say?"
*An outrageous claim. Delusional, even. He pleaded for his master's permission with a haughty smile and eyes glistening with madness. And indeed, his insane proposition was met by an answer similarly existing beyond the fringes of reason.*
Reinhard: "As you wish. I shall look forward to your tutelage. Consider your proposition accepted. After all, it is my duty as commander to soothe the hearts of my troops. Fight for your prize and claim it as your own. I look forward to an entertaining battle, Bey. "
Wilhelm: "Jawohl, mein Herr."
*Wilhelm rose to his feet and left the throne room, his heart racing impatiently in his chest, his very being trembling with joy. He would soon fill the void in his soul, becoming a rose to rob the whole cosmos of its vitae. A white rose that remained forever pallid in the moonlight, regardless of how much crimson it ingested.*
Wilhelm: "How about you? Do any of you have a problem?"
*Wilhelm addressed Rubedo and Nigredo, who had both been standing by outside the throne room.*
Wilhelm: "If ya don't, I'll be on my way."
Eleonore: "I have no objections. It is Lord Heydrich's command."
Machina: "..."
*The Einherjar of Valhalla had pride in their names, but none possessed a soul petty enough to be intimidated by new additions to their ranks. If anything, they welcomed new souls to join them in their journey of endless strife and bloodshed — provided they truly possessed the strength and will to become one.*
Wilhelm: "I see."
*As such, no concern was necessary. Those worthy would survive, and those not would simply perish. There was nothing more to it. And Wilhelm certainly didn't need any extra information on Schreiber. As fantastic as it was, the two had already lived as inhuman beasts long before they ever met the Obsidian Table. Consequently, it was easy to foretell that they would share a certain link, both being monsters born only to wreak havoc. In truth, no one in the Order understood better the true power and danger of the ashen knight than Wilhelm.*
Eleonore: "I shall look forward to your bout, Bey. I do not hate you as much as you might think. Your battle shall prove to be the signal flare for the emanation of our Valhalla. May it wake all those slumbering in indolence, showing them what true war is like. Regardless of who ultimately proves to be the victor. "
Wilhelm: "You want to see a good dance? Sure. No need to tell me twice."
*Wilhelm grinned at Eleonore as she puffed on the cigar between her lips.*
Wilhelm: "But what's up with all this meekness all of a sudden, Samiel? Did killin' Babylon get to ya?"
Eleonore: "As if. It's none of your business."
*She answered with a faint smile that made it impossible to discern her true feelings. And there was certainly no one present who would attempt to pry further.*
Eleonore: "I kept the comrades we've left behind in the corner of my mind. And you are no exception, Bey."
Eleonore: "I have to admit, it has grown lonesome here with everyone gone. As such, I hope at least one of you can prove to be a champion. Elsewise, Lord Heydrich will be gravely disappointed. Don't count me as your ally, but I genuinely wish you luck in battle. "
Wilhelm: "Ain't that an honor."
*In truth, Eleonore had been quite curious about the upcoming battle. After all, she too participated in their initial — and interrupted — bout.*
Eleonore: "With Kircheisen gone, I shan't interfere, either. No one will get in your way this time, so feel free to run wild."
Wilhelm: "Yeah, you can marvel at us from your premium seat. I'm sure the long overdue conclusion of that day should entertain you."
*And as Wilhelm was about to pass the two—*
Machina: "Bey—  Fulfill your ambition. You shall mark the beginning. "
*The sombre knight who wished — more than anyone — to be liberated from his accursed fate addressed the ivory demon, his words ringing more like a solemn oath than regular speech.*
*You have one chance to rid yourself of this curse. Do not squander it. The man to whom such a chance had been perpetually denied swore to make it his own if it ever came within his reach. Wilhelm's grin broadened as he stepped ahead, not caring to turn back and face the other two. This was most definitely a place for him. He could not let it be wasted on a lunatic.*
Wilhelm: "That's right, Machina. You're completely right."
*The time was nigh to sever the shackles of his curse.*
*No matter the circumstances, no matter the time — he was denied everything. All that he genuinely wished for would drift away. A nightmarish fate befitting a miserable clown. An absolute law forged of malice — an incessantly recurring sham. Therein lay the cause for that which consumed the flames of his soul. To put it simply, he had a certain beginning that had yet to come to an end. And nothing in his life could change as long as it remained unfinished — he would keep losing everything for an eternity.*
*With an unending beginning, there was no place for anything else to start. A most elementary reasoning. As such—*
Wilhelm: "Kheh... Haha! Aren't you glad, Schreiber?! We're gonna signal the beginning of the end!"
*This was their creed. And who was the first to have been subjugated by and sworn loyalty to Reinhard Heydrich? Each would claim to have been the first, yet only one had the right to proclaim it as an absolute truth. Whoever did that would be Albedo, one of the supporting pillars of the Gold.*
*A white silhouette danced through the night air as the gates of the devil's castle opened. A single beam of white pierced the sky like a bullet without making as much as a sound— It soared towards the conclusion — the end — that it had once been robbed of. After sixty long years of an interlude, the bout that commemorated the initiation of the Obsidian Round Table would now resume in earnest.*
*Apparently, it took me two days to regain consciousness after the events in the castle.*
*I closed the windows, then covered them with curtains to escape the sight of that messed up sky.*
*I didn't want to see my world changed in that way. The mere sight of that dread robbed me of energy. And that was pretty much all I'd been doing since waking up.*
*I knew this place wasn't safe. The whole city had turned into an empty ruin, like some ghost town from a cheap movie.*
*That... That was what had become of our home.*
*And I could do nothing to stop it.*
*The hole on the wall — the window that connected my room to Kasumi's — felt oddly surreal and distant. To an extent, I felt like she might pop her head out of it if I knocked on the wall.*
Ren: "..."
Rea: "..."
*Himuro sat down on the bed, avoiding my eyes.*
*We had already told each other everything that had been on our minds. With no more words left to be exchanged, we remained at each other's side, silent and unmoving like sculptures of wood. Our faint breathing was all that could be heard in the room.*
*We were like moping children, our weathered bodies crushed under the strain of our own powerlessness, as well as the path we chose to take.*
*Marie...*
*No one answered my call. She must have been among us, but before I knew it, I stopped feeling her presence in my right arm.*
*Was she also wallowing in sorrow? Or did she truly vanish somewhere? I couldn't even tell that much in my current state.*
*I knew she had been blaming herself, regretting her decisions. And it hadn't been that long since her heart was born. I couldn't help rechecking the weight of my hand each time the thought crossed my mind.*
*I prayed to the instrument of execution dwelling within my arm. I earnestly pleaded her not to leave me.*
*So please, Marie. You're one of the last of people I hold dear. One of the last people I swore to protect.*
*As I was so busy having semi-monologues in my mind—*
Rea: "Listen."
*Himuro suddenly interrupted me.*
Rea: "Were you thinking of another girl just now?"
Ren: "Huh? Ah... That's not..."
*You could say she hit the nail on the head, preventing me from coming up with an articulate reply right away.*
Rea: "Right on the mark, huh. Well, whatever."
Rea: "It's that one I met the other day, right?"
Ren: "That's... Yeah."
*Himuro met Marie back in the club. She did mention something along the lines of Marie explaining everything to her, but I couldn't tell for certain exactly how much that meant, or how she currently perceived Marie.*
Rea: "Oh, you don't need to explain. I'm not gonna pry into your personal life. Besides, I was curious about her, too."
Ren: "Curious about what?"
Rea: "You feel responsible, don't you? I figured you were explaining things to her, coming up with excuses and all."
Rea: "And so I couldn't help but wonder exactly what you told her."
Ren: "..."
Rea: "Why are you looking at me like that?"
*I felt like she had been misunderstanding something.*
Ren: "I've made no excuses. I don't have any."
*The last time I had the chance to speak with Marie was still in the castle. Ever since I woke up, she hadn't been respoding to my attempts of calling her.*
Rea: "I see. That sucks, I guess."
*Himuro looked away as I told her the honest, embarrassing truth.*
Rea: "I'm not one to psychoanalyze others, but don’t you think she's kinda precarious? Like, it feels like she could get smeared in any color. You have to be very careful with how you treat her, Fujii."
Ren: "..."
Rea: "Did that ring a bell?"
*It did. A whole orchestra of bells. I'd been postponing this issue for the longest time, but Marie changed completely the day I met Reinhard at the church.*
*She started laughing, getting angry, and even crying like a normal girl. I didn't give it much attention since I figured her growing more human-like was a good sign, but in retrospect, that might have been a grave mistake on my part.*
Ren: "Yeah, it's like you said. I feel she gets influenced by my feelings quite a bit."
Ren: "Now that I think about it, every time Marie said something emotional, I would be pretty worked up myself."
Rea: "Isn't that just another way of saying that you two complement each other well?"
Ren: "Well, I can't completely deny that, but your observation was spot-on. There's definitely something precarious about her."
*Marie became extremely agitated when I lost myself in rage back in the castle. Almost like our emotions were synchronized.*
*And look where that got us. I might have received incredible power, but completely lost my senses and even ended up physically altered. I couldn't quite say that in front of Himuro, but I felt as if I had overwritten Marie with that dreadful thing.*
*With my own craving...*
*As such, rather than coming up with meaningless excuses, I should have first tried to get to know her better. I certainly couldn't say I did a particularly good job on that front so far.*
Ren: "I caused her plenty of trouble... so I wish I could do something in return."
Rea: "Is that so. You know, you seem busy guilt-tripping and all, but I get the feeling she's doing the exact same thing on her end."
Ren: "Huh?"
Rea: "I'm just saying it's a bit too hasty to assume the reason she doesn't come out is because she hates your guts now. Rather, she might very well be the one lacking the guts to face you."
Rea: "At least I got those kinda vibes from her."
Ren: "..."
*She had a point. I was definitely going through a lot on my end, but who says Marie would be any different?*
*Still, there was no fixing that unless I managed to make her come out somehow.*
Rea: "..."
*I already knew simply calling out to her wouldn't work, and I didn't have time to expose myself to the kind of the danger that would force her to appear.*
*Our situation was hardly what I could call rosy. Still, I wondered how the bastards were planning to open the seventh and eighth Swastikas with no more people left in town. Didn't they basically force themselves into the corner, putting us into an indefinite stalemate as long as I made no moves?*
Rea: "..."
*But wait, they did summon their castle themselves. Even those psychos wouldn't be braindead enough to screw themselves over that bad.*
*In that case, what would be the best course of action for me?*
Rea: "..."
*What should I prioritize most of all right now?*
Rea: "Ahem."
*An abrupt cough interrupted my thoughts.*
Rea: "Being serious is well and good, but how about we lighten the mood with a merrier conversation?"
Ren: "I-I can't just come up with a merry topic out of nowhere."
Rea: "For example, roughly how many bears are born and die in Kumamoto."
Ren: "..."
Rea: "Or who was the wise guy that first thought of injecting silly bear puns into the dialogue of humanized bear characters."
Rea: "Or what would happen if we pit you against a bear in a one-on-one fight."
*The last one didn't sound very merry to me.*
Ren: "Himuro. Do you happen to have some kinda grudge against Kumamoto?"
Rea: "Nope. Not at all."
*Her reply felt oddly unnatural.*
*Himuro broke our gaze, looking away from me with a hint of irritation.*
Ren: "Um... Did I do something?"
Rea: "No."
*Her behavior hinted at the opposite, though.*
Rea: "You aren't doing anything. And that's pissing me off a little, that's all."
Ren: "Huh...?"
Rea: "You aren't doing anything to me."
Ren: "..."
*I suppose I wasn't?*
Rea: "Maybe it's just me, but I feel like we exchanged quite a few provocative lines and did quite a few dramatic things before coming to this point."
Rea: "I suppose it wasn't that big of a deal from your perspective? Seems you have other girls in your barnyard anyway, and you'd rather think about them than pay attention to me."
Rea: "You're a marriage fraudster, aren't you?"
Ren: "I..."
*I didn't remember saying anything about marriage, though.*
Ren: "I just didn't know what I should talk about."
*She was right in that we said all sorts of things to each other without ever acting upon them. I was half unconscious at the time, but I could still vaguely recall everything.*
*When I had to deal with these things head-on, I'd feel embarrassed and tense up. I just couldn't help it.*
Rea: "And that's why we should talk about something fun."
*She made a faint smile and clasped my hand.*
Rea: "We are prone to losing ourselves in serious or depressing thoughts."
Rea: "You end up wanting to shoulder everything on your own. I turn tail and run."
Rea: "I told you that was a bad habit of ours. Remember?"
*I gave her a silent nod. There was no way I could forget.*
Rea: "This might sound odd coming from me, but I don't think we have too good of a chemistry. We need someone to mediate things between us, or we're no good."
Rea: "Like Yusa, Ayase, and that girl... What was her name, again?"
Ren: "Marie."
Rea: "Like Marie. Without anyone like that, we're basically a suicide squad."
Ren: "Shirou would feel right at home in a squad like that, I think..."
Rea: "Yeah, he does have that vibe about him. But he still lightens the mood when he's around."
Ren: "Lightens? I believe 'ruins' is the word you're loo—"
Rea: "Anyway."
*She squeezed my hand, indicating she wanted me to listen closely for a change.*
Rea: "Let's try being optimistic today. Happy-go-lucky and all that jazz."
*The reality of their situation was entirely too depressing to face head-on. I felt that was the idea underlying her words.*
Rea: "So I'm putting a ban on all things serious and depressing. Might help prevent our bad habits from coming to the surface."
Ren: "I wonder how effective that will be."
*She ignored my wry comment, and continued in a merry tone.*
Rea: "Do you love me, Fujii?"
*That came so out of nowhere it left my mind a complete blank.*
Rea: "I love you, by the way."
*But she went on without a hint of hesitation.*
*Almost as if driven by a kind of impatience.*
Rea: "Lisa is my great-grandmother. Isaak is my grandfather."
Rea: "So I told Lisa that I loved you. She said it scared her."
Ren: "Scared her?"
*Why was that? Her blood relations no longer surprised me, but Sister Lisa's assessment left me puzzled.*
Ren: "Scared of what?"
Rea: "I couldn't properly explain the reason why I fell in love with you."
Ren: "But that's..."
*I wondered how many lovers or married couples could do that. If anything, I felt that those that were too fast to attach explanations and reasoning to their feelings were kind of fishy.*
Rea: "She was scared of some magical force of attraction, apparently. To tell the truth, it scares even me a little."
Ren: "Why?"
*My initial bashfulness had been dispelled by indignation at having our honest feelings denounced for some unintelligible reason.*
*I supposed that meant I was happy she felt that way about me. No point trying to act cool here.*
Ren: "I love you too, Himuro."
*Though it was still incredibly embarrassing.*
Ren: "Um, was there some problem with that, too?"
*Himuro made a slightly troubled face, then peered straight into the eyes.*
Rea: "Isaak, you see, is a blondie with golden eyes."
Ren: "...?"
Rea: "Lisa said she was scared of Isaak because he grew up to resemble his father too much."
Rea: "What do you think that means?"
Ren: "No way..."
*That was hardly a riddle.*
*It stemmed solely from circumstantial evidence, but given our situation, there was only one answer.*
Rea: "That's the kind of blood coursing through my veins."
Rea: "And you..."
*Mercurius. Karl Krafft. The two leaders of the Obsidian Table were amiable friends.*
Rea: "Starting to get the jitters now?"
Rea: "I still wasn't sure if you'd say you love me though. I was really scared to ask, but somehow mustered to do it anyway."
*Himuro's shoulders trembled as she spoke.*
Rea: "Well, I'm basically like a landmine. I can't imagine a worse background than mine, so you'd honestly have to be crazy to want to get involved with someone like me."
Rea: "I get creeped out when I think about it myself. Lisa would, too. So I think I could endure you getting cold feet right about now....Yep, I think I could."
*Yet she ended up going on an uncharacteristically long tangent in order to mask her fear. I had no idea why she thought that would help her hide it, but I supposed that behavior was also a part of what made Rea Himuro the girl she was.*
Rea: "And we don't really have proof, either. I mean, I doubt there's anyone man enough to go and ask that guy for a DNA test."
*A girl I loved.*
Rea: "Ah, darn it... here I go, trying to book a flight to frown town again. Anyway, let's drop that subject and talk about Kumamoto instead."
*You don't need to panic with such a flustered face.*
Rea: "Um... bears... bears... ah, did you know that bear curry was actually a thing?"
Ren: "That's Hokkaido."
*I seized her shoulders.*
Rea: "...!"
Ren: "Your bad habit's struck again."
*She'd start all gung-ho and confident, but would turn and flee the moment things failed to go her way. I didn't think that would be enough to alleviate her worries, but if she wished for a casual conversation, all I could do was comply.*
Ren: "Don't change the subject before I even get the chance to open my mouth."
*Apparently, our chemistry was not the best?*
*It wasn't like we'd start quarreling at the sight of each other, but our thoughts tended to take a dark turn when we were together. Or so she said.*
*As such, I had to advance casually, and avoid putting any needless weight into my words... That was the kind of relationship she wished for, and I agreed.*
*So...*
Ren: "You called yourself a landmine..."
Ren: "And claimed your background to be the worst in existence..."
*But didn't that make her...*
Ren: "Isn't that like totally a damsel in distress kind of affair? From where I'm standing, you've got all bases covered."
Rea: "..."
*Himuro's eyes widened, gazing at me in stupor.*
Ren: "Not to mention your birthday is on Christmas, which is in a few days to boot."
Ren: "That's pretty incredible, you know. I don't know how many worlds one would have to turn upside down to find another girl like you."
Rea: "Ah... Um..."
*Her cheeks flushed red like strawberries.*
Rea: "Then... am I your... you know..."
Ren: "Yeah, you're my heroine. Obviously."
*At that point, I could no longer contain my embarrassment and embraced her with all my strength.*
Rea: "You're... You really are a marriage fraudster."
*It was still beyond me exactly what gave her that idea.*
Rea: "I'm gonna be angry if that's a lie. Even if it unintentionally ends up as a lie in the end."
Rea: "I'm gonna summon you right back into Reinhard's castle if you get yourself killed, you know..."
Rea: "If you don't want that, swear you're telling the truth."
Ren: "Yeah, I swear."
*I'd win. I swore to never lose again.*
*Himuro wrapped her arms around my back, and I answered her embrace, feeling even more love for those tiny, shivering shoulders in my arms. I made sure to engrave my warmth both into her body and memories.*
*Whatever happened, I'd never let anyone else have this. I'd never let her go.*
*I added even more strength into my embrace, as if trying to stress that fact to someone invisible.*
*I'd never let anyone or anything slip out of my hands again.*
*I'd protect what little I had left with the viciousness of a tiger.*
*And I'd pride myself on my naïve conviction. You could dismiss my words with a snort, reminding me that I had already lost far more than what I could protect, but I wouldn't care.*
*I would protect Rea Himuro, no matter the cost.*
*That was my final promise. Surrounded by kindness and affection, I closed my eyes and engraved it upon my heart, vowing never to break it.*

*As a certain kind of fear nestled in my heart about the truth I had glimpsed for a split second back in the castle.*
Let us discuss a certain man. He was an aberration birthed by the era he lived in: a chimera destined to emerge in a world of strife. A monster fashioned by countless coincidental factors that made him favor the embrace of the night over the luster of the sun. Let us discuss how it came about in more detail. 
*He was born in the decrepit slums of a world sliding down into exhaustion within the madness of World War I. His mother was, of course, a prostitute — there was no other way to survive in those days. His father was a lowlife who would drink away all her income. As such, the boy could hardly have been labeled as one born under a blessed star. Without a single ounce of happiness to his name, he practically dropped into this world all on his own.*
*Would you label his circumstances as thoroughly wretched? Or would sympathy blossom in your heart upon learning of his misfortune? Indeed, no man of a sane mind would hope for a life that foul. Those living in the present age would no doubt furrow their brows at the mere notion of such a background existing in any other place than the pages of fictitious novels. Lamentably, such were the times of war. Where madness equaled justice. Where the morals of mankind were warped beyond imagination, devolving into absolutes defying reason.*
*The world in those days was awash with such misery, which is precisely why his savage birth and life had also been acknowledged and allowed without moral repercussions. One could say he had been branded a failure from the moment he left his mother's womb. Although there were still two aspects that ever so slightly set him apart from the rest of his miserable kind.*
*Firstly, that he was born an albino, forever shunned by the light of the sun. It would scorch his skin without mercy, casting him into a world of impenetrable night. One could say he was deprived of his right to occupy half of the world. Deprived since birth; Wilhelm Ehrenburg had been cursed with such a fate all his life.*
*The second aspect was the existence of his mother/sister. They were bound by flesh and unchaste blood. No tale of his could be recounted without making mention of the girl who had sown both the seeds of confidence and mistrust in his very being. These two aspects...  would eventually prove to sharply separate his path from that of a million other failures. Having been robbed of daylight, he instead gained the night as his new domain. He believed it to be a blessing. At the pinnacle of his zeal, he conquered the darkness and made the night his own, cultivating his talent for ultraviolence.*
*Ironically, having been born to the lowest stratum of society gifted him with a bestial —and quite unprecedented — affinity for battle. He expanded his nightly territory like a beast, almost in direct proportion to his misery as a man. In order to transcend his wretched fate, he raced through the realm of darkness, craving to erase — to exterminate — his tainted conception from existence.*
*And almost as the natural end result of that ambition, he massacred his own family. He killed his father, then raped and murdered his mother. All they did was let out disgusting moans of so-called pleasure come nighttime. If he was a worthless piece of trash born in a garbage dump, then those two were no different from a pair of cheap instruments playing off-key. Their murder led him to a revelation.*
*I am a vampire. A bloodsucker of the night. A misconception, yet also the clearest answer to the riddle of his being. The abyss of the night is my world, my domain. Ah, that most pleasant of perversions, that incorrigible false inclination — the cradle of the self's transfiguration.*
*No one can match me in this realm. His fanatic belief warped reality, and — infusing him with undeniable power — deepened even further. As a result, it eventually ended up metamorphosing into truth.*
*He had never once regretted slaughtering his parents. Rather, he gained a tremendous sense of accomplishment from it, despite the relative ease of the deed itself. It was the natural decision for one who wished to transcend his origins. In order to reform himself, he first needed to grind the whole of his past to dust. That must have served as his motive. He never harbored any ill will towards his kin. He was merely a man of action in the most warped of senses — his abnormal mind would permit all actions and ideas, regardless of how hasty or preposterous they were. Still, he had unwavering confidence in his instincts, and they indeed saved him from many a tight spot, with this being no exception.*
*In short, he liquidated his origins. If his birth shackled him, he would destroy all and everything that might have constituted those chains. The past would not move, incessantly tying down one's limbs. Heavier than mud, more persistent than a snake. If betraying it meant eventual retribution, then turning one's back on it was out of the question. As such it, the easiest and most effective method was to simply kill it. He could have all the fun in the world after taking care of this. For only after he finished this hurdle could he start another — to make room for fun and games. In the mind of a beast, that had been a simple, blindingly obvious train of thought. It worked as a drug that would shield his eyes from his dissatisfaction with reality.*
*And in truth, he did become invincible following the murder of his parents. He met no foes that could match him — no soul could ever stand in his way. The world itself seemed to obey his will. He was a chimera — a werebeast spawned by its own environment. He crushed everything in his path, justifying his existence as a phoenix risen from midnight's ashes. An aptitude both acquired and inborn. He was a product of war — the kind of child exclusive to that era. To him, those days of omnipotence — while slightly on the boring side with no foes to make his blood boil — were the most glorious time of his life.*
*Yet his streak of tyranny came to an end the day he met the kindred Wolfgang Schreiber, and both ended up subjugated by the supreme prowess of Reinhard Heydrich. Thus—*
Mercurius: "I trust a man of your wits must have already figured it out."
*His thoughts, swirling undefined like a wisp of smoke within a vast abyss, were suddenly pulled back to reality.*
Mercurius: "The point upon which you stand now is the very nucleus of what I have explained — a canal flowing with blood both hoarded and shed."
*As if waking up from a dream. Shirou understood what the shadow had been trying to make him aware of.*
Shirou: "Hmm."
*He answered the voice reverberating in his head with indifference. Indeed, the thing that spoke was correct. The scenery before Shirou matched the information he had just received. The tone of voice and the words it used resembled those of a conman. However, though roundabout in its descriptions, it did not appear to be lying. Blood. Darkness. Crimson roses.  The scenery of this labyrinth exuded obvious consistence in its design. Not even artificially managed rose gardens could be grown this precise.*
*As such, Shirou had no difficulty figuring out where he was, given his memories before blanking out and the story he had just heard.*
Mercurius: "How was it? Did the sight of it make your heart skip a beat?"
Shirou: "Like hell.  This isn't even an original setup. I've heard the same crap about cherry blossoms in Japan. "
*It had been a passion of mankind to associate blood with plants. Could it have been due to the irony that corpses served as the perfect fertilizer? Or perhaps men found a certain fascination in watching its crimson drops shower the earth? Shirou didn't know and didn't really care. He had more important things than aesthetic sensibilities to worry about right now.*
Mercurius: "Very well. I expected no less from its friend. You truly are quite wonderful."
Shirou: "..."
*For example, finding out how to get this nauseating voice out of his head.*
Mercurius: "Still, do you not find your actions somewhat foolhardy? Nothing ventured, nothing gained, as they say — yet Bey's belly holds precious little in the way of rewards to be reaped. I know what your goal is, but the method you adopted was beyond foolish. Your determination may be admirable, yet I cannot help but lament the choice you made. "
Shirou: "...You overestimate me. I just don't think things through."
Mercurius: "Nay, that is untrue."
*An abrupt shudder ran up Shirou's spine. The words that reverberated within his mind were those of assertion. The thing — whatever it was — had been certain of its correctness. Or rather, it even—*
Mercurius: "That would most certainly be impossible for someone like yourself."
*The thing's words of absolute verity — like the whisper of a devil — shook Shirou's brain like a microseism.*
Mercurius: "Ahnenerbe devour souls, utilizing them as fuel. As such, they create a phenomenon in which there is a certain amount of disparity between the time of one's body's death and the dissipation of the soul. A more robust soul might retain its identity even after being devoured, much like in your case. And if one managed to seize and gain control of the Ahnenerbe in your position, he would — just like you imagine — be able to rematerialize in the physical world. Indeed, your theory is without flaws. I commend you for ascertaining the very core of my sorcery. "
Mercurius: "However. Ah, indeed, however. All things in this world possess fortitude. And that shall prove to be your undoing.  An inborn chemistry, a special affinity — a vessel prepared for your very being. Most such ideas stem from misconceptions, but are they all mistaken? Nay. 'Tis a rare case indeed, but an inborn affinity with one's vessel is not completely unheard of. As such, no arbitrary intruder could possibly seize it from its master. Like the red string of fate — no one can sever the bond of the two. Once tied, it would remain inert for an eternity. You could dress in the fanciest garbs and masks, but no philanderer will ever tear the two apart. "
Mercurius: "For the dark gift loves Kaziklu Bey."
*The jester asserted it not as a battle of strength between souls and wills, but one of innate chemistry. Shirou had learned of Wilhelm's past. If the dark gift meant the blood of Prince Dracula as he had suspected, then it definitely made sense. A red string of fate indeed. The very symbol of vampires — it was indeed fated for him and Wilhelm to meet.*
Mercurius: "You shan't plunder it. The bond that ties Bey and his Ahnenerbe is not to be underestimated. Their chemistry is exceptional, even within the Obsidian Table.  It might not exceed that of Machina's, but it could almost match it. As such, your scheme failed the moment you met and were devoured by Bey. It is a meaningless postulation at this point, but you should have taken better care in choosing your opponent. You might have succeeded, were you to focus on Malleus or Babylon instead. However, you would be unable to utilize your talents with a thing like Pallida Mors. Even assuming the possibility of plundering its power, the innate compatibility would have spelled your doom. "
Mercurius: "Leonhart and Tubal Cain are bound to their Ahnenerbe by blood, making it impossible to claim them for yourself. I have already mentioned Machina from the Battalion of Three, but the other two would similarly be out of the question. In terms of compatibility and sheer power, they exist on a level of their own. They would hardly even bat an eye at any interference from within.  As such, it was only Malleus' Elizabeth Báthory that you could have possibly both pillaged and utilized as your own. Has realization finally dawned upon you? You have mistaken your opponent. All you can do now is wander aimlessly through this crimson garden till nothing remains of you but bones. "
Shirou: "Hah. That so?"
*Shirou snorted, once again surveying the surrounding area. He figured out that much the moment he fell in here. Regardless of Shirou's affinity with him, the thing had already exchanged vows with someone he deemed perfect for himself. He had other things to worry about. This voice that kept jovially yammering about things he already knew like some school principal was pissing him off to unprecedented levels. Its manner of speech.  Its tone.  That mug that existed only in his mind's eye. They all rubbed him the wrong way, like some ethereal sand paper — like a kind of poison that seeped in through one's eardrums and sweat pores.*
*He could not see eye to eye with that bastard. They'd be mortal enemies for all eternity. He wished for the thing to disappear, and never show itself in front of him again. No, those were all understatements. What he felt exceeded all description, transcended conceivable emotions. What the hell was up with this instinctive aversion of his? Why did he feel so hostile to the thing's very existence? All he could hear was a voice — he didn't even know what it looked like — so why was he so upset by a few whispers from a damn ghost?*
*It was almost as if— He was born solely to eradicate this thing from existence. The antipathy had been so strong it filled his head with the oddest of thoughts.*
Mercurius: "Aye, that is the answer."
*The thing answered his thoughts.*
Mercurius: "You exist solely for that purpose."
*The voice snickered, twisting its invisible lips into a hideous grimace.*
Mercurius: "Why do you act surprised? That is all you have been doing your entire life. You easily shattered its daily life — its craving —to shreds, and kept doing it over and over again.  Be proud and rejoice. I might have arranged the props, but you were certainly the one to draw the curtains on our Grand Guignol. It would be neither a tragedy, nor a comedy without someone to pull the shut-in protagonist onto the stage. No matter how fine the props, they cannot conjure the play by themselves.  "
*What the hell was the voice talking about? The voice of a decrepit geezer with gratitude in its tone... What the hell was it...*
Mercurius: "You cannot deny it. You shattered it. Always you. All the time. Despite it all. And you guided his way. You demolished his happiness — so oversaturated by common sense and the trivial — continuously eradicating the status quo he so adores. You acted for but a single purpose — to be at the side of our cherished leading man; to introduce an end to his craving. "
Mercurius: "You are to him what my dear friend is to me. You cannot deny it. Should this transcend your comprehension, I implore you reflect upon the past that served as a beginning to it all. "
*Who was the one to smash Ren Fujii's ordinary life that day, on the roof?*
Mercurius: "How do you think it would interpret your current situation?"
*Who robbed Ren Fujii of any hope of regaining his old life by getting himself killed by Wilhelm?*
Mercurius: "Have you never thought it strange? How is it that you two are tied by a bond of friendship? You two are the antitheses of each other. Opposite poles. You might fake understanding in your minds, but your hearts would never acknowledge the other. To wish to repeat the same event over and over again without ever tiring of it...A craving ridiculous beyond words. Insane. Preposterous. You, who cherish new things and seek to overturn the old, are indeed in the right.  "
*And the shadow envied his passion. The ferocity of that wish, as well as the bone-breaking weight of emotions carried within that tone made Shirou feel lightheaded. The thing was indeed envious of Shirou Yusa's being. For it, the thrill of seeking the new had been the most priced jewel in the cosmos. And—*
Mercurius: "That is why beings like you are born next to our side. All to destroy... to liberate me."
*The voice of the devil claimed that Shirou's existence meant salvation through destruction.*
Shirou: "Liberate... you?"
*He instantly regretted asking the question so instinctively, for he could detect a hint of satisfaction in the voice that answered.*
Mercurius: "You could not die, correct? Nor have you ever felt alive. All had been easy, but none of it could satisfy you. You lived your life ravaged by incessant hunger, yet salvation would forever elude you. There will be no beginning, no end, no goal to head towards. And that is hardly worthy of surprise, for what you are is cancer. None of your wishes shall be granted unless you guide your host to death — to the unknown. Like a hero or a king of demons sprung straight from a fairytale. An incarnation of convenient developments, a destructive being far transcending the limits of mankind. Being our natural enemy, you also catch our eyes as heroes of songs and fables. That is who you are. "
Mercurius: "The apoptosis that erodes foreknowledge. [The play is over.](Acta est fabula) "
*One side of the double mirror, inseparable from the other. A dreadnought pulling the protagonist to the flames of the opposite shore. The most important prop on the stage, responsible for pushing the story forward.*
Mercurius: "You long to fall when up high, crave self-mutilation when a blade rests in your hand, and wish to embrace ruination before success. Does it not ring a bell? All those are concepts that a sane mind would rather avoid, yet to yours they are a sweet nectar, numbing and invigorating your senses like a potent drug. You are like this because we want you to be. A miniscule fraction of those who involve themselves with me or that shade of mine end up like that. Your existence is indeed quite convenient in putting an end to foreknowledge. "
*Shirou exhaled a deep sigh.*
Shirou: "So what? You're saying I'm your and Ren's remote-controlled toy? You kiddin' me? I don't know about you, but he'd never waste time on convoluted shit like that. "
*He'd happily end the bastard alone if he wished to disappear so much. Shirou shook his head at the other's nonsense, mustering his all to remain aloof. But that, too, was no use before the invisible man.*
Mercurius: "It dates all the way back to the sin you two concealed from the girl. Indeed. That was the moment you destroyed the ordinary for them both. "
*Shirou's consciousness grew dim as the ghost's stringent voice mentioned that taboo.*
Mercurius: "I believe it occurred eleven years ago. You killed the father of the girl, while your friend concealed the truth. No one suspected you two, given your tender years and uncanny talent for falsehoods. As a result, the incident was ruled an accident: the death of a man who failed to follow safety protocols within his hidden torture room. That must have been a good enough ending for ignorant masses, and that little story ended there for you two as well... What of, then, of certain things only he knew, and thus carried with himself to the grave? "
Mercurius: "For example, the fact that there had never been a blood relation between him and his daughter, your childhood friend."
Shirou: "Huh? The hell did you just say?"
*Shirou let out a foolish gasp at that sudden revelation. The shadow seemed to light up with the glee of a child who had just spoiled the truth behind a magic trick.*
Mercurius: "I take it you didn't know? Hardly a surprise. You might also remember how that man, despite his craven nature, was a petty villain lusting for things beyond his means and abilities. As a result, he was quite adept at covering his tracks, if nothing else. The textbook example of a lowlife, right down to his lack of trust for others. Only his position was special — a descendant of Odessa that had been erected to shelter the remnants of the Nazis. Their branches secretly extended all the way to Japan. "
Mercurius: "He was charged with the responsibility of looking over a certain article.  A grunt like him should never have assumed such a grand duty, but... I suppose the allure of the Transmutation of Gold was too strong for him to resist. His role was merely to supervise and support the thing until it woke up, developed consciousness, and assumed autonomous activity. "
Shirou: "..."
*Shirou's silence prompted the voice to continue. He didn't inquire about the identity of the article in question. He had no reason to. And he didn't feel like puking his guts out when hearing the answer.*
Mercurius: "But the greed of man knows no bounds. Eventually, he began to feel that the article he supervised was not enough for him.  And thus, he pondered what he could do. He possessed neither the talent, nor the courage to wield an Ahnenerbe. He admired transcendental power, yet hesitated to bind his body to a weapon. In his mind, the ideal tool would allow a human to wield it, while also possessing power enough to be considered a trump card, as arrogant as that may sound. He sought an instrument of immense power that would fit into those feeble hands of his. And finally— "
*If there was a word that could finish that story, it was—*
Shirou: "Kasumi."
Mercurius: "Exactly. He had the audacity to capture another Sonnenkind."
*Shirou felt like the shadow made a mocking smile as he let out a sigh of exasperation. He could see it vividly in his mind's eye — that scum of a father dancing with joy as his schemes seemed to succeed one after the other, all the while ignorant to the fact that even his luck had already been pre-ordained.*
Mercurius: "He put his plan into motion before the Sonnenkind had a chance to develop consciousness, disposing of her parents, then promptly adopting her. Luckily, his wife was a creature blessed both with simplicity and a kind heart. She suspected nothing of his dark schemes. Deceived by kindness, she acted out the perfect role of a mother for both the orphan and the article in question. Up until you two disrupted that calm lake surface of an idyll, sending ripples of destruction along its surface. "
Shirou: "Guess we did. Your point?"
*The conversation was on the verge of becoming no more than pointless chattering. Shirou had been slowly growing more and more irritated, unable to find the meaning behind all those revelations, as well as the shadow's obsession with disclosing the truth.*
Shirou: "So what do you wanna say? It's a bit too late to start discussing Kasumi's father. All your beating around the bush is just a pain in the ass. You said something about my destiny or whatever? Is this even supposed to be related somehow? "
Mercurius: "You cannot tell?"
*Shirou's answer came as the most contemptuous and malignant smile imaginable.*
Shirou: "Damn right I can't. How the hell is your nonsense supposed to be related to me?"
Mercurius: "That is it. There is nothing else. I have told you everything that had been concealed. All that is left are things that would not concern you."
Mercurius: "There was never a reason for you to mingle with the two and upset their lives. Furthermore, you are not the type to act the hero, rescuing friends from a perilous situation merely because you felt a rush of indignation upon learning of their unfair fate."
Shirou: "Yeah. So what?"
Mercurius: "Yes. As such—"
*He hammered a fatal crack in the scaffold of that family by removing the father.*
Mercurius: "Why did you kill him, then, despite having nothing to do with the whole affair?"
*Why did Shirou Yusa — originally not even involved with the matter — end up as a central figure of it, shouldering the critical role of executioner?*
Shirou: "Why? Well, that's... !"
*He realized that was the first time he felt the vicious fangs of foreknowledge dig into his brain. Shirou found himself at a loss for words. His throat grew numb. He could barely breath. His vision grew hazy. The world had lost all color and sound. His consciousness voided out, his brain completely frozen by that revelation.*
Mercurius: "Perhaps I ought to paraphrase it. Who benefitted the most from that man's demise? "
*That was neither the wish of Shirou Yusa, nor the girl who had known nothing to begin with. Only one had been saved. Only one did that apply to. From the very beginning, there had only ever been one person—*
Mercurius: "Who was the one that truly wished for the father to disappear?"
*You acted for his sake, and his sake alone. His voice became the fleeting buzz of an insect, unveiling the mischievous smile of a young prankster.*
Mercurius: "Do you understand now? Admit it. You are his inverse mirror, existing only to save, guide, and destroy him. The one closest to, but never in concord with him — a reflection that can only obey its origins. You have electrodes imbedded in your brain. "
*The relationship between the brain and the limbs — Ren and Shirou.*
Mercurius: "Your foreknowledge is incessant and keeps on spreading, much like the ever-multiplying and all-ravaging Legion of the Beast. Your pain and craving — like a fever of the foulest kind — infect all those around you."
*The curse of Mercury — defying all protests — now descended upon Shirou's life.*
Mercurius: "Go now, and fulfill your duty, apoptosis. Drag the main actor on the stage once again. There is no other way for you to attain your long-cherished desire. Refuse, and you shall remain a prisoner to me and my spawn for all time to come. "
*The scenery returned back to normal as the voice began fading away. A garden of crimson roses stretched once again before Shirou's eyes as the words — like a puddle of bad omens — hurled the last droplet of ill will towards him.*
Mercurius: "Allow me, then, to impart you with one final piece of advice. If you wish to flee this world, seek its core — the starting point of Bey's mortal days of yore. That is the only place where you could wedge open an escape route. May luck be with you on your journey. Know that I, too, have been fascinated by your exploits. "
Shirou: "Fuck off...!"
*Shirou spat out the piece of his tooth that broke off from grinding his teeth too hard. Grinding the bloody thing into the ground with the sole of his boot, Shirou glared at now-empty darkness — although, it might very well have been empty from the beginning. By now, his brain was filled with adrenaline, his mind broken beyond repair. Yet even he realized that he had been on the verge of fury fierce enough to make his very blood boil and evaporate. He'd never felt worse in his entire life. If sludge could talk, it would no doubt sound like that voice.*
Shirou: "You can go ahead and rave all you want where I can't hear it. I don't give a shit about your nonsense."
*He casually rejected the shadow with a mocking smile. The thing could most likely see and hear everything, anyway. There was no point in holding back.*
*In which case, the piece of voyeuristic garbage could bring it on. Though grudgingly, Shirou would take his bait. As long as he remained trapped here, he was powerless — that much was clear. The thing could keep on chirping that nonsense as much as it wanted — even if what it had said was the truth, all that meant was that Shirou had the power to end the piece of shit.*
Shirou: "..."
*A familiar voice suddenly reached his ears, making Shirou turn around. Two silhouettes — likely having noticed him from a distance — were running his way. He couldn't help ruffling his hair in exasperation at the sight. Their timing was impeccable, almost artificially so.*
Kasumi: "Shirou! Thank god we finally found you! I can't believe you really were here! Thank god— wghgh?!"
Shirou: "Calm down, you munchkin!"
Kasumi: "Owowowoawawawaw... St... Stop!! Cut it out, geez!!"
*He ruffled her hair with enough strength to make her eyes spin. It was all well and good to be happy-go-lucky, but did she really understand the situation they were in? Probably not. Definitely not.*
Ellie: "Sup. Having fun?"
Shirou: "Nope. I've never felt worse. Arrive a bit later next time, bozos."
Ellie: "What's that supposed to mean? You seem to be in a genuinely bad mood, like, for real. What happened?  "
Shirou: "Nothing. I've just been made to feel like a spoiled brat for a while. Hardly anything worse than late measles during puberty."
Ellie: "Thanks for making a hell lotta sense."
Shirou: "'I am myself! Stop trying to control my life, Mom!' That kinda shit. The kind you wanna kill yourself over in retrospect."
Ellie: "I thought you were the kind that would steal a bike and run away."
Shirou: "I sure am."
Kasumi: "Arrrgh, let go of my head already, you nincompoop!"
*Kasumi finally escaped Shirou's grip, and pursed her lips. It was nice to see that she retained her vitality even in a place like this. Shirou couldn't contain an exasperated smile.*
Shirou: "Alright. I got my partner and animal sidekick alive and kicking. Guess we can move on."
Kasumi: "What? Who're you calling an animal sidekick?!"
Ellie: "Okay. Do you have a lead?"
Kasumi: "Hey! Stop ignoring me! If anything, I'm the master of that rabid dog over there!"
Ellie: "She's got a point."
Shirou: "Leave her alone. She'll calm down eventually. Anyways..."
*Cutting the slapstick routine short, Shirou directed his gaze at the garden. He pointed at the faraway end of it that had been hidden from sight.*
Shirou: "That spot's fishy, I think. Just a gut feeling, but... well, things will sort themselves out if we just do it all laid-back like we always do."
Ellie: "Ah, thought so. You're a fairly good sensor most of the time, but your reasoning leaves much to be desired."
Shirou: "Reasoning, huh."
*He had a few thoughts of his own, but decided to keep them to himself, instead answering Ellie with a self-deriding smile. He was pretty sure he was on the right track. His nature would always lead him to the right place. He didn't believe that crap one bit, but according to the disembodied voice, he'd end up on the correct path regardless of his will, anyway.*
Kasumi: "Actually, um, what on earth is this place? Like, this super dangerous-looking scary guy shows up, and the next moment I'm in a place like this. "
Ellie: "Together with me."
*Shirou was the only one separated from the rest. It seemed like that stupid voice went through the trouble of splitting him from the others just so it could push a bunch of unneeded revelations on him.*
Kasumi: "I followed Ellie since she told me you were definitely somewhere around, but... what is this place? It's giving me the creeps."
Kasumi: "Everything looks the same no matter where we go, and the air is kinda unnaturally humid... or even slimy, I should say. And these roses look kinda like... um... "
*Like blood. Their vigor felt eerily unnatural.*
Kasumi: "There's something obviously weird with this place! It's not right!"
Kasumi: "What happened to us? And why are the two of you here? What's up with this situation? It makes no sense! Could it be that we're already... "
Shirou: "That's enough, Twitsumi."
*Shirou cut short her gloomy tirade. Kasumi's eyes lit up with indignation, but they all had more important things to worry about right now. Like getting out of this place.*
*There was no need to go out of their way to explain the situation to her. If anything, the less she understood, the better. All they needed to do was push forward. They wouldn't get anywhere sitting in one place.*
Kasumi: "But—"
Shirou: "Idle chatter ain't gonna get us any closer to answers."
Ellie: "If you hate the place so much, focus your energy on getting out of it."
Kasumi: "Getting out? How?"
Shirou: "Dunno. But if there was an entrance, there should be an exit or two as well."
*His indifferent remark didn't seem to pleased Kasumi at all, as she gave Shirou an indignant glare.*
Kasumi: "Why don't you ever try to properly think things through?"
Ellie: "No point arguing. You know he's always like this."
Kasumi: "Hahh. Fine. I get it. Can't say I'm confident, but I'll do what you say for now. I'm already used to being pushed around by you, anyway. "
Shirou: "Ohh, must be my lucky day."
*It took a while, but it seemed like they managed to sort everything out for the time being.*
*There was no point in remaining in this place now that they agreed on how to proceed. It would suck if the smell of blood filling this place seeped into their clothes to the point it wouldn't wash out. Shirou's nose was about to rust from all the copper in the air — he most definitely didn't want it to become the last thing he inhaled. He would rather end his life breathing the air of freedom. He couldn't even smoke in a humid and slimy atmosphere like this.*
Shirou: "Well then..."
*A labyrinth of roses extended before him, its inner chambers barred by countless flower petals — it would prove no simple journey. They were inside Kaziklu Bey. It was no surprise their footsteps would reverberate with despair — there was no telling how long it would be until they became nutrients for the flowers. But now they had to concentrate on pushing forward. With no alternatives to pick, they had to put their all into the one single thing they could do.*
Shirou: "Just you wait. We'll be there in a heartbeat."
*Who did he utter that to, and for what reason? Who did he want to reach? He did not doubt that it was his emotions — the incessant need to fulfill his role — that pushed him onwards.*
*Time did not seem to have an effect on the place. The three pushed forward through a never-changing scenery of darkness and crimson. Right. Left. The branches in the road would manifest with nothing to set them apart. The invariable design of the place eroded one's sense of direction like poison. All the branches they would come upon seemed like they led to exact same place, without a single alteration in their appearance. None of them could possibly find their way back at this point.*
Shirou: "..."

The heart of a vampire would pump malice and bloodlust through its veins, exposing them to a dreadful and merciless torrent of bile as they ventured through one such blood vessel.*
Shirou: "Let's go... this way."

Kasumi: "Shirou... Are you sure this is the right way?"
Shirou: "Little point in bickering over which one to choose when they're all the same."
Kasumi: "Well, you've got a point, but..."

They could at least try to devise a plan and come up with something to counter him with. Or was he a fool for expecting such things from mere humans? He deeply furrowed his brows.
