*It was in no way surprising. It made all the sense in the world for scenes like these to play out within Wilhelm's belly. Blood carried all the information of one's body. Nutrients. Oxygen. Its job was to supply the whole body, answering the call of every single cell within it. As such, it was an integrated circuit posessing even more information on processing than the brain. Shirou: "Still, it's gonna be a pain in the ass if that's the case."

Shirou: "Here, take it."

Kasumi: "Kyaaaaaaa...?!"

*I didn't know if my weapon could absorb souls other than Marie's, and even then, I had no way of telling if it was possible to form them into physical shape.*
*So far, other than Marie, I'd only seen the three Battalion Commanders formed into shape through the power of Ahnenerbe. Obviously, one's soul had to be of incredible tenacity to reach that level.*
*Hell, for all I knew, giving physical shape to the souls he absorbed had been Reinhard's special ability as the commander of the Einherjar, and he could do it to anyone.*
*If so, Marie alone would be a special case.*
*I wondered whether or not the soul of Sakurai's brother could be that strong.*
Ren: "Do you have an opinion?"
*I posed him a question, knowing it was futile.*
*Putting aside my ability to form him into shape, I guessed this meant it would be a while until I could return to my normal life.*
*I'd have to keep Sakurai company until she either found a more sensible way to bring her brother back, or gave up.*
*It felt like a major pain in the neck, one that I brought upon myself through my softness — and against my better judgment. I had no idea how I could've gotten myself into this.*
*Still, it beat having a clingy woman stalk me for the rest of my life for killing that giant bastard.*
Ren: "Guess I have no choice..."
*But in that very moment—*
Tubal Cain: "...?!"

*Even if it wasn't as replete with madness and savagery as Schreiber's, as seeped in bloodlust as Wilhelm's, or as heavy and fierce as Cain's, the sheer dread exuding from its vicinity froze me in my tracks, paralyzing me with ghastly terror.*

*I was too naïve. Valeria Trifa — the source of this terrible miasma of dread that filled the area — wasn't the kind of opponent Sakurai could tackle on her own.*
Ren: "I'm not saying I didn't consider this."
*To tell the truth, back when he asked me if I was the Divine Vessel, I momentarily considered two options.*
*And it seemed like I picked the wrong one. I should've done this from the start.*

*I pointed at the entrance to the church.*
Ren: "Your sister will die!"
Tubal Cain: "...!"
*The word seemed to affect Cain like a magic spell, freezing him in place.*
*Could he still remember her? Hell, I didn't even know if this thing was really her brother or not.*
*Which was why I never made use of his resentment towards the Divine Vessel to shatter their unlikely alliance to pieces.*
*Had I come here alone, I would've likely done that from the get-go.*
*I didn't want Sakurai to see Cain like this.*
*After all—*
Ren: "That idiot still believes in you!"
*She had yet to abandon the idiotic notion that this rotting corpse of a man was her beloved brother.*

*Though her steadfast resolve to face her past by challenging the priest also made me hesitant to try and get between them.*

*Now was not the time to wallow in sentimentality.*
Ren: "I'm going to save Sakurai. Help me do it!"
*But in that very moment—*
Ren: "...?!"
*A sudden kick sent me tumbling down the hard tiles of the road.*
Ren: "Ghh...!"
*I crashed into the wall. I received an attack that could've very well proven lethal, but as luck had it, I somehow pulled through it in once piece.*
*Did the bastard change into another Cain mid-conversation?*
*Whatever, I had no time for this.*
Ren: "The hell are you doing... you piece of shit...!"
*Even the blood I vomited up reeked of death.*
*I gave zero shits as to the true identity of this piece of filth standing before me. I knew her brother must've been somewhere inside that dead lump, and I wanted him to answer my question.*
Ren: "Don't you get it?! Are you really this far gone, you useless sack of shit?!"
Ren: "I'm saying your sister's gonna die over there! How about saving her, you stupid son of a bitch!"
*I had no brothers or blood relatives.*
*But I knew what family was — Kasumi taught me. I knew of friendship. And companionship.*

Tubal Cain: "Ghahghag..."

Tubal Cain: "If sHe wIsHeS nOt to iNheRiT mY fAte... sHe caN pErish... fOr aLL I caRe..."

Tubal Cain: "I cArE nOt whIcH pAth she chOoSes."

*Tubal Cain was Sakurai's brother, but no matter how I looked at him, he felt like someone else now.*
*Meanwhile, he boasted four Creation Figments, his weapon and manner of speech shifting with each activation.*
*In other words, the thing wasn't really just a "he", but a "they".*
Ren: "I see, so you can switch the guy at the wheel."
*That damn fool could've had the decency to tell me. Although in retrospect, it was probably my fault for never really giving her the chance to speak about the matter. In any case, it sounded like her brother was the fourth one inside Cain.*
*It was only him I had business with — the other three could fuck right off.*
Tubal Cain: "YoU hAve aLRreAdy seAleD tHe pAct of oUr blOoD."
Tubal Cain: "You aRE wORThy. caRRy THe pEDEstAL oF A ThoUSAnd REParATIonS, sASURahiME."

*Sealed the pact of their blood? Could it have meant—*

*Putting aside the truth of my relationship with Sakurai, one would have to be out of their mind to rejoice at any recognition from these abominations.*
*I wasn't interested in becoming some zombie warrior for an eternity, thanks.*
*My anxiety peaked as I had to keep dodging a torrent of their never-ending attacks.*
*I had no time for this. I needed to get to the church as fast as possible.*
*Unless I did, she'd die.*
*So what now...?*
*Alright, now or never. I had no other choice.*
Ren: "D-Dammiiiiiiiit...!"
Tubal Cain: "..."
*I caught Cain's weapon again, forcing it against the blade of my guillotine with all the strength I could muster.*
*I had no time to come up with a better strategy right now.*
*I would destroy his weapon. Realizing my intentions, Cain began to struggle — but I wasn't gonna let him go.*
*After having exchanging direct blows with them repeatedly, I could tell that the physical strength of the first two bastards wasn't that bad — if I put my all into it, I could more or less overpower them.*
Ren: "Whatcha gonna do now, eh?!"
*That was a bluff, obviously. All they had to do was relinquish control to the guy that could knock me out.*
*The one whose Creation Figment transformed their own body.*
*There were two like that inside the bastard — the one that used poison, and the other with the lightning. If the former came back up to the surface, I'd likely die in an instant.*
Ren: "I can't—"
*I had no choice but to bet my life on this. After all, I couldn't—*
Ren: "I can't let that fool die...!"
*So—*
Ren: "Come out!"
*And in the very next moment...*
Tubal Cain: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
*Did my words finally get through?*
Tubal Cain: "Donner Totentanz Walküre!"
*As an explosion of purple lightning knocked me off my feet, I realized that my prayers had been answered.*
*That was exactly what I'd been aiming for. All I had to do now was to negotiate with this one.*
*However—*
Tubal Cain: "KiLL... mE..."
*Instead, the bastard lunged at me at lightning speed, rambling incomprehensibly.*
Tubal Cain: "If yoU pRoVe unAblE... You, tOo, sHall fAll..."
*What the hell? What was wrong with him now?*
*He gave me two choices, and no time to consider the alternatives.*
*Kei's sword pierced through the burning air for the fiftieth time with seemingly inexhaustible ferocity.*
Kei: "Khh... Hahh...!"
*Unfortunately, it didn't look like she'd be going anywhere without at least another fifty strikes. Her opponent was but one man — the wicked saint. The blade she held had spilled the blood of countless men, and devoured souls beyond count. Each strike she launched came with a full intent to take a life —  her technique was utterly devoid of faints or trickery. No man that met this blazing inferno of a calamity in battle could escape unharmed. And yet—*
Kei: "Why...?!"
*The fire of her steel raged undisturbed, yet her heart and soul were slowly beginning to frost over from mortal dread. Why wouldn't he fall? How could he still keep on standing? All of her attacks had been perfect — he could not dodge a single one. All of them were clean hits, crashing straight into his vitals. Any other opponent's body should have been mercilessly shredded to bits.*
Kei: "Why...?!"
*Her sword had no effect. It couldn't so much as graze her completely motionless opponent. She understood but one thing.*
Kei: "Gh...?!"
*She could not stop attacking — the moment she halted in her tracks, her life would be forfeit.*
Kei: "Haaaahhhh...!!"
*Kei lunged forward with a cry that was as much a vigorous roar as it was a scream of terror. Not allowing herself to falter even for a second, she focused her entire being on maintaining an incessant torrent of attacks.*
Trifa: "Your efforts are futile. Know when to quit."
Kei: "...!"
Trifa: "It appears I overestimated you. I must confess I am thoroughly disappointed."
*His words ringing like a prayer of lament, Trifa caught Kei's sword with his bare hand.*
Trifa: "I believe I taught you not to blindly assault a foe you do not fully understand. If your sword has no effect, you should first consider why. And if you conclude that victory is impossible, you should swiftly retreat."
*He added more strength into his grip. Realizing that her blade might shatter, Kei leapt backwards — the priest did not bother to pursue her, and instead made a faint smile.*
Trifa: "The three most fundamental rules of the battlefield, yet you seem to have forgotten them all. Passion certainly has its time and place, but I suggest you cool your head a little.  So? What say you to that? "
Kei: "..."
*The priest was urging her to stop, yet Kei — heaving a deep sigh — readied her sword once again.*
Kei: "That it's a meaningless proposition."
*She could no longer back down.*
Trifa: "And that, child, is a foolish answer, if I have ever heard one."
Kei: "I wouldn't say so."
*Indeed, the first couple of blows admittedly made her lose her cool. The truth revealed by the priest had certainly shaken her to the very core. She could not blame the outcome on luck or coincidence, either, for the tall man did everything on purpose. She was still a relative newcomer to the battlefield, and thus his reprimand had been on point. But it would not be like this from now on.*
Kei: "Who on earth are you, Your Eminence?"
*When faced with an enemy of unknown origin, she had to use everything in her power to identify them, then come up with an effective neutralization strategy. She recalled him saying that the Divine Vessel was indestructible.*
Kei: "So that wasn't just a figure of speech."
*A hundred blows failed to even leave a scratch on his body, and it certainly wasn't for lack of strength on Kei's part. His sheer endurance simply defied all common sense. Was the difference in their soul density to blame? No, it couldn't be... The priest possessed several immense souls, but certainly not enough to maintain such a colossal advantage.*
Trifa: "You should know that there are more to souls than mere numbers."
*Likely guessing what had been on Kei's mind, Trifa addressed her like he would one of his students.*
Trifa: "For starters, one has to be all sorts of things to join the Obsidian Table, but one of the basic requirements is a certain amount of souls, as you are no doubt aware."
*One had to possess at least a thousand to call themselves a knight of the Obsidian Round Table.*
Trifa: "You have around that much, I would say. Malleus possessed the amount to form a regiment, while one could call Bey a brigade. However, that is only if you look at the numbers. I myself hardly possess any more souls than our First Lieutenant. If anything, I am inferior to him as far as quality is concerned. After all, it is mostly women, children, and the elderly that constitute me, while he braved countless battlefields as an immortal vampire with a taste for warrior's blood. It is the weak that need saving. Therefore, your supposition is incorrect. "
Kei: "..."
*Then what on earth was going on? It made no sense for the sword that split Wilhelm apart to lose its edge against the priest.*
Trifa: "Allow me to first tell you the truth of the matter. To destroy me — the Divine Vessel — you would require a whole legion of souls, at the very least."
Kei: "Impossible...!"
*She could not prevent a gasp from escaping her lips — the man's words made no sense to her. A legion meant over a million souls — it did not even possess an upper limit. It merely meant the entire army.*
Kei: "Who are you...?"
Trifa: "Ponder and reflect. That is how one matures."
Trifa: "If you are my daughter..."
*The next moment, the priest's palm crashed into Kei's solar plexus.*
Kei: "Ghh...!"
*The blow came with such force she expected it to shatter her spine, but before Kei could collapse from the pain, the priest's hands seized her uniform and sent her flying towards the ceiling. However, as she crashed into the concrete, she held on so as not to fall down — had she fallen back into the priest's deadly embrace, it would've been the end for her.*
Kei: "Uwoohhhhh...!"
*Instead, she kicked off the ceiling, and shot towards her foe at the speed of a bullet. If hacking at him from all angles had no effect, she would instead concentrate on a single point, stabbing it until her sword got through like a needle.*
Trifa: "Oh..."
*Directing all the kinetic energy of the fall into her thrust, Kei plunged her sword into the priest's abdomen, right where the stigma of the knights of the Obsidian Table had been located. Yet despite pouring all her strength into the attack, the blade bounced back, causing no damage. But that was fine. She didn't care. If one thrust wasn't enough, she'd keep stabbing him until her blade got through.*
*She directed all of her subsequent attacks at the same precise point, not deviating a millimeter in her aim. From the side, the action seemed akin to trying to open a hole in a concrete wall using only a needle.*
Trifa: "Not the worst of ideas, but..."
*One of his long arms suddenly jerked towards her like a snake. She had no time to dodge!*
Kei: "...!"
*The priest's palm crashed into her jaw, popping a few teeth out of their gums while numbing her brain. Yet Kei persevered, never once halting her onslaught.*
Kei: "Bey had a stronger punch!"
*She was not merely trying to act tough. While the priest boasted an impenetrable armor, he had yet to unsheathe a truly intimidating weapon. She would endure a hundred of his punches if she had to. In short, their battle came down to which one of the two would yield first.*
Trifa: "Well, this is troublesome."
*Trifa took a step back as Kei kept stabbing at his side. Her attacks had grown even fiercer and deadlier, but the impregnable Divine Vessel showed no signs of contorting, much less cracking open. The priest's palm flew through the air haphazardly — as if he had been trying to wave off a fly — and landed a clean hit on the unsuspecting Kei's temple. Nonetheless, she endured and launched her next thrust.*
Kei: "Hahh...!"
*The priest lost his balance to the blow, and crashed into the stained glass window behind him, sending a rainbow of shattered glass dancing through the air. Under normal circumstances, the hit should have proven lethal, but Kei judged it to have had no effect. She had to choose between pursuing the defenseless target, or using the momentary break to rest. However—*
Kei: "...!"
*As she was about to continue her onslaught, her feet inexplicably stopped dead in their tracks. A nigh-palpable sense of danger hung heavy the air. Her sixth sense told her that if she took another step forward, she would find herself in mortal peril.*
*Abiding by the priest's prior warning — that no good would come from mindlessly attacking a target she didn't fully comprehend — Kei decided to wait and observe. After all, her foe had yet to even form his Ahnenerbe. Watching him activate it without interrupting him would be the height of folly, yet a careless lunge now would only earn her a fierce counterattack. In short, she stood before a turning point, expecting the priest's armor to grow thinner once he brought his weapon out into the open.*
Kei: "Why don't you stand up already? I know you're still hiding something."
*Valeria Trifa handled both defense and offense with his bare hands. As such, Kei's current priority lay in figuring out the nature of his Ahnenerbe. She believed that to be the key to unraveling the secret behind his inhuman sturdiness. What could it be, though...? She hadn't the faintest notion.*
Trifa: "The Divine Vessel of Gold."
*The priest rose to his feet, brushing dust and pieces of glass off his mantle.*
Trifa: "That is the name of my Ahnenerbe. Although I imagine you might have already guessed. You are waiting for me to form it, so you can — with that newfound information — conjecture a more efficient approach to deal with me. Hardly a misguided plan, for certain, but futile nonetheless. "
Kei: "Futile?"
*Did he mean to imply that the forming of his Ahnenerbe would unveil no holes in defense, nor would it hint at one? No, that could not be true. No being in this world could be completely invincible.*
Trifa: "You see, I, along with Lord Machina, am somewhat of a special case. You might not be able to comprehend it, but absolutely nothing would change whether I consciously formed my Ahnenerbe or not."
*Not a single of one Kei's attacks could even scratch him. And while she could endure his blows for the time being, they were gradually beginning to wear her down. Could the priest have meant that...? No, impossible...! They were locked in a battle of attrition; she would stab him a hundred times for each of his punches — the last one standing would emerge as the victor. If he planned on hiding it, then so be it. She would keep on hacking away at him until he had no choice but to unveil his secret.*
*Kei lurched forward, thrust once again at the priest's left side. This time, however, he indifferently brushed her sword away with his palm.*
Kei: "Ah..."
Trifa: "Good grief. Your swordsmanship is too predictable. Did you truly believe I would simply stand and let you go at me like this forever?"
*Focusing on penetrating a singular point was indeed a sound strategy when faced with armor this sturdy. However—*
Trifa: "Anyone can defend himself when he knows where the attack will land. I allowed you to have your way before because I assumed you would eventually give up. But I seem to have underestimated your obstinacy. I am afraid we might find each other in an eternal stalemate at this rate, so I will try fighting back a little from now on. "
*His palm crashed into Kei's breastbone, right above her heart.*
Kei: "Ghahh...!"
*The strength of the blow remained the same as before. In other words, she could endure it well enough. And yet, for some odd reason, its impact reverberated across her whole body.*
Trifa: "In terms of raw fighting prowess, you most likely surpass me."
*Kei staggered backwards as the priest leveled a rapid succession of punches at her, each heavier than the last. Her heart grew weaker with each successive hit.*
Trifa: "How admirable. You have matured splendidly, my girl. Although I might not be a true soldier, you still managed to surpass your master in an exceedingly short time."
*Indeed. As far as fighting technique was concerned, Kei had been obviously above the priest. She outperformed him at everything, andyet—*
Trifa: "But it still won't be enough to shatter the Divine Vessel."
*Kei had yet to reach a level where she could answer one of the priest's attacks with a hundred precise thrusts of her own. Would this be the end of her? No, she would not acknowledge it—*
Kei: "Ghh...!"
*Her countless wounds had stained her clothes a deep crimson, yet Kei still launched a desperate swing at the priest. Her blade hit, yet it stopped right at the priest's neck, lacking the strength to even graze his skin, let alone draw blood. Another palm crashed into Kei's solar plexus, sending her flying as blood burst forth from her mouth.*
*She finally realized that while the priest's attacks lacked in raw destructive power, they were all designed to slowly but surely end her life. However, there was one rule that no one in this world could bend — those that wielded Ahnenerbe could only be killed by one. In other words, if he truly planned to kill Kei with his bare hands, it could mean only one thing—*
Kei: "Your own body is your..."
Trifa: "You are correct — I am the Divine Vessel."
*His own body was his Ahnenerbe. As a special case that encompassed both materialization and fusion, it continually existed in a formed state.*
*In other words, that was already the extent of his offense and defense. Much like he had said, the flow of this battle would not be affected by whether or not he formed his Ahnenerbe. The truth rang in Kei's mind like a death sentence.*
Kei: "No...!"
*It was still too early to give up. At least now she knew it was unlikely he could raise his destructive power. That, at least, she could still endure. She needed to come up with a plan before her soul yielded to despair.*
*She had to find a weakness — a fatal flaw —in his defense. Such a thing might not exist, and she could very well end up only wasting her time. But she couldn't simply give up at this point.*
Trifa: "I see."
*Trifa gave a deliberate nod as he observed Kei rise to her feet.*
Trifa: "You would look for a chink in my armor... and indeed, that is a wise choice to make. Or should I say... the only available option to you, is it not? Listen closely, Leonhart — there are actually three ways to destroy the Divine Vessel. "
*Was he telling the truth, or was that merely another one of his lies, woven only to thwart her? She could not tell, but it would not hurt to listen for now. Trifa, meanwhile, raised three of his fingers before her.*
Trifa: "The first would be Lord Machina's fist, for his strike is the harbinger of absolute demise, regardless of reason or logic. The second would be to make an entire legion of souls clash with it, much like I had previously said. Both would be impossible for you. "
*An all-ending decree that ignored the laws of physics, or strength surpassing that of an army. Kei possessed neither of these things.*
Trifa: "The sheer destructive power of Lord Heydrich's legion and His Excellency the Vice Commander's sorcery defies all reason. The two exist on a level of their own. To tell the truth, the second option is merely a conjecture of mine, and I cannot for certain tell whether such a density of souls could possibly exist in this world."
Trifa: "Therefore, Lord Machina has earned both my respect and constant vigilance as the second strongest in our ranks. After all, he possesses power enough to feasibly attempt the murder of our very own lord and master."
*A wry smile appeared on Trifa's lips as he described the nature of their Deus Ex Machina with a hint of reverence in his tone.*
Trifa: "In other words, Leonhart, only Lord Machina could destroy me in the straightforward way you have been attempting thus far. Unless you find yourself capable of mimicking his prowess, you ought to focus your attention on the third option instead."
Kei: "And that is..."
Trifa: "Yes. In short: locate a chink in the armor."
*Provided such a thing truly existed. It had to. He implied it himself.*
Kei: "Why are you telling me this now...?"
Trifa: "A curious question, that..."
*Trifa shrugged his shoulders with a smile, as if implying he had said all this merely on a whim. The unveiling of his only weakness did not seem to affect his air of mocking superiority in the slightest.*
Trifa: "The choice whether to believe it or not is solely yours. After all, I might be merely fooling around with you."
*He might have been trying to instill false hope in her, only to later plunge her into an even deeper pit of despair. After all, it was a truly effective way of breaking one's heart and resolve. This would hardly be the first time he had done it. However...*
Kei: "There is one thing you should not forget."
*That she was a tremendously sore loser. The chink in the priest's armor would likely not manifest under normal circumstances. There was no patch of skin on his body she hadn't attacked yet, and Kei would've noticed if the priest was consciously trying to defend a particular spot. As such, she had to make a gamble with fate. She would pour her entire being — all the strength and vitality she still had left after that ceaseless onslaught — into this final attack.*
*Kei realized that the priest likely revealed his secret in order to incite this very action from her. As long as she could not overpower him in a regular battle, he would not show a gap in his defense. As such, Kei needed to put her life on the line if she wanted results. After channeling her being into this strike, she would need to follow it up with another to deliver the finishing blow. Whether or not she possessed the power to overcome that contradiction, she did not know. But there was no other way.*
*Various scenes from Kei's life flashed through her mind as she entered a state of trance, singing her aria of war. The happy memories of her childhood. Those blissful days filled with warmth. And the merciless whirlwind of blood that swept them all away.*
Kei: "I see. After all that has been said..."
*Deep down, she was just like Fujii. She had already gone past the point of no return. So she hoped that he, at least, could avoid becoming like her.*
Kei: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
*Her flames turned into a storm, their crimson wings enveloping the church. This would decide everything. If the Divine Vessel felt himself powerful enough to shatter the blazing scarlet fire of her conviction, he was more than welcome to try!*
Kei: "Go ahead."
*It was the priest's turn to take the bait. No mere punch would extinguish her flames now. As such, he would need to unveil his trump card. He would need to open up his defenses in order to reveal the zealous craving burning in his heart.*
Trifa: "..."
*Tears of blood trickled down the priest's cheeks as he witnessed Kei evoke her Creation Figment. The stigmata on his hands, legs, and abdomen all howled in unison, leaking fresh blood.*
Trifa: "They are getting ahead of themselves..."
*Having reached the final stage, it appeared they could contain themselves no longer. Yet Trifa remained unconcerned, for he shared in that sentiment with all his heart and soul. And for that reason, even though he could've worn down the girl till she was all but dead, he chose to reveal his trump card in order to end her life in an instant. Only that would break her heart and resolve.*
Trifa: "The seventh shall open before long."

There are things that cannot be forgotten. Things that should not be forgotten. Even if you know full well that what-if scenarios don't mean a thing in reality, at certain times, you nonetheless cannot help but wonder: "Were there actions I could have taken to prevent that from happening?" 
*There once was a man who'd set his heart on becoming a priest since boyhood. And his dream came true. He did not possess a particularly special talent for that profession. He was just an average man who achieved his position through countless days of effort. A completely ordinary life befitting an ordinary man.*
*However, his motives were somewhat different from his peers; peculiar. Men and women of the cloth were supposed to believe their duty brought others salvation, and hold it as the most sacred of their callings. Yet what he desired was salvation not of others, but himself.*
*In short, he clung to faith — to his own love for God. It had been a concept ubiquitous among human societies. While religion divided into different sects with their own values, all of them had one thing incommon — prayer. A belief in the existence of a greater power that created mankind. The man depended on that kind of worldview. He thought of himself as both mediocre and an aberration. He possessed no special talents as far as living as a normal man was concerned, yet he excelled at matters that had been most certainly both unnecessary and abnormal.*
*He could see and hear thoughts and memories dwelling in all things, both living and dead. That by far exceeded simple concepts such as mind-reading. He saw people as books. Pebbles on the roadside as radio. The world he had been born into was a surreal aberration that no other soul would likely ever be able to comprehend. He felt alone and scared. In the end, that caused him to hasten down the road of the clergy. He hoped that being a part of the world's largest organization would make him feel like human, like he belonged.*
*God had created the world. He loved mankind and watched its acts from high above. As such, the man too must have been a blessed child of the Father, who art in Heaven. He prayed, believed, hoped, and implored, but all of his laments ultimately fell on deaf ears. After all, the world he'd plunged into was in truth the most harrowing Purgatory there was in the world of Man.*
*It was oft-said religion was a drug:"The fact that a believer is happier than a skeptic is no more to the point than the fact that a drunken man is happier than a sober one." Man was an imperfect creation, and as such, the largest faction in the society of mankind, too, had its fair share of depravity and madness.*
*As a result, the man too started falling apart. He was worn thin. His unnatural abilities had passed the threshold of mere agony, evolving into something that chiseled away at his very life. If he kept this up, his very existence would probably fade away in the near future. Thus the man resigned himself to the mindset of a prisoner sentenced to be slowly but surely tortured to death. There was neither salvation nor refuge in his world. But one day, this man, who had given himself to die, met a being of genuine and radiant light.*
Trifa: "On December 24th, 1939... I saw the light of truth."

*It didn't matter if it made sense or not. Mystery novels were the only things that needed to be grounded in logic, and all that cause-and-effect business.*
Kasumi: "I don't think anyone can explain their feelings. Is that so strange?"
Trifa: "Thinking that in itself is also part of reason. Ah, but do not get me wrong — I am not trying to find fault in you. It is perfectly fine. I understand. That is just the type of person you are, I suppose.  However... "
Rea: "That's enough."
*Rea, who had remained silent up until this point, cut in as though to protect Kasumi.*
Rea: "Stop trying to put weird things in her head. She's rather simple-minded, you see."
Kasumi: "Simple-minded..."
*Rea's comment wasn't particularly nice, but Kasumi didn't feel too mad. For she heard genuine sympathy in Rea's voice.*
Rea: "Don't play along with him either, Ayase. You're just asking for trouble. Rea: This guy's good at cornering people with words. "
Trifa: "Why, you wound me."
*Trifa smiled wryly, and lightly pushed up his glasses.*
Trifa: "My eloquence is but child's babble compared to His Excellency the Vice Commander. Our prior dialogue did not have any deep meaning to it.  At any rate, leaving that aside, you have already realized it, have you not, Theresia? "
Trifa: "Isn't that why you have been unusually restless for a while now?"
Rea: "..."
*Kasumi had no clue what they were talking about.*
Trifa: "You are hesitating, are you not? You do not know what to do. Very well, then go. I do not doubt you have many a word you would like to share with him. I believe you understand very well that the boy hardly has a chance when faced against me with no information at his disposal."
*Rea kept her mouth shut. She hung her head down and shivered as she bit her lip. Was she angry? But if she was, then at who? It didn't seem like her indignation was directed at Father Trifa.*
Rea: "Hey Ayase, promise me something."
*Rea met Kasumi's puzzled eyes head on and spoke as though making a plea.*
Rea: "I'll be right back, so don't try to pull anything stupid.  Rea: Everyone loves you. So don't be reckless. "
*"It's okay. Everything will be okay." — was what Rea's eyes said.*
Rea: "Have faith everything will turn out fine."
Kasumi: "Rea..."
*As Kasumi was momentarily rendered speechless by the sudden display of mature compassion, Rea turned around and started back the way she came.*
Kasumi: "Ah, where are you going?"
Rea: "To change clothes. I have an outfit just for the occasion."
*And with those ambiguous words, she faded down the dark hallway.*
Kasumi: "..."
*What was she trying to do? What was happening? Kasumi didn't know, but her heart was beating an ominous beat. People who said lines like those would always end up doing something reckless, and leaving their loved ones miserable.*
*She'd already had enough of stuff like that...*
Trifa: "Such a wonderful display of growth, no? It was well worth the risk, if I say so myself."
*Trifa paid no heed to Kasumi's worries, letting out a sigh of admiration.*
Trifa: "It is good to be positive. Looking towards death like Leonhart does is dangerous.  Memento mori — 'remember you will die'... this expression has two meanings. Either it means you should live an earnest life since you will die eventually, or that you should not cling to life since it all leads to the same place anyway. She was the latter up until now. Well, after all, she was born into a religious background. She knows all there is to know about salvation after death. "
Trifa: "But that train of thought begets no good. To coin a phrase from Theresia, that is just asking for trouble. The idea that salvation is found in death, not life, opens the doors to Hell."
Kasumi: "Hell?"
*Kasumi urged him on. That word hit very close to home at the moment.*
Kasumi: "Does Hell really exist?"
Trifa: "Why yes. I have seen it myself."
*Kasumi didn't know what he meant by that, but she had a feeling it was no metaphor. She could tell he wasn't referring something like battlefields or poverty. No, Father Trifa was saying he'd seen the real Hell.*
Trifa: "It is a country of the dead. The realm of the departed. A world of endless escalating strife... I suppose that is how you would describe it. I call it Valhalla, though the Buddhists like yourself might be more familiar with the name Path of Asura — a realm of endless strife. I have seen a place that fits that description, and I know those who have gone there."
Trifa: "There is not a thing in this world more repulsive than that place."
*His tone was as mild as always, but now it carried a barely perceptible echo of a tremor. He appeared to fear that Hell from the bottom of his heart.*
Trifa: "As such, everyone should live to their fullest while they can. I would like to hold on to that mindset. So should you, Ms. Ayase. It would be the end of me if the devil's castle actually would synchronize with you."
Trifa: "That would make Mr. Fujii's efforts come to nothing as well."
Kasumi: "Huh...?"
*What did he just say?*
Trifa: "Like I was saying, he's here. Theresia noticed and went to intercept him."
Kasumi: "Wha..."
*Kasumi's mind went blank at that moment.*
Kasumi: "Why...?"
*Why did he never do what she told him? He didn't have to come. He shouldn't have. She was supposed to put everything to end by herself...*
Trifa: "Remember what Theresia said? Everyone loves you."
*But she felt the same way. It was because she loved everyone that she didn't want to put them in danger. And yet...*
Trifa: "When your motives and goals are the same, and with so few options available, a vicious game of musical chairs is inevitable. Such beautiful and lovely selfishness."
Kasumi: "Ren's really on his way here?"
Trifa: "It is not as though I have seen him myself, but I am almost certain. If Bey's life opened the seventh, then it is extremely unlikely Leonhart was his opponent. She lacks the strength to beat him.   Meaning it was a third party. There are so few potential candidates that it barely requires thought to determine who it could have been."
*All the dots finally connected inside Kasumi's mind. She realized why Rea had been mad now. She and Kasumi were trying their hardest, only for some fool who couldn't read the mood to muck it all up.*
Trifa: "I see. Indeed, logic does not apply to emotions. You seem happy."
Kasumi: "Huh?"
*Kasumi hadn't even noticed until Trifa told her. He let out a pleased chuckle.*
Trifa: "Splendid. I mean it. Truly splendid. How wonderful. One should never deify death.  Yes, I know. You did not come here intent to become a sacrifice. You were planning on defeating me... the Divine Vessel, were you not?"
Kasumi: "Defeat? Well..."
*Kasumi was slightly taken aback by Trifa's kind smile. Though she felt no hostility from him, the warning bells in her heart were ringing like crazy.*
Kasumi: "Why? Why are you smiling? You don't think I'm capable of it?"
Trifa: "Oh? Am I smiling?"
Kasumi: "You're always smiling, aren't you!?"
*She unconsciously raised her voice. Her heart was pounding so hard it hurt her eardrums.*
Kasumi: "You're the only one I can't get a read on. I don't how much of that... stuff you showed me at the amusement park was true, but... "
*The miniature garden known as Lebensborn. If Lisa Brenner's memories weren't a false illusion, Kasumi possibly knew more than Ren at this time.*
*She only knew of the members of the Obsidian Round Table through Lisa's viewpoint, but it was still enough. However, even with that, there was one person who was lacking. Only Trifa never showed up in Lisa's memories.*
Kasumi: "What are you?"
*She couldn't imagine he had deliberately covered up information regarding himself. Valeria Trifa hadn't existed until 60 years ago. Trifa let out a light but troubled sigh.*
Trifa: "I told you, I have seen Hell. No, to be more exact, I'm still there."
Kasumi: "...?"
*She didn't understand a word.*
Trifa: "I don't know how Lisa's memories portrayed me, but I was probably there. You simply didn't notice. But let us cease with this fruitless conversation. We are comrades right now. "
Kasumi: "Comrades?"
Trifa: "Or rather bitter enemies in the same boat. Either way, our interests align. We are both hopeless optimists.  Take out the part how we wish for the each other's death, and we are basically trying to achieve the same thing. "
Kasumi: "..."
*It seemed like the priest had seen through all of her schemes, but rather than condemning her, he empathized. In that case, they really were bitter enemies in the same boat. However...*
Kasumi: "Can I say something?"
*She took a deep breath, sorted out her feelings, and looked up at that smile of a mask.*
Kasumi: "Father Trifa, you've had the wrong idea for a while now."
*Maybe she shouldn't be saying this, but she was so angry she couldn't help it.*
Kasumi: "About all that talk of beating you or wishing for your death..."
*The heck was that all about? She was just a high school student. She didn't want to be treated like some crazed psychopath on a killing spree.*
Kasumi: "I, uh, never thought of killing you."
Trifa: "Well now..."
*Trifa sounded truly surprised. It seemed he'd never expected those words.*
Kasumi: "I mean, how the heck would I even do that? I'm just your everyday lovely kendo club girl. I can't seriously put a fight against trained soldiers like you.  And besides... "
*She never wanted to see someone die ever again.*
Kasumi: "If you were to die too, then Rea might be sad."
Trifa: "I beg your pardon...?"
*She truly had struck an unexpected chord. Trifa stood dumbfounded for a few seconds, then started laughing as if he could hold back no longer.*
Trifa: "Hah... Haha... Hahahaha... Well well, what a conundrum. I don't know what to say."
Kasumi: "Wh-What's so funny?!"
*Kasumi's face flushed all red. She never expected him to burst out into laughter. Did he find her that amusing?*
Kasumi: "N-No one would be happy about someone close to them dying! That's why Sakurai turned out the way she did, I'm sure of it...! T-The families of the people I-I... "
*She felt cutting short would be cowardly, so she made sure to finish.*
Kasumi: "Killed... I'm sure they're all crying. I don't want any more people like that popping up on my account... What's so strange about wanting that?! "
Trifa: "Heh heh, no, no, hahahaha... Yes, yes indeed, you said it. You are not particularly strange.  You just have it all wrong. I am not amidst the ring of those Theresia holds dear and loves, you see. "
Kasumi: "What makes you think that?!"
*Not to mention that wasn't even her point.*
Kasumi: "Like or dislike, seeing someone you know die is never a happy occasion, right? Normally, you don't seriously wish for people to die just because they're bad or something like that."
Kasumi: "Even if they really piss you off, it still leaves a great big hole in your heart when they suddenly go away. It hurts."
Trifa: "Well now..."
*Trifa narrowed his eyes, stroking his chin, then looked at Kasumi as though he were looking deep inside her.*
Trifa: "You sound as if though you speak from experience. Now who was it that you despised that suddenly died on you? "
Kasumi: "Th-That's..."
*His eyes were deep blue like placid lake waters, yet there was also something like seething gold within them... Kasumi was momentarily taken aback by that sight, but when she came to, she shook her head.*
Kasumi: "That doesn't matter! You're like a father to Rea, right? No matter how much of a bumbling idiot you may have been, she would never be happy to see you go. "
Trifa: "Oh really? Not even a father who killed her mother?"
*Trifa continued without missing a beat.*
Trifa: "I am the one who killed Lisa. Since you were touched by her soul, you should already know that."
Kasumi: "..."
*True, she hadn't exactly been unaware of that.*
Trifa: "In other words, I should be a target of revenge for you. It was thanks to her that Johann escaped, resulting in your birth. She is the reason you are living. And it was I who crushed her heart. Objectively speaking, shouldn't I be the worst man there is from your view? "
Kasumi: "Ghh..."
*He had a point. It still hadn't really sunk in that Lisa was technically her family, but even if she hadn't been, Kasumi had known her personally. She'd admired that beautiful and kind lady who treated her so well. What the priest did was unforgivable. And indeed, he did anger her very much. However...*
Kasumi: "Please tell me why you did that, if nothing else."
*A rare restrained voice echoed forth from Kasumi's mouth. She suppressed herself just because she hated talking at Trifa's pace. That was it.*
Kasumi: "I'm not very smart, so I don't know what's right or wrong. It's natural to want to kill someone if you hate them. In that case, I should be the first to die, but I don't want to... And I don't want anyone else to die either."
*Not even Kasumi really knew what she was saying anymore. She cursed her own stupid head.*
Kasumi: "I'm always like this, so everyone always just makes fun of me — I'm never part of any serious discussions. No wonder. They probably think I'd just get in the way. I'm not what you'd call a calm person, I just confuse things, and I'm bad at figuring stuff out...  When you get down to it, I'm always just causing people trouble. "
*She actually was happy Ren had come after her, and she knew her decision to go off and do this on her own was causing him trouble.*
Kasumi: "But even so, I can't just stop caring. That's not how people are."
Kasumi: "I want to always take everything head on. Think about it. I want to be given the chance to seriously worry about things that matter. I'm going to screw up or regret some, sure, and I actually already have, but that doesn't mean I want to run to the other extreme and give up. Otherwise, that would be, uh, how do I put it... "
*She spoke her honest thoughts.*
Kasumi: "It would feel like I was letting my choices be made by someone else, wouldn't it?"
*And that kind of position would only make her wish to shift blame.*
Kasumi: "I don't want a way out for myself or to blame everything on someone else. Sure, I like complaining things are tough from time to time, or that others are wrong and I'm not, but that's just because I'm a normal person. I have dark thoughts too."
*She was possessed. She wasn't doing it on her own will. Those dozen or so people were killed by some power completely unrelated to her. She was a victim, if anything. It would be so easy to run from guilt like that, but she couldn't. On that note, was it really her own will telling her the man in front of her was an inhuman monster that should disappear from the face of the planet? Could she declare that was something she came up by herself after hours of worrying and pondering? No. She couldn't.*
Kasumi: "So I want to know about what you're thinking. After all, it's one's hands and feet that act, right? "
*And the one that was responsible for controlling them was her brain, regardless of how ill-constructed it was. And so she wanted them to be in proper synch. She wasn't a remote controlled vehicle that moved according to intercepted radio signals...*
Kasumi: "Gah, dammit, even I don't understand what I'm talking about anymore. Should I start over and explain it in a different way?"
Trifa: "No..."
*Trifa met Kasumi's heightened state of excitement with a strange look on his face. He gazed at her with dazzling eyes like those of a martyr who had discovered his holy object. He then followed up with a solemn voice unfitting of his usual detached behavior.*
Trifa: "Your wisdom has stirred my heart, Ms. Ayase. You possess a wonderful philosophy."
Trifa: "I see, so it is one's hands and feet that act. You only end up shifting the conclusion treading on a road decided for you by another... Yes, it is indeed as you say. I can understand why everyone loves you. It appears Lisa's judgment was not misplaced. "
Kasumi: "Ah, no, uh..."
*Though she didn't really understand why, Kasumi got very flustered at being praised so honestly.*
Kasumi: "I-I'm just stupid, that's all."
Trifa: "No, you are a smart girl. Much smarter than I am.  Yes, you somewhat resemble Lady Kircheisen. I can see why Leonhart found herself inexplicably conscious of you."
Kasumi: "No, really, that's not..."
*He gently rubbed her head, putting her at an even bigger loss at how to react. She didn't know exactly what he found so admirable about her, but discussing that could wait.*
Kasumi: "Please answer my question."
Trifa: "Ah, about Lisa? Anything I say will merely come off as an excuse. You can simply interpret me as getting rid of her because she was in my way. That is what it essentially boils down to. "
*With those words, Trifa let go of her, and...*
Trifa: "But I was happy about what you said. I never considered that Theresia might be saddened by my passing.  Well, I will not die, at any rate. "
Kasumi: "Ah..."
*Kasumi felt as if something was being drained from her body.*
Kasumi: "Aah... Ahh..."
*Her consciousness was fading. She fell to her knees. Impossible... What was happening? "Was I... being... too... naïve?"*
Trifa: "In short, you are saying you are trying to prevent Lord Heydrich's advent, are you not? Indeed, I feel the same way. He is not an ideal personage for this world. But I must have my wish granted. Unfortunately, no amount of persuasion will sway my mind. As you would put it, I am a fool who runs to the other extreme. For shifting blame is the very essence of my craving. "
*She was falling. Her vision grew dark. But a moment before the darkness consumed her...*
Kasumi: "Father Trifa..."
*Kasumi voiced the question she wanted answered most of all.*
Kasumi: "If nothing else, your love for Rea... is genuine, isn't it?"
Trifa: "..."
*He didn't answer. He could not answer. The Divine Vessel had nothing to say. Though it shouldn't have been a difficult question, he kept as silent as a statue, until suddenly...*
Trifa: "I would not be doing this if I knew."
*His voice full of a bitterness spurned by neither anger nor lament filled Kasumi's ears as she collapsed.*
Trifa: "The birth canal to Gladsheim has already been sealed off. I wonder, how long will it be until a new path opens by your side? But it hardly matters. Your birth canal is narrow. It does not have the ability to emanate the devil's castle.  If anything, death of the mother is a much more likely outcome. Still, you should know it is preferable to being caught by Isaak, Ms. Ayase. "
*Trifa tilted his head as he spoke in a truly emotionless voice.*
Trifa: "Yet I fail to understand."
*Had he overestimated her, or was it the other way around?*
Trifa: "Was attempting to persuade me truly your only goal? Did you really believed it to be possible? If so, then I am truly honored to have been viewed as so much human."
Trifa: "However—"
*The wicked saint turned around, picked up Kasumi, and carried her down deeper into the darkness.*
Trifa: "You are a fool. I am no human. I have long abandoned that vessel. It was defective, you see. "
Trifa: "I wish we could have met back then. That way, I could have beheld what sort of color and sound your soul and heart possessed..."
*Self-mockery seethed out of those lips. It was beyond hilarious to think he, if momentarily, desired a power he had loathed and abandoned himself.*
Trifa: "But that is but a pipe dream. I will never go to Valhalla again. Now then, shall we greet our guest together, Ms. Ayase? "
*The iron doors opened and slowly closed. All that remained was pitch-black darkness and silence.*
*I went through the blown up chapel. And as I was looking for a hallway that wasn't completely devastated by the earlier explosion, I ran into her.*
Ren: "Himuro..."
*What was she doing here?*
Rea: "I finally found you..."
*She was panting slightly. It seemed she'd been looking for me. Her face was as expressionless as always, but I could spot sweat on her bangs and forehead.*
Rea: "Don't wander around so much... I got tired looking for you."
Ren: "Ah, uh, well..."
*No words came to mind right away. The fact that she'd burst right out of the room next to me was indeed a part of what had caused my speechless surprise, but more than anything...*
Ren: "Uh, Himuro... what's up with that outfit?"
*I was taken aback to see her wearing a robe... or a cape... Or something very revealing in any case.*
Rea: "Stop staring."
*That was an impossible request, but this wasn't the time to be talking about stuff like that. I did everything I could to ignore her outfit and focus.*
Ren: "Anyway, your fashion sense aside, where are Father Trifa and Kasumi?"
Rea: "..."
Ren: "Glaring at me won't help, you know."
*I didn't have a clue what was going on. Himuro considered me for a long moment, and then bluntly spoke.*
Rea: "Why don't you leave?"
Ren: "Come again?"
*I had no immediate response for her unexpected answer.*
Ren: "What's that supposed to mean?"
Rea: "Your arrival has screwed things up."
Rea: "To be honest, you're an unwanted wrench in our affairs."
Ren: "..."
Rea: "Are you going to fight him?"
*I silently nodded. By "him", she must have meant Father Trifa.*
Rea: "I figured I'd try as hard as I could to keep that from happening, but you just had to go and mess it all up. Learn to read the mood for once."
Rea: "Do you really think Ayase and I want you to die?"
Ren: "I don't plan on dying."
Rea: "I have no idea where you get that confidence from."
Ren: "I could say the same to you. Your confidence makes even less sense."
*Defeating Valeria Trifa was my job. I was grateful for Kasumi and Himuro's feelings, but I highly doubted they had a way to stop him.*
Ren: "I've come to put an end to this fantasy tale. If someone's gotta do it, then I'll step up to the plate. I'd say I'm the best suited for the job as it is."
Ren: "So let me ask one more time: where are Father Trifa and Kasumi?"
*However, as I expected, Himuro kept quiet and only glared back at me.*
*I didn't want to get into a fight with her here. So I sighed and decided to stop pursuing this thread.*
Ren: "Fine, whatever. I'll go search on my own, so you head outside. Shirou and his buddy Honjou should be out there. Please go with them."
*At any rate, I had a good idea of the situation from the way she talked. Though this wasn't the time to act all carefree, I was now confident I could still avoid the worst case scenario at least.*
*Valeria Trifa was probably lying in wait for me somewhere here. There was no fear of him running off to the eighth Swastika, and he'd keep Kasumi and Himuro safe until it was opened.*
*To him, killing me here would be a waste of a Swastika, but the last one was at the hospital. He could simply cause a massacre there, not to mention he still had Sakurai as backup. He had no need to rush — in fact, getting rid of any obstacles now would make things that much easier for him.*
*It wouldn't be easy, but I was glad he'd gone with that choice. If I beat him here, everything would be over. It was as simple as that.*
*And just as I began to wonder where he could be hiding...*
Rea: "You're not going to ask me anything?"
*Himuro called out to me from behind.*
Rea: "Aren't you curious? I could be a horrible person for all you know."
Rea: "You're not going to ask me stuff like how much I know or how long I've known it?"
Rea: "Lisa and I came across you sitting by the crossing not too long ago, remember?"
Rea: "Aren't you interested in what I was thinking about back then?"
Ren: "Oh yeah, now that you mention it, that did happen, didn't it?"
*Yeah, I remembered. That was when I fought Spinne, and now that I thought about it, Kasumi was also almost kidnapped that day too.*
Ren: "If I remember right, you got mad and said I was the kind of guy who'd die young."
Rea: "Yes. I was quite furious."
Ren: "And you were looking for Father Trifa, weren't you?"
Rea: "Well, yes, I suppose so..."
Ren: "What of it?"
Rea: "What of it...? Is your head screwed on right?"
*Wow, she flat out insulted me.*
Rea: "Is that all you have to say?"
Ren: "Well, yeah? I mean, is there anything else to be said?"
Rea: "Are you serious?"
Ren: "I don't understand what you're getting at."
Rea: "Then what about after that? The next time we saw each other was at school, right?"
Ren: "That's true. I went there to save Kasumi... She must have a thing for Princess Peach, now that I think about it. Well, I guess I'm a major dumbass for letting her get kidnapped over and over again too."
Ren: "But what about it?"
Rea: "So your image of me must have completely changed around that time, right?"
Rea: "You're not going to comment on that?"
Ren: "No. Besides, nothing has changed."
*I fired that reply back without missing a beat. Honestly, this was getting irritating.*
Ren: "Look, what do you want me to say?"
Rea: "Huh?"
Ren: "I think I've already told you how I feel."
*In hindsight, that was a really embarrassing thing to say, so I didn't want to repeat it over and over.*
*Himuro wasn't seriously going to force me to say it again, was she?*
Ren: "You're important to me. Isn't that good enough?"
*I couldn't replicate the mood from back then, so I just looked away as I said it.*
Ren: "I mean, I can tell you're worried about me."
*There was no point in even bothering to check whether she was on my side.*
*And as such, there was no need to waste breath on asking.*
Ren: "Besides, even if you'd told me to leave town before all this began, I probably wouldn't have listened to you anyway."
Ren: "Who in the world could have imagined all this shit going down and messing up the whole place in barely three weeks?"
Ren: "You yourself didn't believe it until it began for real, did you? That's only natural. Nothing weird about that."
*All I cared about was that she was safe. The rest we could turn into a funny story we reminiscenced over a decade later.*
*If I said that...*
Rea: "Ayase said the same thing, you know?"
Rea: "I'm happy, but didn't you ever suppose I wanted to talk about it?"
Rea: "Or rather, wanted to be asked about it?"
*She grabbed my sleeve and looked at me with upturned eyes.*
Rea: "Well, it has been mostly like you've said..."
Rea: "In exchange for not being told anything, I deliberately remained ignorant of everything."
*Himuro started talking about everything that had happened until then.*
Rea: "Lisa and that man never told me any of the specifics. But it's strange — as I grew up, I just sort of realized I knew them anyway."
Rea: "I think it happened right around when I got my first period."
*That should have been a joyous topic. A topic of the process where the body matured to the stage where it could conceive and bear new life.*
*Perhaps it was something instinctive — no matter what kind of animal you were, you picked up on that knowledge naturally without being told by anyone.*
*Humans were no exception. Even if they were shut out from all information about modern society, their three great desires and animal instincts were still active — commands imprinted in genes, if you will.*
*But in Himuro's case, there was something else mixed in all that.*
*The Lebensborn Institute. The Ubermensch Project. I had that information too now.*
*The holy virgin who would give birth to Reinhard. The Swastika was her womb.*
Rea: "At first, I just thought it was one of those delusions you got when you hit puberty."
*Himuro said that with self-derision in her voice.*
Rea: "But when I took a closer look, I realized there were a lot of things weird about my reality. Like how Lisa never aged."
Rea: "Like how Father Trifa never changed at all."
Rea: "You could argue that it was hard for me to see how Lisa aged since I saw her on a frequent basis, but what about him then?"
Rea: "How old does he look to you?"
Ren: "..."
*I had wondered that myself when I first met him.*
Rea: "He looks like he's in his 30s, right?"
*Yet he was Himuro's godfather. That status didn't match up with his age.*
Rea: "You came here with Ayase before, remember? I got chills when I saw him then."
Rea: "I thought, 'Could it be...'"
*"Could it be that my delusions were actually true?"*
*Though not quite of the same nature, I felt a similar kind of fear when I was being run ragged by those dreams of the guillotine at the time.*
*That moment where the fence between reality and unreality became vague. I was lost, in a position where I didn't know which side I was on anymore.*
*It was as if the ground had suddenly collapsed under me one day.*
*I understood quite well. Too well. Unlike me, who still had Kasumi, Shirou, and Marie by my side, this girl had been shivering in fear, stuck in this place that had been growing more and more into a lair of demons with every passing day.*
Rea: "How in the world did I become friends with you and Ayase?"
Rea: "With my personality and that vague anxiety I always kept with me, I figured it'd be better if I never did make friends — or rather, I felt I was incapable of the feat."
Rea: "I was a rather gloomy child. I figured that if me and everyone else were going to die anyway someday, then being alone would be better."
Rea: "I seriously believed that, and so that's how I lived."
Rea: "So why was it that I became friends with you guys? How could I?"
Rea: "Ayase called it an amazing coincidence. I'd like to believe so too... Listen, do you think this feeling is really mine ?"
Rea: "Did I choose it for myself?"
Rea: "What do you like about me?"
Rea: "What do I like about you?"
Rea: "Think about it. Sorry for asking you during such an emergency."
Ren: "It's no problem."
*I didn't find it a bother at all. The weight she was carrying on those fragile shoulders was just too heavy.*
*She hit me with her fears and anxieties head-on, so I'd have liked nothing better than to alleviate as many of them as I could.*
*Even if I might've not looked especially reliable, with those moderately fragile shoulders and gentle features that got me being constantly mistaken for a girl.*

*And that went up to about 200% when it was a pretty girl asking.*
Rea: "What about if it's a girl you love?"

Rea: "Then what about me?"

*Himuro looked at me with an earnest gaze as she spoke.*

*Girls shouldn't say stuff like that.*

*Father Trifa had no intent of harming her. So she probably wouldn't be in any danger so long as she didn't get caught up in the fight, but...*

*She shouldn't have to see me fight Father Trifa. It probably wouldn't be a pretty picture.*
*I didn't know how she felt about him, but regardless of the circumstances, he was like a father to her. There was no way she coud watch me kill him and feel nothing.*
*And besides...*

*The biggest secret there was, one only Shirou and I knew about.*
*But several members of the Obsidian Table seemed to have found it out somehow. That I had killed my surrogate father. That I was a murderer.*
*I'd been told something similar when I first saw Marie at the museum. "Murderer".*
*Maybe they could sense the scent of death on me. Marie had driven her parents to death by madness and execution, and Wilhelm and Rusalka had lived violent lives themselves.*
*Then there was Sakurai... She had her dead brother, and Sister Lisa had lost her son. It was likely the majority of the people involved in this incident either killed or lost family.*

*I couldn't avoid a fight with Father Trifa. I knew persuasion wouldn't work on him.*
*So I would end up taking a life of a father of a girl I cared about not once, but twice.*
Ren: "I don't want you to see me do it."
*I squeezed those words out.*
Ren: "I still don't know whether I should tell Kasumi or keep my silence forever. There's problems with both choices, and it terrifies me."

*Himuro looked up at me and spoke in a sad voice.*
Rea: "So you want to kill someone in secret again?"
Rea: "Not telling anyone? Not showing anything? Keeping everything to yourself again?"
Ren: "That's... not it..."
*If I told Kasumi the truth, she might be hurt. And it undoubtedly would be painful for Himuro if I was to show her my fight with the priest.*
*I definitely felt that way. But what was the actual truth of the matter?*
Ren: "In the end, I think I was just afraid of anyone hating me, that's all."
*I didn't want the girl I loved to hate me. It was a coward's way of thinking.*
Ren: "It's nothing as cool as that."
Rea: "Then how about this..."
*She cupped my face in her hands, then quietly spoke.*
Rea: "You can start being cool now. Don't run. Don't hide. And stop trying to do everything by yourself."
Rea: "I can list off ten of your flaws in no time flat."
Rea: "They drive me crazy, but I also think they're cute."
Ren: "..."
Rea: "You're not mad?"

*I felt like I was being wrapped in a mother's embrace. It was kinda embarrassing, but Himuro wouldn't let go.*
Rea: "I too want to accept reality with my own eyes. I've been too irresponsible up until now."
Rea: "Don't try to show off just for the heck of it. I like the honest you, like right now, more than when you're trying to act stubborn."
Rea: "So please..."
Ren: "..."
Rea: "You're going to settle things, right? Then you have to settle everything. You can't cheat and ignore things inconvenient for you."
Rea: "That's what me and Ayase are trying to do."
Rea: "She said she was going to put everything back in its place."
Ren: "Kasumi did?"
Rea: "Yeah. She's a strong girl, isn't she?"
*Himuro smiled softly, like a girl boasting about her little sister.*
Rea: "You, me, and Yusa are a little destructive, while Ayase is the only one in our group who's assertive and positive minded."
Rea: "Well, thanks to that, she has a sad fate of constantly falling out of the loop."
Rea: "People like her are the strongest there is. She's like the sun, don't you think?"
*Kasumi was sunlight. A symbol of my day-to-day life.*
*A sun I didn't want to lose — one I couldn't live without.*
Rea: "Number VI of the Longinus Dreizehn Orden's Obsidian Round Table, Sonnenkind — the Child of the Sun."
Rea: "I'm the real thing, but my light won't do this time."
*We needed not the sun of Reinhard's battlefield, but the one that illuminated the path to our day to day lives.*
*Kasumi might have been inferior goods to those bastards, but she was just right for us. She was exactly what we needed.*
*That's why I couldn't lose her.*
Rea: "If you want to be with Ayase, then be the man she deserves. Otherwise I won't approve your relationship."
*I couldn't help smiling at the way she put it.*

*I believe that was what people called a matter of opinion.*
Ren: "Okay."
*I nodded, and steeled my resolve.*

*Now that it'd come to this, there was no turning back. I would end everything right here, tonight.*
*Then I would finally return to my sunny world.*
*I swore to that oath, and let Himuro guide me to the church's underground.*
*Kasumi Ayase thought. She was trying to find what it was she could do even at the very last moment. She was not arrogant in any way. She didn't think she could do anything all that overambitious, nor did she come up with any ideas of the like. For better or for worse, she knew fully well how average she was.*
*But neither was she the type to lose spirit. She considered all realistic solutions that she could reasonably carry off in this situation. In a way, her method could have been labeled a compromise. She would first imagine a conclusion she liked, then predict any obstacles she would need to overcome to make that a reality. Was it feasible or not? If it was, what about the odds of success? She wasn't exactly great at theoretical thinking, but she nonetheless did her best with utmost earnestness.*
*The most desirable result would be no one dying at all, of course — for things getting resolved peacefully without conflict. But she knew that was most likely impossible. After all, several people had already died to even reach this stage. But even so, Kasumi wanted to keep the list of casualties from growing any longer. Others may have called her naïve and stupid for that, but she didn't believe that not acting towards the best conceivable conclusion was the right way to go. So even though that prior conversation had not been the most intelligent course of action, she had still chosen to do it.*
*She never believed she could persuade Valeria Trifa. She was never an eloquent speaker to begin with, and her opinions and tenets were probably little but nonsense to the priest. Her few days were no match to the weight of sixty years he bore, and even if that was not the case, changing another's mind with words was already a nigh-impossible feat in human society. How could she even entertain that, when she couldn't even change the mind of a boy she saw almost every day?*
*But though Kasumi held no illusions of conveniently changing someone's convictions and views, she wondered if it was perhaps possible to reach, if only slightly, into their heart. She wondered if it could perhaps, in some way, end up influencing the outcome if the absolute worst truly came to pass. It was wishful thinking, but Kasumi didn't give up on that possibility. And no one would be in the worse for trying at this point.*
*Then there was her current plight. She couldn't speak or move, and to an outsider, it might have looked like she was out cold, but she was actually very much conscious, and could both see and hear. She didn't understand how it was possible, so she decided not to think about it. She had a more important matters to consider anyway. Ren was on his way. He'd come after her. So she was fretting once again about what she should do. Regardless of the how things turned out, it would not be a happy ending.*
*She didn't want Ren to die. She couldn't bear the thought of it, and she didn't want to see him get hurt either. But in that case, how was she to win? Let Valeria Trifa die?*
Kasumi: "No..."
*She muttered that in a voiceless whisper. She didn't want to force Ren to kill someone.*
*Besides, he was up against the man who was like Rea's father, so she couldn't let him. Never. Thus she had to stop Father Trifa somehow. She knew the idea was far beyond the capabilities of someone like her. His shell was harder than iron. If there was something that could break through those curtains and reach him, it would be...*
Kasumi: "There's probably only one thing..."
*She pondered what could reach his heart. She had a feeling she was the only one who could, though why, she didn't know. It defied reason, but she couldn't help inexplicably believing in that baseless assumption. That faith was what had led her here. There was no other way for her to put things back in their place and atone. So she had to hurry and figure out just what it was exactly.*
Kasumi: "You idiot, you got here too fast..."
*The doors opened, revealing her rather impatient white knight. He looked up at her with a seriously desperate look on his face.*
*She was happy, but she wanted to apologize. She was mad, but also sad. She was grateful he'd worried about her. Sorry she'd caused trouble for him. But why couldn't he have just stayed put and waited? It pained her to see Ren getting hurt. Yes. She was in pain.*
Kasumi: "My stomach hurts..."
*It felt like the contractions of labor. She'd figured she'd be going through this sort of experience some day, but...*
Trifa: "Welcome. We've been expecting you, Mr. Fujii."
*But she'd always wanted to give birth to a child in the normal way — between her and the man she loved. Not how her great-grandmother was forced to...*
Ren: "Give Kasumi back."
*She still wished to fulfill that happy dream, so she prayed with all her heart for him to live.*
Trifa: "And if I were to say I cannot?"
Ren: "I'd make you pay."
*She didn't want him to say that when he was shedding tears inside.*
Trifa: "Then a battle to the death, is it?"
Ren: "Yeah, get outta my way."
*She didn't want to force Ren...*
*...to bear that cross again. She had to fulfill her goal to coming to this church as soon as possible. At this rate, she would just end up nothing but an idling fool.*
Kasumi: "I don't..."
*She didn't want that.*
Ren: "Please stay back, Himuro."
*I said that in a low voice to urge the girl behind me to stop. I didn't know just how powerful Father Trifa was, but he was clearly not an opponent to be taken lightly. I needed to face him with my full strength.*
Trifa: "Do what he says, Theresia. You will be in danger if you get too close."
Rea: "..."
Ren: "C'mon, hurry."
Rea: "All right..."
*I could tell she nodded. Now everything was ready to go.*
*All I had left to do was defeat the priest. I hadn't completely figured out how I was going to do that, but I knew for sure that I'd be killed if I wasn't fully resolved. I had to rid myself of all worldly thoughts.*
Ren: "Marie..."
*I called out to my right arm, forming my blade. Marie hadn't shown herself to me in a while, but I could never forget her. I'd probably need to settle things with her somehow once this was all over. I took up a fighting stance, but Father Trifa just kept standing there, completely unarmed.*
*Was he that confident?*
Ren: "What's wrong? You're not going to show your weapon?"
*No, it was more than that — I couldn't sense any intent to fight or kill from him. Wilhelm, Rusalka, Sakurai, and Cain had been absolutely brimming with those, so this had me taken aback.*
*It looked like he had no motivation whatsoever.*
*However...*
Trifa: "Oh, by all means, you are free to come forth. I am not taking you lightly, let me assure you."
Trifa: "Well, that said, it is not like I am particularly wary of you either."
Ren: "..."
Trifa: "Too nervous to take the first step? Very well—"
*Father Trifa closed the gap between us with a single, almost casual step. He then continued casually as though we were having a friendly chat at a café.*
Trifa: "Now then, go ahead and try to cleave off my head cleanly. This is the first and last chance you will get."
Trifa: "You learned how to from Ms. Ayase, yes?"

*Those words lowered the firing hammer within me.*

Trifa: "Put all your spirit into it."
*All my strength.*
Trifa: "Hit me with your strongest strike."
*At that precise moment, I swung my guillotine.*
Trifa: "A slash filled with my respect for that gallant but tender girl."

*What the hell was going on? Father Trifa was totally defenseless, and I hit him head on, so how—*
Trifa: "I did not make the wrong choice. It appears no one stands a chance at defeating Lord Heydrich after all."
*He was uninjured. Completely unharmed. I couldn't cut a single tear into his skin.*

*I hadn't hesitated at all. And the guillotine Marie dwelled in was undoubtedly among the sharpest things in this universe.*

Trifa: "Though most aren't aware of it, it forms the lead of a pencil. It is quite brittle. However..."

*Judging from his attacks, his abilities in single combat were about on the same level as Sakurai, and certainly below Wilhelm. Still, it was incredibly difficult to mount an offense against an opponent with no need to protect himself. I couldn't just keep focusing on one point forever, as he would fight back.*

*I had no choice but to up the number of my attacks. I would land a thousand strikes in the time it took Father Trifa to land ten.*

*So to get back the hundred million yen you dropped, you'd have to scrape together a hundred thousand 1000 yen notes. That was how it worked.*

Trifa: "The source of these miracles is within Gold itself — Lord Heydrich. In other words, if immortality is your desire, He will just absorb you, and same rule applies to bringing back the dead. You will become His slave and shadow, bound to endless strife for all eternity."

Trifa: "Once the Monarch of Destruction is released, all shall be swallowed and bent to His will. Everything will be Him, and He will be everything. The world will be Him, and He will be the world. And all who shall dwell in this new world shall be a part of Lord Heydrich; as His slaves."
Trifa: "This truly is no laughing matter."
*It was far beyond the level of a joke. If what he was saying was true, then the vague fear and anxiety Sakurai felt was all too well-founded.*
Trifa: "Perhaps it was only those like me and Lady Kircheisen who have realized the truth. In hindsight, it truly is unfortunate she ended up parting from us forever."
Trifa: "The Battalion Commanders are insane. Lord Machina aside, Lady Samiel and Lord Schreiber are utter lunatics. They actually believe becoming soldiers — slaves to the Devil's legion — is the greatest honor there could be."
Trifa: "Well, perhaps Bey might share that sentiment, but I cannot imagine the rest of us being much in its favor."
Trifa: "Therefore, I made a decision."
Ren: "..."

*A gunshot reverberated across the wide hall. It had been launched to neither hurt, nor even intimidate. *...Dreizehn.*
Mercurius: "Karl Krafft."
