*And behind the sweet and gentle — in a sense, even meek — disposition of the man lay...*
Mercurius: "Vice Commander Karl Krafft — Mercurius. A name I have long since discarded, but I suppose it should be the most apt way to describe myself to you two."
*...a nature most callous — he paid them no more heed than he would a piece of furniture. At the very least, that was Kasumi's first impression of him.*
Mercurius: "I suppose I ought to humor the friends of my son."
*A terrifying sensation of despair and repulsion took hold of Kasumi's heart.*
*I kicked the remnants of the church's gates out of the way, following after the weird sword as it suddenly zapped out of its place in the ground.*
*And what I saw there—*
Reinhard: "It has been far too long, First Lieutenant."
Beatrice: "It truly has, Lord Heydrich."
*Three people stood at the far end of the chapel, right in front of the altar.*
A thoroughly astonished Sakurai, and a man I would never forget: Reinhard Heydrich, the head of the Obsidian Round Table. 
*In-between them stood a third person — a blonde woman wearing a soldier's uniform.*
*Where did she come from? What on earth was going on here?*
Beatrice: "Why did you stay your hand, Your Excellency? We are hardly more than pebbles in your path — you could have ended us both with ease."
Reinhard: "I nonetheless wished to see the heroic fire spark to life in your eyes as you confronted me. Well done, Valkyria — your gallant visage fascinates me still."
Beatrice: "I see. So I played straight into your hands."
Kei: "Beatrice..."
*I could not contain my amazement at the sound of that name.*
Ren: "Beatrice...?"
*Beatrice? Wasn't that the name of the member who died eleven years ago?*
*Why was she here, alive and acting as though she came to protect Sakurai?*
*Either way, now was not the time to be lost in thought. If she came here to help us, then all the better — I only had to proceed with my initial goal.*
Kei: "...? Kyah!"
*I took a long leap towards Sakurai, coiled my arms around her waist, then leapt backwards again. I had no idea what was going on, but being that close to the golden bastard couldn't have been safe.*
Ren: "You okay?"
Kei: "Ah, Fujii...?"
Ren: "Where'd the priest go?"
*Did she kill him? If that was the case, then where did his body go?*
Reinhard: "I am here."
*Reinhard answered my bewilderment with a thin smile. He pressed his left palm against his chest before narrowing his pair of golden eyes.*
Reinhard: "The Divine Vessel is my flesh and blood. He has fulfilled his role of protecting it, and as a reward, I have inaugurated him into my legion of heroes. You shall meet him again one day."
Reinhard: "As I have blessed you, too, Valkyria. You might have borrowed the power from Leonhart, but materializing one's soul into physical shape is no trifle matter."
Beatrice: "I know. Kei's prayer has certainly helped me to return, but it was your power drawing ever closer to the mortal realm that made it possible to begin with."
Beatrice: "With seven Swastikas open, most of your souls have already transformed into full-fledged Einherjar."
Reinhard: "Indeed. Only the last one remains. And regarding that, I have a proposition."
*Straightening his back, Reinhard retracted his lance. At the same time, Beatrice, too, sheathed her blade and promptly took a few steps back towards us.*
Beatrice: "Thank you for releasing me. I'm sorry for causing you so much trouble."
*With that line, I finally noticed...*
*...that the sword in her hands was without a doubt...*
Ren: "You were the fourth?"
Beatrice: "Yes, but I'll explain later."
Beatrice: "Kei, how long are you planning to keep standing there? Your boyfriend's going to get disillusioned with you unless you get a hold of yourself."
Kei: "Wh—?!"
Beatrice: "Seriously. I expected you to be a bit more of an adult after all these years."
Kei: "S-Shut up! I am perfectly—"
*She shook off my arms and stood on her own two feet.*
*Well, at least it seemed like she got some energy back. The problem, however, was the man facing us from the other end of the hall.*
*Reinhard considered us three for a moment before parting his lips to speak.*
Reinhard: "I shall leave the choice to you."
Reinhard: "We require five colors to activate the Ark of the Covenant. My vessel should still function as Citrinitas, but we need someone to fill the void that Albedo left behind."
Reinhard: "And as luck would have it, the three of you remain."
*After giving each of us a brief glance, he uttered the most insane thing I'd ever heard in my life.*
Reinhard: "So fight each other to the death."
Ren: "..."
Reinhard: "The one who falls shall mark our eighth sacrifice, while the remaining two can split the roles between Albedo, and the chosen one that would grant me the taste of the unknown. Choose your destiny."
Reinhard: "All those I recognize as champions are worthy to become a part of the pentachroma. Go forth now, and fascinate me with your gallant bravery — let me see how your paths diverge and crumble; how the truly valiant prevails."
Ren: "The bastard..."
Kei: "What on earth...?"
Reinhard: "Remember, I can just as easily make the choice for you. In that case, however, I believe it is quite clear to whom each role would fall."
Beatrice: "Indeed, the best option is quite evident, Your Excellency."
*While Sakurai and I were still pale as ghosts, Beatrice — by contrast — answered Reinhard in a stern, direct tone.*
Beatrice: "You want me to slay Kei. Is that correct?"
Reinhard: "Aye. That would be the most natural outcome, First Lieutenant."
Reinhard: "Karl's substitute is bound by duty to amuse me, while your soul has nearly undergone the transformation to Einherjar. It hardly requires a brilliant mind to realize who the least important is among you."
Reinhard: "Her fate is ultimately a matter of time. You may think of this as mercy. A reward, even."
*After all, they would all eventually become a part of him — it was their destiny. Hence, there was no need for doubt or hesitation. Reinhard regarded us in an arrogant manner, completely disinterested in our peril, yet a certain air of near-amicable mildness still lingered about him.*
*The bastard gave that command like it was the most natural thing in the world.*
Reinhard: "This would become your final and only chance to liberate both the man of your heart, as well as your beloved sylph from the fate of having to clash with me. For who would wish to see the faces of their loved ones contort in agony as hellfire consumes them?"
Reinhard: "Hold high the blade of the executioner, instead, and deliver those you love unto the plains of Valhalla. Grant them peace. Hardly an unattractive proposition, would you not agree?"
*He was neither scornful, nor patronizing — rather, I could see genuine consideration in his eyes. The guy was serious, as crazy as that sounded.*
*He genuinely thought that a battle to the death would cause us less woe than trying to challenge him. He truly believed it to be a form of mercy.*
Kei: "I see. So that's the kind of person..."
Beatrice: "Yes. Now you know."
*This was Reinhard Heydrich.*
*The head of the Obsidian Round Table. The Lord to whom the likes of Wilhelm, Schreiber, and Trifa answered — the Harbinger of Beguiling Light.*
*He was neither human, nor a beast — "devil" was the sole word I could come up with to describe him. The bastard was so far off the deep end I couldn't help but rely on banalities to explain his nature.*
Beatrice: "There is nothing more sickening than a tank expressing its love for ants."
Kei: "And nothing more dangerous than a natural calamity that speaks in a human tongue."
*He considered destruction and carnage the highest form of blessing. He believed that being swallowed to become a part of him meant the utmost honor one could receive. He was Mephistopheles — the Beguiling Light.*
Reinhard: "Well? What shall you do?"
*We had but one answer to spit back at him.*
Misc.: "I refuse!"
*Any further conversation would be pointless.*
Ren: "It'll all end if I kill you here."
Kei: "You don't belong in this world."
Beatrice: "And so, before the eighth opens and all is lost..."
Reinhard: "Hah hah... Hahahahaha..."
*Reinhard, gazing down at the three of us — all ready to plunge ourselves into lethal battle – could hardly contain laughter spilling forth from his lips. According to Beatrice, the bastard's power had yet to reach its full capacity.*
*If we ever wished to bring him down... it had to be now.*
Reinhard: "Karl. Karl, my friend, are you listening, by any chance?"
Reinhard: "Ah, how I sincerely wish to adhere to your advice..."
*The massive lance shifted in his grip, its golden tip atremble as something invisible emerged from it...*
*A moment later, a powerful sense of imbalance assaulted me, as if the ground itself had been swept out from under my feet.*
Reinhard: "Alas, I'm afraid the night will have to take a somewhat different course. A master should be ever considerate of his servants."
Beatrice: "No...!"
*Beatrice leapt towards Reinhard as an odd sensation of weightlessness overtook me. Sakurai and I, realizing something ominous was afoot, followed after her.*
Reinhard: "Samiel."
*Right. Even without Schreiber under his command, two of his Imperial Guard still remained.*
Reinhard: "Machina."
*The crimson knightess and the sombre knight — Rubedo and Nigredo. The two indomitable captains of the Einherjar.*
Reinhard: "They are yours. Devour them."
Misc.: "Jawohl, Mein Herr."
Beatrice: "...?!"
Kei: "Beatrice!"
*A gust of crimson fire swept forth from Reinhard's left shoulder, engulfing Beatrice in its seething embrace.*
*As for myself—*
*A black fist with the power of a battering ram — having suddenly emerged from Reinhard's right shoulder — came crashing down on me, dwarfing even Tubal Cain in size.*
*The goddamn freak!*
Ren: "Sakurai!"
*The three of us were swept apart in an instant. Although I leapt into motion just in time to barely evade a direct blow from the giant, the terrible gust of air that came to life as he swung his monster of an arm sent me flying, as if my body was a mere pebble before his might.*
*I felt as if gravity itself had taken a permanent leave from the pocket dimension now keeping us prisoner, lacking a beginning and an end, a ceiling or firm foundation; a void of fierce vertigo boiling in the fury of his golden flame. As I was being flung around in that violent whirlwind of impenetrable darkness, I finally understood what was happening.*
Reinhard: "[Dieser Mann wohnte in den Gruften, und niemand konnte ihm keine mehr,](No mortal man under the sun, no powers that be, no chains that bind shall constrain Him,)[nicht sogar mit einer Kette, binden.](For He dwells in the nether; a soul from the grave is He.)"
Reinhard: "[Er ris die Ketten auseinander und brach die Eisen auf seinen Fusen.](His shackles crumble, His chains fall limp onto the ground before His will; He, the Dweller in the Grave, His cries of mingling agony and madness) [Niemand war stark genug, um ihn zu unterwerfen.](No man, no divine breath that course the veins of this universe hold the power to subdue Him.)"
*The world itself twisted before my eyes as the invocation reverberated in the air. From within the seething sea of molten gold rose an army of a myriad skeletons, welling forth with no end, numbering in the millions.*
*They merged and joined to each other, their bones forming a fortress of the fallen.*
Reinhard: "[Dann fragte ihn Jesus. Was ist Ihr Name?](And so the Lord asked – what manner of beast are you?)"
*This was the world Reinhard craved for.*
Reinhard: "[Es ist eine dumme Frage. Ich antworte.](Your lips breathe folly; your question a sage intellect would never hatch. If you know not what I am – very well, I shall answer.)"
Reinhard: "[Mein Name ist Legion](Know my name, for it is Legion.)—"
*A throne built from a sea of corpses, forged for Reinhard Heydrich alone to rest upon.*
Reinhard: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
*The golden chaos erupted with a thunderous roar, swallowing me, Sakurai, and Beatrice into its depths — before us stretched the sacred halls of Valhalla.*
Reinhard: "[Gladsheim](Apotheosis)――[Gullinkambi fünftes Weltall.](The Fifth Universe of Gold)"
Beatrice: "Agh...!"
*Beatrice Kircheisen could no longer escape. She struggled with all her might, but the hellish flames coiled around her throat like fingers, their iron grip mercilessly preventing any and all attempts at flight.*
Beatrice: "Major Wittenburg...!"
Eleonore: "Spare me that look, Kircheisen. It has been sixty years — we have stories aplenty to share."
Beatrice: "I..."
Eleonore: "Aye, well done. I am pleased to see you returned. It would appear my participation in Kristoff's farce had not been entirely wasted effort. You did well in meting out the rightful punishment for the mongrel. Now claim your reward. "
Beatrice: "Hgh— Hghaaaaaahhh...!"
*An inferno violent enough to melt even steel swallowed Beatrice, and plunged into the depths of chaos like a giant snake, carrying the two women to their designated field of battle.*
Eleonore: "I will not let anyone interfere. You and me, we shall return to those days gone by,  and spend nights reliving our heroic deeds. I have waited long for this. "
Beatrice: "I... I too..."
*Enveloped by a fresh wave of hellfire, Beatrice steeled her resolve. She knew it would eventually come down to this — in fact, she too had been awaiting this hour just the same. The crimson knightess before her was but a shadow of her former superior — a mere husk of the woman she once respected from the bottom of her heart. The two of them had braved countless battlefields together, weathering storms of gunfire on several occasions. Beatrice could hardly bear to look at her in this state — the sight filled her chest only with anguish. Nonetheless, the immortal princess of blue steel — swallowing her tears — addressed the other with a loud cry.*
Beatrice: "I will save you, Major Wittenburg. You have cast aside your sword, pride, even humanity—"
Beatrice: "So long as you stand bereft of those, I will never yield to you!"
Eleonore: "Haha... Hahahahahahahahaha—"
*Stern and vigorous, yet foolish and reeking of inexperience — the famed Valkyrie of Thrud, the lily of the battlefield.*
Eleonore: "Don't mock me, whelp!"
*Eleonore demanded that the girl remain in her service for all eternity.*
Kasumi: "Wh—?!"
Shirou: "The hell's going on?!"
*Before they knew it, the underground of the church — the chamber of the Obsidian Table — had been filled with countless skeletons. They emerged from walls, the floor, the ceiling — everywhere — enveloping the room in a white mass of bones.*
Mercurius: "Too late. You cannot escape now."
*Still on his seat at the table, Mercurius' lips curled into a faint smile.*
Mercurius: "The Creation Figment of the Beast is bereft of weakness — no one can destroy it. Once swallowed, you have no choice but to join the Legion of eternal slaves. Although..."
*Without even glancing at the man, Shirou pulled the trigger of his gun, shattering Mercurius' cranium. Yet the obsidian shade continued his tirade, seemingly unaffected by losing half of his head.*
Mercurius: "Indeed, struggle with all your might. The transmutation of demons, after all, is a feat befitting the weak and fragile, not entirely unlike yours truly. It might be as well that you — humans — hold the key to the end of eternal recurrence. I must confess, I in part even envy your vigorous spirit. "
Shirou: "Babble-babble. You ain't one for making sense, are ya?"
*The bullet had most certainly hit him right in the head, but instead of causing damage, it seemed to have been swallowed into a dark mist the moment it touched him. For not a single scratch blemished the obsidian shade once Shirou turned around to face him.*
Shirou: "The more I look at your mug, the less I can believe it."
*Clad in the darkest of robes that made the contours of his lean frame obscured like a hazy shadow, the long-haired man did not seem older than twenty, his face a mirror image of a person Shirou knew all too well.*
Kasumi: "Um, d-did you say you were Ren's father...?"
*Kasumi spoke with a trembling voice — the shock from that statement overwhelmed her even more so than the emergence of the castle of the dead. She needed an answer, no matter how terrifying it might be.*
Kasumi: "Answer us! How are you related to Ren?!"
Shirou: "Or rather, who is Ren to ya?"
*Father? Son? Shirou would not believe such drivel. Still, the man before him must have been related to Ren in one way or another.*
Mercurius: "I called him my son as a mere figure of speech."
*The Obsidian Mercury answered their animosity and befuddlement with a thin smile. Such a poignant question — the emotion men called friendship was indeed most dazzling. Even a jester like himself could comprehend the beauty of that ephemeral glimmer. Thus, once asked, he could do naught but provide an answer.*
Mercurius: "He is my shadow — my own creation."
*The transmutation of a demon; if he could not wield the girl and her power, then all he had to do was to create one who could.*
Mercurius: "To transcend infinity, and lay waste to the eternal spiral of recurrence. Everything I have prepared, I did so for his sake alone."
*The Longinus Dreizehn Orden had been merely an experiment — a little test before putting his true design into motion.*
Mercurius: "He is my Ahnenerbe."
*A sentient terminal that had been in better synchrony with Ewigkeit — his sorcery — than anyone else.*
Mercurius: "The one true violinist of our Day of Wrath."
Machina: "Yes, you are like me."
*A sombre voice — heavy like an iron hammer — reached my ears through the raging whirlwind.*
Machina: "You cannot imagine how long I have waited for this day, Brother."
Ren: "Ghaaaaaah...!"
*I couldn't tell how long it took — maybe a moment, or perhaps aneternity — but before I knew it, I had found myself in an unfamiliar place.*
Ren: "Where is this?"
*Under the gaze of skies the color of lead, I landed on a stone floor cold as ice, and reddish brown like congealed blood.*
*It took but a mere glance to understand that thousands of men had lost their lives in this place. It looked almost like a...*
Ren: "A colosseum...?"
*An architectural design of olden times, dating back to ancient Rome. This massive thing looked just like it. And... and I...*
Ren: "Ghh...!"
*I collapsed onto my knees, assailed by an abrupt, splitting headache and a sudden lack of air, like my lungs had ceased to function. It felt as if something mortally ominous had been trying to tear through my chest and skull to escape into the open.*
Machina: "A nostalgic sight, isn't it?"
*A stout man towered before me, clad in black, his eyes like those of a dead fish. Yet an undeniable aura of ruination hung about him — I remembered seeing him before.*
Ren: "Machina..."
*That was what they called him — a word that described him in two senses.*
*A machine whose sole desire was to put an end to all — to lower the curtains on the play of life.*
*The sole survivor and champion of this gauntlet of malice. A man who had been born from the deaths of thousands upon thousands of soldiers.*
Machina: "This is where we were born."
*Götz von Berlichingen — once a war hero, now a mere shell with no recollection of his past glory.*
*He and I...*
Machina: "May these grounds be awash with our blood one more time, Brother."
*We were brothers in the strongest sense of the word — we shared the same flesh and blood, came from the same father.*
Reinhard: "Welcome to my abode, Leonhart."
*Left behind by the other two, Kei alone stood in the wide and exquisite hall, face to face with the Golden Beast. Not even a semblance of the church remained. It had transformed into a majestic throne room that reminded Kei more of a lavish and ancient temple than a sanctuary to the meek Christian faith. In any case, she could tell what had happened.*
Reinhard: "We are in the Castle of Wewelsburg."
Machina: "The cradle of the Obsidian Table—"
Eleonore: "And the Valhalla of our souls."
Mercurius: "Well then, let the curtains rise on tonight's final Grand Guignol."
Reinhard: "You of younger blood might not know, but we — the old members — have spent many a night discussing the truths of the world in this very place."
*The Castle of Wewelsburg was a gathering place of the Obsidian Round Table when it was still but an innocent eccentricity of a select few men.*
Reinhard: "Only a hundred or so knights had been permitted entry to this castle: Himmler, Hess, Haushofer, Dietrich, Eicke, Manstein, Marseille... then Rudel and Wittmann. Their names, at least, should be familiar to you."
*The titans of the Third Reich, the heroes of the Nazi regime. Reinhard turned his back to Kei, and started up the steps to his throne with sluggish movements, as if savoring the memories of his nostalgic surroundings.*
Reinhard: "This place was their designated Valhalla; their promised heaven — Gladsheim — where the souls of heroes took nest after death. Although, only I remain from the initial members at this point. All of the others ended up becoming a part of the castle. "
*The "Weltall" — the promised fifth universe — built from the bones of millions. Yet depending on perspective, it was also but a pit of chaos — an abyss, no more. Death in this place meant being shackled to their bony walls for an eternity. Having finally reached his throne, Reinhard faced Kei once again.*
Reinhard: "And so I find myself wondering what shall happen next. I cannot imagine Machina losing in battle, though such an outcome would only gladden me even more. The same can be said of Valkyria. She lacks the strength to overpower Samiel, yet even if she did somehow manage to accomplish that feat, it would not amount to a loss in my pentachroma.  "
Kei: "Why...?"
*That was different from what she heard before. In fact, Reinhard himself said that they would need a substitute for Schreiber — it took time for Einherjar to be revived. They couldn't possibly make it in time till the seventh seal opened.*
Reinhard: "Karl is currently here in this castle."
Kei: "..."
Reinhard: "The man is capable of instantly reassembling souls that have fallen here. After all, it was Karl, Isaak, and I who installed this castle within the realm that exists beyond the reaches of recurrence. The spell beats alive still, and Karl's powers are on another level while he remains within the walls of this fortress. Reanimation. Revival. Reformation. Those who fall here can be revived and reassembled without limit. The true blessing of the Swastika that you all desired is a miracle that allows this phenomenon to occur outside the castle walls. Or should I say, allows it to seep into the physical realm. In any case, the result is the same. "
Kei: "Then..."
*This was no good — she couldn't imagine a way out of this situation. At this point, the pentachroma would remain intact, regardless of what happened. Even should all parties fall dead during their respective battles through some form of miracle, the sorcerer would simply revive them right away as part of the Beast's army of Einherjar. The only move to hinder their scheme — in other words, killing them on an already open Swastika — had been sealed with the emergence of the castle. And all because they found the idea of opening the eighth Swastika with anything but a large-scale display of carnage dull beyond imagination.*
Reinhard: "An endless ocean of chaos that swallows the dead without limit, and is destined to erupt once the time is right."
*Reinhard made a self-mocking smile.*
Reinhard: "They call me a devil, and my abode hell, but in truth, I am nothing more than an insignificant gravekeeper."
Reinhard: "And you are valkyries — grim reapers — who hunt and fatten me with souls; artisans to haul building materials for my citadel. I suppose one can call you a manifestation of my own greed. In any event, you have performed splendidly.  And with Karl back in the castle, your role now remains exactly the same within its walls as it was outside them. Leonhart, do you still refuse to supply me with cadavers? You should know that there is a certain benefit to obeying me. Well, how do you answer? "
Kei: "I..."
*Kei hesitated. Her feelings had not wavered, nor did she feel like abandoning her struggle. It was just that... she could not understand. Why had he been so obsessed with the construction of the castle, and why on earth did he require outside help? If playing at war was all he desired, he should have done so on his own without involving them.*
Reinhard: "Your life had not been laden with fortune and mirth, this you cannot deny."
Reinhard: "How many tears, and how much blood have you shed? I doubt you found much enjoyment in that life, nor would you care to repeat any of it. But know this: that path is without a conclusion. Suppose that you manage to defeat me. That Karl changes his mind. You would still be a girl bound by her lion sword. No matter how hard you struggle to change it, your destiny will plunge you back into an abyss of grief. That is the hellish nature of this world, this ghetto. And so I will destroy it. Bring me souls to further that end. "
Reinhard: "Karl designed his spell in order to disrupt that very recurrence. The more souls we gather in a single spot, the more shall the eternal spiral be disrupted, and sooner or later, it will rupture. You could, in a sense, think of us as a blood clot. Although, the process is nowhere near as trifling as I make it sound. After all, our foe is a system that governed mankind from its very cradle. A few thousand souls would be far from enough to induce a thrombosis inside it. Which consequently leaves me with only one option — swallowing you all. "
Kei: "..."
*Reinhard uttered the words so naturally that for a moment, Kei had trouble understanding what he had meant.*
Reinhard: "I will devour past, present, and future alike — up until the blood of the system clots, and this ghetto ruptures. My Legion shall swell and spread till my jubilation is saturated and hell bursts forth into the realm. And once the god of this system is torn down from his throne, you shall all find yourselves liberated from the torment of eternal repetition. "
Kei: "Are you out of your mind...?!"
*Utter insanity. Reinhard might have transcended all mortal men that ever lived, but not even he could sustain the weight of billions of souls. To Kei, he now looked more like a raving lunatic than a godlike being.*
Reinhard: "I will continue onwards, till I chance upon something I have yet to ravage."
*Reinhard regarded her with a smile. This was not a question of possible or impossible — he would simply do it.*
Reinhard: "That is the only way I know how to live. And if I succeed, I might meet the architect of the current law — be it a god or a devil. Do you not feel the heart in your chest begin to race? Our immortal Legion shall declare war against the foolish creator, all in order to escape the mundane law he bound us with. I would lead, and you — Einherjar — would follow. A perfect stage for our long-awaited Dies Irae. Although that, too, is merely a selfish ambition of mine. Karl most likely has a different goal, and alternate means to achieve it. This current struggle of ours is but a curtain raiser for the true performance."
Reinhard: "Hence, I ask again."
*The glimmer of the Beast's golden eyes left Kei spellbound, urging the girl to sacrifice herself, to bind her soul and bones unto the eternal walls of Valhalla.*
Reinhard: "This has already been decided, Leonhart. You have but two choices."
*To bend the knee of her own will, or have her soul be subdued before his magnificence. She knew how foolish and utterly ridiculous it was to try and challenge Reinhard Heydrich alone — an action only for the mentally unsound. She knew, but...*
Kei: "A stupid question."
*Kei readied Hihi'rokane. Having spent all her strength in the battle with Valeria Trifa, she could barely stand on her own two feet before this supreme being, let alone engage in a proper fight with him — she felt like her very soul might evaporate any minute. However—*
Kei: "I won't back down. I've already told you I refuse."
*Even when faced with a checkmate...*
Kei: "You may recall that I'm a dumb child and a sore loser."
*...she would flip the board upside down, betting on a miracle. It was too early to give up.*
Reinhard: "You do not fully comprehend the cruelty of this ghetto's nature. What if I told you that this was not the first time you pointed your blade at me? Your life need not end in agony and terror for the thousandth time. "
*Kei answered Reinhard's lament with a wry smile.*
Kei: "Me giving up won't rid you of your foreknowledge, Lord Heydrich."
Kei: "Or rather, the sole reason you're doing this is because you already know I will not give in."
*In that case, she would simply have to remain loyal to her other selves. And believe in her future self.*
Kei: "I'll admit that I do not truly understand your words."
*Ghetto? Recurrence? She'd neither heard of, nor felt such things.*
Kei: "But being the fool that I am, I'd given my all in everything I did to survive. I found myself lost at crossroads, made my fair share of mistakes, but in the face of a thousand regrets, I never once gave up.  "
*She pressed on even as her very soul begged her to quit.*
Kei: "And now I stand before you proud. I wish to remain true to myself to the very end."
*She would make choices by herself, for herself. It mattered little what she did or didn't do in her alternative lives, or what destiny itself had dictated.*
Kei: "Ridiculous. You are just a weak man who could not believe in himself. A truly strong man would not blame fate or this foreknowledge of yours, and rather hold his head high, carrying the cross of hard choices on his own shoulders."
*Kei knew of one such man. She might have been overestimating him — a manifestation of "love sees no faults", in a sense.*
*But that was how she truly felt, and the very reason why she chose him. There was no way she'd allow the Golden Beast to mock her decision.*
Kei: "I won't let you dismiss us with your foolish delusions! I stand here now of my own choosing! "
Reinhard: "I see."
*Reinhard silently acknowledged Kei's outburst.*
Reinhard: "Your words resonate deeply within me. I cannot deny it — both Karl and I are dull men. At this point, it is but an old habit of ours. We tend to unconsciously imagine dozens of possible moves — both good and bad — and end up testing them all. It was not my intention to dismiss your passion.  "
Reinhard: "Well, I suppose this is the end for our parley."
*Reinhard languidly motioned for Kei to come closer... ...urging her to attack him, provided she truly believed in the veracity of her choices to that extent.*
Reinhard: "Gift me with the unknown — I'm not fond of being disappointed."
Kei: "You won't need to tell me twice."
*Reinhard remained seated on his throne. His lance had been unsheathed, but it did not appear he planned to fight her on equal grounds. But Kei did not care. Reinhard was welcome to look down on her. Their powers were on completely different levels, and even trying to imagine what the garish man would be capable of felt like a notion both futile and laughable. Now was not the time to worry about appearances. Particularly since her allies were likely facing situations just as impossible as hers.*
Kei: "Everyone else is fighting their own battles as we speak."
*And so, she wouldn't allow herself to be the only one to take the easy way out.*
Kei: "Prepare yourself, Lord Heydrich."
*Kei darted forward, quickly ascending the steps of the throne.*
Kei: "I am very much aware of your near-invincibility."
*His soul carried the density of a Legion. Kei's sword couldn't even scratch the Divine Vessel, which made her understand — to a sobering degree — how utterly powerless she was against the genuine Gold.*
Kei: "However—"
*Now the situation was different. A wound must have remained on his invulnerable body — a hole that Kei's sword had pierced when she defeated Valeria Trifa. It should not have healed until the eighth Swastika was opened. He had a lethal crack on his body.*
Kei: "Could it be that your tried to get me to surrender—"
*Kei let out a cry upon reaching the top of the steps, and plunged her sword into the Beast, who still sat motionless upon His throne.*
Kei: "—only because you aren't really in a state to fight yourself?!"
*Not even the Obsidian Mercury could possibly reassemble in time the gehenna of souls that whirled within this man. And if the girl succeeded in felling the Beast, all the Einherjar in his service would likely end up incapacitated in the absence of their master. Whether it was an hour, a minute, or a mere few seconds—*
Kei: "I will defeat you and eradicate Karl Krafft from this world!"
*Such was her only choice. No alternatives presented themselves. This was not a question of possible or impossible — she simply had to defeat Him to survive.*
Reinhard: "A poor and wretched maiden you may be, yet not without charm."
*The Gold had yet to move an inch in response to the girl's fast approaching steel. And thus, at the summit of Valhalla, a fight that would decide the fate of everything had begun to unfold.*
Eleonore: "And so it begins."
*Eleonore von Wittenburg narrowed her eyes. As an Einherjar, she could tell the state of her master's mind.*
Eleonore: "Lord Heydrich is pleased. Aren't you glad, Kircheisen? The little cur has been given the chance to become one of us."
Beatrice: "..."
*Beatrice did not respond to those words. She merely glanced around the room in silence, letting out a brief sigh.*
Beatrice: "Now I see what's going on."
*As one of the initial members of the Obsidian Round Table, she of course knew this hall... knew this castle.*
Beatrice: "What a depressing Valhalla, Major. I can't say I have a single good memory of this place. I can most certainly see why Lord Machina would despise it."
Eleonore: "Hmph. Ever the loose-tongued simpleton, I see."
*Not many could taunt the stern and short-tempered Eleonore without their blood freezing in terror. Yet there was one person in this whole world whose insolence she welcomed.*
Eleonore: "Machina's feelings do not concern me. Has Brenner's hypocrisy infected your mind? All you fools ever did was suck on your thumbs and watch us do all the work."
Beatrice: "That... I cannot deny."
*An apt way to describe their relationship would be to liken them to a pair of sisters whose polarizing personalities only amplified the bond they shared. Yet now, those very same sisters were about to enter into a bout of life and death.*
Eleonore: "Kristoff flogs himself with guilt, Brenner feigns ignorance, and you loiter around, accomplishing nothing. The decades changed precious little. Mongrels, dimwits, and failures, the lot of you. And even in the very end, you only aggravate my woes. Does this farce know no end...? "
*Following a short pause, Eleonore let out a muffled snort as if reveling in the situation, unable to contain the sheer jubilance washing over her heart.*
Eleonore: "Dimwit."
*Even her curses carried faint glimmers of affection.*
Beatrice: "I bet you looked just like this when you killed Lisa."
Eleonore: "Oh? You saw that?"
Beatrice: "No. But I can tell."
*As the fourth Tubal Cain, Beatrice was indeed a witness to Lisa Brenner's demise. Although she possessed no actual memories of the deed, she had been able to vaguely sense what her former superior did from the other Cains.*
Beatrice: "I see you still look after your subordinates, Major. First Lisa, and now me..."
*Kei and even Cain.*
Beatrice: "You orchestrated everything, haven't you? I never took you for a scheming type... You have changed."
*Hiding behind a veil of comradery, Eleonore was, in truth, guiding the Divine Vessel into a trap. She never bothered to soil her own hands directly, instead manipulating Kei, Ren, Beatrice, and Cain to do her bidding.*
Beatrice: "You're acting like His Excellency the Vice Commander."
*An utterance soaked deep in sarcasm, for there was not a single member of the Obsidian Table who would have enjoyed being likened to Karl Krafft.*
Eleonore: "Kristoff is cancerous. I had to find a way to do away with him."
*Eleonore, however, answered in calm voice. It was certainly not in her nature to take a roundabout approach; in fact, she would have loved nothing more than to take care of everything with her own hands, but...*
Eleonore: "I cannot harm the Divine Vessel. Bound by that oath, I had no choice but to look for outside help. And the little cur of the Sakurais proved perfect for the task."
Eleonore: "She had both the motive and the will to challenge Kristoff. Power was the sole thing she lacked. What do you suppose would be the best approach in such a situation? Simple — stir the pot until she has no choice but seek allies. The plan came to me the moment I found out what had been in store for Brenner. No little girl could possibly bear the truth of Valhalla, and hence, I could read her actions like an open book. As long as I could get that guillotine-toting whelp to aid her, their confrontation with Kristoff was merely a natural turn of events. It is unfortunate that we ended up losing Schreiber in the process... but I suppose I can count it as a victory still, for we managed to pull you out in exchange. "
*The Divine Vessel fell, and they managed to find themselves a substitute for the void left by Albedo. There was nothing left to hinder the revival of Gold.*
Eleonore: "All is well that ends well. You could say everything is proceeding according to plan. Our design was not so frail to be hindered by weathervanes unable to even pick a side. It was all mere child's play, Kircheisen. You compared me to the Vice Commander, yet what I did was no more than a crude imitation of Kristoff's games. And you show no progress. How many times now have you ended up blindly dancing to the mongrel's tune? "
Beatrice: "I suppose there's not much I can say in my defense."
*Only eight of them still lived — seven if one discounted Sonnenkind. As the acting commander of the Obsidian Table, the Divine Vessel played everyone like pawns on a chessboard for over fifty years. Some he used without their knowledge, some feigned allegiance with hopes of eventually outsmarting him, while others — the ones who tried to rebel — he simply destroyed. Yet this man, whom no one could thus far topple, was easily outmaneuvered by the crimson knightess. And in a game that wasn't particularly her strong suit, either.*
Beatrice: "Quite impressive. And much of it unplanned."
*She hadn't enough time to weave her plans. It was likely that over half of her moves had to be improvised in the midst of action. Her approach was rough, and the victory she boasted of could, in a way, be viewed as a result brought about only by luck. Thus, Beatrice had but one question to ask.*
Beatrice: "Tell me, just for future reference: where does your power stem from? How can you maintain such strength?"
Eleonore: "I have faith."
*Eleonore gave her answer without a moment's hesitation.*
Eleonore: "Unbending faith in both my loyalty and the capabilities of my subordinates. Kristoff thought of you only as a convenient bait to entice me in his reformation of the pentachroma, but I knew you were not so idle a woman. I had faith in your victory — in your ability to turn the tables and exterminate the fool. For I also knew that no choice I made could ever work in Lord Heydrich's disfavor. "
*Ironclad zeal. Loyalty so fervent it threatened to scorch one's body from the inside out. Absolute faith in her veracity was the very foundation of Eleonore von Wittenburg's heroic spirit.*
Eleonore: "As such, my soul is bereft of even a speck of doubt. I stand firm and resolute — I will never waver."
Eleonore: "No swindler's sermon, however sweet, can get to someone who has no gaps in their heart. Do you understand, Kircheisen? Your own frivolity has ruined you. Kristoff — Valerian Trifa — was only left in charge of the Divine Vessel — a task that was clearly too grand for his meager abilities, I might add — because he could originally invade the hearts and minds of others. That man can become anyone he wishes. "
Eleonore: "In a way, you too, could call him an abyss of boundless chaos, although in a different sense from Lord Heydrich. He can pry into the hearts of others, and produce countless identities and acts for any given situation: features that induce affection, shadows that provoke resentment, and, when needed, even clowns that incite belittlement."
*An ability he might've lost alongside his body, yet the keen intuition he had cultivated over many years was still very much present. After all, mind control had already been one of the strongest weapons in the clergy's arsenal.*
Eleonore: "In the end, reading the actions and emotions of you weathervanes was no more intricate to him than breathing. A wicked saint...? Don't make me laugh. A man carrying two contradicting names — what is he, if not Legion? You must have thought him a raving madman, but that is a misconception on your part; instead, you ought to realize that every time you speak to him, you are talking to a different man. "
*A woman whose heart and behavior remained steadfast and unbending, regardless of the opponent. A straight, ever-consistent vector untainted by doubt or hesitation. Yet Eleonore was hardly an exception — all three Battalion Commanders serving in Reinhard's Legion were such beings. Souls not even the Divine Vessel could hope to lead astray. For only a plating clad in pure gold could ever entice the three.*
Eleonore: "The fool should know his place — the likes of him would never become Lord Heydrich."
*A trail of thick, billowing smoke escaped Eleonore's lips as she paused to light the cigar she held between her teeth. Her words had been those of deep-rooted contempt.*
Eleonore: "Did that satisfy your curiosity?"
Beatrice: "I suppose it did. At the very least, it eased my mind a bit."
*Beatrice shrugged her shoulders — all the old grudges and regrets meant little to her at this point.*
Beatrice: "Well, I've been meaning to get back at him for a long time now. I'm grateful for your help, Major... although this whole situation leaves me with mixed feelings. As a result, not only was I granted another chance to meet the little girl, I could also prevent her death. "
*On the other hand, all she appeared to have done was jump out of the frying pan and straight into the fire.*
Beatrice: "Would you say I'm acting the mother hen? Still, I can't say I like the ring of that word very much. I quite enjoyed being able to remain young forever, you know. In any case, this is the extent of what I could do for them; the rest is up to the little ones themselves. Babysitting others was never a strong suit of mine, anyway. "
*Beatrice readied her blade with a self-mocking chuckle. From now on, it would be time to settle some personal business. Caring for, protecting, and guiding the young like an elder was certainly a lovely experience, but it never was the true face of Beatrice. She was to take her superior's advice and believe in her comrades.*
Beatrice: "I'm the type who prefers to chase after others."
Beatrice chased her superior all her life, through a turbulent era of roaring gunfire; a tempestuous period writ in blood and smoke and mayhem, echoing with the cries of dying soldiers. Her relentless struggle would yield to nothing and no one: not to misery, nor to anger or tears. 
Beatrice: "And I can say that because of you, Major Wittenburg. Because you were there."
*Ever since her time as a naïve little girl fresh out of military school.*
Beatrice: "There is a person I respect from the very bottom of my heart. She is a touch intimidating, somewhat haughty, and unbelievably idealistic. You ever try working under a person like that? Someone who believes that everyone is capable of the same things they are? And to make matters worse, the innate abilities of that boss of mine were unparalleled to begin with. "
Beatrice: "All I ever did was make her angry. The words idiot, fool, and dimwit became almost like my second names."
*Her Major taunted, smacked, and reprimanded her on a daily basis, yet she would always, without fail, wait for her to catch up.*
Beatrice: "I chased and chased and chased..."
*How far would she take her? What would she show her next? Would she, in time, become a better subordinate? A person closer to the ideal she represented? And would she eventually grant her words of praise? She toyed with such ideas like a maiden struck by Cupid's arrow. And yet—*
Beatrice: "Is this travesty of a place the conclusion of our journey? Our Valhalla?!"
*A burst of lightning erupted from the tip of Beatrice's blade, cleaving the cigar between Eleonore's teeth in two, scorching it to ash in an instant.*
Beatrice: "It's miserable, Major!"
*What happened to her? What could have changed her so much? Did her true, righteous self perish in the fires that consumed Berlin that night? However, her poignant imputation fell on deaf ears.*
Eleonore: "Nonsense."
*Eleonore smiled, her eyes remaining closed.*
Eleonore: "I was expecting something more sensible from you. The timing of it is impeccable, though. For you see, I had a similar question to pose you."
*The lightning speed of her charge had been lauded by all who caught a glimpse of Beatrice Kircheisen on the battlefield. Closing one's eyes before her in the midst of battle was nothing short of suicide — hardly an attitude that befit a Battalion Commander with a myriad of battles under her belt. Could this have been a mortal blunder on Eleonore's part? Not at all.*
Eleonore: "I have been thinking as of late. It's hardly anything of consequence, really, but considering the utter hogwash you've thrown at me just now, I've grown somewhat confused."
*Full of openings. Defenseless. Her eyes closed, hands locked in front of her chest, head cocked to the side — Eleanore was deep in thought. No matter how one looked at it, this was the perfect chance to strike, one that only a fool would fail to exploit. Yet things were not always as they seemed.*
Beatrice: "Confused about what?"
*No openings would ever blemish the guard of the crimson knightess, the fierciest of all Einherjar. Those who knew how to look would be able to tell right away. After all, heat rivaling that of a nuclear explosion awaited its chance to burst forth from her skin.*
*One could stop a gas leak. One could stop a fire. But no sane person would think of even approaching an erupting volcano.*
Eleonore: "Well, my question can wait."
*Her eyes remained closed as the signal of battle echoed almost tenderly.*
Eleonore: "Come. The moment I draw will be your last."
*The time for words was past, for their conversation would now be carried on through battle.*
*A flash of lightning, and the valkyrie's supersonic blade was already at Eleanore's throat. Beatrice had no intention of waiting for a non-existent opening to begin with. To brave the erupting volcano head-on — the courage and willpower required for such a feat was the first wall to cross before one could hope to defeat Eleanore von Wittenburg.*
*Fangs that tore out one's jugular the instant they were given the chance. The moment you stopped your advance would be the moment you met your maker — the Battalion of Three meant a threat of such caliber. To meet Eleonore's blade in battle meant mustering the resolve to leap straight into the scorching flames. Her pretentious act of vulnerability was merely the crimson knightess' way of testing Beatrice's character. And the Valkyrie passed the test with flying colors.*
*Her abrupt slash, however, could only cut the air in front of Eleonore's face. Rubedo was retreating; the Valkyrie was pursuing.*
Beatrice: "You needn't say another word! I won't let you!"
*Beatrice could neither allow her to escape, nor could she herself retreat. Maintaining a close distance was her only means to victory. Allowing Eleonore to pull out her projectiles — to open the gates of the infernal cannon — would usher in certain defeat.*
*Beatrice's blade was lightning itself — it danced in the air viciously, without mercy, yet never losing its grace. The Valkyrie's strength originated from an entirely different source compared to the likes of Wilhelm or Schreiber, for she was a soldier through and through. A genuine knight. Her finesse was the result of rigorous training, while the countless battles she partook in polished her murderous technique to the point where it could be considered a work of art. She had reached the pinnacle of human capabilities. Beatrice might have received tutelage from the devil, but she never once sold her soul.*
*Nonetheless, her strikes only found air, not flesh. At a glance, the ever-retreating Eleonore might've seemed to be at a disadvantage, but her arms remained crossed, while her expression retained the glimmer of superiority. She couldn't have perceived all of Beatrice's slashes with her eyes — they were but ephemeral glimmers of light. Not even the crimson knightness could surpass the speed of lightning. And yet she kept on dodging, taunting the other's blade as it only struck air.*
Eleonore: "I know how you fight; I've seen your steel dance countless times."
*Their difference lay in experience. Although the two fought for the first time, Eleonore knew her subordinate's steel like the palm of her hand. And how could she not? The two had braved countless battlefields together, and fought side-by-side on numerous occasions. Moreover, Eleonore had fought Schreiber — a beast of similarly breathtaking velocity — in the past. Only once while they still lived as mortals.*
Eleonore: "And in here—"
Eleonore: "I spent nearly every day watching the very same speed."
*That was Valhalla. Such were the Einherjar. For them, morning meant a set of deadly duels, and with evening came the time for resurrection. After sixty years of that daily life, it was no wonder that lightning could no longer scare her.*
Eleonore: "Although my battles with him were hardly different from a perpetual check, ever defying a conclusion..."
*Absolute accuracy versus certain evasion — a bout of contradictions.*
Eleonore: "...I came to learn some new tricks as well."
Beatrice: "...?!"
*A flock of submachine guns manifested behind Eleonore's back.*
Beatrice: "Schmeisers?!"
*A tempest of fire and explosions raged in front of Beatrice's face. It took but a moment for all twenty guns to completely empty their magazines. It was a number not even the Valkyrie could deflect, nor a distance at which she could evade without first breaking off her pursuit.*
*Changing directions, she plunged sideways to escape the barrage. The remains of once-gorgeous floor tiles scattered all about her in the air, while numerous statues — formerly magnificent works of art — became riddled with holes before shattering into myriad pieces. What on earth—*
Eleonore: "Wipe that stupid look off your face."
*A distance of over ten meters opened between the two in an instant, and just like that, dozens upon dozens of flaming "spears" went flying at the bewildered Beatrice. Those were—*
Beatrice: "Panzerfausts?!"
*What was going on? Neither were weapons Eleonore would use. Eleonore's voice echoed over the incoming torrent of destructive projectiles, addressing Beatrice with the tone of a tutor scolding an overly dimwitted pupil.*
Eleonore: "This should not elicit surprise from you. How many thousands do you honestly think I had to prepare for my weapon?"
*A thousand soldiers would be needed merely to operate it. And to account for maintenance and defense, one had to prepare three times that number. Eleonore's true weapon was a mobile cannon, as well as a whole battalion operating it.*
Eleonore: "Tactical corp maneuvers are within my capacity."
Beatrice: "I see."
*Comprehending the situation in an instant, Beatrice's mind regained its calmness. Compared to the barrage of Schmeisers, the onslaught of Panzerfausts was both slower and inferior in numbers. Evading the explosives like a thread going through the pins of countless needles, Beatrice once again homed in on Eleonore. As long as no gapless barrage shielded them, her lightning — notably exceeding the speed of bullets — could still get through and pierce any marksman. Unfortunately, Eleonore was far from a regular marksman.*
Eleonore: "Who do you think controls them?"
*Was the crimson knightess the type to command her battalion from the safe confines of her tent?*
Beatrice: "...?!"
*In perfect harmony with the rapidly approaching Beatrice, Eleonore, too, suddenly lurched forward. Her speed was hardly much of a concern — her timing, however, was an entirely different matter altogether. The very moment Beatrice began her instantaneous leap of ten meters, Eleanore shortened the distance by three steps. And not even the electromagnetic Valkyrie could accommodate to the change that swiftly.*
Beatrice: "Tshh?!"
*With her sword still raised high, she rammed her own temple into Eleonore's crafty kick. A clash between the kinetic energy of lightning and a kick infused with monstrous strength — its sheer power defied the scope of language. Beatrice flew backwards, crashing through a pillar before smashing into the wall with force enough to send tremors across the whole of the castle.*
Eleonore: "You're still green."
*Without a moment's delay, countless guns pointed their barrels towards the dust-veiled area where Beatrice had landed.*
Eleonore: "Stand!"
*Her Schmeissers opened fire. A short cry erupted from beyond the veil of dust, but it almost immediately gave way for the sounds of a blade piercing through metal.*
Eleonore: "Yes! That's better! Now fight!"
*As if answering Eleonore, the maiden of war surfaced from beyond the cloud of dust, her platinum blonde locks as strikingly radiant as ever despite being tarnished by a mixture of blood and dirt. She defied subjugation, spitting in the face of defeat, her emerald eyes aflame with unwavering determination as they fixed upon the other woman. The barrage of Schmeissers could no longer halt her advance. Cutting down each bullet from the air, she once again lunged at Eleonore. After all, she still had so much to say.*
Beatrice: "[War es so schmählich,](Forgive me, for I have sinned)――"
*She began her aria of self-discipline, self-scorn, and self-deprecation, mixing a redundant phrase or two into it for the sole reason that she liked the sound of them.*
Beatrice: "[ihm innig vertraut-trotzt'ich deinem Gebot.](Borne of loyalty, your will I once defied)"
*Back in the day, she weaved those words as if predicting the future — was it premonition guiding her back then, or foreknowledge?*
Beatrice: "[Wohl taugte dir nicht die tör'ge Maid,](Forgive me, for I am naught but a fool, never your equal)"
*It was time for her to embrace the sentence of eternal slumber. Her blade and soul now belonged to the champion that awakened her. However— She refused to obey a man who could not surpass her Lieutenant.*
Beatrice: "[Auf dein Gebot entbrenne ein Feuer;](Let your crimson pyres have their fill)"
*She would not allow anyone else to touch her. She would not let anyone else have her. A useless and dimwitted subordinate she may have been, yet Beatrice still wished for her idol to say that she was irreplaceable. Ah, she felt utterly baffled by the childish naïveté of her own self. Uttering the words only filled her with embarrassment.*
Eleonore: "[Leb' wohl, du kühnes, herrliches Kind!](Fare-thee-well, my dear, bright child.)"
*So how could she expect her of all people to answer words far more befitting a child lost in dreams, than a hardened veteran of a warrior? Amidst a torrent of intertwining joy and bashfulness, her heart yearned for her Lieutenant not to view her as a girl forever shackled by inexperience—*
Eleonore: "[ein bräutliches Feuer soll dir nun brennen, wie nie einer Braut es gebrannt!](I'll present you with the most fervorous of flames, no bride shall ever be your equal!)"
*She had to show her that Beatrice Kircheisen was no Brynhildr. I have awoken, Major Wittenburg. As a blade forged to pierce the blazing flames, I will redeem you!*
Misc.: "[Wer meines Speeres Spitze furchtet, durchschreite das feuer nie!](For he who fears the tip of my lance shall never pass through the river of flames!)"
Beatrice: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
*Her body electrified, her blade enveloped by lightning, Beatrice could feel her very being howl as it transformed into an avatar of divine thunder. Her "craving" was a prayer uttered by a girl longing for light upon a battlefield shrouded in darkness. Beneath the cruel gaze of skies painted the color of smoke and blood, she prayed for her comrades not to lose their way. She hoped for the ideal of her beloved superior to shine through it. She wished to guide the warriors to Valhalla; to become a maiden of war, the beacon to pierce through a veil of darkness.*
*And so, that virtuous prayer of hers eventually took on the shape of her Creation Figment. The strength she had shown during her time as a prisoner of the false lance was but a faint glimmer of her true potential. She was no longer the fourth Tubal Cain. For this was her true form—*
Beatrice: "[Donner Totentanz](On lightning I dance)——"
*A dance of electromagnetic swords, befitting the graceful steps of a warrior princess. No bullet in the world could catch up to her now.*
Beatrice: "[Walküre](For I am Valkyrie!)!"
*Nor the most fervent of flames could scorch her.*
*All my hairs stood on end as the next giant fist whizzed past me.*
*I couldn't allow those things to touch me — a mere brush with that concentrated force of destruction would shatter my very being, bringing my life to a swift end.*
Ren: "...!"
*I felt as if I had dodged a cannonball — after passing by me, it crashed into the crimson stone pavement, causing a blast of air that swept me off my feet. I had completely lost my sense of all direction, unable to tell up from down, left from right.*
Machina: "..."
*The bastard in question, however, didn't follow up with a subsequent attack — he merely watched me struggle back onto my feet, glaring at me with such pressure it made breathing itself a toil.*
*This had been going on for a while now. He would stop and watch me after every missed attack, never trying to pursue.*
*His composed attitude sent shivers down my spine. All the bastards I fought so far would go mental once the battle started — some cackled like madmen, others surrendered themselves to fury, while the third group found sheer joy in carnage. All in all, it had always been a spectacle of boiling emotions.*
*But this guy was different.*
*If battles with Wilhelm and the others felt like flashy gun battles, fighting this guy was straight-up Russian Roulette. My biggest foe was the pressure that increased with each of his subsequent punches, forcing me further and further into a mental corner.*
*I wasn't fighting a wild beast, but a hunter both experienced and meticulous in his craft. The whole giant arena now felt oddly small.*
*My blood would not come to a boil — my emotions would not erupt. I was several times faster than the guy, yet all I could feel was a sensation of steadily increasing dread.*
*And that other thing—*
Ren: "Did you call me brother?"
*For some reason, I unconsciously accepted those words.*
*No, I couldn't give in. I shouldn't acknowledge him. I had to refute the bastard, and do something to dispel this terrible pressure weighing down on me.*
Machina: "A figure of speech, no more."
*But then—*
Machina: "However, it is true that we share the same blood."
*He threw another punch — a simple attack that would be easy to dodge in a calm and collected state, yet the knowledge it would instantly end my life the moment it touched me only served to shackle my mind.*
*Besides... Why the hell did I know this?*
Machina: "Can't you feel it? Don't you remember? All that we have been forced to go through in this place?"
*I once saw him fell Cain with a single punch.*
*Yet this conviction — this terror — seemed to stem from something entirely different...*
Machina: "This is the gauntlet of malice that the Obsidian Table organized to discover the last of the Fangs."
*I managed to slip out of the trajectory of his swing by the skin of my teeth, but the fierce gust left by his attack swept me off my feet again.*
Ren: "Ghh!!"
*This one was too close — his fist never connected, yet the condensed air pressure around it was strong enough to shatter a number of my ribs.*
Machina: "You bore me, Brother."
*The sombre knight began to advance towards me with slow steps once I'd collapsed to my knees. His attacks lacked any and all passion — it felt more like I was fighting a tank.*
Machina: "December 24th of the year 1939."
Machina: "The day that saw the birth of the current Obsidian Table, under the leadership of Karl Krafft and Reinhard Heydrich."
*Morgendämmerung — the epoch of twilight. The Obsidian Table was forged in the crucible of World War II.*
Machina: "The first to join the two were Bey and Schreiber. Samiel, Malleus, Kristoff, Babylon, and Valkyria followed soon after."
Machina: "In the beginning they were nine, and in need of four more."
*Another fist flew my way. I dodged the tremendous uppercut — its force shattering the stones at Machina's feet — with an over-exaggerated, panicked leap.*
*And as before, he did not pursue.*
*However—*
Machina: "Kristoff used his connections with Eicke — the commander of the Totenkopf — to pull out Spinne, a concentration camp official at the time."
Ren: "Ghh!"
*He languidly raised his right hand and caught me in the air, almost as if by accident.*
Machina: "Samiel used Haushofer's own orders to summon Tubal Cain from Japan."
*And then he tossed me up into the sky like I was a rag doll.*
Machina: "Two more remained."
*I couldn't move in the air. As my body reached the highest point it could, it began to descend, plummeting straight into the fists of the sombre knight.*
Machina: "At the time, however, the seat of Sonnenkind had already been reserved."
Machina: "And so, they were left with one empty seat without a candidate to fill it."
Machina: "Do you have any idea what they did?"
*He launched another fist, with a tremendous roar of wind following in its wake. There was no way I could dodge it.*
