Beatrice: "I killed many, and failed to save even more. I have my regrets, but that's just how war is. You were right, Major."
*They might have gained power surpassing that of armies, yet they were by no means omnipotent. In the end, her power clashed with her ideals, for she was the type that could only achieve things through murder.*
Eleonore: "Indeed, killing is our trade. We know how to survive, and how to prevent others from doing so.  Bringing people back from the dead is not within our jurisdiction. "
*How could someone whose very essence was to kill wish for something as contradictory as the revival of the dead?*
Eleonore: "Let others worry about that nonsense. Neither I, nor Lord Heydrich had ever, in essence, died. We simply transcended death while we were alive."
Eleonore: "And so will you. Unable to return to the cycle, your soul will linger here, eventually transforming into that of an Einherjar. Brynhildr never died, she was merely sentenced to eternal sleep. However... you do not wish for such an outcome, do you? "
*And that was why Beatrice denounced Valhalla; why she refused the glory of an Einherjar.*
Eleonore: "You can defy me if you so desire. I am used to having compelling, yet unwilling misfits to keep me company. You can snivel or howl in tears all you want — it shall not change the fact that I am taking you with me."
Eleonore: "And therein lies my initial question... Why join us in the first place?"
*Neither bringing back the dead, nor the thought of immortality could entice Beatrice. But then why did she remain with the Obsidian Table after the war?*
Eleonore: "I very much doubt you naïvely misunderstood our intentions like the Sakurai whelp did. Am I correct?"
*Born into a family of counts, Beatrice Kircheisen was a German of the purest blood. Just like Eleonore. She couldn't have been blind to the truth behind the warmongering Einherjar.*
Eleonore: "Bey has probably never seen a blackboard in his life. Malleus, being on the other end of the spectrum, had her mind packed full of rubbish. Brenner could never comprehend a warrior's spirit, and that little cur of another race is another matter entirely... You were unlike any of them. The more I think about it, the less I comprehend your actions. "
*And thus, the crimson knightess' eyes urged Beatrice to answer, demanding an explanation.*
Eleonore: "This is an order, Kircheisen! Tell me your wish — depending on the answer, I may even grant it."
Beatrice: "..."
Eleonore: "Or could it have been sheer laziness? Did you aid Brenner in her schemes simply because you had nothing better to do?"
Beatrice: "No."
*Beatrice's retort was brief but firm.*
Beatrice: "I did have a wish of my own, Major."
*To this day, she had refused to give up on it.*
Beatrice: "I believe I've told you about a person I respected from the bottom of my heart."
*She was a bit intimidating, somewhat haughty, and unbelievably idealistic...*
Beatrice: "Her wits are sharp... they certainly should be. But at the same time, she's, well... sort of a fool."
Beatrice: "Despite excelling at everything... turns out, she had one cardinal flaw."
*A painfully human Achilles' heel. A common weakness so unlike her. Yet one tremendously befitting someone of her constitution.*
Beatrice: "Love is blind—"
*A knightess who made a fatal mistake in choosing her master.*
Beatrice: "Your taste in men is terrible. Depressingly so."
*The noble Einherjar, defined by perpetual war, perpetual revival — their only destination, the dawn of Ragnarok. Warmongers. Eleonore herself found the expression crude, yet that was indeed the nature of immortals, their very existence one woven of battles eternal. And in the end, her heart was never at odds with that reality. She was content.*
Beatrice: "I'm a soldier — I won't attempt to justify myself. I didn't want to die, so I killed others. You could've wished for the twilight of the world itself, and I would still have stood by your side."
*As long as she remained herself.*
Beatrice: "But then I realized. Or rather, I knew it from the very start, but simply chose to look past it. Both of us were blind, in truth. What did Lord Heydrich do during the fall of Berlin? Do you remember what you ordered us?"
*Suffer defeat tonight, and let the filthy mongrels believe they have the upper hand! “Murder your comrades. A million subhumans slain is but a drop in the ocean compared to a German soul.”*
Beatrice: "I'm not naïve enough to think we could've saved them all, but..."
*“It is all a matter of quality. Your dearest kinsmen and loved ones will serve as the sweetest of sacrifices. Lives not easily forfeit will, in turn, mature into the most valuable of offerings.”*
Beatrice: "Why did we have to—"
*“Slay your comrades. Annihilate them all with love burning in your hearts.” Not a single man loyal to the Reich must be allowed to survive — let them be consumed by the sacrifical flames!*
*That order was beyond insane. It defied common sense, contradicted the fundamentals of soldierhood. No genuine warrior, no true protector of the land and its people should have uttered a command like that.*
Beatrice: "Weren't we both soldiers?!"
*There were indeed many who cared little for their country among the Obsidian Round Table, but they were criminals and witches in the first place. Beatrice and Eleonore were supposed to be different from them, andyet—*
Beatrice: "That day, your orders left Berlin a hellish wasteland!"
*A merciless inferno that swallowed all without distinction. This Valhalla was but a devilish lair erected from the corpses of their former comrades.*
Beatrice: "And in the end, even you fell..."
*Not even Eleonore could escape the scorch of hellfire — it turned her into the demon that now stood before Beatrice.*
Beatrice: "And so—  What I wished for... "
Beatrice: "...was to rescue you from this place!  To tear you away from Lord Heydrich, and make you return to your old self. That's all I ever wished for... "
Eleonore: "..."
*Eleonore had no words to throw back at the grievous resolve of her former comrade. Only the faint crease on her forehead betrayed her bewilderment, though whether it signaled a lack of comprehension or sheer astonishment remained unclear.*
Eleonore: "Why should I let you dictate the choices of my life? You spout an absurd wish. No Swastika can grant such a thing. "
Beatrice: "You're right. I'm painfully aware of that."
*Eleonore von Wittenburg never died — she became an undying Einherjar during her lifetime. There was only one way to liberate her.*
Beatrice: "That is why I decided to kill Lord Heydrich."
Beatrice: "Isn't that but another wish for the Swastikas to grant? He can't even reappear without them pulling him through. I was the one who lured the Doppeladler to Shambhala eleven years ago. I hoped to avoid civilian casualties by opening Swastikas with their... and our blood. Using the ensuing chaos as my cover, I planned to kill Bey, Malleus, and the Divine Vessel. And finally— "
Beatrice: "I would summon this castle back to the surface of the earth — the cursed Gladsheim that sullied the very souls of your soldiers. I believed my chances to be the best with Sonnenkind still young, and Zarathustra absent. "
*And there was another reason that made her want to put an end to it all at the time.*
Beatrice: "In the end, though... I failed."
*But she did not regret it. For she was finally liberated from her days of hatred and contrition.*
Beatrice: "Haven't I told you that I was the type to chase after others? I have faith in the success of the little boy and girl, as well as the other little ones. I want to shine bright as a beacon to illuminate their path. I wish to remain your useless subordinate till the very end. "
Beatrice: "That is why I am here. I will make your sword shed its rust of blood and regain its former brilliance. I swore to myself to rescue you from this demonic castle, and no words will change my mind. You surely know how stubborn I can be. "
*Beatrice, ever firm and steadfast, declared her goal.*
Beatrice: "Did that help you comprehend me better, Major?"
*She posed her question in an almost jovial manner, smiling through tears. Eleonore considered Beatrice for a a long while before eventually letting out a sigh.*
Eleonore: "Fool."
*It was a long, deep sigh of affectionate bewilderment, the kind one would express towards their recalcitrant little sister.*
Eleonore: "To think one day you would lecture me on being a soldier.  Ah, now that I think about it, Berlin was indeed your birthplace. So even now, after all those years, you still cannot forgive the order I issued that day. A vexing situation, truly. What am I supposed to do with you, foolish girl? I doubt an illustration of the blessings granted by being a part of Lord Heydrich's legion is going to convince you. And I am not one to enjoy hiding behind excuses, either.  Above all else, however— "
*Her eyes, like a pair of daggers, pierced Beatrice. Eleonore's wry smile contorted in contempt as her pupils lit ablaze in demonic fervor.*
Eleonore: "You uttered two things you never should have."
*Both her figure and its surrounds grew hazy like heat shimmer in the middle of a desert.*
Eleonore: "The first was that inexpiable bilge about killing Lord Heydrich. Know your place, runt."
*The temperature of the area suddenly rose a dozen or so degrees, with blasts of hot air chaotically swirling within the hall.*
Eleonore: "And the other—"
*Truth be told, it was the other one that disappointed her the most. And that was why she despised women. They only ever had but one thing in their silly heads.*
Eleonore: "Love, of all things..."
*A cheap banality befitting a depraved runt.*
Eleonore: "You insulted... my fealty."
*Crimson flames erupted across the room. The final remnants of Eleonore's goodwill — her wish to put her former comrade out of her misery without much suffering — had melted into nothingness.*
Eleonore: "Your platitude begs punishment, Kircheisen. You have disappointed me. Even in spite of your qualities as an Einherjar—"
*Crippling pain and paralyzing dread — Eleonore would carve both into Beatrice's insolent soul so that she would never dare spout such nonsense again.*
Eleonore: "By the time we meet next, you might have already gone mad. But I no longer mind. I won't let you get away. You shall crawl by my side and entertain me for an eternity. "
Beatrice: "Angry because I got it right? And I believe I've already told you — you cannot use your figment in this ca— "
Eleonore: "Nonsense."
*Eleonore practically spat the word out, vexed by her subordinate's ignorance.*
Eleonore: "You show no progress, you naïve fool. What on earth made you think you knew everything about me?"
Eleonore: "An explosion that expands without limit? Indeed, I won't deny having used that. But it was merely something I created to suit the needs of the battlefield."
*A large-scale weapon system, a hellish instrument potent enough to devastate entire cities — a weapon of mass destruction. Her Creation Figment manifested in such a way because that proved more effective for military operations.*
*However, the Wittenburgs were an old lineage of respectable knights. Their honor was earned in duels — one combatant against the other. An explosion capable of expanding without limit was merely an arid tool utilized to eradicate cannon fodder.  Therefore, in cases where her opponent was a knight like herself—*
Eleonore: "I will now unbind it. Feel honored, Kircheisen. Only Lord Heydrich knows of its true form."
Eleonore: "And you shall be the first to actually witness it."
Beatrice: "...!"
*The expanding pressure pounded Beatrice like a hammer. The scent of burning steel and oil at her nostrils — the unforgettable heat wave of the battlefield. It was coming. An Ahnenerbe of unprecedented destructive power — a cannon so monstrous one could hardly envision it in a sane mind.*
Beatrice: "But..."
*Something was not right here. Knowing full well that she could not afford letting her superior draw her weapon, Beatrice's legs, nonetheless, refused to move.*
Eleonore: "[Echter als er schwur keiner Eide;](No man more honest ever took an oath;)[treuer als er hielt keiner Verträge;](None more true made treaty;)[lautrer als er liebte kein andrer:](None was more pure in love;)"
*The aria was not the same Beatrice remembered her superior chanting in preparation of the infernal cannon during their battles.*
Eleonore: "[und doch, alle Eide, alle Verträge,](And yet none so betrayed all oaths,)[die treueste Liebe trog keiner wie er](All treaties, his truest love!) [Wißt ihr, wie das ward?](Answer me, O mortal man: can you understand why?) "
*Was the weapon of mass fiery destruciton no more than a tool outfitted for the battlefield? Then what in the world could this be?*
Eleonore: "[Das Feuer, das mich verbrennt, rein'ge vom Fluche den Ring!](The fire raging within my breast shall melt all taint, all impurity to oblivion!)"
Eleonore: "[Ihr in der Flut löset ihn auf, und lauter bewahrt das lichte Gold,](Let yourself be purified, your taint washed, melted clear away; your soul thus released, exalted)[das euch zum Unheil geraubt.](Till naught is left but radiant Gold, its luster pure.)"
*Rubedo was the last of the molds to shape the Gold's gestalt — she stood closest to the Beast. And as the one who revered him the most, she turned herself into a loyal blade that would obliterate any and all impurities threatening her master.*
Eleonore: "[Denn der Götter Ende dammert nun auf.](Aye, the twilight of the gods is upon us) [So - werf' ich den Brand in Walhalls prangende Burg.](And so shall I be reborn as the fire that cleanses our sacred halls of Valhalla!) "
*Utterly overwhelmed, Beatrice found herself unable to move, though it lasted for no longer than a second or two. However, that was enough for her to be far too late.*
Eleonore: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
*It left its scabbard — the Surtr's sword, meant to remain suppressed at all costs, had finally been unsheathed and revealed in all its glory. A microcosm of condensed, raging flames that would never allow their prey to escape. Its name was—*
Eleonore: "[Muspellsheim Lævateinn](Harrowing Sword of Inferno)!"
Beatrice: "...?!"
*The castle walls gave way for molten crust — the two were transported to a land of simmering crimson. Beatrice felt like she'd been transported into a furnace, feeling the heat of matter melting in the flames, turning to vapor, and dispersing into heat waves. No way out. No shelter to be taken. Despite being a large area that stretched as far as the eye could see, this new landscape filled Beatrice with a tingling sensation of claustrophobia, as if she was stuck in a long yet suffocating tunnel. Indeed, an ant crawling across the rails of a subway might have felt just the same. And so it dawned upon her.*
Beatrice: "Is this... the inside of the cannon?"
*That she had been swallowed by a thirty meter long barrel being used by 800mm shells used as a runway; that she was within the jaws of the “Demon of the Hunt” — the Dora railway gun.*
Eleonore: "Precisely. And thus... you understand what this means, do you not?"
*That there was no escape. That the cannon could not miss. The absolute nature of Eleonore's weapon. A bullet that pursued its target? An explosion that expanded without limit? No. It was nothing so frivolous.*
*Beatrice proclaimed herself to be one who chased after others, yet the label fit Eleonore all the same. The Hegemony of Gold bewitched her, drove her mad — she yearned to burn in its absolute radiance for all eternity. Eleonore had never possessed the concept of fleeing or turning back. She would chase her goal to the ends of the earth and beyond — to burn in the beguiling luster of her idol for all eternity. Therefore, this place had no exit, no means of escape.*
Eleonore: "Something can only truly be inescapable when the notion of fleeing is impossible to begin with."
*A microcosm ruled only by scorching hellfire. The world that the crimson knightess imagined lived inside the cannon, burning everything to ashes with incandescent fury. The flawless dominion of Rubedo's everlasting fervor. The symbol of her fealty, her oath, her... love.*
Eleonore: "And so our battle is concluded. There is nothing you can do now."
*A wall of boiling hellfire closed in on Beatrice from behind Eleonore like a pyroclastic flow in the wake of a freshly erupted volcano — even the Valkyrie had doubts she could survive its relentless fury.*
Eleonore: "For you are bare."
*The souls Beatrice had carried have all but vanished with the opening of the first Swastika. The only soul that dwelled within her now was her own. And even that had begun to shown signs of wear. Even the most brilliant of blades, no matter how sharp, would be useless against a whole army on its own. To survive a blast from the already-drawn sword of harrowing without armor should have been a notion beyond the wildest dreams of even the most deluded.*
Eleonore: "Your soul is wearing down with every second you spend in battle. I can literally see through you already, Kircheisen. It's about time you made peace with your fate. I cannot hold back now, but the more you struggle, the more of your soul you lose. The sole thing you could achieve at this point is heightening your own despair. "
Eleonore: "Accept your defeat. Resign and kneel before me. In the end, you could not even best me, let alone defeat Lord Heydrich."
Beatrice: "Never!"
*Yet in the face of that impending calamity, Beatrice remained stalwart and true, her resolve firm as steel.*
Beatrice: "I will save you!"
Eleonore: "What makes you so stubborn?"
*The Valkyrie's intentions were but an unwelcome nuisance to the crimson knightess. And yet Beatrice stood before her, unyielding. She would risk her life, transcend death, and sacrifice her soul. A meaningless struggle. One she would garner no praise for.*
Beatrice: "I mean... you don't have any friends besides me, Major!"
*How she could still spout such nonsense was beyond Eleonore's comprehension.*
Beatrice: "You are too strong, too stern, too pure... too woeful. Treated only as a tool by the only man you truly loved, and unable to realize your own feelings.  The unapproachable Loge of blazing flames that Wotan has bestowed upon you... You are the only one who's worthy of the name Brynhildr here! "
*Beatrice knew she no longer had a chance at victory. Lævateinn had been cast, its flames already having swallowed most of Eleonore's hazy figure. For a swordswoman like Beatrice, the only way to fight would mean diving straight into the furnace. Staying at a distance would only delay, but not prevent her demise. There was nothing she could do. Any action she took would be futile. And yet...*
Beatrice: "So this is a wall I must traverse, no matter what. Open your eyes, princess! The man who entrusted you with your flames was a bastard! "
Eleonore: "..."
*The words did not anger Eleonore, nor did she take Beatrice's plea as particularly impudent. A smile of thinly-veiled bewilderment lingered on her face as she mentally traversed through the memories of her past. She remembered how no amount of discipline would ever make this girl learn when to hold her tongue.*
Eleonore: "You think yourself Siegfried?"
Beatrice: "Yes. Although, I imagine you don't exactly fancy the fact that I'm a woman."
*Her lips curling into a fleeting smile, Beatrice lowered her hips and bent forward. Was she seriously contemplating jumping into the flames? To traverse them? Was such a thing even possible?*
Beatrice: "Remember how you told me that having a gun pointed at you wasn't actually as terrifying as you thought? Now I can wholeheartedly agree. Indeed, it hardly makes me flinch. "
*Readying herself for the leap, Beatrice abruptly cried out towards the heavens.*
Beatrice: "Karl Krafft! I know you are listening. And I beseech you! This is a duel between knights — a bout no sorcerer has any right to interfere with! If I succeed in defeating Major Wittenburg— "
*Just until the end of their battle.*
Beatrice: "You will keep your wicked schemes and sorcery to yourself! How do you answer?!"
*Was it merely a failing of one's senses that it seemed like the entirety of Muspellsheim flickered in obsidian in response to valkyrie's harangue? However, at the very next moment...*
*——Jawohl, Fräulein Walküre——*
*Something that was neither a voice, nor a thought, nor a figment of one's imagination reverberated across the fiery prison, making even Rubedo's inferno feel chilly to the skin for a fleeting moment.*
Eleonore: "That monkey..."
Beatrice: "Did you know that he — surprisingly enough — had a soft spot for the weak?"
*And thus, she made peace with her fate, realizing that this was as much as she could do.*
Beatrice: "Kai, I'm begging you. Lend me your strength... ...so I can protect your little sister— "
Beatrice: "I care not if I end up perishing here. But I swear to take her down with me. "
*Back to those days of radiant bliss.*
Beatrice: "Let us return to those times, Major Wittenburg — when there were no Valkyrias and no Samiels. Our true Valhalla exists there, in the past! "
Eleonore: "Don't make me laugh, you fool! It is you who must accompany me — together, we shall brave a myriad battlefields till the very twilight of time! "
*Like in those days when they still shared the same passionate vision.*
Eleonore: "You can no longer turn back. Your place is at my side!"
Beatrice: "I will never illuminate a path forged from the bodies of innocents!"
Eleonore: "Cease your foolishness!"
Beatrice: "You are the one who's deluded!"
*Flames swallowed the flash of lightning, enveloping the two maidens of war in their embrace. The victor was certain — unless a miracle occurred, the tide of battle was as good as set in stone. Yet what, indeed, was a miracle? Was it not called such because it manifested in precisely situations like this?*
Reinhard: "Hm?"
*Reinhard raised an eyebrow as a slight aberration stirred the air. The girl leaping ever so valiantly towards him had yet to break through the skeletons that emerged from the foot of the throne, let alone hurt or even draw close to their master. A single company — a sole strand in the Beast's Mane, the entirety of which contained a Legion comprised of millions. And yet, that was more than enough to stop the poor girl. Nevertheless...*
Reinhard: "Oh?"
*Little by little, Kei's withdrawal began to slow. She could no longer advance, and a breakthrough was out of the question. However, she had yet to lose her will to fight, despite being cornered by an opponent boasting of immortality. But what of it? It did not mean she stood a chance — her foolish actions were hardly worthy of admiration. And even if she managed to break through, it would be hardly anything more than a momentary flash of light on the verge of being swallowed by darkness. And so, Reinhard pondered what approach would ultimately prove to be the most interesting.*
*Should he summon reinforcements to crush the girl in an instant, or would it be more amusing to observe her struggle for a while longer? Reinhard was not one to relish the act of torturing a maiden so young, but he enjoyed seeing the spark of courage and valor light up in the midst of battle — hence his dilemma. Both wishes commanded an equal presence in his heart. Although, if death was the only result available to the girl, he ought to focus on it, coming up with the most interesting way to orchestrate her demise. Unless... there was a third option that the Beast himself could not yet grasp.*
*In the midst of pondering such delightful thoughts, yet another aberration stirred within the castle. Walter Gerlitz — the leader of this particular company — suddenly dispersed, having been pierced by Kei's blade. And with his disappearance, other skeletons broke formation, falling apart.*
Kei: "You underestimate me...!"
*It only took a moment for Walter to resurrect, but Kei bet everything on that meager span of time. Kei had been on the defensive only to make out the leader of the skeleton company. Her plan was to slay him swiftly, and use the momentary confusion to assault the general upon the throne. When a small unit had to engage a superior enemy force, speed meant the difference between life and death. However—  Although it was certain that she had been severely underestimated, and Reinhard had let his guard down, it was also true that the wall separating the two remained immense beyond mortal imagination.*
Reinhard: "Marseille."
*A casual utterance from the Beast materialized a colossal gun behind the throne that seemed like it belonged on a fighter plane. It directed its aim at Kei, calculating the trajectory of its bullets with such precision it seemed almost as if the girl had been drawn towards them and not the other way around.*
Kei: "Agh...!"
*An ace pilot in times past known as the Star of Africa, his guard nigh-impenetrable. Kei fell back like a shot plane — blood dancing through the air instead of fumes — and was swallowed by Walter and his troops as they revived. In that moment...*
*Hihi'irokane soared through the air, aimed directly at Reinhard's neck. It was, of course, hit by the Messerschmitt in an instant, losing its trajectory. Yet had this result been a mere coincidence, or an inevitability?*
Reinhard: "...?!"
*If miracles were real, the world had just witnessed one.*
Machina: "[Tod! Sterben Einz'ge Gnade!](Death, O glorious, final death! Savior of man!)"
*A voice somber as the night reverberated amidst the raging howl of the wind, while a pair of tremendous iron fists maintained their onslaught.*
Machina: "[Die schreckliche Wunde, das Gift, ersterbe,](My heart, drowned in venom, ravaged by time, may beat its last within your embrace)"
Machina: "[das es zernagt, erstarre das Herz!](May spear's wound, may venom's bane, all perish at your coming)"
*He began activating his Beri'ah. I knew the danger, and that it was in my best interests to interrupt him as soon as possible.*
*Still, I chose to leap back a distance, instead observing him from afar.*
Ren: "..."
*All my senses told me that I should avoid prolonging the fight.*
*After dodging attacks that might as well have been considered an artillery strike, my mind and body were on the verge of complete collapse. If I interrupted him now, all that awaited me was a drawn-out battle of attrition, lasting until I either got hit or fell dead from exhaustion. If this kept up, I stood no chance against him.*
*And so—*
*I would use this moment to bolster my strength to its absolute limit and end the fight right here.*
*A risky choice for sure, but transforming this battle into a bout of quick-draw was the only thing I could do to make it not completely hopeless for me.*
Machina: "[Hier bin ich, - die off'ne Wunde hier!](Aye, behold! This festering void gnawing at my soul;)"
*Machina began to change. The core of his being had been trapped within a shell of iron — he had adopted human form for now, but upon revealing his craving, he would return to his true shape.*
Machina: "[Das mich vergiftet, hier fliesst mein Blut:](This life-blood, its crimson pearls feeding the earth; this malice, ever coursing my veins — behold!)"
*A pair of iron arms — not mere prosthetics, but genuine iron.*
Machina: "[Heraus die Waffe! Taucht eure Schwerte](Clasp your blade, draw your steel!)[tief, tief - bis ans Heft!](And plunge deep, deep till the hilt!)"
*A beast of iron. Human in shape, yet more reminiscent of a tank.*
Machina: "[Auf! Ihr Helden:](Hark, brave knights, and know this:)"
Machina: "[Tötet den Sünder mit seiner Qual,](As the sinner finds his last refuge, his anguish done)[von selbst dann leuchtet euch wohl der Gral!](So shall divine light be shower'd from the heavens above)"
*Indeed, his soul had been trapped in an iron vessel of terror, and now, one could glimpse its true form in the sombre knight's limbs.*
Machina: "[Beri'ah](Creation Figment)—"
Machina: "[Miðgarð Völsunga Saga](End of the Mortal Realm)—"
*The Volsunga Saga — a ballad of heroes sung in the mortal realm of Midgard. A story that lauds divine predestination as the highest form of glory. It insisted on the beauty of death, and acknowledged the need for the curtain to fall.*
*A Creation Figment that hoped, prayed, and craved for the end of everything it touched.*
*He had now turned into a sentient avatar of Deus Ex Machina — a vessel of the gods that would put an end to all.*
Ren: "You hate fighting?"
*I couldn't help but ask. After all, I too was about to launch an attack infused with all of my being.*
Machina: "Never in my life have I gained any joy from battle. Not once."
*The sombre knight — my opponent — shared my sentiment.*
Machina: "There is glory to be found on the battlefield, true — a place for men to prove their valor. However, I am not so savage as to revel in bloodshed. And neither are you. Am I correct, Brother?"
Machina: "The sooner it ends, the better. The refusal to allow impurities to taint the field of battle is the hallmark of a true warrior."
Machina: "It needs not joy, doubt, or despair."
Ren: "Or anxiety, anger, or passion."
Machina: "They are all worthless and must be discarded. No place exists for them in our duel."
*A clash of pure, undiluted fighting spirit — our battle required no more. And only beyond it lay the true Valhalla.*
*A prolonged battle did not guarantee glory — if anything, it would only taint the beauty of the dance.*
*On that point alone, we seemed to be of the same mind.*
*We would soon clash. One would stand, the other would fall — there was nothing more to it.*
*Therefore—*
Ren: "I won't lose."
Machina: "Then act upon those words."
*Oh, he could bet his ass I would. I'd mop the floor with this suicidal nutcase.*
*As our muscles tensed up — pushed to their absolute limit — we both leapt forward. Would my speed exceed his, or would his fist find me first?*
*I had to win this, no matter what.*
Ren: "I don't want to die."
*I wanted to live. I'd show him how survival instincts and the attachment to life could elevate one's strength to new heights.*
*I mean, I'd even told this to Sakurai.*
Ren: "You're all just cowards."
*A bunch of losers trembling in Reinhard's shadow.*
Ren: "So stop talking down to me!"
*And in that moment, we both pulled our figurative triggers.*
*My body shot forward like a bullet. I was confident I exceeded him in terms of speed, and if I had a shred of fear left, I wouldn't have been able to step within his reach to begin with.*
*I had to keep my eyes peeled, make all my nerves stand on end.*
*Would his blade — or rather, fist — come from the right or the left? If I missed his initial motion, my fate would be sealed.*
*Anyone would need at least a moment to ready their attack — to pour strength into the punch.*
*And that fleeting span of time would prove to be the moment of truth. That was why I chose to observe him while I could instead of trying to get in the way of his Creation Figment's activation.*
Machina: "Sieg Heil."
*His frame was that of the ideal man — the perfect body of a warrior. No wonder he reminded me of the statue of David the first time I saw him.*
*He was a puppet — an artificial being. A machine shaped to perfection.*
*And so, he couldn't hide the creaking of his joints, nor the rumbling of his gears.*
Ren: "Right!"
*His iron fist shot at me like death itself, but I read its trajectory before it could reach me.*
*It carried no spirit within. No matter how sharp an eye an observer possessed, they would not have been able to discern something their own consciousness refused to acknowledge as existing. Under normal circumstances, I would've never been able to dodge it.*
*But no longer was I bound by the limits of mundane humanity.*
Ren: "You lost because—"
*I dodged his fist, and twisted my body round, throwing my hand forward to deliver him the fatal back blow.*
Ren: "—of your own body!"
*An artificial man that possessed no blood or flesh. Even though he had mastered the technique of perfectly blank mind, he could not hide the creaking of cogs that would come alive bustling a split second before each of his movements.*
*Apparently, I had lost to him here in the past, but the fool forgot that we possessed different bodies at the time.*
*My guillotine pierced through the air — despite being at a distance that would normally prove lethal, the air pressure resulting from his punch and the stoutness of his arm made it impossible for my weapon to reach his neck.*
*But I predicted that much.*
*We both put everything into our attacks, but I wasn't really aiming at his neck.*
Machina: "..."
*I would cleave his arm off. The blade of my guillotine found his elbow,and—*
*—sliced through it, separating my opponent from his fists of concentrated Deus ex Machina.*
Machina: "Wonderful."
*Was that him rejoicing at his long-awaited end?*
*Or perhaps—*
Machina: "I trusted you could do this much."
Ren: "...?!"
*The sound of cogs and gears turning in reverse filled my ears.*
Machina: "[Höchsten Heiles Wunder:](O the fleeting miracle, most exalted)"
Machina: "[Erlösung dem Erlöser](Bestow your blessing upon my Messiah)"
Ren: "Wh—?!"
*His left fist came without warning. Could it be that he, too—*
Machina: "It seems we even think similarly."
*—thought the very same thing as me?*
*To destroy the opponent's weapon with the first hit before finishing them off with the second?*
Machina: "You lost because—"
*I felt like I was staring into a mirror. Machina, the harbinger of death, even repeated the very same line I uttered moments before.*
Machina: "—you didn't believe my words."
*That we both survived the gauntlet of malice. That we were two facets of the same man, forcefully split apart.*
*I wouldn't believe it. I wouldn't acknowledge it. Even if it happened to be true, I would have kept denying it. And that proved to be my undoing.*
Machina: "And so the moment of truth arrives. I trusted that you would act the way you did."
*My spirit and backbone — the weapons that pulled me through countless battles. I believed — and never doubted — that they were essential for my survival.*
*Yet in this fight, they proved to be the very reason for my defeat.*
*In the end, his belief in an identical conclusion under the same circumstances overshadowed the trust I had in both my craving, and my hope for victory.*
Machina: "This is the end. Allow me to correct a foolish misconception of yours."
*As the iron giant's fist drew closer and closer, carrying absolute and final death, he parted his lips to speak.*
Machina: "I am not afraid of Heydrich. It is merely that my sole weapon is as good as trash before him."
Machina: "It has to be you. Only you can fill the void inside me."
Machina: "And that is only natural. After all, you are the only one I had ever called a comrade."
*But then... how would I face my comrades?  What would I tell them?*
*That it was my destiny to fall and lose my life to him?*
*No. I couldn't acknowledge that!*
*I...!*
*I wouldn't acknowledge such an end!*
*The man clad in obsidian robes suddenly came to a halt. The two following behind him had no choice but to do the same. They were in a wide hall, the walls of which were molded of countless human bones. The whole thing went beyond the comprehension of both Kasumi and Shirou. And while the body of the man was indeed still with them, his mind was not.*
Mercurius: "I owe you an apology, Marguerite."
*For he currently occupied the world of twilight, addressing a woman he cherished dearly.*
Mercurius: "Allow me to amend a previous statement of mine: it would appear that necklace ill befits you, after all."
*Marie remained silent despite the gentle apology. Or rather, she could not answer. Her eyes had been closed, her mind in deep in sleep. She merely lingered there in an unconscious state, shackled by the chains of roses to the symbol of her own essence — a guillotine. When Mercurius talked about an ill-befitting necklace, this was what he had meant.*
Mercurius: "His duel with Machina was never of significance, for everything depended on whether or not he chose you. None of this would have come to pass, had he done so."
*An outcome brought about by the wrong choice.*
Mercurius: "It is most unfortunate, but what has been done cannot be undone. It appears a number of loose threads remained in the plan I came to weave over these past sixty years. And so, you shall be swallowed by the twilight before long. Forgive me, Marguerite. I had always been blind to human emotion. "
*The heart of the lover he had prepared specially for her had directed its passion at another. That, by itself, was of no real significance — he could have still been able to carry through with his plans, as long as that affection was not the unadulterated love for a woman.*
Mercurius: "Alas, you two share far too weak a connection. I suppose Machina would be partly to blame for that, now that I reflect back upon it. They say that the flames of passion are not necessarily proportional to the passing of time, yet even in terms of sheer quality, what exists between the two of you is far from sufficient. I very much doubt either of you think of the other as quite irreplaceable. "
*At least, his shadow had yet to reach the level of affection he felt for the girl. And that was no good. It was not enough to bring about an emanation. In short, Marie watched over Mercurius' wallowing in his own failures with silence.*
Mercurius: "In order to destroy the laws of the corporeal world, two Hegemonies must clash. Without the resulting renewal, there would be no meaning... and the way you are now, Emanation remains but a dream fruitlessly sought after. Self-sufficient Transcendence is hardly enough to envelop the whole world in love. Do you understand, Marguerite? And you, I'm afraid, have yet to learn of true affection. I had hoped for you to become an embodiment of love, like my dear friend. A most unfortunate turn of events, truly. "
Mercurius kept saying one incomprehensible thing after another. Yet despite it all, he seemed to be enjoying himself. Despite the opaque nature of his words, Marie could tell that he was confessing to his failures — to the crumbling of his plans. Yet no matter how hard one looked, it did not appear like he was truly grieving the fact. If Marie had her consciousness about her, she would have doubtlessly said: 
Marie: "You're being odd, Cagliostro."
*A single word would hardly do the man's myriad facets justice, yet to Marie, it sufficed just fine. Mercurius made a troubled smile.*
Mercurius: "Do you find my disposition peculiar?"
Marie: "Yes. After all, you are still—"
*He was still expecting something. Waiting for it to happen.*
*He claimed that world would see no emanation occur. That his ambitions had ended in failure and defeat. That it was all so unfortunate. And yet... He had been sure of something else. He was still trying to make the girl cause something.*
Mercurius: "How agonizing. Pardon the trite comparison, but in the present moment, I truly stand at the crossroads between friendship and love. As Karl Krafft, I have to remain loyal to my covenant with the Beast. However, as Alessandro di Cagliostro, I believe you to be the true vessel of the goddess. If I allowed him to emanate his Hegemony alone, I would lose my love. Yet if I were to stop him, I would lose a friend. Ah, such fierce antinomy. Brush it off as the drivel of a ridiculous man. However, and I utter this as mere speculation— "
Mercurius: "If there existed an outcome in which I could avoid betraying either..."
*In that moment, a crack appeared on the hazy obsidian robe covering the man.*
Mercurius: "...it would only manifest through a miracle that neither He, nor I could have predicted."
*Indeed—*
Mercurius: "For instance, like the spectacle unfolding before us now."
*In that moment, an aberration swept across the scenery, surprising each participant of this final Grand Guignol.*
Eleonore: "Ngh?!"
Machina: "What?!"
*Although fleeting and scarcely discernible, its advent staggered the two indomitable Einherjar, Rubedo and Nigredo.*
*The devil's castle trembled. For a tiny fraction of a barely perceptible moment, Wewelsberg, that unassailable Valhalla, that hell forged from the skulls of millions, did indeed feel an unprecedented tremor. An impossible notion, for if true— —their Lord Commander was likely in peril.*
Eleonore: "Impossible... Lord Heydrich!"
*Her eternal devotion to her Lord caused a great anxiety to well within her, which for a creature of passion such as Eleonore was impossible to ignore. Heeding the growing dread in her heart, her thoughts strayed from the battle, and instead were directed towards her master.*
Machina: "You knave! How dare you get in my way?!"
*On the opposite end of the spectrum — Machina, whose mind remained an unwilling slave to his master — attempted to resist, and stopped in his tracks as a result.*
*A brief distraction, which precipitated only a moment's faltering, and yet...*
Marie: "..."
*It was enough for Marie to comprehend the situation after being abruptly awakened by the tremors.*
Mercurius: "Well now, what shall it be?"
*The answer was a castling that ignored the rules.*
Ren: "Wh—?!"
*My right arm suddenly shot forward as if to protect me against the incoming fist of absolute death. What the hell?! I hadn't done anything!!*
*Even if this had been an action caused by an unconscious reflex, it couldn't have made it in time to cover me from Machina's attack.*
*Yet even his iron fist appeared to have faltered for a second. My mind might not have caught up in time, but my arm certainly did, saving my life in the process.*
Machina: "It is futile — no man can stop my fists!"
*I knew how this would end, as well as the feelings it would birth.*
Ren: "Stop it, Marie...!"
*By the time I cried out her name, it was already too late.*
*His fist of Deus ex Machina crashed into the blade of the guillotine, shattering it to pieces. And with my Ahnenerbe destroyed, I, too, would soon meet the same fate.*
Machina: "This changes nothing. Victory is mine."
*The sombre knight threw another punch, declaring his victory to be certain. Having fulfilled his long-cherished desire left Nigredo utterly intoxicated, yet I had nothing with which to capitalize on the opportunity.*
*Why?! Why would Marie do this?!*
*There was no reason for her to sacrifice her life...!*
Mercurius: "No, I'm afraid you are mistaken."
*The performers were still up on the stage. As ironic as it was, getting separated from Ren — a man who proved to not be her destined partner — shattered her rose-chains, liberating Marguerite Breuilh from the covenant, thus returning her to the original state of a free soul.*
Mercurius: "And if you are free—"
*The tremor that shook the devil's castle birthed a crack in the body of one of its architects — Mercurius. And that fissure became a gate connecting the worlds of Twilight and Wewelsburg. Which meant—*
Marie: "Kasumi—"
*She could reach those on the other side.*
Marie: "Shirou—"
*Her voice, her visage — even her touch — could pass through.*
*Kasumi was a woman who lived by instinct, and Shirou had been a shrewd man on top of that.*
Shirou: "I see."
Kasumi: "Marie!"
*And precisely because they relied on intuition rather than logic to judge the events around them, the two — to whom the situation of the whole castle had been made clear — realized that this was their chance to turn the tables. That this was the miracle they had been waiting for. This would result in saving Ren from the brink of death, and Kei from mortal peril. And someone else whose defeat was imminent.*
Kasumi: "Here...!"

Shirou: "Gotta save the ladies first!"
*Shirou flung Marie's soul to where it was needed the most.*
Eleonore: "...?!"
Beatrice: "Khh...!"
*Beatrice, now on the verge of death and under a constant siege by the flames of Muspelheim—*
Eleonore: "Luck appeared to have favored you today."

Beatrice: "Does that mean I no longer possess the strength to..."
Eleonore: "That is correct. The difference between the density of our souls is far too great."

Eleonore: "Still, I must commend you. Tearing through countless of Lord Heydrich's men is a feat to be proud of."
Eleonore: "You truly outdid yourself today. I am thoroughly impressed."

*She could not best her. Nor could she save her.*
Beatrice: "But I failed to liberate you from this hell."

*Vigor returned to the waning Beatrice. It once again filled her with energy and radiance, infusing her voice with the strength it had previously lost, allowing it to soar unfettered and full of conviction.*
Beatrice: "I am not done yet! My blade has yet to shatter!"
*Her soul had yet to perish. And as long as she drew breath — no matter how little time she hadleft — Beatrice would keep on fighting.*
Beatrice: "I have learned this from you."
Beatrice: "Even if I cannot free you—"
*Even if she lacked the strength.*
Beatrice: "If I were to yield here, how would I face myself, Major?"
Beatrice: "I was unable to save the people I love; my family, my friends, my comrades. My loyalty to my former commander — to who she was — is all I have left.  I have nothing else, Major Wittenburg. Therefore...! "
Eleonore: "Do as you like."
*Vigor and bloodlust alike drained from Eleonore's face. Instead, she resolved to console Beatrice in her final moments.*
*The battle no longer mattered. In mere moments, Beatrice would fade away and die. Had circumstances been different, Eleonore would have bolstered the intensity of the flames enveloping Beatrice, bringing a swift end to their conflict. However—*
Eleonore: "You are a foolish child! An interminable half-wit who will carry her callowness to the grave. And yet, you've matured into an admirable knight. It would be remiss of me as your former commander not to bid you farewell with respect. Once you have become an Einherjar, return to my side. I shall lend an ear to all your complaints. "
*The cause behind the castle's tremors still eluded Eleonore, but no further oddities occurred. It was likely nothing significant. Lord Heydrich's might was unparalleled. Nothing in this universe could harm him. Consoled by these thoughts, Eleonore's disposition lightened as she placed a hand on her moribund subordinate's head in an attempt to soothe her distress.*
Beatrice: "...?!"

Eleonore's body was strengthened by the untold legion of souls under her command, and for a simple sword to be passing through her so easily defied all reason. Beatrice lacked in power, and her sword had been hollow.*

*The wound that had begun to close reopened once more, and fresh blood gushed forth with the force of a raging torrent. The heat of the scorching inferno surrounding them was no longer sufficient to vaporize the entirety of the outpouring fluid — Rubedo was splattered in crimson, altering her appearance to now completely match her title. Eleonore grasped the blade in both hands as she strived to force it away from her body. An instinctive action, which accomplished little other than slashing her hands.*
Eleonore: "What... have you done?"

Beatrice: "It seems the little ones saved me in the end."

Beatrice: "You were powerful beyond imagination. Were I alone, I would have fallen regardless of how much I struggled."

Eleonore: "I..."

Eleonore: "I care not for such trivialities! I have but one desire!"
*To serve Him as his Rubedo, to act as the Claws and Fangs of the Beast, to become a champion worthy of His grand ambition!*
Eleonore: "To live and die as Lord Heydrich's vassal means everything to me! I desire no redemption! No aid! For as long as I serve by his side, I cannot afford to falter!"
Eleonore: "I yearn only to be with him for an eternity. The advent of Dies Irae — the day we become one — is my only true Valhalla!"
Beatrice: "About time you showed your true colors."

*A smile graced Beatrice's lips as she acquiesced to the will of the soul inhabiting her sword. A soul that demanded she executed — through decapitation — the one standing before her. To resist was pointless.*
Eleonore: "Kircheisen..."
*Muspelheim was crumbling. The barrel of the cannon that contained the inferno had split, its flames licking the perimeter of the castle.*
Eleonore: "In time, I will revive. And once I do, we shall continue this. In the interim, don't think I'll allow you to escape. You shall perish alongside me! "

*Beatrice's sword finished its journey and sent Eleonore's head soaring into the sky.*
Eleonore: "Sieg Heil. May victory be yours, Lord Heydrich."
*Muspelheim erupted into flames. An explosion which threatened to shatter the walls of the devil's castle was perhaps an appropriate way for the purest of all women — one so passionate and sincere — to leave this world. And though she was immortal, an eternally resurrecting Einherjar, she still suffered a kind of death here.*
Beatrice: "Auf Wiedersehen, Obersturmführer."

Beatrice: "Be on your way."

Beatrice: "You would rather be with him than me now, wouldn't you? I'll be all right, so hurry along..."
*She threw her blade into the air with a gentle swing — it began to grow faint before disappearing for good.*
Beatrice: "A sweet girl..."
*Yet so miserable as well. Beatrice wished that she, too, could have found happiness in this world.*
Beatrice: "I'm sorry... I never possessed enough strength to make a dent in this world. But I did my best. Will you forgive me, Kai? "
*With the grace of a snowflake, she fell to her knees. In her present state, she was hardly different from snow — prone to crumbling at the lightest of touches. Not only was Beatrice's soul tremendously worn down, she had also received a fatal wound from the flames of Muspelheim. She knew she didn't have much time left.*
Beatrice: "You know how the Major is — I need to pursue and keep an eye on her. But don't worry — no matter what happens, I will remain myself. So please, forgive me. I love you all, and I wish I could have spent more time with you, but as you no doubt know, I am not from this age. The fatherland I left behind on that fateful day is where I must now return. "
*At this point, she did not even have enough strength to raise her face. Her feet and ankles had vanished, and the area around her thighs, too, was already growing faint.*
Beatrice: "I'd be lying if I said I had no regrets. After saying all those things to the Major, even I grew a bit ashamed of myself, you know... I mean, seriously. I'm an old lady at this point. I should be embarrassed of myself. I'm acting like such a fool. "

Kai: "You are beautiful."

She hid her worries, kept silent about her insecurities... but this was one sucker punch she couldn't foresee. Beatrice felt it simply unfair.*
Beatrice: "You ruined everything..."
Beatrice: "You fool..."

Beatrice: "I... I've been meaning to say this for the longest time now. I love you."

Machina: "Ngh?!"
Ren: "What the...?!"
*Seconds before my body shattered to dust just like Marie's guillotine, the strangest of things occurred.*
Machina: "Valkyria?"

Machina: "You knave—"

*And seeing how I could no longer halt time, luck was about the only thing left for me to rely on.*

Machina: "..."

Ren: "Aaaaaaarrrrrghhhh...!!"

*By claiming a new Ahnenerbe, I managed to save my soul from destruction.*
*All that was left now—*
Ren: "It's your turn to fall, Michael!"

Machina: "Ogh...!"
Ren: "You don't feel it was fair? To tell the truth, I feel pretty pathetic myself."

Ren: "I will be the one to survive."
*I would be the one to keep moving forward.*
Ren: "Your obsession with death blinded you to the future. All you could think of was how to die, and not how to live."

*Even if I was tainted by the shame of defeat, I would not succumb. I would continue pressing onwards.*
*Survival meant exactly that.*
Machina: "That... name..."

*In his eyes, I saw confusion, hesitation, and an undeniable feeling of nostalgia — he seemed like a child who had recovered something lost in ages past.*
Machina: "I see... Indeed, that was once my name."
Machina: "And you? What name do I use to address the man who defeated me? Tell me, comrade."
Ren: "..."

Machina: "Then live on, and remain true to yourself. No one can defeat Heydrich, nor can anyone escape Karl Krafft. As long as those two remain in cohorts..."
Machina: "I will make sure to watch your struggle as the events unfold, Kamerad. My wish may have crumbled to dust, yet this finale is one I can also accept. Being locked in eternal battle with you could very well be a form of release as well."

Ren: "...but there won't be a next time. I'm going straight home after I kick that bastard's ass."

Ren: "I've no intention of turning into this Einherjar crap you guys keep going on about."
Machina: "Then you must heed my words, at least this once."

Machina: "Let us meet again. Remember that we are fated for a rematch."

Ren: "Marie..."

*Even now, I could feel her presence slowly fading from the sword. Her place was within the guillotine — she couldn't stay here for long.*
*Beatrice's sword didn't have the capacity to sustain Marie's soul.*
*Only a handful of things ever went the way I wanted them to. If a few things worked out, a dozen others fell apart in their wake.*
Ren: "Damn... Some hero I turned out to be..."
*I swore not to acknowledge an end I didn't like.*
*And I vowed to save Kasumi and Sakurai, to protect Himuro until the very end. But in exchange, I lost her. I couldn't save Marie.*
Ren: "Fuck this... Fuck this. Fuck this. Fuck this...!!"

*Would she remain at that twilit beach in complete solitude? Would she continue to sing to the vast nothingness around her, unable to even laugh or cry?*
Ren: "I..."
*I knew I had to hurry. That every second counted.*

*You could call it self-serving sentimentality, but if I discarded even that part of myself, I truly would become nothing but an unfeeling killing machine.*
*We knew each other only for a short while. Hardly enough time to form an unbreakable bond.*
*That was Ren Fujii — that was the kind of man you'd saved.*

Marie: "Tears...?"
*She was seeing them for the first time. She knew what they were, but she never thought she would ever shed them herself.*
Marie: "Strange..."
*She felt something stir within her heart, something vexing and frustrating. But it wasn't entirely unpleasant. Though to say it was pleasant would have been a lie, too.*
Marie: "Oh. It's because Ren's crying."
*She witnessed something similar just a short while ago.*
*Something about how the one being rejected ends up in the worse position if the rejector breaks out in tears. She had no idea what to do, now that he was the one crying.*

*For some reason, she had been convinced of that. Her guillotine had shattered, and she lost all connection with the man — under normal circumstances, she should have known she would never meet him again.*
*Marie never understood the concept of reasoning all that much, but this feeling wasn't the result of mere wishful thinking. After all—*
Marie: "You're such a big fat liar, Cagliostro."

*For that man, the very concept of the unexpected did not exist. It was the very core of the curse that bound him — as such, nothing under the sun could betray his expectations until he fulfilled his goal. In short, he had foreseen even this particular turn of events. Alessandro di Cagliostro could never abandon Marguerite Breuilh, and so, this tale — with her as its main diva and crowning jewel — could never end like this. It would continue on and on, as many times as needed. And in one of those—*

Mercurius: "Ah, you needn't worry, Marguerite. I won't make you wait long."

Reviving a battalion is far more arduous a task than the resurrection of a mere handful of legionnaires. In any event, our military prowess appears to have suffered quite a humiliating blow indeed. "

It felt almost like this shade of a man cloaked himself in insecurity and repulsion, invoking anxiety in all who laid eyes upon him. Yet at the same time, it felt almost not right to kill the man. This wasn't an issue of possibility. Instead, it felt like the very idea of slaying him would invite terrible disaster upon the person who dared conceive the notion. Shirou didn't know how to properly explain the feeling, but long story short: he wanted nothing to do with the bastard. He was the walking embodiment of foreknowledge — the very phenomenon Shirou hated more than anything in the world.

Mercurius: "I am ___."

Shirou: "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAARGGGGGGGGGGGHHH!!!YOU MOTHERFUCKER...!!!"
At that point, he had lost his very ability to form words. Possessed by undiluted, unbridled fury for the very first time in his life, Shirou began firing his gun like a madman. And each of those moments: the flickering muzzle flash, the smell of gunpowder, the sound of exploding bullets, everything— It had been painfully known to him, burned into his memory. Foreknowledge, overwhelming him. Foreknowledge wherever he looked. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge. Foreknowledge.

After all...*

Reinhard: "I see. I must have underestimated it."
