*His words were the signal for the final holy war, long-awaited by the nameless, sombre slave of battle.*
Ren: "Ah...!?"
*Clad in a raven overcoat, a new opponent leapt over Reinhard's large corpus and fell right towards me.*
*I couldn't counterattack. No matter how much I accelerated my own time, I needed to constantly keep my attention on Reinhard, or face the consequences.*
*What could I do? Take the defensive? No, that was out of the question.*
*I needed to retreat. No matter by how small an amount, I had to distance myself from the field of destruction around his fist.*
Ren: "Guh, aaaaaaghhhhh!"
*Overexertion tore my leg muscles apart, but I ignored the pain, instead leaping backwards with power enough to make me fly far outside the radius of the tower's peak platform.*
*As I fell from a height of one hundred and fifty meters, I heard the tower's hulking mass being pulverized.*
Reinhard: "Go forth and impress me, final survivors of the gauntlet. Show me what is left when one consumes the self."
*As Reinhard walked towards the magic circle clouding the distant sky, the words he spoke rang bizarrely in my ears.*
*Consuming oneself? Gauntlet? What was he talking about?*
Reinhard: "Ouroboros and Caduceus. Though both are serpents, they are wholly different."
Reinhard: "Consuming their tails would reduce them to nothing, while making the two intertwine creates a spiral."
*It was either Machina or me.*
Reinhard: "Who will be the one to win his existence?"
*As I fell within the rain of shattered rubble, my gaze met with a pair of stygian black eyes.*
*They were like those of a dead fish — gloomy, cloudy, and with no visible emotion.*
*I had never exchanged words or blows with him — I had only seen him a second time now.*
*I should've had no connection to a man like him.*
*Yet somehow, I recognized him. A sudden feeling akin to a hunch told me that I had known this man for a long time.*
*Less like a delusion and more like foreknowledge, it made me remember the smell of gunpowder smoke.*
*The countless battles I had braved granted me an illusion of long-sought repose.*
*Yet in my foolishness, I did not realize that the glory earned in victories past was but a herald summoning me to the next stage of bloodshed.*
*I had enough. I wished for it to end.*
*The crimson of blood. The white of bones. The black of charred flesh. The gray of splattered entrails.*
*The gleam of bayonets. The metal of bullets. The oscillation of the ground in the wake of an army of creaking tanks. The feculent smell of trenches.*
*To escape them now, I had no choice but to embrace the carnage once more.*
Machina: "I cannot end unless I kill you."
*The iron Nigredo's bloodlust was intense enough to make me completely forget the impact of hitting the ground.*
Reinhard: "Karl, what is your prediction?"
*As he stood on the magic circle — the ark of the new world — all by his lonesome, Reinhard spoke to his non-present companion.*
Reinhard: "In all honesty, this is beyond me. Machina is unlikely to be defeated, but do take a look at this."
*The Beast exposed the left side of his neck — where he recently received a slash — revealing a thin crimson line moist with blood. He felt pain. How long had it been since he was last made aware of the crimson cradle of life flowing within him?*
Reinhard: "Would I have been slain, had I allowed him to continue? Hahaha. What say you, my friend? "
*Reinhard was unable to deny that possibility. The temporal axis of his recovery had deviated from that of Ren's development, so it was entirely possible for the continuation of that battle to completely turn the tides of war. The Beast couldn't tell if that was outside or within his expectations. However, that very deviation was what gave importance to the boy's battle with Nigredo, and made the course of events take a more dramatic turn.*
Reinhard: "Still, hmm... things are moving slower than I expected."
*The torment of foreknowledge had vanished. Following the emanation of Valhalla, he could no longer perceive it — at least not upon this magic circle. Yet the unknown eluded him still. The situation was perfectly centered in a way that made it difficult to predict where it would go. It implied an incompletion — the emanation wasn't proceeding as it should have. What had been the cause of that peculiar lag in progression? Reinhard gazed up with a pensive look on his face.*
Reinhard: "Did Isaak reconsider?"
*Or maybe there was more to the girl than met the eye?*
Reinhard: "Or perhaps..."
*Reinhard shifted his gaze downwards as a voice from somewhere far beyond gave an answer to his question.*
Mercurius: "Another Hegemony is on the verge of emanating."
Reinhard: "I see..."
Mercurius: "You drew your lance."
Reinhard: "Is it the girl?"
Mercurius: "Indeed; a change caused by you piercing her. For a rose bleeds when its thorns are plucked."
Mercurius: "She, the gem of the abyssal depths, has begun to emanate."
*In other words...*
Reinhard: "I see. So nothing was without meaning."
*His opponent's raw determination not to allow the opening of the eight prompted Reinhard to draw his lance. With that, the songstress — once a vessel of Transcendence — began to show signs of emanating a Hegemony, birthing a conflict that made Isaak's world stagnate. Zarathustra Ubermensch seized the opportunity and began to develop at menacing speeds. All those factors combined to create a situation which delayed the young Sonnenkind's — Rea's — melting. Thus, it was possible that she would make an attempt to resist.*
Reinhard: "A state of utter chaos, I see."
*Sublime and splendid. Events which did not go as Reinhard intended were a rarity for him.*
Reinhard: "Hardship only sweetens the taste of victory. A Hegemony? Aye, I do see what you mean. This script of yours is unexpectedly tasteful, Karl. "
Mercurius: "Now, whatever do you imply?"
Reinhard: "No need to feign ignorance. Do you still deny holding this situation in the palm of your hand? If so..."
Mercurius: "Yes. At the very least..."
Reinhard: "Let us retreat to the seats of observers for a short while."
Mercurius: "That is for the best. My interference seldom births joyous results. I shall remain a part of the audience and await you at the other plane, my beastly companion. "
Mercurius: "I am certain that these three battles will be worth a gander."
Reinhard: "Indeed. Why not make a wager, as well?"
*The twin devils gazed down upon the three scenes unfolding far below, speculating with regards to their respective outcomes.*
Mercurius: "Why, of course..."
Machina: "Let us now begin."
*The sombre knight, Nigredo...*
Eleonore: "Come with all you have."
*The crimson knightess, Rubedo...*
Schreiber: "You're not getting away."
*The ashen knight, Albedo...*
*The two leaders doubtlessly believed that their three Battalion Commanders would grasp the victories they so fervently believed in.*
Eleonore: "That was quite the farce back there."
*Standing atop the bridge, Eleonore faced her opponent with a confident grin.*
Eleonore: "No one was foolish enough to fall for it. I'm sure you didn't have foul play in mind, so what were you planning?"
*The one to answer that question was...*
Kei: "Nothing much. It is a personal matter."
*...Kei Sakurai. The very same person who had her Ahnenerbe shattered by Reinhard for the opening of the eighth. Her presence here was consequently both impossible and inconsistent — the completion of the Swastika stood as undeniable proof. The destruction of Kei's Ahnenerbe — along with the scattering of its souls — remained a fact difficult to deny. Why was she here, then?*
Eleonore: "You claim it doesn't matter to us?"
Kei: "At the very least, I knew full well that I could not fool you."
Eleonore: "Makes sense. After all..."
Kei: "You are the one who gave me this."
*Kei brandished Tubal Cain's Wewelsburg Longinus. The very same moment her Scharlachrot was vaporized, she made a new pact with the other Ahnenerbe. The only souls to scatter on the opening of the eighth were those of people the girl killed by herself. Her own soul was still with her, in Cain's heirloom — the greatsword that lost its size and became more of a longsword.*
*Or perhaps a more apt way of describing it would be to say that her soul was about to be devoured by the instrument. Normally, such convenient exchange of weaponry would be impossible. Ample proficiency might allow one to use another Ahnenerbe, but an actual switch of pacts simply could not be done. After all, their wielders were chosen; the Ahnenerbe themselves would discern and select the kind of souls they wanted. Compatibility was key. Those who wielded Ahnenerbe were essentially slaves meant to provide them with sacrifices.*
*Any master would pick a useful slave instead of the other way around, so the wielder was completely stripped of the freedom to pick their weapon. If there was anyone who could overturn this system of control, it would be someone who was born for that sake, such as an Ahnenerbe meant to wield other Ahnenerbe.*
*However, Kei was an ordinary person without any such extraordinary privileges. Thus, this was merely another case of the weapon choosing its wielder. Moments before her death, Kei was conveniently chosen by the other Ahnenerbe she possessed. Such an event could easily be acknowledged as accidental or miraculous, yet neither she nor the woman before her saw it as anything special. Eleonore nodded.*
Eleonore: "Wouldn't expect anything else. That thing only goes after you Sakurais. The previous owner died and the next fodder was made empty and contractless, so it came after you without hesitation."
Eleonore: "Many would label it a curse, but it saved your life. Or rather, you were the one who made good use of it. Admirable tact, whelp. You deserve my praise. I have always taken you for a dimwitted cur, but you appear to have a decent head on your shoulders. "
Kei: "You seem very knowledgeable."
Eleonore: "Of course I am. I'm the one who had it made."
*She shook her head and spoke in a voice devoid of pride or delight, sounding more like a complaint.*
Eleonore: "The Wewelsburg Longinus... A trifling thing not worthy of a second glance. Kristoff would probably call it a heretical forgery of God."
Eleonore: "It sickens me to be in agreement with that priest, but in all honesty, its very existence tries my patience.Himmler's pathetic jealousies and fears about Lord Heydrich being the only one able to wield the true lance are of no concern to me. However, Lord Heydrich ordered me to do it, and His word is absolute. The replica would work as a symbol to fulfill Himmler's vanity, give him peace of mind, and grant us at the Obsidian Table some new war potential... In that sense, it was not completely without value. Thus, I had your great-grandfather leave this country and come to us. Although I wasn't too fond of the idea, I was kind enough to have you, as honorary Aryans, join us at the table. "
Kei: "Kind enough...?"
Eleonore: "Yes. Be delighted, for your kin are now blessed with the honor of having a seat alongside us."
Kei: "We swing this forgery for generations on end, eternally bound to the Obsidian Table... And you speak to me of honor?"
Eleonore: "What else would I call it?"
*The voice of the crimson knightess was devoid of sarcasm — Eleonore honestly believed what she had just uttered, and their previous exchanges had taught Kei not to question her sincerity. Thus, Kei's heart would not waver. Her opponent would not be felled by a mere outburst of anger. In fact, the girl was strangely calm — even a bit joyous. Kei felt like this event was a gift from the divine. Almost as if she had been born solely for the sake of defeating the woman before her.*
Kei: "You have my thanks, Lady Samiel."
*The girl raised the false lance like she would a sword. Tonight would mark the end of the road they were forced to walk for sixty years — a path paved in blood and death.*
Kei: "No battle is as meaningful as this."
*The Wewelsburg Longinus only consumed the Sakurai bloodline — its owners and creators. Over time, using its powers as an inferior Einherjar producing tool, it built the corpse warrior known as Tubal Cain.*
That was Kei's fate if she were to wield it: to be a living corpse that knew no pain — a slave to strife till the day she crumbled to ash. However, she was fine with that — the girl would merely follow in the footsteps of her bloodline. That was the "personal matter" she had mentioned before. 
*In her eyes, Ren Fujii was a great bully. Survival? Joining the party? Impossible. She would do neither. Kei couldn't return to their world. She couldn’t live alongside them. Kei hoped the others would think her dead and leave it at that. Yet if she were to die, she would take her opponent down with her, no matter the cost.*
*Eleonore von Wittenburg. The crimson Rubedo. A Battalion Commander of the Obsidian Table. If returning to the world of sunlight had been denied to her for good, Kei would at least drag her foe down to hell. Not to Lord Heydrich's Valhalla, but the true depths of the abyss.*
Kei: "I'm done looking at your face."
*She was standing before a true Einherjar — an immortal abomination. To fight and defeat her, the girl herself had to become immortal as well, even if her means were inferior. Kei had to cross this woman's hellfire, no matter the cost. Even if she lost her arms to the flames, or had her legs consumed and vaporized — even if she remained nothing but a skull without limbs — she would fight on and sink her teeth into Eleonore's windpipe. Her entire being was afire with burning resolve.*
Kei: "I won't leave a single strand of your hair in this world."
Kei: "You likely died as a person the very moment you met Lord Heydrich."
Eleonore: "Hmph... Bold words from a whelp too young to have been there."
Kei: "True, but I feel like I'm right."
*Kei felt strange. Almost as if she was both herself and someone else at the same time... ...and that person was talking through her. It might have been a hallucination, but she didn't mind. After all, it made her certain that she was alongside 'them'.*
Eleonore: "You..."
*The look in Eleonore's eyes changed. Her stare was cold as ice, yet her pupils lit up with a devilish blaze.*
Eleonore: "You're unpleasant."
*A sickening subhuman that knew not her place.*
Eleonore: "I'm quite certain I told you to stop making a mockery of my subordinate."
*How dared this yellow-skinned, dark-haired wretch of a girl imitate her valkyrie. Even if it truly was her, to Eleonore, the girl addressing her was nothing like the one she knew all those years ago.*
Kei: "You truly have changed."
*Words that the woman didn't want to hear her say.*
Kei: "Are you still as blinded as before, 'Lieutenant'?"
*Her words were the final spark to their battle.*
Kei: "I will save you."
*Lightning, fierce and pure, began to flow through the false lance. Kei didn't know what the sparks meant... ...while Eleonore instantly recalled a certain foolish girl. Valkyria — the Obsidian Table's very own battle maiden. The one and only woman who — even as she braved countless battlefields thick with madness and reeking of blood — never once discarded her humanity.*
*Kei felt like she knew her opponent well. With unmistakable conviction burning in her heart, she spoke — of her own volition — words that belonged to someone else.*
Kei: "You are weak."
*Weak enough to be content with being eternally scorched by a light forever beyond her reach. Discarding pride and honor, she gave her heart to an utter scoundrel of a man, choosing to present the act as loyalty.*
*A person hardly deserving to be called human. A woman less experienced than most maidens. Any observer could easily puzzle out why she harbored such a fierce dislike for Lisa... ...while being completely blind to the true reason herself. Eleonore avoided acknowledging it.*
Eleonore: "Are you done..."
*A demonic cannon muzzle materialized out of thin air about twenty meters away from the girl. The distance itself posed no problem for Kei — she could close it in an instant.*
Eleonore: "...spouting your nonsense?"
Kei: "Yes. From now on, my steel does the talking."
*She would make her understand. Without fail.*
Kei: "As a fellow woman, I simply couldn't bear losing to you."
*Someone whispered a confirmation of agreement... ...and told Kei that she should be able to understand it now. She replied with a faint, bitter smile.*
Kei: "Well, you might be correct."
*A short while ago, she became aware of a feeling not entirely unlike love blossoming within her heart. She had quite a bit to say about that, but she also acknowledged that denial could lead to her becoming just like her enemy. Kei wasn't fond of such a scenario.*
*And so, she vowed to prevail, no matter what.*
*The devilish artillery opened fire upon the girl, who began running along its trajectory and straight towards Rubedo. The cursed lance rumbled as it absorbed her soul and gradually made her into a corpse, limb by limb. However, she wasn't afraid. Until the moment Kei's blade pierced the woman's chest, conveying their feelings... ...the girl vowed to fight on, even beyond death.*
*At the same time, another battle — its flames ignited earlier than the rest — edged ever closer to its conclusion.*
Schreiber: "Is that really all you've got?"
*Wolfgang Schreiber sat on the ruins of the amusement park and heaved a saddened sigh. Not a hair on his head was harmed — in fact, his opponent had yet to land a single hit. On the other hand...*
Shirou: "Come on now, don't rush me. Just gimme a moment."
*...Shirou had sat down, his body covered in wounds and gleaming with fresh blood. Though none of his injuries proved fatal, the power differential between him and his opponent was blatantly obvious. It was barely even a fight. Shirou was quite a big deal. While Kei — the self-proclaimed normalgirl — was handling Ahnenerbe for eleven years, and Ren — the one under the auspices of Karl Krafft — had been in this for only two weeks, Shirou had a mere three days. Materializing his Ahnenerbe and facing Wilhelm right on the spot was excellent proof of his downright miraculous talent.*
*However, that was the extent of it. Despite his rapid growth, he was far from being powerful enough to rival Albedo, one of the Gold's Imperial Guard. Not to mention that Schreiber held a troublesome characteristic which completely nullified any standard differences in ability.*
Schreiber: "Alright. Let's talk, then. You may use this as an opportunity to heal or search me for openings. Do whatever you want."
*Schreiber's lips curled into a smile, sending the clear message that Shirou's attempts would be futile. The ashen boy was brimming with confidence, but not to the point of conceit.*
Schreiber: "Krafft once said that we Battalion Commanders work as a three-way deadlock. Do you know what I mean? 'A' wins against 'B', but loses to 'C', which loses to 'B'. Do you people have a name for that? "
Shirou: "Rock, paper, scissors...?"
Schreiber: "Yeah, that."
*The three Battalion Commanders were a three-way deadlock. Strengths and weaknesses went in a circular pattern.*
Schreiber: "I don't agree with it, though."
*The animal believed he could lose to no one. However, once the three's characteristics were considered, they could easily have such formulas applied to them. There was nothing more to it than that.*
Schreiber: "Machina, who kills in one clean hit. Samiel, who never misses a shot. And... "
*Wolfgang Schreiber's unique trait.*
Schreiber: "...I, who never gets hit."
*None were able to touch him. He could dodge all attacks with swiftness surpassing human cognition. Schreiber was a being of raw speed, soaring faster than anyone else. As long as time itself didn't grind to a complete halt, the maddened Albedo would never be caught. No matter the battle, a critical difference in speed never left any hope for the slow.*
Schreiber: "Machina is strong, yes. I even respect him a bit. However, he could never defeat me."
*Though Nigredo's fists were dreadfully fatal, they meant nothing unless he could land a hit. Not to mention that Schreiber — his mind a whirlpool of madness — knew no fear at all. The worry of getting hit would not even enter his mind.*
Schreiber: "Now, apparently, Samiel might be able to catch me... but I'm not too sure about that. Well, take it with a grain of salt. It's not like you can do what they can."
Shirou: "Hah..."
Schreiber: "Hmm?"
Shirou: "How does black win against red?"
Schreiber: "Oh. Well..."
*Schreiber shrugged as if to state that it was obvious.*
Schreiber: "The strength of their souls is about the same. While Machina is unable to dodge Samiel's cannons, he probably wouldn't die in one hit. Then comes the logic of any heavy weaponry. Just like artillery needs to reload, so does Samiel needs to recharge. That is when Machina closes in and shoves one in her face. In any shootout between fatal artillery, the deciding factor is who can stand the longest. It's just a contest of endurance. "
Shirou: "Oh, I get it."
*Seemingly realizing something, Shirou slowly got up.*
Shirou: "So you're just a bug who'd get blown away by a single hit, right?"
Schreiber: "Huh?"
*That was the first time he had heard something like that. Schreiber widened his eyes, bursting out into a roaring laughter.*
Schreiber: "Hah, hahah! I see, I get it. That makes sense. You may be right."
*The ashen boy never got hit, so he couldn't deny that possibility. However, he wouldn't give anyone the opportunity to find out.*
Schreiber: "Khah, hahahah! I like you. You're so funny! You're a sharp one. I didn't think you'd notice something like that. You actually surprised me. "
Shirou: "You'd have to be stupid not to see it."
Schreiber: "Really? Not many people could think that far in your situation, if you ask me."
*As in, a situation in which they faced an enemy they couldn't catch. Even if Schreiber's flesh was as fragile as glass, it didn't matter if no one could land a hit on him.*
Shirou: "Big words coming from a chickenshit who's only good at running around."
Schreiber: "Hmm. Okay. Let's just say that I won't be falling for any of that."
*In spite of his nature, Albedo was also a composed character. He was one for nonsensical mood swings and creating storms of violence, but — strangely enough — he wasn't stupid. He was likely too simple to be influenced by external forces. His broken reasoning knew no sympathy, so anyone's state of mind was but a phenomenon to him. One could go as far as to say that he was the greatest profiler. Through all the blood he bathed in and screams he savored, Schreiber was a monster very much familiar with his prey.*
*Psychological warfare was meaningless against him.*
Schreiber: "Apparently, my craving is to not be touched by anyone. I don't really think it's true, but that’s what Krafft says."
Shirou: "What, your old man rip it off or somethin'?"
Schreiber: "Oh, how did you know?"
Shirou: "'How did I know'? Oh, hell no..."
*Shirou was astounded by the boy’s nonchalant way of answering the question. Was that it? Was that the reason behind it? And the nimble bastard didn't even realize it?*
Schreiber: "My circumstances were hardly uncommon, really. I loved my Mutter. That was just how I made a living. If I couldn't get any customers, we'd have no food on our table, you know? "
*Schreiber spoke with a beaming, cherubic smile. Shirou could tell the bastard was being completely serious from the lack of any speck of gloom on that innocent visage.*
*It was enough to make him sick. A curse that drove bile up his throat.*
Schreiber: "Mutter wanted a daughter. So the two of us could be sold together and loved by customers till the end of our days. Be gentle. Lay with me. Embrace me. Love me. She was a beautiful woman. She didn’t need a son. So Vater took away the part that made me undesirable. That way, we could be sold as a set, just like Mutter wanted. My real name is Anna. Wolfgang was my Vater's name. "
*Shirou's instincts told him to not let the ashen boy continue his speech. Though the whole thing made him sick to his stomach, Shirou wasn't one to allow sympathy to stifle his battle lust. Therefore, the decision was entirely tactical.*
*If he allowed that thing to continue his talk, it wouldn't end well. Shreiber himself seemed to be oblivious to it, but his opponent felt like there was a sordid, festering broth of rotten emotion boiling within him... ...one that was about to burst out into the open.*
Schreiber: "I was called a mistake."
*The ashen knight looked up at the distant sky, spreading out his arms as if to embrace something.*
*Things were looking bad. He was talking too much. Shirou fixed his aim and pulled the trigger. The bullet shot forth with a gunpowder explosion.*
Schreiber: "You filth, you scum, don't get conceited, you trash! You're nothing but a man! I'm prettier and I'm an actual woman!"
Schreiber: "You're just an abomination, a freak of nature! A wretched mistake!"
*Leaving a thunderous burst of sound behind him, Schreiber vanished from sight.*
Schreiber: "That's right! I'm neither man, nor woman!"
*The impact that followed preceded a scream.*
Shirou: "Ghh, aaaaghhhh!"
*The surprise attack from the left was likely a full-body ram, no more. However, its speed made it feel more like a cannon shot. Blown away, Shirou flew through the air like a piece of wood. It would take less than a second for him to hit the ground, but that was enough time for Schreiber to attack him more than a hundred times. Amidst the ruins of the amusement park, a devilish circus would be enacted.*
Schreiber: "I killed my Mutter and my Vater — a woman and a man. I slaughtered everyone, young and old alike!"
Schreiber: "They just died! They all died so easily! What am I, then!? What am I if I don't die no matter how many times they kill me!?"
*The maddened Albedo showed no sign of stopping. Like a ray of light diffusing throughout the area, he soared across the skies while delivering blows to Shirou in midair. More than four seconds had passed, but he didn't fall — his opponent didn't let him. Little by little, he was being scraped, clawed, and bitten. The attacks would continue until there was no more flesh to be torn from his body. Thus, Shirou had to put up some form of resistance.*
Schreiber: "I am an immortal creature. To not leave children is the same as never dying!"
Shirou: "Quit spouting your bullshit, you fucking..."
*He couldn't fix him in his sights, nor could he catch up to his speed. Therefore, there was only one thing for him to do.*
Shirou: "...Oedipus complex freak!"
*Since he was the target, Shirou's position was right above the trajectory Schreiber would surely follow, so he spread his chains out, centering on that one point. He couldn't see or seize him by being assertive, so building a net and waiting was the rational course of action. His enemy would come in less than a hundredth of a second. However...*
Schreiber: "Ahahahahahahah! Too slow!"
*Rational tactics meant nothing against a monster so thoroughly bereft of common sense. Schreiber slipped past all chains in his way and closed in on Shirou.*
Schreiber: "I don't die, and yet, you killed Anna."
*His blue eye gleamed with the hue of bloodlust as he took out his guns, aiming them at Shirou from a point-blank range.*
Schreiber: "How dare you kill me?"
*Spouting some unrelatable nonsense of a reasoning, the ashen boy was about to pull the trigger...*
Shirou: "Yeah, I'll kill ya right now."
*...but then he — the unseeable, unpredictable, and uncatchable — was right before Shirou's muzzle.*
Shirou: "I knew this shit couldn't catch you, dumbass."
*The net was only meant to limit Schreiber's movements and help Shirou predict them. No matter how fast he was, anyone could beat him to the punch if they knew his trajectory.*
Shirou: "Go to your mommy. Sweet dreams."
Schreiber: "...!"
*Suddenly, a ring of fire bloomed before him.*
Shirou: "Ghhh...!"
*The weapon in Shirou's hands was no ordinary gun, imbued with characteristics from Rusalka's Ahnenerbe, housing devilish bullets able to deal critical damage. The shooter was blown away by the shockwave and rolled on the ground. From the feeling in his hands, he could tell that his shot was a clean hit.*
Schreiber: "[Yetzirah](Formation)."
*Nonetheless, he could hear an ominous voice coming from beyond the blackened smoke. It wasn't shaking with rage, nor trembling with shock. The voice remained silent and still. If pure murderous intent was audible, it would surely sound something like this.*
Schreiber: "[Lyngvi Vanargand](Tornado of Carnage)."
*The curtain of smoke scattered as if torn apart by the demonic beast.*
Shirou: "Ah...!"
*Before he could realize what had just happened, Shirou's nostrils and mouth were clouded by a certain stench. The smell of blood. A foul stench from victims numbering in the tens of thousands. All pointing to a terrible machine-beast that ground myriads to dust, casting them to the depths of the abyss as they wailed in hellish agony. Its soul-chilling rumble was the fierce exhaust of combusted blood. The single headlight, reminiscent of the owner's one eye, sliced through the stygian night and illuminated Shirou. It was...*
Schreiber: "So you made me bring this out."
*...a Zundapp KS750 — the military two-wheeler designed to blitz through the carnage of the battlefield. It was far smaller than many monster machines of the present, but its sinister shape and heavy exhaust note gave it a downright devilish impression. This beast of a machine was in a completely different league compared to vehicles created for public roads or trifling games in stadiums. In essence, it could be regarded in the same category as tanks and fighter planes. The steel demon was created for war, the flesh it pulverized standing as undeniable proof of its nightmarish nature.*
Shirou: "I see... So that's the main unit."
*Shirou finally realized that Schreiber had yet to suffer a single injury. He was completely unscathed. His shot only hit the ashen knight's guns, which explained the intensity of the explosion, as well as the boy coming out unscathed. The guns weren't Albedo's Ahnenerbe. After all, there was no reason for someone faster than a speeding bullet to ever rely on something so counter-productive. The fierce beast was still completely undamaged.*
Schreiber: "...You've gone and done it now."

*It wasn't about repeating the same things over and over, but being reborn sometime into the future.*
*If her world had a similar design, wouldn't it be possible for me to meet everyone else again?*
*Our ages would probably be all over the place.*
*The countries we'd be born in would likely be different, too.*

*A moment later...*
*I could feel her...*

Ren: "Hah..."
Ren: "Hahah..."

Ren: "Then..."
Ren: "I have to tell Kasumi to live a long life."
*We would surely meet again.*
*As I stood there, cradled by sunlight, its warmth conveyed that my wish would not be in vain.*
*Other Story――"Omnia vincit Amor" unlocked.*
*Both her consciousness and body floated in the air. The ever-continuous sensation of rising went on for a while longer until she finally landed in her determined spot.*
Rea: "Ah..."
*The first thing to fill her vision was a field of flowers. Scenery she had seen once before. The hell of affectionate love welcomed Rea Himuro to its confines with blooming flowers.*
Rea: "..."
*Again. It seemed like the place of her damnation did not change. The brisk atmosphere and the scent of flowers remained the same as before. The light breeze gently caressed her cheeks, and as such, she could not keep disappointment away from her heart. Nothing had changed. A picture was worth a thousand words.*
*Rea shook her head, casting the dark thoughts away. Now was not the time for idle thoughts. Things had changed. And she would prove it. Believing that she was not invited here without a reason, she stood up out of her own volition.*

The scenery seemed as gentle as always, the air carrying the scent of earth, flowers, and honey. A Hell that looked like paradise. At the very least, it was bad enough for her to never wish to come here again.*

This was a graveyard birthed by love. Be it excessive or deficient, a nigh-tangible sorrow filled its every pore. As such, those orphans from before should still be somewhere around...*
Rea: "Where are they?"
*She couldn't find a single soul.*

The priest — their substitute father — was similarly nowhere in sight. Rea felt like a lone flower in the entire garden. Strange. This was an eternal torture chamber of affection and hate. No emotions or obsessions could come into being without having a target, and thus, it made little sense for her to be here alone.*

There was not a hint of emotion in those vessels of glass — he clearly did not regard Rea as a fellow human being.*

He carried out his procedures with utmost uniformity — equally and without limit. The eternal engine could manage Hell precisely because it was unchanging.*

Confirmation and denial were both equal as a response. There was nothing odd about his impregnable demeanor. If anything, Rea's insistence to ask a question she already knew the answer to could be labeled far more strange.*

The mind of a devil that failed to find true value in the entire cosmos. Ravaged by a hunger to devour all, yet unable to appreciate a single thing.*

Men call something absolute precisely because nothing else can match it. "

*The castle above me burst apart, spreading across the heavens and taking the shape of a giant magical circle.*
*I knew well enough what the opening of the eighth Swastika meant.*

*The Serpent retained his smile — neither his voice nor his gaze betrayed any sign of trepidation. He had come to know a billion differing hues of despair. Reinhard: "...!"
*Reinhard felt bereaved of his sense of reality. He woke suddenly, and with unprecedented discomfort.*
Reinhard: "Where am I...?"
*Still in a daze, he turned around to be met with a familiar sight reflected in his confused eyes. That worn, wooden desk. The mountain of papers resting on it. The cup of tea, now seemingly cold as ice. There was nothing strange about this. He was in his very own office — the one he had been granted following his promotion to Lieutenant General.*
Reinhard: "Did I fall asleep?"
*He shook his head, his features contorting in frustration. Not due to the headache, but rather the irritating fact that he nodded off before finishing up his papers. He must have slept for about... ten minutes, it seemed. He reflected upon himself apathetically.*
*Negligence and sloth were two characteristics a man of his stature — the executioner of the state — could under no circumstances be allowed to exhibit. His pride would never forgive it, either. Responsibility was the duty of a modern man. It mattered little if the task itself was trifling and time-consuming. He was no more than an automaton at whom the world would hardly even bother to bare its fangs. Lieutenant Generals or mere rank-and-file — all were but cogs in one giant mechanism. There was no place in it for those who failed to fulfill their duties.*
Reinhard: "..."
*Reinhard skimmed through one of the papers, scribbling his signature at the bottom of the page. A highly menial form of labor he had been repeating for countless days now. Scandals, censorship, regulations, propaganda. They were all the same. Death to all the guilty, as well as those in the gray area, just for good measure. He would then pick one or two from the innocent to make an example. Anyone could do it. No one in the Third Reich would hold him accountable, even if he made a mistake.*
*The kind of menial labor even a child could carry out. Reinhard received this position only because he would rest less than the others and thus do it slightly more efficiently. The world had yet to see a blander man. It seemed almost as if he was born only to carry out the work that others instructed him to.*
Reinhard: "Quite the preposterous dream that was. Me, a master of Hell?"
*The dream he had was simply that far beyond the realm of common sense. He became a King of the Dead — a Totenkopf Emperor — that lorded over an entire Legion of abominations.*
*He hadn't heard of anything more ridiculous. A notion fit for a child's daydream or a madman's delusions. A rotten hallucination experienced by lunatics as they drifted asleep, pumped full of sedatives. Vile and in utterly bad taste. Incomprehensible. The apparent vileness of his own subconscious left Reinhard somewhat surprised. The final morsels of love and respect he still felt for himself evaporated then and there.*
Reinhard: "Did the war finally get to me...? Surely not."
*Ridiculous. The very definition of nonsense. He had been born immune to the thrill of emotions. Not once had he felt warmth in his breast. The only smiles he knew how to produce were ones that sent a chill down the spine... And even those he managed only once or twice in his life. As such, it was difficult to imagine that a turmoil of fickle and aimless justice could possibly affect him in any noticeable fashion.*
*Country. People. Ideals. Race. Religion. They could all fight for whatever they wanted — it mattered little. There was no shortage of pretexts in the world. Meanwhile, he would simply continue doing his job. He would carry out all orders that reached him from above without a moment's rest, for Reinhard Heydrich's entire existence hinged on the fact that he refused to ever cut corners when it came to his profession. A boring man who lived in a monochrome and orderless world.*
Reinhard: "Yet to think how joyfully I laughed in that dream..."
*Never would he wear a smile so broad. To even toy with the notion was folly, for it was an aspiration that no amount of years would fulfill. The derisive smirk of a devil or a god gazing down from beyond the far heavens. The muscles in his cheeks were rigid as steel. Merely opening his mouth meant a troublesome task — one could almost hear his jaw creak with effort.*
*So was that dream a manifestation of his secret desires? The delusional yearnings that he himself had not been conscious of? A far-fetched fantasy that all men dream of at least once or twice in their youthful days? The self-consolation of the psyche. A demolition of reality.Could it be that becoming the lord of a legion of demons was precisely what his heart truly desired?*
Reinhard: "Come in."
*He answered the knock at the door. Reinhard's pointless contemplation vanished without a trace by the time he raised his face from the papers on his desk. A man entered the room in an orderly manner. As Reinhard spotted the insignia of a colonel on his collar, all his attention instantly shifted to work.*
Colonel: "Pardon my intrusion, Lieutenant General!However, there is a certain matter that I judged you should..."
Reinhard: "You can dispense with the long-winded introductions. As you can see, I still have a mountain of reports to attend to. If the matter is indeed of great urgency, go ahead and get on with it. My time is limited."
*The colonel glanced at the papers on the desk. He knew Reinhard was not a man to mince words, and as such, promptly straightened his back and began his report.*
Colonel: "Yes, sir! We've received reports that a mere few hours ago..."
*A noise. He could feel a lid slide away from his memories. Ah, the man did not need to utter another breath, for Reinhard already knew.*
Reinhard: "A failed assassination attempt?"

Reinhard: "..."
*Reinhard's features remained impassive in response to his subordinate's surprise. But it was he who wished to be surprised. Reinhard uttered words that he could not have known as if having remembered them. In fact, the sensation did not feel fresh at all.*
*An oddly uncanny feeling, as if he had just stared into the eyes of his reflection in the mirror, unsure of which one of them was real. A sensation that he had been intimately familiar with, as if it had tormented him his entire life. An immense feeling of discomfort stirred the resignation nestling within his heart. Reinhard found it unpleasant, yet never would he allow it to show. He instead stood up as if trying to continue the conversation, taking a few steps towards the door...*
Reinhard: "Lead the way. You can brief me on the details as we walk."
*...as if attempting to expunge that inexplicable emotion from his chest.*
Mercurius: "November 20, 1939... A sudden explosion occurs during the speech of the German Empire's Führer and Chancellor, Adolf Hitler. This event — sending tremors across the whole of Europe — would prove to bring us together."
Mercurius: "The German Empire, having fallen into poverty and despair following its defeat in the first World War, had risen from the ashes like a phoenix with the advent of its new charismatic leader, and set out on a new path to hegemony by promptly invading its surrounding nations."
Mercurius: "The event would go on to spark the flames of the second and — as many had hoped — last World War, far exceeding in scale and terror the one that preceded it. And it is now that the curtains of that very same war begin to silently rise. "

And that was hardly a surprise — only about ten percent of the offenders brought in could leave the place alive. Such were the prospects of one apprehended by the Gestapo. Past offenses did not matter. Short of a select few exceptional circumstances, they would merely cook up a charge of their own, and proceed to execute the hapless convict before they realized what was happening.*

*Reinhard could decide both the sin and the degree of the punishment. That was right within the limits of his current authority. As such, he would simply do it again in this case.*
*Though it might seem like the excuse of a callous bigot, being in the wrong place at the wrong time was just as grave a sin as any other in the present state of society. The weak had ways to protect themselves. The past deeds of the current "culprit" failed to guarantee his innocence, and that was more than enough to put him to death. Reinhard condemned the ineptitude of a man he had yet to meet.*
Colonel: "How exactly do you mean?"
Reinhard: "What was his name?"

*It was time to take care of the situation in that cell.*
*He proceeded down the coarse hallway. He was but a few steps away from the rusted iron bars separating him from the man inside.*

*Paying no heed to the odd sensation akin to discontinuous intoxication, he finally reached the cell. A shade of a silhouette sat inside in utter serenity with an almost mocking smirk on its lips.
