He could not help narrowing his eyes at the odd man who — despite most certainly being here — seemed almost like a projection from somewhere afar.*
*His very existence was thin, as if it had withered and shriveled up. He resembled an old man who had achieved everything he could ever want in life; Reinhard could not feel even a hint of vitality or hope from him. His obsidian eyes seemed to have been frozen in a state of eternal decay, like a pair of colorful — yet lifeless — agates. Gazing into his eyes felt like looking at a dead fish, or rather... A sea creature that somehow survived being pulled out of the unknown depths.*
*A fish that should have only been able to live in complete darkness, yet — by some mistake — learned how to breathe oxygen and found itself awfully out of place. And so it remained unable to accomplish its only desire — to die and vanish for good. It yearned to return to the water, yet all it could do was meaninglessly hop up and down on the ground. It craved succor. A being that seemed a condensation of its reliance on others — a human trait Reinhard despised.*
*As such, he could declare one thing with absolute conviction. There was no way this man could have plotted to kill the Führer. He... it had no feelings or aspirations to begin with. He would find no meaning in an assassination. He would not care if the whole country turned upside down on the morrow. A random piece of nonsense he uttered happened to accidentally coincide with the truth. That was all. At that point, the possibility of that man being the culprit had completely vanished from Reinhard's mind. A withered tree had no aspirations. It could only wish to eventually become fodder for the flowers.*
*And that fact — for some inexplicable reason — filled him with disappointment. Reinhard, despite his inability to feel empathy or emotions, seemed to have been expecting something from this man without realizing it. Ridiculous. He directed his gaze back to the vague shadow. Its beady glass eyes answered him with a hint of curiosity.*
Reinhard: "So you are the rebel they speak of? You don't look much the part, I'm afraid. My name is—"
Mercurius: "Lieutenant General Reinhard Tristan Eugen Heydrich. The director of the secret state police, the Gestapo. Your official name encompasses all that is noble about our Great German Empire, while your other title can be heard whispered in the shadows — The Hangman."
Mercurius: "I am honored to meet you. My name is Karl Ernst Krafft; I am usually a swindler, and at best a terrorist. Those labels most certainly fit me better than the dubious title of magician."
Reinhard: "I see."
*The man interrupted him, finally showing some life in his bearing. With that, Reinhard had to up his impression of him a little. It had been a long time since someone got ahead of him. That voice certainly sounded fit for lies and deceit, and indeed, gave the impression of insensitivity to pain. Regardless of how much malice had been directed at him, that smile of his would most likely never waver.*
Reinhard: "You seem an interesting sort. Not many could smile in my presence, especially men in your circumstances."
*He had courage, at least, for all the good it did him.*
Reinhard: "Allow me to be direct: do you wish to die?"
*For if he hoped to survive, that previous tirade was a severe blunder. It was hardly the attitude one ought to assume in front of the head of the Gestapo.*
Reinhard: "My livelihood is to punish those that pose a threat to our country. Should you truly turn out to be a swindler and a terrorist, I will have no choice but to stay true to that fatuous second name of mine."
Mercurius: "Oh? Could it be that you are not proud of your label?"
Reinhard: "Perhaps. But I do not mix personal feelings with my occupation, or rather, I serve in this position precisely because my emotions are faulty."
*His world had no colors. His breast had not known heat even once in his life. As such, there was no one more fitting to mete out impersonal punishment. He judged everyone equally, leaning towards neither of the extremes, mixing no hint of emotion into his decisions.*
Reinhard: "Answer me, then: are you a man to whom my duties should extend?"
*The swindler smiled, not minding Reinhard's piercing gaze in the slightest.*
Mercurius: "A colossal pity it may be, but my only choice is to acquiesce. However..."
Mercurius: "In regard to the attempt on the life of His Excellency the Führer — and my supposed involvement with the nefarious plot — I have to answer in the negative. I have done no such thing."
*A meaningless statement, if Reinhard had ever heard one. He had long since grown tired of those accused pleading innocence, and knew exactly how to deal with them.*
Reinhard: "They all say so at first."
Mercurius: "Then I take it you aim to torture me for the truth?"
Reinhard: "I could. But I would only be wasting my energy."
*The man understood the situation as well as Reinhard — his smirk stood as proof of that. Hiding the truth had no meaning in this place.*
Reinhard: "You see, I myself care little for the matter. Guilty or not, all people die when their time comes. A man ought not be surprised to find himself staring down the jaws of death if he had led a life that would attract the malice of others. It does not matter whether or not you have participated in that earlier commotion. Someone attempted to murder a vulnerable man. There is not much else to this trite situation. "
Mercurius: "Are you trying to imply that my words would change little?"
Reinhard: "His Excellency was a man in a vulnerable position. I have told you this earlier."
*It didn't end with internal and external political foes. His very existence gave birth to terrorists and malice. Entire countries wished for his demise. There would be little meaning to a Gestapo that preoccupied itself with the truth.*
Reinhard: "As such, the possibility of allowing the true culprit to slip away by executing you is but a drop in the ocean. It will change nothing. I am neither free nor mad enough to obsess over erasing a single enemy in a thousand. Punish the suspicious... Apologies for sounding banal, but this is how the Gestapo operates. "
*His life had been worth that little. Yet the man still betrayed not a hint of fear. He merely observed Reinhard with thinly-veiled interest. Was he evaluating him? Not quite. That gaze was hardly so simple. It appeared to pierce far deeper.*
*It reminded Reinhard of the eyes of a scientist. The look of someone scrutinizing a phenomenon through a microscope to the slightest detail. Like those white-coats working day and night on chemical weapons. Did this man still think he could get out of this alive? He even cocked his head with an ironic smile.*
Mercurius: "I see. The rumors spoke true of you. But... may I be granted the permission to pose a question?"
Reinhard: "You have it. Go on."
Mercurius: "What are you planning to make me do once you release me?"
*Reinhard was rendered speechless for a few moments. It did not sound like a thing a man sentenced to death should ever dare to utter to his would-be executioner. But above all...*
Reinhard: "Hmm? You certainly are a strange man. Haven't you been listening to anything I've said?"
Mercurius: "Oh, but I have. You arrived to meet the swindler who had been sentenced to death regardless of the truth, even asking me if I wished to die. If one were to turn your earlier words on their head, you could have been taken to imply that you would not mind releasing the true culprit, were it to serve a purpose of sorts. At the very least, that is how I have taken the liberty to interpret it. Have I misread your intentions, executioner? "
Reinhard: "..."
*The two men regarded each other in silence.*
*This thing indeed seemed like a magician. Or at least, that is how this shrewd and silver-tongued swindler should have been called. He allowed none of his own thoughts to show, meanwhile choosing to toy with every other word Reinhard uttered. A queer and aberrant fellow, yet far from the realm of ineptitude.*
Reinhard: "Hmph.  Interesting. You appear smarter than I have given you credit for. Or perhaps it is I who had shown myself to be a fool? Very well. Your conjecture has been valid, magician. If there is indeed one misunderstanding to be rectified, it would be that it was not I who came up with the design. "
*Reinhard held up the papers he had brought in earlier, displaying them for the prisoner to see. Penned on it had been a most ridiculous scheme — a mere prolongation of senior officer games.*
Reinhard: "It's an offer. You can choose to die here, or survive and live the life of a puppet. Albeit, the two might as well be the same."
*He would lose his free will either way. If he agreed, every single action in his life would then belong to another.*
Mercurius: "This... comes from the Ministry of Propaganda, does it not?"
Reinhard: "Nothing slips by our dear minister. Rather than identifying one or two rebels in a thousand, he would instead use the survival of our leader to his advantage — and through your prophecy, no less."
*To imbue the safety of their Führer with the supernatural.*
Reinhard: "It seems that Nostradamus has come quite into fashion among the old maids of our capital in recent years. And as you might know, it is always women and children who end up providing the foundations of public opinion. We will win. His Excellency the Führer is invincible. We need our own Nostradamus to wipe away the smear of our earlier defeat and instill our soldiers with courage. That is all, more or less. "
*He opened the cell doors without waiting for an answer. Life or death. Whatever his choice, he would have to leave. His posture made it quite evident that he posed no physical threat. And not even an athlete could flee this place. Reinhard himself could subdue him. He had yet to allow a single man to escape.*
Reinhard: "Your choice, magician. I have opened the lock. Your shackles are no more. You can leave your cage and save your life at the cost of your free will. Your future would be to live as an obedient lapdog of the state. As I have earlier implied, either would be fine by me. Killing you here could very well prove to be an act of mercy. As such, I thought it fair to at least provide you with a choice. "
*A statement smeared in near-ironic hypocrisy. His whole existence was far removed from the very concept of fairness. Whatever the man's choice, he would be subjugated by Reinhard's authority.*
*Death of the body or death of the mind — a choice only a devil would bestow upon a man. And to Reinhard, it came as second nature. Even his ability to feel abjection had long since withered. No longer could the world light a spark in his breast. Everything he did would be part of a bleak routine, including this very moment of waiting for the prisoner to make his choice.*
Mercurius: "Tell me...  Why do I perceive a certain discontent in your eyes? "
*His words spoke not of his choice, instead voicing a question. The prisoner regarded Reinhard with the eyes of a curious child.*
Reinhard: "What...?"
*It was if the man's words had pricked something in Reinhard's heart. His nature? The furtive puddle of his frustrations? He did not know. He could not. He felt nothing of the sort. He narrowed his eyes, unable to find the words to address the other man with.*
*Karl Krafft, observing Reinhard's momentary confusion, made an exaggerated gesture of mock consternation. He cast his gaze downward, resembling an actor in the scene of a great tragedy. As if deeply tormented by something. A display that precipitated anger and irritation rather than empathy, yet the other man's obsidian eyes of the deep sea still pierced Reinhard with absolute sincerity.*
Mercurius: "You could overturn a decision from His Excellency Goebbels, depending on the situation. Ah, and not only that. As the commander of the Gestapo, you wield the authority to force even our revered Führer into a corner, potentially destroying him, should you so desire. Such power and authority for one so young. The underworld of an Empire that threatens to subdue the world at large, and you, our black prince of peerless talent, hold it in the palm of your hand. Men across the globe would surely aspire to be like you. "
Mercurius: "And yet, our lauded lord of the dead — with the whole Reich in his grasp — resembles a child forced to endure a game he deems astonishingly dull."
Reinhard: "..."
*To say the magician's words did not surprise him would have been a lie. Not because the swindler had read his heart like a book. But rather due to his ability to impeccably name and define that inexplicable sensation whose nature not even Reinhard could assess.*
Mercurius: "Very interesting. You are most curious indeed."
*He finally stood up and left the cell, but would not cease talking. His voice rang dispassionately, yet ardent at the same time; sudden, but absolute — like a poet reciting a verse to the heavens. The swindler sang, as if slowly transforming into some unfathomable creature from another world, shedding the skin of a man like a crude cloak.*
Mercurius: "Wherein lie the origins of your thirst, and where shall it ultimately lead you?"
*Nonsense. Yet any sort of refutation would turn into poison at the tip of his tongue, sinking down to his soul, rather than flying out into the open.*
Mercurius: "What is it that you crave for in your turmoil?"
*A blunt question followed by a hyena-like smirk.*
Reinhard: "I thought I was the one asking a question."
*He had no obligation to answer the madman.*
Reinhard: "To speak nothing of the life you had already forfeit—"
*The odd sensation returned the moment his thoughts drifted to his duties, accompanied by an onset of dizziness.*
Reinhard: "Wait."
*Noise.  Noise.  Noise.  That accursed noise devouring his consciousness would refuse to subside.*
Reinhard: "Wait. What in the world is going on?"
*His worn-out memories flashed through his mind, detailing the continuation of the conversation — the one he had yet to have.*
*Tiresome communion. Uninspired conversation. A feeling of repulsion bordering on physical pain. Everything. Everything flashed through his mind. He remembered. All manner of information flashed through his mind in limitless droves, without ever ceasing — he begged for it to stop. An outcome to exceed all eccentricities and delusions. Only the wickedly smiling silhouette of the swindler remained etched into his vision. Reinhard could tell he was laughing.*
Mercurius: "My, what appears to be problem, most esteemed Lieutenant General? Your complexion has adopted a hue I can only describe as worryingly pale. Perhaps you ought to lie down and rest for a spell? Your handsome features, compared by many to the brilliance of gold, appear to have wrinkled up a touch. Ah, the world is now a darker place for that staggering loss of beauty. Many a lady would doubtless consider this a sight most disconcerting and worthy of grief. "
Reinhard: "Keep such concerns to yourself. And silence that tongue of yours..."
Mercurius: "Then may I perhaps receive an answer to my prior question?"
Mercurius: "Your choices and your beliefs. I cannot contain my curiosity as to how they shape themselves within you. I wish to know them, more than anything. Down to the slightest detail. I want to forever savor your answers in my heart, for this is a most nostalgic exchange between the two of us. "
Reinhard: "What...?"
*The madman seemed to affirm the very aberration currently consuming Reinhard's mind. A past he couldn't have possibly known emerged once again in his consciousness with renewed vigor. Reinhard found himself utterly without an explanation. No soul could possess knowledge of such things.*
Reinhard: "You are..."
*And even the words that abruptly escaped his lips were in complete concord with the bizarre sensation.*
Reinhard: "A delusional megalomaniac, I see. I'm certain you find the world tremendously enthralling, then."
*Yes, that had been exactly what he said. Pictures and scenes flashed through his mind, like a fast-forwarding movie. The unpleasant, sickening feeling refused to subside.*
*A scene he knew nothing about. The aberration of remembering the present as it unfolded before his eyes. If there was one word to describe that sensation... it would be foreknowledge. The volume of his knowledge increased exponentially. Yet the actual amount never truly changed, for indeed, he was merely remembering, not learning new things. The traces of emotions and sensations that still lingered in his soul had now been completely expulsed. A sensation that grew only worse in the presence of the accursed trickster.*
Mercurius: "Oh, do you not remember, then? Our conversations. Our meeting. I recalled it all the moment I met you, but could it be that you have not?"
Reinhard: "I most certainly haven't. This is ridiculous."
*Reinhard flatly denied the other's nonsensical remark. He had no obligation to go along with mad delusions. An aberrant sensation might have inexplicably assaulted him there for a moment, but that was certainly not enough to affirm the madness on the man's lips.*
Reinhard: "You are but a delusional megalomaniac. That is all I see when I look upon you, and we certainly have no shared past to speak of. Expecting something? You are off the mark, jester. I am hardly a man of any consequence, really. "
*The furtive pool of resignation remained ever-stagnant in his mind. Reinhard harbored no ardent desires, nor any grand ideals to boast of. It was only the surrounding rabble that — in their envy — projected onto him some inexplicable dignity or glory.*
*Medals that hardly served a purpose other than decorating the room. Endless praise that amount to little more than hollow lip service. No applause or cheers had ever moved his heart, not in his entire life. He did not grow tired. He was unfeeling to begin with. His senses were merely dull, both to happiness and pain. If anything, to label such things as wonderful and to be envied seemed like madness in itself.*
Reinhard: "I had never known restraint, not since my youngest days. I faced all that life threw at me with utmost earnestness, and soon enough, I found myself in this position. I am like a car that knows not how to stop. Capabilities aside, anyone will eventually traverse the world once or twice if they kept their stride continuous. "
Reinhard: "I cannot imagine what you may have seen in me, but that is the extent of the man known as Reinhard Heydrich. If it is excitement you seek, there are no doubt thousands out there you would find far more interesting than me. I suggest you go trouble them instead."
*And he could have all the fun in the world with them. A mind ruled by madness likely translated all sensations to amusement. Any attempts at insulting or rejecting him would fall on deaf ears, no doubt.*
Mercurius: "Do you mean to imply that I am overestimating you?"
Reinhard: "What else is there? I am neither immortal nor invincible. I was neither born to a virgin, nor did I descend from the heavens. I am but a mortal man, no matter how you look at me."
*He was not born with the burden of duty. No revelations graced his mind. He survived by doing what he was told, much like everyone else. Disregarding the scale and the amount, Reinhard had only ever done a single, utterly basic job. There was not a single shred of uniqueness about him.*
Reinhard: "Strip him of his status, and a man becomes no different from any other of his fellow humans. That is about all there is to it — no, that is indeed how it must be. We fall when struck; we die when shot. That is how man ought to be. No one can escape death. And so we live our lives till death's hour is struck, and we return to the dust from whence we came. And I am more than content with that myself. Death is the inevitable fate of all that lives. I am no exception. "
Mercurius: "Ah, this cannot stand. A man of your capacity should never utter such folly. This is what happens when one fails to see himself. You should first return to your room and glance at the mirror. Marvel at what you see. With you like this, I cannot help but feel sorry for the many subordinates that so admire you. "
Reinhard: "You seem unsatisfied, swindler. I said you should look for someone else."
*He knew not how to utter words of lament. He had no desire to humor the magician any further, and no longer tried to hide his contempt. His tone had grown coarse, his words losing their former eloquence.*
Mercurius: "I want you to answer my question, just this once. I want you to realize that you are simply bored of the world. Have you ever put your whole body and soul into doing anything? Have you not been merely walking, deceitfully telling yourself that you ran at full speed? "
Reinhard: "It doesn't matter whether I run or walk. Eventually, I will come to a halt and die."
*He was moving forward in either case. Speed mattered little.*
Mercurius: "You misunderstand. That is not your limit. It exists far beyond what you imagine. As such, you have yet to meet a hurdle. You have yet face anything with full strength. An adversary that would make your heart dance. A challenge you have to overcome. The fulfillment that emerges once you succeed. Can you truly claim to have no desire for such things? "
Reinhard: "Have I not just told you this was ridiculous? What of it?"
Reinhard: "Man must hunger, lust, and crave for as long as his heart beats in his chest. No matter where life takes him, no matter what nourishment fate offers him, his thirst fades not — all that would await any such being is ruination. If there really was anyone like that, I think his very birth would be an error of nature. "
*A beast would die the moment its hunger was satisfied. And this man was urging him to become such a thing? The very notion felt ridiculous beyond description.*
Reinhard: "We all die one day. And that is fine. What does it matter if a few decades of man's brief life fails to fulfill him? Words of discontent are to be saved for one's deathbed; it need not come any sooner."
*If dying was the fate of all men, then all he could do was live an earnest life. Why would he wish to escape death if he never cared much about living?*
Mercurius: "I see. Then your motto would be..."
Reinhard: "Indeed... Memento mori. We all die eventually, and death does indeed weigh heavy upon man's soul. As such, we ought to treat it with due dignity."
*He would not try to fool himself into thinking there was equality in mankind. But in death alone, all had the right to line up with each other. All had to embrace it. No one was exempt. That grim final stop loomed visible in the distance for all men to see. How could one even dare reject it?*
Reinhard: "People who cannot die when their hour is struck end up being left behind. I know not who came up with the words, but I cannot help but wholeheartedly agree with them."
*The words of someone he couldn't quite remember. The vague memory of a man rigid as iron flashed into Reinhard's mind, yet both his name and appearance seemed to have eluded him. But he could remember his conviction — the vigor of his craving. And he had to agree. Humans could exist without life, but what of those without death? Where would they find themselves?*
Reinhard: "To reject death is to exist as the living dead. I see no reason to cling to this existence at the cost of becoming a monster. What point is there in breathing if the heart fails to beat? One life is enough for me. I am not the beast from your banal delusions of grandeur. Nor am I interested in such a position. "
*Reinhard Heydrich would have turned into the monster from the magician's dreams, had he only overturned this logic. The aberration transcending life itself; the devil soaring beyond the precipice of the unknown. The very thought of it made him dizzy with repulsion.*
Mercurius: "I see. So you would rather remain human? You do not mind growing old completely bereft of fulfillment, and would accept death without a second thought?"
Reinhard: "Yes."
*He could happily live and die as a man — as one soldier out of many who merely carried out his sworn duty.*
Mercurius: "Are you certain? Is that truly a wish from the bottom of your heart? Your honest feelings without a shred of embellishment?"
Reinhard: "How many times do I need to repeat myself?"
*He rejected the life of an aberration. And why wouldn't he? His whole being recoiled at the very notion of it.*
Reinhard: "That is how I am. I cannot become someone else. The Hangman, the Commander of the Gestapo... I require no other title. If you still wish to invent more, you are free to come up with whatever you desire. But I am no clown that will eagerly masquerade as a beast at the mere suggestion of a madman. "
*The words of the sneering swindler were but drivel in his ears. He emanated no trace of the supernatural. The inexplicable discomfort that took hold of him merely got to his head. His philosophy on life and death would never change. Live. And die. If one wanted to spend that time in fulfillment and worldly pleasures, they should have joined a hedonist sect.*
Mercurius: "Then—"
*In that moment, the silhouette of the jester contorted and creaked.*
Reinhard: "...!"
*His back swelled like a balloon. A change that should have been impossible for a child of man. The giant sac suddenly burst, almost like it had a flaming missile inside— His head had changed into Caduceus — the twin-headed serpent. An obsidian blade sprouted from him, almost like a child being born. It pierced through the air, advancing to Reinhard's chest, and...*
Reinhard: "...?!"
*A mortal blow as abrupt as it was unimaginable.*
Ren: "Die as a man."
*His voice had changed, together with the head. The sound of rending flesh. The violent pain. The gushing of blood. He could feel the chill of steel pierce his heart. Someone he had been vaguely familiar with burst out from the shadow of the swindler, reaping his life.*
Reinhard: "Impossible..."
*What had just occurred? His thoughts could not keep up. An anomaly that defied all common sense had skewered him like a piece of meat. Foreknowledge began seeping back into the crevices of his mind. Sometime, somewhere... an adversary he had once met wielded a guillotine sprouting from his arm. A blade that now pierced his chest. He could feel blood filling his mouth, his very life pouring forth from his body.*
*He could simply not comprehend this. What of the swindler?  Who was this, appearing in his place?  Was that blade truly a part of his body?  There were limits to how inscrutable a phenomenon could be. Could that thing truly have been demon born from the magician's delusions?*
*Blood filled his trachea, preventing him from breathing. He could feel his consciousness growing dim. He had lost so much blood that he could no longer move his limbs. No, that was not it. Some form of invisible power held him completely immobile. He could hear the approaching footsteps of death.*
Ren: "That's right. You should have died here."
*The Grim Reaper made his declaration with scythe in hand. He opened a hole in Reinhard's existence with inexplicable anger and contempt, yet not without a hue of sadness to tinge his bearing.*
Ren: "To tell you the truth, I'm relieved. I never imagined I'd hear something so human from you. Ren: That's right. No one is born a monster. And even if they were, they could've lived as men if raised as such. "
*Nigh-palpable relief. Youthful sorrow in response to the theory of life Reinhard had uttered.*
*He could not understand. Why was he so moved by his simple words? He merely told the magician that those born as men should also die as such. It was but common sense.*
Ren: "I was impressed that you didn't doubt the concept."
*Reinhard had no idea what was so significant about that. But he could no longer voice his questions in his numb throat. His ability to form thoughts had been deteriorating by the second. The blood that gushed forth from his chest like a torrent turned into a mere trickle.*
Ren: "Your philosophy is right. I can acknowledge that much. The crazy bastard who filled your head with nonsense was to blame from the start. Ren: That's right. Death weighs heavy upon all our souls. As such... And precisely because of that...! "
Rea: "You shouldn't have met the swindler."
Reinhard: "Wh...?!"
*A voice of a girl reverberated in his head. He could not see her. It was most definitely not the young man before him, but he could not think of the words as a mere illusion. After all...*
Rea: "You should've used your authority and left him to someone else. You shouldn't have lent an ear to his insane whispers."
Ren: "Rejoice. And be thankful. You'll be able to die as a mortal man, Reinhard."
*He could hear a voice urging him to return to living as a trifling flicker of light.*
Rea: "You shouldn't have become a Golden Beast."
*The Beast? What was this girl of an apparition talking about? Was she, too, implying that he was some sort of monster from the pages of a fairytale?*
Rea: "And not only you. All those who get involved with you end up bereaved of death — forced to move forward despite being empty of life."
*He and those that followed him would turn into monsters? Insatiable demons to wage war for an eternity? That... that almost sounded like an awfully convoluted metaphor for cancer.*
His breathing stopped. The blade scraping at his spinal cord chafed flesh from his bone like a rasp. Death was near. Indeed, he had it right earlier: we would fall when struck, and die when shot. A stab wound like this was no different in that regard. Having been born as a man, he would die as one. There was nothing more to it than that — a simple anticlimax of a finale. 
*Underwhelming. Abrupt. Had he possessed the strength, he would have likely burst out laughing. He would die from the mere prick of a needle without even knowing the reason for his demise. He was but one of the hapless many. He possessed no—*
Mercurius: "Is that really what you think?"
*Another voice came from the nothingness — the shade-like man re-emerged within his mind.*
Rea: "Even if being a beast was your true nature, you lived your life resisting it with everything you had. You never once tried, like a selfish child, to rob others of what you yourself lacked. I know of no other man more adept at self-restraint than you, Lord Heydrich."
*Self-restraint? Aye, he was confident in that one skill, at least. As no emotions ever plagued his heart, he ended up more patient than his peers.*
Rea: "There was but one person who could keep up with you in your full power. Rea: You shouldn't have taken his hand. If he made your heart dance, you should have unleashed your passion upon him rather than looking for someone else. "
Ren: "So die here with dignity. Perish while you're still human."
*The demon twisted its blade in Reinhard's chest. Unbearable pain assaulted him, followed by the remainder of his blood gushing forth from his mouth. The scythe of the Grim Reaper gave off an icy gleam, as if portending death.*
Ren: "Open your eyes and look at it all. I will present you with equality. I will turn the words you uttered into reality."
*The demon urged him to burn the scene into his memory.*
Ren: "I... am your death."
*And with that, the blade of the guillotine separated Reinhard's torso from his lower body. Fresh blood rained down upon the room. The end came silently and without warning—*
Reinhard: "Ah..."
*Yielding to the force of gravity, the separated halves of his body fell towards the ground. Was this truly the end? How utterly plain. The first thought crossed Reinhard's mind was the re-affirmation of his self as a boring, insignificant man. He observed even his own death with calm indifference. So much for magicians. This was the true face of Reinhard Heydrich. Just another corpse in the gutter. He could not imagine a more fitting end.*
*But in that moment—*
Mercurius: "My, my. You utter nonsense, my beastly companion."
*His heart jolted alive, his consciousness returning before it could plunge into the depths of the abyss.*
Mercurius: "A prick from a needle is hardly enough to fell you."
Reinhard: "..."
*A near-mocking remark. A moment of uncertainty had saved his life.*
*Time had stopped — literally. His body remained suspended mid-air. He could even make out the droplets of blood frozen in the air. Only his consciousness seemed to have remained active, experiencing a surge of astonishment at this inconceivable sight. The whole world, save for his own mind, had come to a complete halt. Only the words of the shadow tickled his ears from within.*
Reinhard: "A needle?"
Mercurius: "Correct. To you, all it amounted to was the prick of a needle. You cannot deceive me. In that moment, you most certainly thought that you could not possibly die from such a trifling wound."
Reinhard: "..."
*Indeed. For a brief heartbeat, his consciousness had certainly formed such a thought. A blade pierced his chest, skewering his heart. A wound that should have been lethal to any man... ...yet for a moment, he felt it utterly trivial. That impression — that criteria — did not belong to a common man.*
Reinhard: "Impossible. Then am I..."
Mercurius: "Indeed. You are not a being to perish from a mere cut. In my eyes, you never have been a simple, mortal man."
*The shadowy silhouette reappeared in his vision. The magician gave him a friendly smile. Reinhard felt it unpleasant, yet oddly familiar at the same time.*
Mercurius: "Allow me to reiterate. You are far too great to fit within reason. For you to obey human principles would be the height of folly. If anything, you are the one who bends such principles to his will."
Mercurius: "Death lies before you. It only takes a moment to fall. If this is a fleeting vision you see before death, then time is of the essence. Why not take another look at this situation and reconsider? What is your wish? What is the craving that burns in your heart? What moment would you trade for no other? And what should you do to attain it? Your memories hold the answer — go on, remember. "
*Foreknowledge assailed Reinhard's consciousness like a storm.*
Reinhard: "I..."
*Remember. The time you spent as something other than a man. The brain you have now is far too unfit for a beast of fantasy. You must re-establish connection with the outside. Do not merely recall experiences. Remember the land you rode off to claim with your Legion, and project it upon the world.*
Reinhard: "...! ...! ...!!"
*The Longinus Dreizehn Orden. The Obsidian Round Table. The Beguiling Light. Atziluth. Ewigkeit. Longinus. A world for him to dwell in. The ardor of destruction. The baleful Gold. The Day of Wrath he sought with all his being — Dies Irae. He did not know this. He could not know this. Yet he remembered. The scenery he had to traverse. All he had to claim, all he had to bestow — the covenant of his new being. What craving scorched his heart when he transcended time?*
Ren: "This is the end, Reinhard."
*The young man condemned him to death, as if repulsed by his very existence. They were born in differing worlds, and as such, the youth urged him to embrace death while he still drew breath as a mortal man.*
Rea: "Goodbye, Lord Heydrich."
*The girl silently lamented his mistake. She, too, wished for him to remain a man, yet rather than death, she would have wanted him to walk a different path and seek those that could have brought happiness to his life.*
Mercurius: "It is time to open your eyes, O Monarch of Destruction."
*Meanwhile, the magician sung each word. Remember. And destroy the young imposter. Let us do it all again. The shadow stirred Reinhard's confused memories with utmost confidence, burning away all traces of hesitation in him.*
Reinhard: "I..."
*The words, questions, and desires of the three converged in a whirlpool of curses on the verge of erupting within Reinhard. What did he once believe in and wish for? What craving burned his chest? And where did it lead him?*
Reinhard: "That's right. I..."
*Did he wish to die as a man? No, that was merely a natural outcome he had once accepted. He never wished for his own demise. Did he command a Legion of demons for a wish of that caliber?*
Reinhard: "No."
*A clear and robust voice boomed across the frozen dreamscape — a bell to wake the long dreamer, its very echo capable of shaking the world to its foundations. A fissure opened in the sky. The pain faded like a receding wave.*
Reinhard: "No! Not in the slightest! I wasn't merely waiting for my death. That is the life of a dead man. How is it any different from a prisoner on death row?"
*He gazed down upon his wound; it was hardly worthy of note. A mere prick from a needle. His skewered heart regained its prior vigor, and began to beat once more.*
Reinhard: "I have yet to achieve anything. Does that not contradict my dignity?"
*His heart raged. The Golden Beast slowly rose from slumber—*
Reinhard: "I distanced myself from the thrill of men, labeling all as waste by the wayside as I passed through. I wished to love all and everything, yet none could withstand my love. Ah, why can't you endure my touch? If a mere graze upon your delicate skin sends you shattering to a myriad pieces, how can you hope to withstand my embrace? Such cruelty. Why must this world — from the tiniest blade of grass to the vastest of mountains — be so painfully fragile? So be it, then. My love shall take the form of destruction. I shall ravage so I can cherish. I adore the weak that bow before me, as well as the defeated that bend their knees. My love expands to the vassals that rebel, and those that mean me harm. I love all and everything. And so shall I lay waste to all before me. "
Reinhard: "That is the sole principle resonating within me. I lived gazing at and feeling death. But that was not out of an aspiration for self-ruination. I merely found it unbearable to leave all the little things I cherished without attention. And for that very reason must our inevitable end be remembered— memento mori. "
*Those his love extended to. As well as he himself. Nothing could match the significance of death. And so, he wished all to welcome his love with equal solemnity.*
*The boundless void in his heart. To soothe its listlessness, he embarked upon a quest to devour the world, hoping to chance upon that which he had yet to ravage. But it still proved insufficient in satiating his beastly hunger. An adversary that would make his heart dance. A challenge that required the whole of his strength to be overcome. One that he would keep devouring for, one that would make him prove his own existence, and beyond...!*
Reinhard: "I shall love all. There shan't be an exception. For it would be remiss of me not to cherish and reward all and everyone in equal measure."
*The one he had yet to annihilate. He who had been the most worthy of his love. To separate him by a wall of friendship was an insult to his credence.*
Reinhard: "That's right. I..."
*His hair grew in length; his clothes changed. He could feel the Holy Lance in his hands as Weltall swirled within his heart like a whirlpool. Love that filled his entire being. His opened eyes sparkled in acute, golden luster.*
Reinhard: "I love all and everything!"
*The power he unleashed in that moment took the form of a comet, vaporizing the dark cell in an instant. The scenery of the past shattered into a thousands of pieces. The mighty explosion swept the whole world and the alien bodies it contained aside like puny leaves in a storm.*
Ren: "...!!"
Rea: "...!"
*Zarathustra and Sonnenkind vanished into the recesses of the cosmos.*
*Yet he had nothing but gratitude for them in his heart. This would not have been possible without them. Phantasms. Flickers of light. The meaning of his very existence. They presented him with it all. They had his deepest gratitude. Behold, dear spectators. The last and final Dies Irae. The ultimate struggle between destruction and transcendence. This is what the two have been aiming for from the start, but Reinhard would not admit to being had.*
Reinhard: "Well then..."
*For he wished for this moment more than anyone.*
Reinhard: "Shall we begin, Karl?"
*He faced the sole exception to the rule, and — his Holy Lance shimmering in elation — launched a blinding thrust.*
*The golden light of destruction ravaged the cosmos... ...turning all matter to ash in its path. But it aimed at but one—*
Mercurius: "Ahh. It appears my apoptosis has finally begun. "
*With an expression that seemed like a tearful smile—*
*The shadow of Mercury finally unveiled its true form.*
*That cry of neither sorrow nor delight continued but for a moment. Reinhard's golden light was repelled by an even more luminescent serpent, his strike — possessing power enough to obliterate a city with ease — vanishing into nothingness before the Caduceus coiling around the cosmos. In that vacuum of absolute silence, all that remained was the golden devil and an unmasked jester. The two greatest entities in the universe faced each other on a monochrome canvas — the blank page of the new world. The spark in their eyes indicated both boundless love and unavoidable separation.*
*Machina once told Ren about the sole path to end this phenomenon. And now, that very possibility had reached fruition. The two invincible bastions of the Obsidian Table would diverge.*
Reinhard: "Nothing less from my friend. Only a great man could paint over the world and remain on its Throne."
*Reinhard applauded Mercurius for withstanding the full brunt of his power. Incredible. And inevitable. He commended his friend from the bottom of his heart.*
Reinhard: "Or would it be an insult to the name of god if you could not endure a strike from a mere child like myself? I can see your tribulation. That is why you appeared as a prisoner. You were far too large an existence, and the world too small to hold your grand being. Aye, I can share in your torment. The world is small. Water and nutrition are but a dry well to us. From the very advent of the stars, we had been locked in coffins. I suppose I can confess it now. You looked to me like a withered tree when we first met, your being lacking even a single drop of water. You seemed shriveled even in the eyes of a dead man like myself. "
*The words of the devilish commander sheltered a hue of self-reproach as he reminisced about the past.*
Reinhard: "I cannot believe how blind I had been. It appears I am unable to grasp the true nature of things before destroying their form. All my eyes perceive is the outer shell, and with no holes in it, I can never see inside. Forgive me. I am but an insignificant man. That alone — this assessment of my own self — has not changed in the slightest. "
Reinhard: "As such..."
*Light accumulated at the tip of the lance as it danced in the air. The shimmer of the Holy Lance grew more potent, attaining a golden glow—*
Reinhard: "I wish to exact my love on you."
*His tremendous power and immense bloodlust had not been directed at his sworn friend. His declaration to wage lethal battle rang more like an invitation to a pleasant stroll.*
Reinhard: "A foolish thing indeed. I have exchanged words with all my subordinates, yet I shunned my friend. Forgive me, Karl. It seems I have mistreated you without even realizing it.  I kept ignoring your wish since the very day we met. But I shall grant it now. "
*He would bestow upon him the unknown — the finality of absolute death. He was born for that purpose alone. Reinhard Heydrich was about to exercise the very meaning of his existence.*
Mercurius: "Nothing less from a man I consider a kindred soul. I expected you to say that."
Reinhard: "Indeed. Even a mule would realize it at this point. Their bout was a sight radiant beyond measure, touching even my heart. Only a lifeless scarecrow would fail to sympathize with their struggle.  "
*Otherwise, we would be insulting the very concept of friendship. He could barely keep his eyes open at the shimmer of those two shooting stars.*
Reinhard: "That was precisely the bond we had to share. The outline we needed to follow."
Mercurius: "I see."
*His meaningful smile had not changed even in the presence of an enemy. Their love for each other changed little, yet their cravings could now only be fulfilled through the other's demise.*
Mercurius: "Ah, but the adversary and the hindrance both still occupy the stage. Do you mean to imply that even in full bloom, my Ahnenerbe remains insufficient?"
Reinhard: "A foolish question. I am merely fulfilling our promise."
*No matter what he did, that sensation of tedium, extending to infinity, would never fade. An oversaturation of countless victories continuing for an eternity. Who promised to alleviate that pain? Reinhard had not forgotten a single word from their conversation.*
Reinhard: "You promised it yourself. You are too late to complain, and any attempt to debate it would be no more than a waste of time. You promised to prepare a stage for me to unleash my full power, and that the unknown would await me beyond its horizon. I recall agreeing to those exact words. "
*All of them participated in this scheme. Everyone had motivations of their own. The aspirations of some conflicted, while many did not even comprehend the true meaning of the Day of Wrath. Yet all of them nodded their heads to the oath. All embellishments would melt before the boon of Gold. Their deepest, unabashed nature sealed a pact with the devil. They had no right to complain. They all joined the Legion of demons of their own volition, melting equally into its Hell to became one... ...seeking but one reward — victory.*
Reinhard: "An entity at whom I can unleash my full power has manifested before my eyes. And it appears I was born to face him. 'Tis the only way to avoid defeat and claim victory. After all, I encompass an infinite abyss. If I were to find a natural foe to clash with, I would no doubt have to seek him amidst the heavens. Those from ancient myth and legend had always aspired to reach the summit. Besides... "
*The Beast's golden eyes gleamed with indomitable pressure... ...as his eruptive bloodlust filled the air. His gaze was replete with boundless elation.*
Reinhard: "It is the first time I get to be the challenger, Karl."
*And that filled the Golden Beast with uncontained joy.*
Reinhard: "I am not meeting an attack. I am not subjugating anyone. Now is my sole chance to challenge someone above. Can you believe it? My heart is dancing in my chest, like that of a young child."
Reinhard: "And beyond it lies the unknown. Or should I say... this is the sole path for me to attain it. What good would defeating a mere substitute do? Even if it proved to be a paramount task, it would not dispel my foreknowledge. You gave birth to this world. As such, you know how this should unfold. It might have been different had I been left in the dark, but now it is too late. Deep within my heart, I had craved this outcome with every fiber of my being. "

*For how long had he sought this outcome? How many eternities had he passed before arriving here? How many times did he fight, love, and die? At the aftermath of multiplying eternity by an infinite number, he still sought to attain the same conclusion as every other time.*

I will not give up, no matter how many times it takes. I felt that this time, maybe... "

What was this? What kind of phenomenon was tormenting him? Why could he not die? He had enough time. He could vaguely remember the curse of foreknowledge in his mother's womb, and killing his family at a young age. He was but a proxy, while the real him remained at the center of the Throne, wishing in zealous madness for a certain something.*

After understanding he was never strictly human, he also realized he could move more freely without being constrained by the limits of a body. There were countless things he had yet to try at that point. Ten thousand years passed. Then another ten thousand before they reached the present day, yet nothing truly changed.*
*He believed his craving to be a means to escape from foreknowledge. Naturally, he realized the contradiction contained within that very train of thought. He lamented the accursed phenomenon to no end, yet it persisted as the law governing the world that his own, original self had once unleashed upon the universe. In short, he simply grew tired of it all. He had long since lost count of the years, yet in his mortal days, he must have possessed a vulgar and nigh-boundless thirst for knowledge. He wished to know everything, and ultimately emanated a world in which all was known to him. That was most likely what transpired.*
*Where it all began mattered little. He was foolish beyond measure, a hapless clown eternally tormented by his own wish. He believed it to be his mission to perish alongside his foolish world — to put this farce to an end once and for all. A colossal lack of prudence. A misconception to surpass all others. And every single time, only upon arriving here would he finally see the truth. The universe itself must have laughed at his misery.*

Mercurius: "How I wish I was capable of succumbing..."

Mercurius: "One more time. Just one more time..."

Mercurius: "It is most unfortunate, but I cannot expunge this one obsession."

*December 25, 1945. Berlin, Germany. 12:27 AM*
*By the time I came to my senses, the night had already marched past midnight. And so, I lifted my gaze from the book in my hands. With it, the new year was preparing for its graceful entry, promising thrice the turmoil. Although, "chaos" would have been far more fitting a name for what was surely to come, truth be told. Four months had come and gone since the invasion of Poland. Four months since the United Kingdom and France issued a declaration of war against Germany. Although it would allegedly prove to be the retaliation to humiliation and poverty we — the young generation — suffered in the aftermath of the previous war, the thought of another grand-scale conflict breaking out nonetheless filled my heart with gloom.*
*And all those elderly veterans that fought on the frontlines and experienced the bitter taste of defeat firsthand would no doubt feel it tenfold. So why did we plunge headfirst into a new war? I realized the importance of possessing land, resources, and food. I truly did. You'd find plenty who hungered for honor and glory. And even more who wished for victory to wash our nation's reputation clean of the taint of defeat. Should the events from two decades ago be recorded in history as the only World War fought by men, Germany and its people would forever be remembered as a nation of the defeated.*
*Either way, this was a choice very much made with the future in mind. And to that end, the present was now being sacrificed. I realized this might have been the hollow, infantile grumbling of one who'd seen precious little of life. Yet it did not change the fact that the whole thing was messing up my life. My comfortable equilibrium of the “here and now” was being torn to shreds. Stop it. Leave it be. I know how selfish and arrogant that may have sounded, yet it was how I truly felt. In fact, it would have made me particularly sad to miss the next installment of the serialized book I was just reading. I didn't care for the circumstances of the author or the world, I wanted to know how the story ended.*
*Even I was amazed by how foolish this train of thought was.*
Ren: "..."
*I heard the sound of approaching footsteps from behind.*
*What was this now? I had a terrible feeling about this. Or so my gut told me. And to my misfortune, those hunches of mine rarely ever missed the mark. I knew I should've retreated to my own chambers for reading. Sitting in the middle of a bench in a hall as large as this left me with nowhere to hide.*
*I knew this person did not come here to meet me in particular, yet I couldn't help but feel a tingle of unease trailing up the back of my neck. Though I was not sure who it could be, simply ignoring their presence might have been the best route to take here.*
Reinhard: "Excuse me."
*And so, even when the man stopped right next to where I sat and uttered those brief words, I hung my head and refused to look up and meet his eyes. The man went on.*
Reinhard: "Is Director Sievers available?"
*A low, yet refined voice — even without looking him in the eye, I could tell that it belonged to a man of considerable power. His soothing tone was contrasted by an echo of confidence, as well as a definite coldness lurking behind it. He was a soldier. And although, at present, I could say the same thing about myself, a lowly grunt like me paled in comparison to a high-ranking official. In other words... he was not the type of man I would have wished to ever associate with.*
Reinhard: "Did you not hear me? Is the Director–"
Ren: "A-Ah, right. Sorry, but he's out."
*I crudely waved my arm as I gave him an answer.Frankly, I wanted him to be gone as soon as possible. If he ended up introducing himself, decorum would force me to politely oblige him. And that would have just needlessly complicated things. In fact, it would have been better for everyone if I never heard his name. Let him think of me as some boorish whelp who knew not how to speak in front of a commanding officer. That would have made things easier. At any rate, it wasn't like he'd shoot me dead on the spot.*
Reinhard: "I see. Understandable; I did fail to notify him of my visit in advance, after all."
Ren: "Yeah, well, in any case, door's that way if you're done."
*I lifted a thumb to point to the back of the hall without turning to face him.*
Ren: "He's been meeting with these doctor types a lot as of late. I heard them muttering something about measuring skulls and whatnot."
Reinhard: "Ah, that must be a plastometer — a device capable of determining Aryan heredity."
Ren: "Yeah, that's the one. He's attending a dinner party with a group of researchers from Strasbourg... although it's a bit late to be having dinner at this hour, if you ask me.  Ren: If you still insist on catching him, you might want to head over there. "
*“And that's the end of our conversation, so goodbye.” I meant to drive him away with that masked implication, but the man, oddly enough, refused to move an inch. On the contrary, I could practically feel his gaze piercing my skin, fixating on me from above. I was starting to feel sick.*
Ren: "Look, sir..."
Reinhard: "Ah, never mind the Director. I shall ask you instead. Raise your head. "
Ren: "..."
*I was really starting to hate that big mouth of mine.*
Reinhard: "Raise your head."
*Unable to deny his pressing tone, I reluctantly raised my head to look him in the eye.*
Ren: "...!!"
*I was taken aback. I figured he wouldn't be an ordinary soldier, but his looks alone were enough to leave anyone speechless. This may have sounded odd coming from another man, but I'd never seen anyone so handsome before. He must've been roughly a decade my senior, yet displayed an uncanny balance of youth and mature dignity. Someone with my childlike complexion — an attribute both myself and my peers could attest to — could spend thirty years trying in vain to reach his level.*
Reinhard: "Is something the matter?"
Ren: "Ah..."
*In any event, just maintaining eye contact with him was wearing me down. I wasn't exactly doing all this out of the kindness of my heart, but if he had a question, I'd give him his answer; after that, he'd better be on his way.*
Ren: "Nothing. Don't worry about it. Anyway, can I help you?"
Reinhard: "Ah, yes. Do you happen to know a man by the name of Karl Krafft?"
Ren: "Karl Krafft?"
*His question came so out of the blue that I could do nothing but repeat the name he had uttered. Karl Krafft... if I wasn't mistaken, he was–*
Reinhard: "A veritable con man, I assure you. He joined the Ministry of Propaganda just the other day.  He makes his living through fortune telling, conjuring up predictions for the future that reflect positively on the nation. All things considered, while I do understand the reasons behind his actions, the fact remains that his profession is rooted in trickery and fake miracles. "
Ren: "...And?"
Reinhard: "Do you not find it absurd?"
*I couldn't quite follow his train of thought. Noticing my distress, he flashed a faint bitter smile.*
Reinhard: "Worry not. Seeing how you are no acquaintance of his, my question is not one you could have answered. I do have another one for you, however. Did anyone working here happen to visit the church tonight to receive a certain package? "
Ren: "The church...?"

Reinhard: "This is the Bureau for the Study of Ancestral Heritage — the Deutsche Ahnenerbe. Your duties consist of the collection of such artifacts, do they not? If you have even the tiniest morsel of information to share regarding the matter I had just brought up, I would very much appreciate your co-operation."
Ren: "..."
Reinhard: "You are sworn to confidentiality, I take it? I see. Misfortune on my part, then."
Ren: "No, it's just that... I genuinely don't know."
*At the very least, no such matter had ever reached my ears, that much I could say with certainty.*
Ren: "But why would you be interested in such a thing?"
Reinhard: "Ah, if only I knew. It's a mystery even to myself.  I merely... felt something in my bones, so to speak. "

Ren: "Well, aren't you the peculiar one."
Reinhard: "Aye, this I cannot deny."
Reinhard: "From time to time, I find myself assaulted by certain... sensations. Albeit, I confess it has only been a month.  I would encounter events I had never seen before, ideas I had never heard before — couldn't have heard before — and think to myself: I know of this. I know this has already happened. "
Ren: "..."
Reinhard: "At other times, I would think: no, this is not the man I ought to be. Do you, perchance, have an inkling as to what I speak of? "
*I couldn't quite find it in myself to say yes. I mean, judging by his description, this must have been the effect of some severe personal delusion of his. Frankly, I was this close to telling him to just go see a doctor. The man shook his head, no doubt having sensed my feelings.*
Reinhard: "I assure you, I do consider myself sane.  Or should I say... that is what I wish to believe, desperately, with all my heart. A pitiful state of mind, truly. "
Ren: "I think..."
*What was I going to tell him? He was exactly the sort of man I wanted nothing to do with. In fact, even now, I still desperately wished to avoid any and all unnecessary communication with him. And yet... Something in me drove me to action. A sense of duty, if you will. A feeling that this was something I, and I alone, could do. There he stood, still strikingly handsome, his locks golden. I looked him in the eye—*
Ren: "You are sane."
*...and uttered those words. Curtly, and with emphasis.*
Ren: "We all live in the real world. And while life gives us plenty to cherish, it offers its fair share of misfortune just the same; we march on, hungering after dreams we keep locked up in our hearts, forever unfulfilled."
*The transience of the here and now, that fleeting moment I so adored — I would long to make its miracle eternal. A childish notion, true, but one I could not discard; rather, knowing it was a dream never to be fulfilled, my thirst for it refused to ever fade. And so we lived, ever discontent, haunted by doubts, frail on our feet...*
Ren: "But isn't that exactly what makes us human?"
*I was content to be such a man.*
Ren: "Our lives are but petals in the wind; moments lost in the annals of time. No matter how fiercely we struggle to make it ours, eternity will always elude us."
*In other words...*
Reinhard: "Live your life to its fullest, with your head held high. Indeed, your words do ring true. Man must hunger and lust and crave for as long as his heart beats in his chest. No matter where life takes him, no matter what nourishment fate offers him, his thirst fades not. But that is fine — merely natural. If there existed any being who refused to accept this sentiment... all that would await him is ruination. "
Ren: "If there really was anyone like that, I think his very birth would be an error of nature."
*We looked each other in the eye, uttering those words without really comprehending who they were aimed at; almost as if to reproach ourselves... ...claiming that things were fine this way, that this was how it ought to be. And so, my next question followed naturally.*
Ren: "What's your name?"
Reinhard: "Heydrich. Reinhard Heydrich."
*I'd be lying if I said the name didn't surprise me. The man I'd suddenly gotten all friendly with was none other than the revered golden beast, in the flesh. It would have been small wonder to see him have my head right this instant.*
Reinhard: "I am hardly a man of any consequence, really."
*Yet he continued on with a smile, insisting — sincerely, not out of mere humbleness — that he was no beast, but a man.*
Reinhard: "Strip him of his status, and a man becomes no different from any other of his fellow humans.  That is about all there is to it — no, that is indeed how it must be. We fall when struck; we die when shot. That is how man ought to be: living his life till death's hour is struck, and he inevitably returns to the dust from whence he came.  I believe... I believe I merely wanted someone to tell me. And for that, you have my gratitude.  Eternity eludes us... We cannot become phantasms. "
*He then turned around and began to make his exit. And so ended our chance encounter. Whatever fate may have had in store for us, I knew we would never meet again.*
Reinhard: "Death is the inevitable fate of all that lives. I am no exception. And so shall I vow to live and die as a man...  as a soldier out of many who merely carries out his sworn duty. "
*I closed my book as if to answer that thought. The story had come to an end, and I had to return to reality. No matter what color the world turned, this was where I was born, and where I should and would live. A man must never once forget that; should we do so, we will be haunted by our dreams forever, longing after eternity.*
Reinhard: "I bid you farewell. Pray tell me your name before I depart."
Ren: "Reichhart."
*Though I wasn't too fond of the name itself, uttering it was my way of accepting reality.*
Ren: "Lotus Reichhart. I'm in the same business as yourself, overseeing executions. Well, just the leftovers, really."
Reinhard: "I see..."
*Naturally, Reinhard was aware of what that name signified. As it turned out, my family produced quite a number of famed executioners in the past, so to someone like Reinhard, I must've felt like a distant relative.*
Reinhard: "This explains a lot. I do have to say, though, albeit the world considers Johann the most prominent practitioner of your profession, I would nonetheless deem you a more fitting candidate.  The lotus... an opium that cripples the mind and makes it forget all the world's hardships.  Had it not been for Odysseus, they would have repeated their folly for all eternity. "
Ren: "Which is why... I'll become that Odysseus."
*I would break free from that cycle. Like the runaway son, who leaves his past home to find a new cycle to fit into, one defined by his own terms. I realized the sheer contradiction of that theory, but in the end, I think it fit me just fine, all things considered. I was no hero. I'd be the first to admit that. Yet...*
Ren: "I feel... that there may be something for me to accomplish beyond that horizon. Or... something I may have already accomplished. Either way, I plan to live my life with that in mind."
Ren: "Goodbye, Lieutenant General. Sieg Heil."
Reinhard: "Aye. Sieg Heil."
*However, just as he was about to close the door behind him...*
Reinhard: "I now feel fulfilled and desire nothing more. I will continue to live my life, not knowing what the future may hold. For that is what I swore to do. "
*...he said something I couldn't quite comprehend.*
Reinhard: "May your future be littered with bliss. Live in both realities alike. By meeting me, you must have come in contact with enough residue of our phantasm to break through the fold. Embark to Japan. "
Reinhard: "Theresia is waiting for you."
Ren: "...!"
*I felt something odd once I heard that name.*
Reinhard: "Frohe Weihnachten. This shall be my tribute to the victor. The Goddess' embrace is quite a pleasant one, wouldn't you agree? "
*And with that, Reinhard made his exit.*
Ren: "... Ren: Theresia. "
*I couldn't quite explain the warmth that filled my heart as I uttered that name, but...*
Ren: "Japan...?"
*...I felt like l'd glimpsed an old promise in that yet unseen, faraway land.*
*Other Story――"Nihil difficile amanti" unlocked.*
Machina: "..."
*The abrupt sensation of falling; of drifting backwards in a stream. His awakening occurred abruptly and with unprecedented naturality.*
Machina: "This place..."
His thoughts were crystal clear; he could determine his own identity and where he was with perfect accuracy. Yet one thing — responsible for his befuddled gasp — escaped him: the knowledge of time. If his senses did not lie, this present moment should have been in the past. 
Ren: "Hey. Hey, are you listening to me?"
*A sudden voice from behind brought his disoriented consciousness back to reality. He turned in the direction of its source, only to find one of his comrades squinting at him, clearly irritated.*
Ren: "What are you doing, spacing out like that? And what's with that mug? You got a stomachache or something?"
Machina: "No. I am fine.  However, it appears I was indeed slightly disoriented. Perhaps I had slept too much, which no doubt prompted strange dreams. "

*They'd returned from the front lines just the other day. Needless to say, the place was a complete hellhole that offered no opportunites for proper sleep, so it was little wonder they'd need some time to readjust themselves after leaving all that behind. Wounds suffered in war weren't always physical. If anything, the mental scars left by being exposed to the horrors of war were a far more serious issue, as it rendered their hearts unable to ever find respite. Many a man, no matter how great, had to struggle with adjustment disorders upon returning from the battlefield.*
*Compliance and adaptation were unnerving things indeed — a man could eventually acclimatize even to the most terrible and savage of conditions. Or rather, man would not have survived as an animal otherwise. The very fact that he and his comrades were still alive was by itself proof that they had gotten used to living in hell. And that was why they would now find themselves alienated from the world outside it. Anyone realized that the world extended to all sides indefinitely, yet few could account for all the hills and mountains contorting the terrain.*
*As such, a disparity of that kind was probably responsible for disorienting him tonight. A shameful display of softness, but not the kind that necessitated hiding it from a kindred soul. He did not doubt that most people suffered from the same ailment in this day and age. That was how he honestly felt on his way back to civilization to receive his medal at the end of June of 1944.*
Ren: "But well, you can't say we didn't benefit from this whole mess. Whatever other qualms we might have, it's still great to finally be able to eat and sleep in peace.  Ren: That's what you get for being a hero, I guess. It's all thanks to you, Michael. "
*Michael. Right. That was his name. Being surprised and even oddly moved by the sound of his own name was certainly a sign of his abnormal state of mind, although the phenomenon did not upset him. Rather, he felt it important to maintain his consciousness in this drowsy and vague state.*
*He was a man of iron — just another cog in the giant machine of war. His name was of little importance. As such, he cast aside his emotions and acted only to carry out his role as an instrument of slaughter. The only reason he had been called a hero was because he'd ended up being slightly better at taking lives than the rest. To paraphrase, he was unmatched in terms of ignoring reality and retreating to his own delusions and phantasms. That was all.*

There's no point in separating our own selves depending on our environment, calling one version the real deal while labeling the other as the false, useless one. "

They hadn't known each other for long, but their bond — forged in the fires of war — surpassed any shallow relationship they could have established in times of peace. To be as iron; to be hard as a tank in both appearance and spirit.*

He cast aside all that constituted his self, and became a machine excelling at war, and only war. Ren: "So you should treasure yourself a little, too. It might sound a bit corny, but it's these kind of things that stack up and grow to hold meaning later, don't you think? My wish to protect the present moment — and my labeling it ephemeral — constituted a pompous assertion that it was brittle and infinitesimal. As such, I never considered that it could possess the power to undo me.*
Machina: "Our arrogance opened a lethal chink in our defense."
*Many a great man perished by being stabbed in the back by a woman. The notion that they would be harmless in a fair fight proved to be their undoing.*
Machina: "We have returned from the most horrifying of battles. And we believed there could exist no chaos terrible enough to surpass what we have already conquered.  That notion must have made us appear to them like unsuspecting fish in a barrel. "
Machina: "We thought we were safe while standing right in the middle of a snake's coil. And so, we received their invitation while being none to wiser to what truly happened. After all, the battlefield was the worst possible hell we could imagine. Or rather, hell itself must have manifested on earth in the form of the battlefield.  They tempted us to tread the path of carnage.  Just like so many of our comrades in that age...  we were cast inside a destined gauntlet of malice. "

Machina: "You will soon understand."
*With that...*
Machina: "Or rather, you have to know."

Machina: "Where should I go...?"
*Anxiety coiled around his heart. Even within that unbearable heat, a vague but undeniable chill rushed through him. He was crumbling to ashes with every passing moment, barely retaining human shape, yet that alien surge of anxiety made his blood freeze.*
*To his friend, repose was merely another facet of the everyday, yet Michael — after all was said and done — failed to imagine and discover a life after the war. And for that reason, he could not cling onto life, either. He had already made peace with his fate. He understood that a man like himself could have no other future. Yet he could not grow to enjoy fighting, and as such, poured his entire being into putting it to end. His friend once warned him not to lose himself — this was Michael's answer.*
*It was not like he desired death. He merely acknowledged and embraced it as the only way for his battles to end. As a result, he would close his eyes with pride — he had fulfilled his goal in life. His friend warned him not to become a monster by wearing one's fur, and this was the only way for him to remain human. Or at least, it should have been.*

*Did his friend try to call out his name in that last moment? Had Michael heard his voice, he would have likely been able to embrace death with absolute conviction about his identity. A man who adapted to the battlefield by melding his soul with iron allowed something mortally important to escape his grasp, just as his friend had forewarned. And so, it was impossible to tell whether the soldier engulfed by flames in that moment was man or machine.*
The question followed almost naturally: where was he supposed to go? Or rather, where was he being taken? He could feel a set of humongous fingers — belonging to an entity far beyond human comprehension — coil around his soul. 
Pride and self-esteem sprang forth from his being on the verge of death, as if dragged out by force, completely disregarding his own convictions. A terrifying truth had been revealed: that a man robbed of the very rule he imposed upon himself would no longer be a man at all. And so, he screamed. As he sank deeper into that mercurial sea of apathy, his craving surged forth with maddened zeal. "How dare you... Don't rob me of my deserved end." 
All he had left was a wish to retain the glory he had lost. That was all he demanded: the climax — the finale — he earned as a mortal man. It stood as the very proof of his existence. He would not tolerate this disgrace. 
Machina: "..."
*And with that, he eventually came to within Heydrich's castle. He could recall neither his name nor the moment of his death. The only thing left to him was the humiliation of having been robbed of what belonged to him. A wretched un-life of shame.*
*The countless battles he had braved granted him an illusion of long-sought repose. Yet in his foolishness, he did not realize that the glory earned in victories past was but a herald summoning him to the next stage of bloodshed. He had enough. He wished for it to end. The crimson of blood. The white of bones. The black of charred flesh. The gray of splattered entrails. The gleam of bayonets. The metal of bullets. The oscillation of the ground in the wake of an army of creaking tanks. The feculent smell of trenches. To escape them now, he had no choice but to embrace the carnage once more.*
Machina: "I cannot end unless I kill you."
*Words he uttered to everyone he met within the gauntlet of malice. For he no longer knew who his opponents were. He killed and killed, wreaking havoc and sowing carnage as an undead slave to strife. All for the sake of his eventual liberation.*
Machina: "Come. You are the last one. We may have even known each other once."
*That day, Michael killed him with his own hands.*

Ren: "You're trying to say I was once a man who fought alongside you."

Only one who has attained the degree of Atziluth could possibly paint this vast sea of information in their color.  But you should already have comprehended that fact. "

But is that a choice stemming from your own soul? Were you not merely forced into putting a leash around your neck by countless bitter circumstances? "

If I fought and ended up painting the world in my color — freezing it in time — then Marie would probably do something about it. With her at my side, I might be able to emanate without destroying the world.  Ren: But once my world emanated, it would be too late. There'd be no turning back. "

If Marie attained the Throne with her craving — a wish to envelop all — she would most likely embrace my dangerous craving as well. I could probably coexist with the Goddess. But then what would become of Himuro? I couldn't possibly abandon her. If I became a phantasm while she remained a mortal woman, we couldn't walk the same path, nor share the same life. I didn't want that.*

*December 25, 1939. Berlin, Germany. 12:27 AM*
*By the time I came to my senses, the night had already marched past midnight. And so, I lifted my gaze from the book in my hands. The same year that may end up being remembered by future generations as a period of incessant turmoil steadily edged towards its closing days. With it, the new year was preparing for its graceful entry, promising thrice the turmoil. Albeit, "chaos" would have been far more fitting a name for what was surely to come, truth be told. Four months had come and gone since the invasion of Poland. Four months since the United Kingdom and France issued a declaration of war against Germany. Although it would allegedly prove to be the retaliation to humiliation and poverty we — the young generation — suffered in the aftermath of the previous war, the thought of another grand-scale conflict breaking out nonetheless filled my heart with gloom.*
*And all those elderly veterans that fought on the frontlines and experienced the bitter taste of defeat firsthand would no doubt feel it tenfold. So why did we plunge headfirst into a new war? I realized the importance of possessing land, resources, and food. I truly did. You'd find plenty who hungered for honor and glory. And even more who wished for victory to wash our nation's reputation clean of the taint of defeat. Should the events from two decades ago be recorded in history as the only World War fought by men, Germany and its people would forever be remembered as a nation of the defeated.*
*Either way, this was a choice very much made with the future in mind. And to that end, the present was now being sacrificed. I realized this might have been the hollow, infantile grumbling of one who'd seen precious little of life. Yet it did not change the fact that the whole thing was messing up my life. My comfortable equilibrium of the “here and now” was being torn to shreds. Stop it. Leave it be. I know how selfish and arrogant that may have sounded, yet it was how I truly felt. In fact, it would have made me particularly sad to miss the next installment of the serialized book I was just reading. I didn't care for the circumstances of the author or the world, I wanted to know how the story ended.*
*Even I was amazed by how foolish this train of thought was.*

*I heard the sound of approaching footsteps from behind.*

*Was it just my delusion? A groundless fantasy?*
*But whatever it was, that void alone was undeniably real.*
*I yearned to meet the man of my dreams.*
*Even if that was but a delusion to escape loneliness, he lived inside me. And that was enough to make him real for me.*
*Things once lost would never return. No identical thing could be born twice. I had no way of telling what kind of a story awaited me in this land, with my life starting anew from zero.*
*The transient scenery I glimpsed in that visionlike dream vanished as soon as I opened my eyes. I no longer knew what it was.*
*But I remember loving it. Treasuring it. Those feelings alone remained with me. And I could declare that with absolute conviction.*
